\chapter{API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{api_reference:api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section is organized by public object first, not by whatever file happened to generate the page.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstepscope


\section{PlussMic API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{api/plussmic_root:plussmic-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{api/plussmic_root::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic is organized by public surface first, so you can enter through the exact family of objects you are using.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table}} covers tabular analysis surfaces such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindle}} covers aligned stream containers such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Archive}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bundle}} covers heterogeneous record containers such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Slot}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Registry}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plotting}} covers plotting and display\sphinxhyphen{}oriented helper surfaces.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{PlussMic \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{table}}}
\label{\detokenize{api/plussmic_table:plussmic-table}}\label{\detokenize{api/plussmic_table::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table}} model is the main analysis surface in PlussMic.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}}}}}} for named, mixed\sphinxhyphen{}type tabular analysis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}}}}}} when you want one typed column outside a frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{atlas_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}}}}}} when you want a depth stack of frames.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}}}}}} when you want a named, multi\sphinxhyphen{}table workspace
with declared relationships and join\sphinxhyphen{}graph queries across several frames at once.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{DataFrame::abs}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:dataframe-abs}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{abs}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every numeric feature with its absolute value, cell by cell. A negative value
becomes its positive counterpart, a positive value is left as\sphinxhyphen{}is, and a null cell stays
null — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{abs()}} only ever changes the sign of an observed number, never invents a value
for a missing one.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by its
absolute value. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) are left
exactly as they were.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Take the absolute value of a signed numeric feature.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{delta}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{\PYGZhy{}5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{\PYGZhy{}2.5}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Ho}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Output (after)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:output-after}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
====================
     | delta  city  
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | 5      Accra 
1    | 3      Tema  
2    | NULL   Kumasi
3    | 2.5    Ho    
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both negative cells (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5}} at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2.5}} at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}) flipped sign; the already\sphinxhyphen{}positive
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is untouched. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} stayed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{abs()}} never fills
a missing value — and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}}, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature, was never a candidate for the operation.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{abs()}} applies to \sphinxstylestrong{every} numeric feature on the frame at once; there is no
per\sphinxhyphen{}feature selector. Apply it to one feature at a time via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}} if only some columns should change.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nulls pass through completely unchanged — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{abs()}} is not a substitute for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/add:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise addition, for every numeric feature on the frame.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} is one of eight identically\sphinxhyphen{}shaped arithmetic methods
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pow}}}}}}}) that all share the exact
same overload set and alignment rules — only the arithmetic operation itself differs.
Reach for the named method over the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+}} operator when you want to chain it inline in a
pipeline, or when the broadcast direction needs to be explicit rather than implied by
operator overloading.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/add:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand, in one of three shapes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}: one scalar, broadcast against every numeric feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}: another frame, added feature\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}feature and case\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}case after
the two frames are aligned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}: one column of values, broadcast according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} (see below).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand is broadcast:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (the default): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} supplies \sphinxstylestrong{one value per feature} — its
length must match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}}. Feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}’s value is added to every case in
column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}. This is the natural shape for “add a different constant to each column.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} supplies \sphinxstylestrong{one value per case} — its length must match
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}}. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}’s value is added across every feature in row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}. This is the
natural shape for “add a per\sphinxhyphen{}row adjustment across every column.”

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand is aligned to the current
frame before the arithmetic runs (by position, case label, or feature name), and how
missing values are filled during alignment. Defaults to strict positional alignment.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/add:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature increased by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) are always left unchanged,
whether the right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand is a scalar, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, or another \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (one value per column) is the default for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (one value per row) must be requested explicitly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the reflected form (useful mainly for readability when the frame is the
right\sphinxhyphen{}hand conceptual operand), see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}}}}}}} — though for addition
specifically, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a.add(b)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b.radd(a)}}\sphinxhyphen{}style reflection produce the same result
either way, since addition is commutative.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sub}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::mul}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::div}}}}}}}:
the other arithmetic methods sharing this exact overload shape.

\item {}

paired operations.

\item {}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::aggregate}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:dataframe-aggregate}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{aggregate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{msharp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Of}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{SummarySpec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{specs}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Collapses the whole frame down to a single summary row: each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SummarySpec}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{specs}}
names a source feature, a reduction (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SummaryOp}}), and an output column name, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate()}} computes one scalar per spec, packing all of them side by side into a
one\sphinxhyphen{}row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"summary"}}. It is the “dashboard row” counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}} — where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} gives you a fixed, canned set of
statistics per feature, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate()}} lets you hand\sphinxhyphen{}pick exactly which statistics on
exactly which features go into a single, custom summary row, in whatever order you
like.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate()}} is a thin \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} wrapper around the frame\sphinxhyphen{}oriented
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarize()}}; use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarize()}} directly if you want the plain one\sphinxhyphen{}row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
without the view’s auto\sphinxhyphen{}render behavior.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}SummarySpec\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
An ordered list of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SummarySpec\{output, feature, op\}}} instructions, one per output
column:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): the source column to reduce. Cannot be empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SummaryOp}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}): the reduction to apply —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Median}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Prod}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}} accept a feature of any kind (they count non\sphinxhyphen{}null values or
distinct non\sphinxhyphen{}null values respectively); every other op requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} to be a
numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} and throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::summarize: numeric reductions require numeric Series feature"}} otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{output}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): the name of the resulting column. Leave it empty to
auto\sphinxhyphen{}generate one as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{feature\}\_\{op\_name\}"}} (for example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{amount\_max}} for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"", "amount", SummaryOp::Max\}}}) — note the auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated name for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{feature\}\_distinct\_count"}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{feature\}\_nunique"}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two specs that resolve to the same output name (whether both explicit or one
auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated) are rejected with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::summarize: duplicate output name \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{}"}} — give every spec a distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{output}}, or vary the auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated name by
using different \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} combinations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, following the same convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} returns a quiet view you print explicitly; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} allows
the view to auto\sphinxhyphen{}render itself in a temporary\sphinxhyphen{}expression context.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A one\sphinxhyphen{}row view (case label \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"summary"}}) with one output column per spec, in the
order the specs were given.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrame::summarize: numeric reductions require numeric Series feature
DataFrame::summarize: duplicate output name \PYGZsq{}x\PYGZsq{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region}} is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}} needs an actual numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} to add
up, so it throws rather than treating text as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}. The second call gives two
different specs the same explicit output name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"x"}}) — rejected up front,
before either reduction runs, exactly like an auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated name collision
would be.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Duplicate output names (whether explicit or auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated) are rejected up front,
before any reduction runs — give each spec a distinct output name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}} tolerate any feature kind; every other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SummaryOp}} requires a
numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature and throws otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}} on an all\sphinxhyphen{}null numeric feature (after dropping nulls) returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Prod}}
returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} — the identity element for each operation — rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}; every
other op returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} in that case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate()}} always collapses to exactly one row; for a per\sphinxhyphen{}group breakdown instead
of a single summary row, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/aggregate:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe}}}}}}}: a fixed, canned set of per\sphinxhyphen{}feature statistics,

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/align:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{AlignSpec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spec}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/align:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reindexes the frame onto a new target case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis, a new target feature order, or
both at once — the general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose “make this frame line up with a shape I already
know” tool. Every source case is matched to a target case \sphinxstyleemphasis{by label value}, not by
physical row position: a case label that appears in the target axis is looked up
among the source’s rows carrying that same label (matched in order, for the rare case
of repeated labels), and a target label that has no match in the source becomes a
brand\sphinxhyphen{}new row, filled with the null cell (or with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}, if provided).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align(new\_label)}} is the shorthand that only touches the case axis, leaving every
feature untouched. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align(spec)}} is the full form: an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignSpec}} can reorder features
independently of case labels, introduce brand\sphinxhyphen{}new feature columns that don’t exist in
the source at all (also null\sphinxhyphen{} or fill\sphinxhyphen{}filled), or restrict the output to a smaller
feature subset — all in the same call.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/align:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{new\_label} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, case\sphinxhyphen{}only overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The target case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis, in the exact order you want the output rows in. Equivalent
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align(AlignSpec\{.label = new\_label\})}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{spec} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignSpec\&}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}Thread\textgreater{}}}, default unset): target case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis. Leave
unset to keep the frame’s existing case axis unchanged while still reordering
features via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default empty): target feature order.
Leave empty to keep every existing feature, in its existing order. A name in this
list that doesn’t exist on the source frame becomes a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new, entirely missing
column in the output (filled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}, if set) rather than an error — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}
never rejects an unknown target feature name the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}}
does.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}double\textgreater{}}}, default unset): a numeric value used to fill
any newly introduced gap — a target case label absent from the source, or a target
feature absent entirely — instead of leaving it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} only ever applies
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind (numeric) columns; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} gap is always
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}, since there is no sensible way to “fill” a missing
string or date with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/align:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame reindexed onto the requested case axis and/or feature order. Existing
cells are carried over unchanged; new gaps are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} unless \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} says otherwise.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/align:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrame::align: duplicate target feature \PYGZsq{}price\PYGZsq{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two identical entries in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} would mean two output columns both
called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"price"}} — ambiguous, so it’s rejected rather than silently
producing a duplicate or overwriting one with the other.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/align:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matching is by case\sphinxhyphen{}label \sphinxstyleemphasis{value}, not physical position — this is what
distinguishes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}} from a plain {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}\sphinxhyphen{}style reorder.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing target feature is manufactured wholesale rather than rejected, unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}}’s multi\sphinxhyphen{}name projection, which throws on an unknown
name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} only rescues \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind gaps from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}; text and calendar features stay
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} regardless.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::conform}}}}}}} builds on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}: it matches feature order to
another frame’s exact feature list first, then calls the case\sphinxhyphen{}only overload of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}} to match that frame’s case order too.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/align:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/conform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::conform}}}}}}}: align both feature order and case order to
match another frame’s structure in a single call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::features}}}}}}}: a stricter feature\sphinxhyphen{}subset projection that
rejects unknown names instead of manufacturing them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::take}}}}}}}: reorder/select cases by physical position instead of
by label.

\end{itemize}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/all:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether \sphinxstylestrong{every} value is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} along the requested axis, over a set of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features — the counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/any::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{any()}}}}}}}, which only requires
one. Every feature it reduces over must already be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} is
left empty, it defaults to \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} column in the frame, so a frame that mixes boolean
flags with other feature types must pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} explicitly to select only the
boolean ones.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two overloads differ only in whether you supply an axis: the short overload always
reduces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (down each feature’s cases); the longer overload lets you choose
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} instead (across each row’s selected features).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/all:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features to reduce over. An empty range (the default) selects
every column in the frame — which only works if every column actually is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; otherwise, pass the specific boolean feature names you want.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} when omitted)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} reduces down each feature’s cases, producing one
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} per feature — “was this flag true on every single row?” \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}
reduces across each row’s selected features instead, producing one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} per
case — “does this row satisfy every selected flag?”, a common eligibility\sphinxhyphen{}gate shape.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects the reduction’s validity. A missing cell is
always treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} while computing the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} value itself — a null can
never \sphinxstyleemphasis{cause} an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all()}} result to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} on its own, since it’s excluded rather
than counted as a failing observation. What \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull}} changes is whether that
computed result is trusted:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): the result is reported as\sphinxhyphen{}is, regardless of any nulls present.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: if any cell that participated in a reduction was missing, that reduction’s
result comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} instead of the computed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/all:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} entry per participating feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}, the default) or per case
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), holding whether every value was \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

1  false
2  false

4  false

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/all:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
is\PYGZus{}priority  false
ptype: Series
is\PYGZus{}priority  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{is\_priority}} has an observed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} value (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}), so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all()}} computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
either way. With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}, that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} is reported as\sphinxhyphen{}is. With
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, the missing cell at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} invalidates the whole result — the
presence of \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} missing value in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}} reduction is enough to make
that feature’s result \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, even though the computed answer didn’t depend on the
missing cell.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/all:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all()}}’s result is labeled by feature name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or by case index
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced
from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every selected feature must already be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}
explicitly whenever the frame contains non\sphinxhyphen{}boolean columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing value never makes an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all()}} result \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} by itself; it can only make
the result \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} (under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}) or be silently excluded (under
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty selection (a feature with zero cases, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} matching nothing) is a
validation error, not a vacuously\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} result.

\end{itemize}

truthiness.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signatures}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/any:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether \sphinxstylestrong{at least one} value is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} along the requested axis, over a set
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features. Every feature it reduces over must already be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{any()}} never coerces numbers, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} columns
into truthiness the way some languages implicitly do. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} is left empty, it
defaults to \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} column in the frame, so a frame that mixes boolean flags with
other feature types must pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} explicitly to select only the boolean ones.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two overloads differ only in whether you supply an axis: the short overload always
reduces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (down each feature’s cases); the longer overload lets you choose
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} instead (across each row’s selected features).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/any:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features to reduce over. An empty range (the default) selects
every column in the frame — which only works if every column actually is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; otherwise, pass the specific boolean feature names you want.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} when omitted)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} reduces down each feature’s cases, producing one
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} per feature — “did this flag ever fire across all rows?” \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}
reduces across each row’s selected features instead, producing one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} per
case — “did this row have at least one flag set?”

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects the reduction’s validity. A missing cell is
always treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} while computing the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} value itself — a null can
never \sphinxstyleemphasis{cause} an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{any()}} result to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} on its own. What \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull}} changes is
whether that computed result is trusted:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): the result is reported as\sphinxhyphen{}is, regardless of any nulls present.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: if any cell that participated in a reduction was missing, that reduction’s
result comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} instead of the computed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} — even though the
value was still computed the same way underneath.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/any:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} entry per participating feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}, the default) or per case
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), holding whether at least one value was \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/any:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
is\PYGZus{}priority  true
ptype: Series
is\PYGZus{}priority  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{is\_priority}} has one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} value (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}), so both calls compute the same
underlying answer. With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}, that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} is reported as\sphinxhyphen{}is.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, the missing cell at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} invalidates the whole result —
even though the answer would have been \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} either way, the presence of \sphinxstyleemphasis{any}
missing value in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}} reduction is enough to make that feature’s
result \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/any:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{any()}}’s result is labeled by feature name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or by case index
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced
from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every selected feature must already be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}
explicitly whenever the frame contains non\sphinxhyphen{}boolean columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing value never makes an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{any()}} result \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} by itself; it can only make the
result \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} (under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}) or be silently ignored (under
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{assign}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{DeriveSpec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{specs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{assign}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{assignments}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add or replace one or more features on a DataFrame and return the resulting frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::assign(...)}} is the main column\sphinxhyphen{}creation surface when you want a pipeline\sphinxhyphen{}friendly, non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating way to engineer features. One overload accepts already\sphinxhyphen{}computed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} values; the other accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DeriveSpec}} expressions so PlussMic can compute the features inside the call.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The motivation is the same as any non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating feature\sphinxhyphen{}creation call: instead of
mutating a frame in a sequence of separate statements
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df{[}"total"{]} = ...; df{[}"passed"{]} = ...;}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}} lets a chain of feature
derivations read as a single expression —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.assign(\{...\}).filter(...).sort\_values(\{...\})}} — which keeps intermediate,
partially\sphinxhyphen{}derived frames out of named variables you would otherwise have to track.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{assignments}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(feature\_name, thread)}} pairs.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this overload when each output feature is already computed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a feature name already exists, the existing feature is replaced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a feature name is new, the feature is appended to the frame.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DeriveSpec}} instructions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each spec provides:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}: the output feature name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expr}}: a callback that receives the current frame and returns the derived \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this overload when you want the frame to compute the derived features inside the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign(...)}} call itself.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested features added or replaced.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Existing features keep their current order. New features are appended in the order you supply them unless a name collision causes one to overwrite an existing feature in place.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::transform: compute one derived thread from a callback when you are working row\sphinxhyphen{}wise or feature\sphinxhyphen{}wise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::set: write one feature directly when you already have the final thread.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::put: update selected cells rather than constructing whole derived features.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assignments}} overload is best when you already computed the target \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} values before the call.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DeriveSpec}} overload evaluates specs from left to right against the progressively updated frame. That means later specs in the same call can depend on features created by earlier specs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign(...)}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating. The current frame is not edited in place.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Casts one or more existing features to new scalar dtypes — the typed conversion surface
for turning imported or computed columns into the representation later code actually
needs — normalizing a
column that arrived as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}} but is really integer counts, converting a 0/1 numeric
flag into a proper boolean before it’s used in filtering, or tightening precision once a
computation is done and the extra headroom is no longer needed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two shapes are offered depending on whether every selected feature shares one target
dtype or each needs its own:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Shared\sphinxhyphen{}dtype overload} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype}}): cast a list of feature names to the
same dtype in one call — the common case when several columns arrived with the same
wrong type.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mapping overload} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_dtypes}}, a list or initializer\sphinxhyphen{}list of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(feature\_name, dtype)}} pairs): cast each selected feature to its own dtype, when the
targets differ feature by feature.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Either way, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}} returns a new frame; features not mentioned in the request pass
through completely unchanged.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names to cast when every one of them should land on the same target \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype}}.
Features not listed are left unchanged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dtype} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shared target scalar dtype for the feature\sphinxhyphen{}list overload. Common choices include
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Bool}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Int64}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Float64}}.
Pick the narrowest dtype that still matches what downstream code plans to do with the
column — casting to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} too early can throw away information a later filter still
needed as a raw number, for instance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_dtypes} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string\_view, pluss::ScalarType\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string\_view, pluss::ScalarType\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(feature\_name, dtype)}} pairs for mixed casting, one target dtype per
listed feature. Use this overload once the shared\sphinxhyphen{}dtype overload is no longer expressive
enough — for example casting an ID column to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} while casting a flag column to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} in the same call.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested feature casts applied. Features not mentioned in the
cast request are preserved unchanged, including their original dtype.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Cast one selected feature to a shared target dtype.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the feature\sphinxhyphen{}list overload (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype(\{"a", "b"\}, dtype)}}) when several features
should land on the same target dtype; use the mapping overload
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype(\{\{"a", dtype\_a\}, \{"b", dtype\_b\}\})}}) when each feature needs its own.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This method returns a new frame; it does not mutate the current \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} in place.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Casting does not validate that the conversion is lossless — casting a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} column
with fractional values to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} truncates, the same way a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static\_cast\textless{}int\textgreater{}}} would.
Confirm the source values are already integral before casting for cleanliness rather
than for rounding.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For casting an entire feature onto a different \sphinxstyleemphasis{payload family} (for example forcing a
numeric\sphinxhyphen{}looking column onto the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} text family before string operations), see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cast::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cast()}}}}}}} instead — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}} changes the scalar dtype within a feature’s
existing payload family, not the family itself. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cast()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CastSpec}} overload accepts a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastTarget}} (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastTarget::Note}}) for exactly that purpose.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

family (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/etc.), not just its scalar dtype within the current family.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Backward\sphinxhyphen{}fills missing values: each null cell is replaced by the next \sphinxstyleemphasis{observed} value
below it in the same feature, propagating upward. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}} works on every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
kind PlussMic supports — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — not just
numeric features, since propagating an existing observation doesn’t require numeric
semantics the way interpolation does.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A trailing run of nulls with no later observed value in the same feature is left
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — there is nothing below it to borrow from.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Maximum number of consecutive nulls to fill per run, counted starting from the null
closest to the next observed value and moving away from it.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} (the default): no limit, fill every null that has a later observed value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A non\sphinxhyphen{}negative value: fill at most that many nulls per run; any remaining nulls
further from the anchor stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FillOptions}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Structured form for targeting a feature subset:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}: the feature names to fill. Empty (the default) targets every feature on
the frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}: same meaning as the simple overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with nulls backward\sphinxhyphen{}filled in the targeted
features. Untargeted features are unchanged.

=============

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} both borrowed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}} (the next observed value below them), and case
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} borrowed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Kumasi"}}. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} was never null, so it is untouched.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Cap the run length with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = 1}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{partially\PYGZus{}filled}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{bfill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{partially\PYGZus{}filled}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
=============
     | city  
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | Accra 
1    | NULL  
2    | Tema  
3    | Tema  
4    | Kumasi
5    | Kumasi
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[6 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = 1}}, only one null per run gets filled — the one closest to the observed
value it borrows from. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} (adjacent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}}) is filled, but case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (one step
further from the anchor) is not, because the run already used up its one allowed fill.
Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}’s run is only one null long, so it fills either way.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}} propagates upward feature by feature; values never cross feature
boundaries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}} is not restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
features — it works on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} columns too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A trailing run of nulls with no later observed value in that feature stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}},
no matter the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the opposite direction (propagating the last observed value forward), see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}}}}}}. For numeric linear interpolation between two observed
neighbors, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bfill:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ffill}}}}}}}: propagate the previous observed value forward
instead of the next one backward.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/interp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::interp}}}}}}}: fill numeric gaps by interpolating between
neighbors instead of copying one of them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::fillnull}}}}}}}: write an explicit replacement value instead of
borrowing a neighboring observation.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::bottom}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bottom:dataframe-bottom}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bottom::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bottom:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{bottom}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bottom:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} rows with the smallest values in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}, with every other feature
carried along unchanged — the ascending counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/top::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top()}}}}}}}. This is
exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values(\{feature\}, /*ascending=*/true)}} followed by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head(n)}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing values in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} always sort to the very end — even here, in the ascending
case — so a row with a missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} value can only appear in the result if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is
large enough to reach all the way down past every real value.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bottom:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The name of the feature to rank by, smallest first.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How many bottom\sphinxhyphen{}ranked rows to return. Values larger than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} return the whole
frame, sorted, rather than erroring.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bottom:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} rows (or fewer, if the source frame is smaller), sorted by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} in ascending order, with every feature preserved.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bottom:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bottom()}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values(\{feature\}, true).head(n)}}; reach for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} directly if you need more than one sort key.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing value in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} sorts to the very end regardless of ascending or
descending direction — this is the same nulls\sphinxhyphen{}last rule \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top()}} follows, not a
nulls\sphinxhyphen{}first rule for the ascending case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the largest values instead of the smallest, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/top::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top()}}}}}}}, which shares
this exact signature.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/top::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::top}}}}}}}: the descending counterpart, returning the largest \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}
rows by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sort\_values}}}}}}}: the general sorting method this is built
on, supporting multiple keys and mixed sort directions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::head}}}}}}}: the plain positional prefix \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bottom()}} applies after
sorting.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces one, several, or every numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature’s values with integer bucket
codes, based on a strictly increasing list of bin edges — the classic “cut into
bands” transform used for grading scales, coarse histogram binning, or turning a
continuous value into a small number of discrete tiers before grouping or one\sphinxhyphen{}hot
encoding. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N + 1}} edges define \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} buckets; every other feature (and every non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
feature, if you called the no\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload) passes through completely unchanged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A value that doesn’t fall into any bucket — outside the full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}bins.front(), bins.back(){]}}} span, given the current \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}} settings — becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the output rather than being clamped into the nearest bucket.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, single\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bucketize exactly this one feature; every other feature is left alone.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bucketize exactly this named subset of features, all using the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}/
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}} settings. An empty list is a no\sphinxhyphen{}op that returns the frame
unchanged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(no feature argument)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bucketize every numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature on the frame automatically. Throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::bucketize: no numeric Series features available"}} if there are none.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bins} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}double\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Strictly increasing bin edges. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N + 1}} edges produce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} buckets: edges \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0, 10, 20, 30\}}} define three buckets. Must contain at least two edges, none of them \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{labels} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicit integer code for each bucket, in edge order. Leave empty to get the default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ..., N\sphinxhyphen{}1}}. If supplied, its length must equal the bucket count exactly
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins.size() \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{right} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which side of each interval is closed:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: every bucket is right\sphinxhyphen{}closed — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(edge{[}i{]}, edge{[}i+1{]}{]}}} — except optionally
the first, governed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: every bucket is left\sphinxhyphen{}closed and right\sphinxhyphen{}open — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}edge{[}i{]}, edge{[}i+1{]})}} — for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{every} bucket, including the first; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}} has no effect in this mode.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{include\_lowest} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only consulted when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = true}}: whether the very first bucket also accepts values
exactly equal to its lower edge (making it \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}edge{[}0{]}, edge{[}1{]}{]}}} instead of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(edge{[}0{]}, edge{[}1{]}{]}}}). Defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, so — unlike some cut\sphinxhyphen{}style APIs elsewhere —
a value sitting exactly on the lowest edge is bucketed rather than dropped by default.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame where every targeted feature has been replaced by its integer bucket
codes (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} for out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range values); every other feature is unchanged.

1    | 1       2

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both features are bucketed with the same edges and default labels; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{amount}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weight}} land in different buckets independently based on their own values —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weight}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{22.0}} (bucket \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{amount}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15.0}} (bucket \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}) demonstrate that each
column is evaluated on its own values, not jointly.

\subparagraph{Output (include\_lowest = false)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest = true}}, the very first bucket is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 10{]}}} (closed on both ends), so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}} lands in bucket \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} alongside
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}}. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest = false}}, that first bucket shrinks to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0, 10{]}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}} no longer satisfies \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} bucket’s lower bound, so it
becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} instead. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25.0}} are unaffected either way, since
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}} only ever changes the lowest bucket’s lower edge.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize:id4}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::bucketize: bin edges must be strictly increasing
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}} followed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}} decreases, violating the strictly\sphinxhyphen{}increasing
requirement — checked up front for the whole edge list before any value is
bucketed.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bin edges must be strictly increasing and non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, checked once up front for the
whole call — a single bad edge rejects the entire \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bucketize()}} call before any
column is touched.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range values become \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, never clamped into the nearest bucket — a value
below the first edge or above the last edge (given the current \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} setting) is
simply missing in the output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The no\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload silently limits itself to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features; it
never attempts to bucketize a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Follow up with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_by}}}}}}} on the bucketed feature to get a frequency
table of how many cases fell into each band.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::count\_by}}}}}}}: tally how many cases landed in each bucket.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cast::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::cast}}}}}}}: change a feature’s underlying dtype or payload kind
outright, rather than binning its numeric values into a small set of codes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/clip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::clip}}}}}}}: cap values into a numeric range instead of assigning
them a discrete bucket code.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/case_study:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose row\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}feature selection method: pick rows by position, by case
label, or by boolean mask, optionally combined with a feature projection, all in one
call that always returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} — even when the selection resolves to a single
row, a single column, or a single cell. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat}} are small selector structs
built via their own static factory methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::at(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::name(...)}}, and so
on, documented below) rather than by setting their fields directly — the fields are an
implementation detail of how the selector is dispatched internally.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third overload, taking a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CasePick}}, is for a different situation: a frame that
already has one or more \sphinxstylestrong{named} case\sphinxhyphen{}label levels, set up via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(...)}}}}}}}. It looks up rows by matching those named levels’
values rather than by position or by the plain default case label.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/case_study:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{rows} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::Case}}) — built with one of:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::at(row)}}: one row by position. Negative positions count from the end
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::at(\sphinxhyphen{}1)}} is the last row).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::slice(start, stop)}}: a half\sphinxhyphen{}open positional slice \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}}, the same
convention {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}} uses.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::take(\{r1, r2, ...\})}}: an explicit, arbitrarily ordered (and possibly
repeating) list of positions — the same generality {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}} offers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::label(value)}}: every row whose current case label equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}. If the same
label appears on more than one row, \sphinxstylestrong{all} of them are returned, not just the
first.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::labels(\{v1, v2, ...\})}}: several labels, in the order you list them — the
output order follows your list, not the frame’s original row order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::span(start, stop)}}: an \sphinxstylestrong{inclusive} case\sphinxhyphen{}label window, from the first row
matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} through the last row matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}. This is a positional
distinction worth noting: it is inclusive on both ends, unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::slice(start, stop)}}, which is exclusive on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::where(bool\_thread)}}: every row where a boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (one entry
per case) is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — the same selection {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} performs.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::Feat}}, optional) — built with one of:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::all()}}: every feature, in source order (the default when this parameter is
omitted entirely).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::name(value)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::at(position)}}: one feature, by name or by position.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::names(\{n1, n2, ...\})}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::take(\{p1, p2, ...\})}}: several features, by
name or by position, in the order you list them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::slice(start, stop)}}: a half\sphinxhyphen{}open positional feature slice.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Feat::span(start, stop)}}: an \sphinxstylestrong{inclusive} feature\sphinxhyphen{}name window, from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}’s
position through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}’s position (in the frame’s own feature order, not
alphabetical) — inclusive on both ends, mirroring \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Case::span()}}’s convention.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pick} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CasePick}}) — a struct with:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: match rows where the named case\sphinxhyphen{}label level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}} equals
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}: the same idea across several named levels at once — every row
must match all of the given level/value pairs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key}}: a full positional key, one value per level in the frame’s own case\sphinxhyphen{}level
order, when you’d rather not name each level explicitly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, removes the matched level(s) from the
result’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label structure after selection, instead of keeping them (now
redundant, since they’re constant across the matched rows) on every result row.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Exactly one of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key}} should be set per call.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/case_study:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing the matched rows (and, with the two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload,
only the selected features), in the order the selector produced them.
