\subparagraph{Output (skipnull = false)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmax:output-skipnull-false}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sales  NULL
 cost  q3
ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}} is missing at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q2}}; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}, the search simply ignores
that cell and finds the maximum (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{100}}) among what’s left, at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q1}}. With
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, the presence of any missing value anywhere in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}}
invalidates the whole result for that feature — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}} comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
outright, even though a perfectly good maximum among the non\sphinxhyphen{}null values still
exists. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cost}} has no missing values at all, so it reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q3}} identically
under both settings. This same call also demonstrates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} passed
explicitly, rather than relying on it being the default.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmax:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmax()}} always returns label strings, never the numeric maximum itself — reach for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/max::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max()}}}}}}} when the value is what you want, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmax()}} when you want to
know where it came from.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two axes produce results with different lengths and different label kinds: one
entry per feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or one entry per case (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}) — do not
assume the result lines up positionally with the source frame’s rows.

\end{itemize}

\item {}

maximum.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/max::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::max}}}}}}}: the numeric maximum value itself, instead of where it
occurs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::cummax}}}}}}}: a running maximum per case, instead of a single
argmax lookup.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::csmin}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:dataframe-csmin}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{csmin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports \sphinxstyleemphasis{where} each numeric feature’s minimum value occurs, not the minimum value
itself — the argmin\sphinxhyphen{}style companion to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}}}}}}, and the mirror of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmax()}}}}}}}. The returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} always holds label strings (case labels or
feature names), never numeric values, so it always prints with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype: Note}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Direction to search along:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default): for each numeric feature, find which \sphinxstyleemphasis{case} holds that
feature’s minimum value. The result has one entry per numeric feature, labeled by
feature name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}: for each case, find which \sphinxstyleemphasis{feature} holds that row’s minimum value.
The result has one entry per case, labeled by the source frame’s case labels.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing\sphinxhyphen{}value policy while searching for the minimum.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed label thread: case labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or feature names
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), one per participating numeric feature or case respectively.

\subparagraph{Output (skipnull = true, the default)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:output-skipnull-true-the-default}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sales  q3
 cost  q1
ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (skipnull = false)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:output-skipnull-false}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sales  NULL
 cost  q1
ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}} is missing at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q2}}; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}, the search simply ignores
that cell and finds the minimum (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{90}}) among what’s left, at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q3}}. With
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, the presence of any missing value anywhere in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}}
invalidates the whole result for that feature — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}} comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
outright, even though a perfectly good minimum among the non\sphinxhyphen{}null values still
exists. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cost}} has no missing values at all, so it reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q1}} identically
under both settings. This same call also demonstrates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} passed
explicitly, rather than relying on it being the default.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmin()}} always returns label strings, never the numeric minimum itself — reach for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}}}}}} when the value is what you want, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmin()}} when you want to
know where it came from.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two axes produce results with different lengths and different label kinds: one
entry per feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or one entry per case (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}) — do not
assume the result lines up positionally with the source frame’s rows.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::cummax}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax:dataframe-cummax}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax:signatures}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cummax}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skip\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every numeric feature with its running (cumulative) maximum, case by case:
the value at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} becomes the largest value seen in that feature from the first
case through case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}, not a single reduced summary value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}}}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}} are all thin wrappers over the same underlying running\sphinxhyphen{}statistic
machinery, so they all share identical \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}} semantics — only the
running operation itself (max, min, product, or sum) differs.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Direction to accumulate along. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) runs down each feature’s
cases in order. Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} accumulates across a row’s features left to
right instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls what happens to the running maximum once a null is encountered:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): a null produces a null \sphinxstyleemphasis{only at that case}. The running
maximum is preserved underneath it and accumulation resumes normally from the next
observed value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the first null poisons every case after it. Once a null is hit, that case
and every subsequent case in the cumulative output become null too.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by its
running maximum. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with the running maximum; it
does not add a new column alongside the original.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the running sum, product, or minimum instead, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}},

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}} semantics described here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To find \sphinxstyleemphasis{which case} holds each feature’s maximum instead of a running value, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmax()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummin:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with the running minimum; it
does not add a new column alongside the original.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the running sum, product, or maximum instead, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}}}}}} — all four share the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}} semantics described here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To find \sphinxstyleemphasis{which case} holds each feature’s minimum instead of a running value, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/csmin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmin()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every numeric feature with its running (cumulative) product, case by case:
the value at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} becomes the product of that feature’s values from the first
case through case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}, not a single reduced summary value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}}}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}} are all thin wrappers over the same underlying running\sphinxhyphen{}statistic
machinery, so they all share identical \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}} semantics — only the
running operation itself (product, max, min, or sum) differs.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Direction to accumulate along. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) runs down each feature’s
cases in order. Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} accumulates across a row’s features left to
right instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls what happens to the running product once a null is encountered:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): a null produces a null \sphinxstyleemphasis{only at that case}. The running
product is preserved underneath it and accumulation resumes normally from the next
observed value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the first null poisons every case after it. Once a null is hit, that case
and every subsequent case in the cumulative output become null too.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by its
running product. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with the running product; it
does not add a new column alongside the original.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the running sum, minimum, or maximum instead, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}}}}}} — all four share the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}} semantics described here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} observed anywhere in a feature collapses every case after it to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}},
since anything multiplied by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} — this is expected behavior, not a bug.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::cumsum}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:dataframe-cumsum}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cumsum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skip\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cumsum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skip\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every numeric feature with its running (cumulative) sum, case by case: the
value at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} becomes the sum of that feature’s values from the first case through
case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} — a running total, not a single reduced summary value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The interesting behavior to understand up front is what happens at a null. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}
does not simply skip the \sphinxstyleemphasis{cell} the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} skips nulls when reducing to
one total; a running total has to decide what to do at every case \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} the null too,
and that decision is controlled entirely by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Direction to accumulate along. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) runs down each feature’s cases
in order — the usual “running total over time/rows” reading. Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}
accumulates across a row’s features left to right instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls what happens to the running total once a null is encountered:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): a null produces a null \sphinxstyleemphasis{only at that case}. The running total is
preserved underneath it and accumulation resumes normally from the next observed value
— the null is a gap in the output, not a break in the running sum.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the first null poisons every case after it. Once a null is hit, that case and
every subsequent case in the cumulative output become null too.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by its
running total. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{score}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output (after)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:output-after}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
=====================
     | student  score
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | Ada      10   
1    | Bola     30   
2    | Chen     NULL 
3    | Dede     35   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Chen}}) is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} because that case’s own value was missing — but case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dede}}) is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{35}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}: the running total silently carried \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30}} forward under the
null and added \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} to it. The null only ever affected its own row’s output cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:output}}

=====================
     | student  score
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | Ada      10   
1    | Bola     30   
2    | Chen     NULL 
3    | Dede     NULL 
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls = false}}, case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} is also \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} even though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dede}}’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}} was a
perfectly good \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} — the missing value at case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} invalidated every running total from
that point on. Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} specifically when a gap in the source data should mean
“we can no longer trust any total downstream of it,” such as an interrupted sensor feed
or a broken audit trail.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with the running total; it does
not add a new column alongside the original. Copy the original feature first (for
example with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}}) if you need both the raw and cumulative values
side by side.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the running product, minimum, or maximum instead of a running sum, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}}}}}} — all
four share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}} semantics described here.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{defined}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{noexcept}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} handle currently owns a usable backing object at all
— not whether any cell inside it is missing. A default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame()}} (no
columns argument) is the ordinary way to end up with an undefined frame; almost every
other constructor and factory method produces a defined one.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
defined() is about object existence, not missing data
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} answers “does this frame exist and can it be used?”, not “does this frame
contain nulls?”. For missing\sphinxhyphen{}data questions, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}}}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}} instead — a frame full of
nulls in every cell is still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined() == true}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if the frame owns a usable backing object and is safe to use in ordinary
operations; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for a default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed, not\sphinxhyphen{}yet\sphinxhyphen{}initialized handle.

recommends, lets calling code sidestep this throw entirely.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{noexcept}} and cheap — it’s a pointer check, not a data scan.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most factory methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}, arithmetic results, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copy()}}, and so on) always
return a defined frame; the main way to encounter an undefined one is the default
constructor, or a moved\sphinxhyphen{}from handle.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling most other methods on an undefined frame throws — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} exists to let
you check first, particularly around optional construction branches or defensive API
boundaries.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::isnull}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::notnull}}}}}}}: per\sphinxhyphen{}cell
missing\sphinxhyphen{}data checks, unrelated to object existence.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/copy::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::copy}}}}}}}: always produces a defined frame, sharing storage with
the source until either side is mutated.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::describe}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe:dataframe-describe}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes descriptive statistics for every numeric feature on the frame and returns them
as a small summary frame: one row per statistic (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25\%}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max}}), one column per participating numeric feature. It is the
value\sphinxhyphen{}level counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/info::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}}}}}} — where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}} tells you the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shape} of
a frame (dtypes, null counts, memory), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} tells you what the \sphinxstyleemphasis{numbers actually
look like}: central tendency, spread, and the shape of the distribution via quartiles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For an ordinary sales, sensor, or grading table, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} is usually the fastest way
to sanity\sphinxhyphen{}check a frame before filtering, grouping, modeling, or plotting it — a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}
wildly different from what you expected, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min}} that is negative when it should not be,
or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max}} several orders of magnitude larger than the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75\%}} line are all visible in one
glance at the summary, long before you would spot them by scrolling through raw rows.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned view, following the same convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}}, and the other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}\sphinxhyphen{}returning
methods:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: keep explicit control over when and how you print or render the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: allow the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} to auto\sphinxhyphen{}render in temporary display
contexts (for example, a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.describe(true);}} statement).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A summary view whose rows are the eight statistics above, in that fixed order, and
whose columns are exactly the numeric features that participated. The result itself
is a small, ordinary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} under the hood — you can chain further operations on
it (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}, and so on) exactly as you would on any other
frame.

unassigned call would produce no output.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} summarizes numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features only. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} features are skipped entirely, the same way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} was skipped in Example 1.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quartiles (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75\%}}) are computed with linear interpolation between the two
closest ranks — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}} therefore coincides with the median exactly, including for
even\sphinxhyphen{}sized samples.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}} uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} in the denominator (sample standard deviation, Bessel’s correction),
not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}. A single\sphinxhyphen{}observation feature would have an undefined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}} — describe a
wider sample, or treat a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count = 1}} column’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}} as not meaningful.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} changes display behavior only; it never changes which statistics are computed
or how missing values are handled.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/div:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise division. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} shares the exact same overload
shape and alignment rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} and the rest of the arithmetic family —
see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s “What It Does” for the full explanation of the scalar/frame/Thread
operand shapes and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
div() and truediv() are the same operation
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}}}}}}} both perform ordinary floating\sphinxhyphen{}point division —
verified against the underlying numeric kernel, they compute identical results for
every input, including integer\sphinxhyphen{}typed features. Neither one truncates or floors the
result the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}} does. Both names are provided so code
reading like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.div(2)}} and code reading like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.truediv(2)}} (for readers coming
from a background where “true division” is a meaningful distinction from floor
division) are both available — pick whichever reads better at the call site, since
there is no behavioral reason to prefer one over the other.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/div:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand, dividing the current frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (broadcast scalar),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (aligned frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (default) supplies one
value per feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} supplies one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature divided by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

=============
     | amount
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
a    | 25    
b    | 40    
c    | 25    
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 1 feat]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s case labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x, y, z}}) are never consulted under the default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions\{\}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}}): the two frames only need the same shape, and
cells are paired by physical position — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}’s row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{100}}) divides by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}) regardless of either side’s labels — so the result
keeps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}’s own case labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a, b, c}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} passed explicitly as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} — one divisor per feature, broadcast down every case in that

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{50.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{25.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{p}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{q}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{divisors}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{div}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{divisors}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Feature}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}thread}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}

=================
     | x     y   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
p    | 25    10  
q    | 50    5   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[2 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{divisors}}’s two values pair up with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}} respectively: every case’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} is divided by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{100/4=25}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{200/4=50}}), and every case’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}} is
divided by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50/5=10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25/5=5}}) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} is already the default
for this overload, so passing it here changes nothing except making the
broadcast direction explicit at the call site.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{DataFrame::drop}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:dataframe-drop}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{drop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{names}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Removes one or more features by name and keeps the remaining frame — same cases, same
case labels, same values — otherwise unchanged. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} is a pure schema operation: it
never removes rows, and it never touches the values of any feature that survives.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Conceptually, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} is the complement of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}}: where
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(\{...\})}} names the columns you want to \sphinxstyleemphasis{keep}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(\{...\})}} names the columns
you want to \sphinxstyleemphasis{remove}, with every unmentioned feature carried forward automatically. Reach
for whichever reads more naturally at the call site — dropping two columns from a
twenty\sphinxhyphen{}column frame is much shorter to write as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} than as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}} list of
the other eighteen.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names to remove. Pass one or more names in any order — order in the argument
list has no effect on the result. Every remaining feature keeps its original
left\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}right position in the schema; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} does not reorder or re\sphinxhyphen{}sort what’s left.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing every unselected feature, in its original row alignment and
original left\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}right feature order. The case axis (row labels) is preserved exactly
as it was on the source frame.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Drop one feature and preserve the case axis.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{labeled}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tamale}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{region}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{south}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{south}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{middle}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{north}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{7.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{12.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A100}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{B200}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{B200}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{D400}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{labeled}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{drop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{region}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===========================
     | city    units  price
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

B200 | Tema    7      4
B200 | Kumasi  12     2.5
D400 | Tamale  5      5
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 3 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region}} is gone entirely — not blanked, not renamed, simply absent from the schema —
while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{price}} keep both their values and their original left\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}right
order. Notice too that the case labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A100}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B200}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B200}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D400}}, including the
repeated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B200}}) are untouched: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} operates purely on the feature axis, so anything
about how rows are labeled or ordered is completely out of scope for this method.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} works on feature names, never on case labels — there is no row\sphinxhyphen{}dropping
overload hiding behind this method. To remove rows, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}} (rule\sphinxhyphen{}based, missing\sphinxhyphen{}value driven) or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} (condition\sphinxhyphen{}based).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The current case axis is preserved exactly; only the feature set changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The surviving features keep their original left\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}right order — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} does not
re\sphinxhyphen{}sort the schema based on the order names were passed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dropping a name that doesn’t exist on the frame is a programming error, not a silent
no\sphinxhyphen{}op; confirm the name is spelled exactly as it appears in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} if a drop unexpectedly leaves a column in place.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signature}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Removes duplicate rows and returns a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} containing only the survivors —
exactly the rows {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}} would flag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} under the same
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} policy. Surviving rows keep their original
feature set, feature order, and case labels; nothing is renumbered or reordered.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features define a “duplicate.” An empty range (the default) compares \sphinxstylestrong{every}
column in the frame — including any unique identifier column, which means no row will
ever be considered a duplicate of another. Pass the specific feature names that
matter (for example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"city", "product"\}}}, ignoring an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} column that is
unique per row by design).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_first} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the first row in each duplicate group survives and every later row in
that group is dropped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the last row in each duplicate group survives and every earlier row in
that group is dropped. Cannot be combined with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing one row per distinct combination of the selected features
— the survivor chosen by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} — with the original feature
set, feature order, and case labels of the surviving rows.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_duplicates()}}’s result keeps the original feature set, feature order, and case
labels of the surviving rows — surviving rows are never renumbered.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Leaving \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} empty compares every column, including any unique identifier —
which means nothing will ever be dropped if such a column is present. This is almost
always a mistake; pass the specific features that define a duplicate for your use
case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally this is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter(!duplicated(features, keep\_first, keep\_last))}} —
anything {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}} would flag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} is excluded here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last = true}} together is a validation error.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::dropnull}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:dataframe-dropnull}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:signatures}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Removes rows according to a missing\sphinxhyphen{}data rule — the row\sphinxhyphen{}removal counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}} (which replaces missing values instead of discarding the
row) and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}}}}}} (which report missingness
without acting on it). Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}} when incomplete rows — a grade that was never
entered, a measurement the sensor missed, a join key that didn’t resolve — should be
excluded from whatever computation comes next, rather than papered over with a filled
value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two overloads cover the same underlying policy at different levels of explicitness:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Short overload} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all}}): the common case — say which columns to inspect
for missingness (or leave it empty to inspect every column) and whether \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{all}
of them being missing should trigger a drop.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DropOptions}} overload}: the fully explicit route, spelling out \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all}}, and additionally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{threshold}} (a minimum count of non\sphinxhyphen{}missing values a row must
have to survive) as named struct fields — reach for this once the short overload’s two
positional arguments stop being expressive enough.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features to inspect for missingness. Leave this empty to inspect every feature on
the frame. Pass a subset when only certain columns — grading columns, measurement
columns, join keys — should have a say in whether a row survives; missingness in an
unlisted feature is simply not consulted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{all} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The row\sphinxhyphen{}drop rule applied across the selected features:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the default): drop a row when \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} selected feature is missing — the strict
reading, “every inspected value must be present.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: drop a row only when \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} selected features are missing — the lenient
reading, “keep the row unless it’s missing everywhere we’re looking.”

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DropOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A structured policy object for the same operation, adding an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} (row versus
feature dropping) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{threshold}} (minimum count of non\sphinxhyphen{}missing values required to keep a
row) alongside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all}}. Reach for this overload when the null policy needs
to be stated field by field in calling code rather than packed into two positional
arguments.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing only the rows that survive the requested null policy, in
their original row order.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Drop rows when any selected grading column is missing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The short overload is the common “drop rows with missing values in these columns”
route; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DropOptions}} is the more explicit route when the null policy — including
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{threshold}} — needs to be written out field by field.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The output preserves the original row order of every surviving case; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}
never reorders rows, it only removes some.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{student}} was never inspected in either example (it wasn’t listed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}), so a
missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{student}} value would not by itself cause a row to drop — only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quiz}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{final}} participate in the decision.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To replace missing values instead of discarding their rows, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}; to inspect missingness without acting on it at all, see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dropnull:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::fillnull}}}}}}}: replace missing values instead of dropping rows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::isnull}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::notnull}}}}}}}: inspect
missingness first, without removing anything.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::drop}}}}}}}: remove whole features by name, the schema\sphinxhyphen{}level
counterpart to this row\sphinxhyphen{}level operation.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{dtypes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DTypes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the concrete dtype of every feature in the frame — not just the coarse payload
family (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) but the specific scalar type
underneath, formatted as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textless{}Family\textgreater{}\textless{}ConcreteType\textgreater{}"}}, for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}float64\textgreater{}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}int64\textgreater{}}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note\textless{}utf8\textgreater{}}}. This is the schema\sphinxhyphen{}inspection method to reach for when
you need to know both \sphinxstyleemphasis{what kind} of column you have and \sphinxstyleemphasis{what precision or storage
type} it actually holds — before deciding whether a cast, a join, or a numeric operation
is safe.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::DTypes}} object rather than a raw map or vector. It
supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contains(name)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{at(name)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator{[}{]}(name)}}, and
range\sphinxhyphen{}based iteration over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(name, dtype)}} pairs, and it has its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}} for a
quick two\sphinxhyphen{}column printout (see the example).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DTypes}}
A feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}dtype summary. Iterate it directly, or look up one feature’s dtype with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes(){[}"feature\_name"{]}}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes().at("feature\_name")}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Inspect concrete dtypes before deciding whether to cast anything.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{raw}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{student\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{101.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{102.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{103.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{passed}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{raw\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Ada}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Bola}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Chen}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{raw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtypes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
features  dtype
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}  \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
student\PYGZus{}id  Series\PYGZlt{}float64\PYGZgt{}
passed  Series\PYGZlt{}float64\PYGZgt{}
raw\PYGZus{}name  Note\PYGZlt{}utf8\PYGZgt{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{student\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{passed}} came in as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}float64\textgreater{}}} even though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{passed}} clearly
holds a 0/1 flag — the loader/constructor did not infer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}} on its own. That is
precisely the kind of thing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}} exists to surface before you commit to a
computation: follow up with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype(\{"passed"\}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool)}}}}}}} once you have confirmed it
from this output, rather than assuming the flag column is already boolean.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note the row alignment above is not a typo: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DTypes::operator\textless{}\textless{}}} prints a fixed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"features  dtype"}} header and a fixed\sphinxhyphen{}width separator, then each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name  dtype}} pair with
a plain two\sphinxhyphen{}space gap and no further column padding — unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s own renderer,
this printout does not widen its columns to fit the longest name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Look up one feature’s dtype directly, without iterating everything.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{raw}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtypes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{contains}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{passed}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{passed}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZdq{}Series\PYGZlt{}float64\PYGZgt{}\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}} reports the \sphinxstyleemphasis{concrete} dtype (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}float64\textgreater{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note\textless{}utf8\textgreater{}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline\textless{}datetime64{[}ns, UTC{]}\textgreater{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex\textless{}datetime64{[}ns, UTC{]}\textgreater{}}}). Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}}}}}}} instead when you only need the coarse payload family without
the concrete scalar type.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} is intentionally reported separately from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}: a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} stores
temporal \sphinxstyleemphasis{values}, while a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} is the temporal \sphinxstyleemphasis{axis} payload used for
time\sphinxhyphen{}label alignment and resampling — they are different roles even when the
underlying concrete type looks similar.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iteration order matches the frame’s current feature order, the same order
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} returns.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::duplicated}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:dataframe-duplicated}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} mask, one entry per case, marking which rows are duplicates of an
earlier or later row when compared across the selected features. Rows are grouped by
the concatenated string value of every selected feature (missing cells compare as a
shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} placeholder, so two rows both missing the same feature are still
considered a match on that feature); any group with more than one row contributes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} entries according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}}. This returns the mask itself —
for the frame with those rows already removed, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_duplicates()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} cannot both be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} at the same time — asking to keep
both the first and last occurrence exempt from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} is ambiguous when a group has
three or more rows, so the two flags are mutually exclusive.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features to compare when deciding whether two rows match. An empty range (the
default) compares \sphinxstylestrong{every} column in the frame — including any unique identifier
column, which means no two rows will ever match if such a column is present. Pass the
specific feature names that define a “duplicate” for your use case (for example, just
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"city", "product"\}}}, ignoring an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} column that is unique per row by design).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_first} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the first row encountered in each duplicate group is left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (not
flagged), and every later row in that group is flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the last row encountered in each duplicate group is left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, and
every earlier row in that group is flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. Cannot be combined with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, \sphinxstylestrong{every} row in a duplicate group
is flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — including what would otherwise be the exempted first or last row —
useful when you want to identify entire duplicate groups rather than just the “extra”
occurrences.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} entry per case, labeled by case index and named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"duplicated"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} wherever that row is considered a duplicate under the current
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} policy.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Flag every occurrence after the first one in each duplicate group — the
default policy.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{product}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Phone}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Laptop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Phone}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{product}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dupes}\PYG{p}{;}
