\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull_:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The in\sphinxhyphen{}place, whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}. Where
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} and lets you target specific features and specific fill
strategies (forward\sphinxhyphen{}fill, backward\sphinxhyphen{}fill, a per\sphinxhyphen{}feature value) through a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MissingSpec}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_()}} is deliberately narrower and blunter: pick the overload matching a
column \sphinxstyleemphasis{kind}, and it fills \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature of that kind on the frame with the same
scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}, mutating the frame directly and returning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} by reference.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no features parameter
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}, none of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_()}} overloads accept a feature list. Calling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.fillnull\_(0.0)}} fills every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature’s nulls with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}} — you cannot target
just one numeric column with this method. If you need a single\sphinxhyphen{}feature fill, either use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}} with an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} list, or reassign the one column
directly (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features("price").fillnull(0.0)}} and splice it back with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/insert::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{insert()}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/place::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{place()}}}}}}}).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each overload only touches features of the matching kind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_(double)}}: every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_(std::string\_view)}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_(const char*)}}: every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_(const pluss::Timeline\&)}}: every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_(const pluss::TimeIndex\&)}}: every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature of a \sphinxstyleemphasis{different} kind than the overload you called is left completely
untouched — calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_(0.0)}} never affects a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} column, even if that
column also has missing values.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull_:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement value, in whichever type matches the overload: a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} for numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features, a string for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} features, or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} scalar
for those respective feature kinds. The same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} is used for every matching
feature on the frame — there is no per\sphinxhyphen{}feature value list.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull_:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame\&}}
A reference to the same frame, now mutated in place. Every feature of the matching
kind has had its nulls replaced; every feature of a different kind is unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull_:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
These overloads mutate the frame in place and return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame\&}} — the only mutating
members in the missing\sphinxhyphen{}data family. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}} is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}},
non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating alternative that also supports per\sphinxhyphen{}feature targeting and forward/backward
fill strategies.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no feature\sphinxhyphen{}selection parameter on any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_()}} overload; the fill always
applies to every feature of the matching kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature whose kind doesn’t match the overload called is left completely alone, even
if it has nulls of its own — call the matching overload for each kind you need filled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Timeline}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::TimeIndex}} overloads follow the exact same
kind\sphinxhyphen{}scoped, whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame, mutating pattern as the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}
overloads shown above, filling every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature’s nulls with
the given scalar.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keeps only the cases where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, dropping every other row, and returns
the resulting frame with all features intact. This is the row\sphinxhyphen{}filtering counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}} takes a string expression and builds the boolean mask
for you, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} takes an already\sphinxhyphen{}built mask — a boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, or a boolean
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} produced by comparing a feature against a value or another feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.get("units") \textgreater{}= 3}}, for example).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} when the mask is more naturally expressed in C++ than in a query
string — built from a helper function, combined from several intermediate boolean
threads with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{||}}, or reused across several calls — and reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}} when a
single self\sphinxhyphen{}contained string predicate reads more clearly at the call site.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Masks are usually built by comparing the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} returned from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(name)}}}}}}} against a scalar or another feature, for example
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features("units") \textgreater{}= 3}}. Note that {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/get::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get(name)}}}}}}} returns
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}Thread\textgreater{}}} rather than a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (it is the “does this feature exist”
lookup), so it needs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.value()}} before it supports comparison operators —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(name)}} is the more direct accessor when you already know the feature exists.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean mask with one entry per case on the current frame. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} keeps the
corresponding row; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (or a null entry, which is treated as not\sphinxhyphen{}true) drops it.
Both a raw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} wrapping one are accepted directly — most
masks arise naturally as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} from a feature comparison, such as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.get("unit\_price") \textgreater{} 100.0}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, mask\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how the mask is aligned to the frame’s case axis when the mask’s own case axis
does not already match the frame exactly (for example, a mask computed from a
differently\sphinxhyphen{}ordered or partially\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping frame). Omit this parameter when the mask
was computed directly from the same frame you are filtering, which is the common case
and needs no special alignment policy.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing only the cases where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} was \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, with the
original feature set, feature order, and case labels of the surviving rows
preserved.

Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, whose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, is excluded from the result along with every row

\sphinxAtStartPar
Composing boolean threads with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{||}} reads naturally once a mask needs more than
one condition, and keeps the logic in ordinary C++ rather than a string that only gets
checked at runtime.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} performs no reordering — surviving rows keep both their original relative
order and their original case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A mask entry that is null (rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}) behaves like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the
corresponding row is dropped, not kept “just in case.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating; it always returns a new frame rather than editing the
current one.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of floor division: divide, then round down to the nearest whole
number. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}} shares the exact same six\sphinxhyphen{}overload shape and alignment rules as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} and the rest of the arithmetic family, but is the one member of the
family whose result is genuinely different from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}}}}}}}
— those two perform ordinary division, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}} always floors the quotient
afterward. Every example on this page uses the identical dataset and divisors as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}}}}}}}’s own examples, since the two satisfy
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x == divisor * x.floordiv(divisor) + x.mod(divisor)}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand (the divisor), in one of three shapes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}: one scalar divisor, applied to every numeric feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}: another frame supplying one divisor per cell, after the two
frames are aligned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}: one column of divisors, broadcast according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (the default): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} supplies \sphinxstylestrong{one divisor per feature}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} supplies \sphinxstylestrong{one divisor per case}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}. Defaults to strict positional
alignment (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature floor\sphinxhyphen{}divided by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are always left unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}} is the one member of this arithmetic family that differs from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}} in its actual result, not just its name — it always rounds the
quotient down to the nearest whole number.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its full overload shape, alignment semantics, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} behavior with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pow()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::flow}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow:dataframe-flow}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{flow}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fn}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A plain escape hatch for chaining a custom, multi\sphinxhyphen{}step transformation inline without
breaking out of a fluent call sequence. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}} calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} with the current frame and
returns whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} produces — there is no validation, no shape
requirement, and no special handling beyond checking that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} is callable and that it
returns a defined frame. Reach for it when a transformation needs several
already\sphinxhyphen{}existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} calls chained together (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} followed by an
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{insert()}}, say) and you want that whole sequence to read as one step in a larger
pipeline, rather than assigning it to an intermediate variable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold()}}}}}}} is the equivalent hook for reducing a frame down to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
instead of transforming it into another frame — the two share the same “run an
arbitrary callback against the current frame” idea, just with a different return type
and (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold()}}) an optional result\sphinxhyphen{}shape check.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}DataFrame(const DataFrame\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback to run. It receives the current frame by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference and must
return a defined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}. Throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::flow: callback is empty"}} if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}}
holds no target, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::flow: callback returned undefined"}} if it returns an
undefined frame.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
Exactly whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} returned.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}} performs no shape or content validation beyond requiring \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} to be
non\sphinxhyphen{}empty and to return a defined frame — unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold()}}}}}}}, there is no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape}} parameter, since a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} result has no single expected size to
check against.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} receives the frame by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}} itself is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}},
the original frame is never modified — only the returned value reflects whatever
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} computed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nothing about \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}} requires the returned frame to share any structure with the
input — it can have entirely different features, a different case count, or both.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::fold}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:dataframe-fold}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{fold}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fn}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ResultShape}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shape}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ResultShape}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Reduce}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A plain escape hatch for a custom reduction that isn’t already one of the built\sphinxhyphen{}in
aggregates ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}}, and so on). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold()}} calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}}
with the current frame and returns whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} produces, optionally checking
that the result’s size matches what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape}} expects. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/flow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}}}}}}} is the sibling
hook for a callback that returns a whole \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} instead of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}Thread(const DataFrame\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback to run. It receives the current frame by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference and must
return a defined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. Throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::fold: callback is empty"}} if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} holds
no target, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::fold: callback returned undefined"}} if it returns an
undefined thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{shape} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape::Reduce}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Governs what size the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is checked against:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Reduce}}} (the default): the result must have exactly one entry — a single
aggregate value, the same shape {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} produce for
one feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Preserve}}}: the result must have exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} entries — one value per row,
the same shape a row\sphinxhyphen{}wise computed column would have.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infer}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Expand}}}: no size check is performed; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}}’s result is returned
exactly as computed.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
Exactly whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} returned, after the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape}} check (if any) passes.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape::Reduce}} — compute a single custom aggregate value.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{o1}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{o2}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{o3}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fold}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ResultShape}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Reduce}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
unit\PYGZus{}price  798.5
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{f.features(\{"unit\_price"\})}} projects down to a one\sphinxhyphen{}column frame first, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mean()}}
on it produces exactly one value — satisfying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Reduce}}’s “exactly one entry”
requirement. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(1200 + 45.5 + 1150) / 3 = 798.5}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape::Preserve}} — compute a custom per\sphinxhyphen{}row value using two
features together.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{revenue}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fold}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{f}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ResultShape}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Preserve}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{revenue}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
o1  2400
o2  227.5
o3  1150
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback multiplies two feature threads elementwise, producing one value per case
— \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2 * 1200 = 2400}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5 * 45.5 = 227.5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1 * 1150 = 1150}} — which satisfies
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Preserve}}’s “exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} entries” requirement (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} rows in, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} values out).
Each case keeps the case label carried by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features("units")}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{o1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{o2}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{o3}}).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/fold:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold()}} does not compute anything itself — all of the actual logic lives in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}}.
It exists purely to standardize “run a callback against this frame and validate the
result’s size” so ad hoc reductions can slot into a pipeline the same way a built\sphinxhyphen{}in
aggregate would.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Reduce}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Preserve}} are the two shapes with an enforced size check; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infer}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Expand}} accept whatever size \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} returns without validation — reach for them only
when neither “exactly one value” nor “exactly one value per case” describes what
your callback computes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} receives the frame by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold()}} itself is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}},
the original frame is never modified by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold()}} call.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::freq}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:dataframe-freq}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{freq}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts how often each distinct value (or, with several features, each distinct
\sphinxstyleemphasis{combination} of values) occurs, and returns the counts as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} labeled by the
value itself — sorted most\sphinxhyphen{}frequent first, ties broken alphabetically by the value’s
own text. With exactly one feature named, this delegates straight to that feature’s
own {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tally::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::tally()}}}}}}}, reshaped into this labeled\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
form. With zero or several features, it builds a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"|"}}\sphinxhyphen{}joined composite key per row from the selected features’ string representations
and counts occurrences of that composite key instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a values\sphinxhyphen{}first counting tool: it answers “what are the most common cities in
this column” or “what are the most common (city, product) combinations,” rather than
“how many rows/features does this frame have” (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ndistinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ndistinct()}}}}}}} for a
plain distinct\sphinxhyphen{}count instead of a per\sphinxhyphen{}value breakdown).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which feature(s) define the value being counted:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empty (the default): every feature on the frame participates in the composite key.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
One name: delegates to that feature’s own frequency count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Several names: counts distinct combinations across exactly those features, joined
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"|"}} into one composite key per row.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{top\_n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} most frequent entries after sorting. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (the default) keeps
every distinct value or combination observed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): a row where any selected feature is missing is excluded from
the count entirely.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a missing selected feature contributes the literal placeholder \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} to
that row’s key instead of being dropped — only the missing feature’s own part of the
key is affected; every other, still\sphinxhyphen{}present feature in the same row keeps its real
value.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} entry per distinct value (or combination), labeled by that value’s (or
joined combination’s) string form, named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"freq"}}, sorted by count descending and
then alphabetically by label ascending on ties.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra}} is the most frequent city (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} occurrences), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tema}} next (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kumasi}} least
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}) — sorted strictly by count, with no ties to break here.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:id4}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Accra|Laptop|South  1
  Accra|NULL|South  1
  Tema|Phone|North  1
Name: freq, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{product}} is missing, so its key contribution becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} — but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region}}
at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, a perfectly present value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"South"}}), keeps reading as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"South"}} in the
composite key rather than also being swallowed into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}. Each selected feature’s
contribution to the composite key is decided independently, so one missing feature
never affects any other feature’s part of the same row’s key.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With one feature named, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq()}} is exactly that feature’s own frequency count (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tally::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::tally()}}}}}}}); the multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature composite\sphinxhyphen{}key behavior
described above only applies when zero or several feature names are given.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorting is always most\sphinxhyphen{}frequent first; ties are broken by ascending alphabetical
order of the value (or composite key) itself, never by first\sphinxhyphen{}appearance order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n = 0}} (the default) keeps every distinct value or combination; a positive
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} truncates the result \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} sorting, so it always keeps the most frequent
entries, never an arbitrary sample.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every missing\sphinxhyphen{}value placeholder throughout this reference — here, in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}}, and elsewhere — reads as the literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}},
matching the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} convention used for missing cells in a rendered frame.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering relation “greater than or equal to”, returning a boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the
same shape as the source. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}} shares the same scalar/string/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
operand shapes as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}’s “What It Does” for the full
explanation.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
ge() has no independent implementation
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}} overload is a thin wrapper: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.ge(other, ...)}} always calls straight
through to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt(other, ..., /* strict = */ false)}}}}}}}. There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}}
parameter on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}} itself — if you need the strict “greater than” relation on the
same call site, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt()}}}}}}} directly instead.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features only),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}). See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} for
the full breakdown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell is greater than or equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. A cell compared
against a missing value on either side is itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. “Greater than or equal to” against a scalar threshold.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}} always delegates to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt(other, false)}}}}}}}; there is no separate code
path and no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}} parameter on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}} itself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A cell compared against a missing value on either side is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}},
matching {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{DataFrame::get}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:dataframe-get}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Looks up a single feature by name and returns it wrapped in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}Thread\textgreater{}}} —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}} if no feature with that name exists, instead of raising. This is the
“ask first” counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(name)}}}}}}}, which returns the column
directly but raises when the name doesn’t exist. Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get()}} whenever the
feature name comes from somewhere you don’t fully control (user input, a config file,
an upstream schema you can’t guarantee) and a missing column should be handled rather
than treated as a programming error.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature name to look up.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}Thread\textgreater{}}}
The requested column, labeled with the source frame’s case labels and its own
feature name as its display name, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}} exists on the frame.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}} otherwise.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
false
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{customer\_email}} feature on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}}, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get()}} returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}}
rather than raising — the call site decides how to handle the absence (fall back to a
default, skip the column, report a schema mismatch, and so on).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get()}} never raises for an unknown feature name; that’s the entire reason it exists
alongside {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(name)}}}}}}}, which does raise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, when present, carries the feature’s name as its display name
and the frame’s case labels as its display labels — identical to what
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(name)}} returns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get()}} only looks up a single feature by exact name; it has no fuzzy\sphinxhyphen{}matching or
case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitivity built in.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/get:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::features}}}}}}}: the raising counterpart, for when a missing
feature should be a hard error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::has}}}}}}}: checks whether a value exists within a feature’s data,
a different question from whether a feature exists at all.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Groups cases by the distinct combinations of one or more key features, computes one or
more aggregations per group, and returns the result as a new, much smaller frame — one
row per distinct key combination, plus one column per requested aggregation, collapsed
into a single call instead of a separate group\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}aggregate pipeline.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Groups are formed in \sphinxstylestrong{stable first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order}: the first group in the result
corresponds to whichever key combination appears first in the source frame, not to a
sorted or hashed order. If you want the result sorted by key or by an aggregated value,
chain {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}}}}}}} onto the result.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keys} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const LabelGroup\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature name(s) whose distinct value combinations define the output groups. A single key
groups by one feature’s distinct values; multiple keys group by the distinct
combinations across all of them (a composite group key formed from every listed
feature).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}GroupSpec\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The aggregations to compute per group. Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupSpec}} names an output feature, the
source feature to aggregate, and an operation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupOp}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}: number of observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}null) values in the group.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}: number of distinct observed values in the group.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}: numeric sum.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}: arithmetic mean.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}: extreme values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}: sample standard deviation / variance.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupSpec}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{specs}} is computed independently, so a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by()}} call can
mix operations across different source features — a sum of one column and a mean of
another in the same call.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull\_keys} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, cases with a null value in any key feature are excluded before grouping —
they contribute to no group at all. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, a null key value is treated as its own
distinct group instead of being dropped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, same convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} gives you explicit control
over when the result is printed; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} allows it to auto\sphinxhyphen{}render in a temporary\sphinxhyphen{}value
context.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A new frame with one row per distinct key combination (in first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order) and one
column per key feature followed by one column per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GroupSpec}} output name. Aggregated
numeric operations ignore null source values; count\sphinxhyphen{}style aggregations count only
observed values.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kumasi}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{avg\_price}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{42}}, the mean of only its one \sphinxstyleemphasis{observed} price — case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{106}}’s
missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} is skipped rather than treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or propagated as a null
result. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} itself groups the six source rows into three groups, in the order each
city first appears in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accra}}, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tema}}, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kumasi}}), not alphabetically.

Example 2. Group by more than one key at once.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{by\_city\_product}} has one row per distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(city, product)}} pair that actually occurs in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} — combinations that never appear in the source frame (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra", "Monitor"}}, for
instance) simply have no row in the result, rather than a row with a zero or null total.
This is the key structural difference from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}}, which
reshapes one of the group keys into columns and therefore does materialize a cell —
typically null — for every combination, observed or not.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/group_by:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Count, sum, mean, min, max, and the sample variance/standard deviation aggregations
all skip null source values automatically; they never need a separate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}
pass beforehand unless you specifically want nulls to participate as zeros.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because groups are in first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order rather than sorted order, always chain
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} explicitly when the output needs to be in a specific order (by key, or
by one of the aggregated columns) — do not rely on incidental ordering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull\_keys=false}} is the switch to reach for when “unknown key” rows are
meaningful and should be reported as their own group rather than silently excluded.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::pivot\_table}}}}}}}: the same aggregation idea, reshaped so one
key becomes columns instead of staying a row\sphinxhyphen{}level group key.

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::mean\_by}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/count_by::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_by}}}}}}}: single\sphinxhyphen{}aggregation
shortcuts when you only need one statistic per group.

result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering relation “greater than”, returning a boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the same shape
as the source. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt()}} is the mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}}: same operand shapes, same
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}} parameter, same comparison\sphinxhyphen{}family alignment rules — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s
“What It Does” for the full explanation of the shared scalar/string/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
operand shapes.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
ge() is implemented in terms of gt()
Just like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}}}}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt(other, false)}} under the hood, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}}}}}}} has no
independent implementation: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.ge(other)}} is literally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.gt(other, /* strict = */ false)}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features only),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}). See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} for
the full breakdown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{strict} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): strict “greater than” (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}) — a cell equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} reports
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: “greater than or equal to” (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}=}}) — a cell equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.
This is exactly what calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}}}}}}} does internally.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell is greater than (or, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict = false}}, greater
than or equal to) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. A cell compared against a missing value on either side
is itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), matching {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/has:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A per\sphinxhyphen{}cell membership check, returning a boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the same shape as the
source.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
has(double) and has(string\_view) are just eq() by another name
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(84.0)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has("Ada")}} are implemented as plain calls to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq(84.0)}}}}}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq("Ada")}} — there is no added value over calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}
directly for a single value. The real reason to reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}} is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
overload below, which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}} cannot do.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(const Thread\& values)}} is the genuinely distinct overload: it checks each cell
against a whole \sphinxstylestrong{set} of candidate values, marking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if the cell matches \sphinxstyleemphasis{any}
of them — an “is this value one of these?” check, rather than “does this value equal
one specific thing?”.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/has:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A single value, broadcast against every numeric (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind (for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}) feature. Equivalent to calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} with the same
argument.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{values} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A set of candidate values to check membership against. Each cell in the frame reports
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if it equals \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} valid (non\sphinxhyphen{}null) entry in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}; null entries in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}} are skipped and never match anything, including a null cell.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/has:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} (or any entry in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}).

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/has:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(double)}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(std::string\_view)}} are plain aliases for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} — prefer
calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}} directly for single\sphinxhyphen{}value checks; reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}} specifically for
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (set\sphinxhyphen{}membership) overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null entry in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}} candidate set never matches anything, including a
null cell — nulls in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}} are simply skipped.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell in the source frame produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the result, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s missing\sphinxhyphen{}value propagation.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::eq}}}}}}}: the single\sphinxhyphen{}value equality this method’s scalar overloads

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::isnull}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::notnull}}}}}}}: membership
checks against missingness specifically, rather than a value set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/head:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/head:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new frame containing the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} cases (rows) of the current frame, in their
existing order, with every feature preserved. It is the cheapest way to eyeball what a
frame actually looks like — column names, dtypes\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}example, and a handful of real
values — without printing the entire thing, which matters once a frame has more than a
screenful of rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} is a read\sphinxhyphen{}only, non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating view: it does not change case order, does not
drop or rename features, and does not recompute anything. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is greater than or equal
to the number of cases in the frame, the entire frame is returned unchanged. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, the result has the same features but zero cases — useful for grabbing an
empty\sphinxhyphen{}but\sphinxhyphen{}typed frame with the same schema, for example as a seed value before
repeatedly calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/extend::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extend}}}}}}} in a loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} looks at position, not value: it always returns the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} cases as
currently ordered on the frame. If you want the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} cases after sorting by some
key, call {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values}}}}}}} first and then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} the result — the two
compose exactly like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.sort\_values(...).head(...)}} reads.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/head:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of cases to keep, counted from the top. Defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} rows. Negative values are
not a supported “everything except the last
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|n|}} rows” idiom here — pass an explicit non\sphinxhyphen{}negative row count. Values larger than
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} are clamped to the full frame instead of erroring.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the default): you get an ordinary “quiet” view back, and you decide
explicitly when and how to print it (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_string()}}, or by streaming it
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: the returned view is allowed to auto\sphinxhyphen{}render itself the moment it reaches the
end of a temporary expression’s lifetime without being captured or streamed anywhere
(for instance, calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.head(3, true);}} as its own statement will print the result
immediately). This exists for quick, interactive exploration; prefer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} and an
explicit print call inside real application code so output timing stays predictable.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/head:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A view over a new frame holding the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} cases and every feature of the source
frame, in the source frame’s feature order. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} behaves like a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} everywhere it matters (it inherits from it) — the “view” distinction only
affects auto\sphinxhyphen{}render behavior via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}}, plus a source/operation label used when a
GUI viewer window is opened.

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
