\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering relation “less than or equal to”, returning a boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the
same shape as the source. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} shares the same scalar/string/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
operand shapes as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}’s “What It Does” for the full
explanation.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
le() has no independent implementation
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} overload is a thin wrapper: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.le(other, ...)}} always calls straight
through to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt(other, ..., /* strict = */ false)}}}}}}}. There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}}
parameter on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} itself — if you need the strict “less than” relation on the same
call site, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}} directly instead.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features only),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}). See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} for
the full breakdown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell is less than or equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. A cell compared
against a missing value on either side is itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/le:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} always delegates to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt(other, false)}}}}}}}; there is no separate code
path and no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}} parameter on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}} itself.

A cell compared against a missing value on either side is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}},
matching {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length:dataframe-length}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length::doc}}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{length}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the total cell count of the frame: {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/width::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width()}}}}}}} times
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/height::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{height()}}}}}}} — equivalently, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures() * ncases()}}. This is the
number of individual scalar cells across the whole frame, not a row or column
count on its own; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}\sphinxhyphen{}row, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}\sphinxhyphen{}feature frame has a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{40}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Not to be confused with DataFrameNoteAccessor::length()
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.note().length()}} is an entirely different method on a different class: a
per\sphinxhyphen{}cell text\sphinxhyphen{}length accessor reached through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/note::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}}}}}}} accessor,
returning one integer per case for a given text feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::length()}}
(this page) is a single whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame scalar with no accessor involved.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width() * height()}} — the total number of cells in the frame.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
24
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} cases and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} features (its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}6 cs x 4 feat{]}}} footer would
confirm both), so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6 * 4 = 24}} total cells — the same value
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders.width() * orders.height()}} would compute directly.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/length:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length() == width() * height() == nfeatures() * ncases()}} always; there is no
separate stored count, it is computed fresh from the two dimensions each call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Not related to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor::length()}}}}}}}
(reached via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.note().length()}}), which reports a per\sphinxhyphen{}case text length for one
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature rather than a single whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame total.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} cases or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} features has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length() == 0}}, even if the other
dimension is non\sphinxhyphen{}zero.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reshapes a wide frame into long form: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id\_features}} are repeated (tiled) once per
value feature, and every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} is stacked into two new columns — one
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_name}}) recording which source feature each row came from, and one
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_name}}) holding the actual stacked values. This is the “melt” / “pivot longer”
direction of reshaping; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot()}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}}
build wide frames back out of long ones.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{id\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Features to keep as identifiers, repeated unchanged for every value feature’s block.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Features to stack together into one output value column. Leave empty (the default) to
use every feature not already listed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id\_features}}. All selected value features
must share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind — and, for numeric features, the same scalar dtype
and platform — since they end up concatenated into one homogeneous output column.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"feature"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output column name recording which source value feature each row came from.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output column name holding the actual stacked values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fresh\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): the output gets a fresh, contiguous \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ...}} case index.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the original case labels are repeated once per value\sphinxhyphen{}feature block, so a
case label can appear more than once in the output.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id\_features.size() + 2}} columns and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases() * value\_features.size()}} rows (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases() * (nfeatures() \sphinxhyphen{}     id\_features.size())}} rows when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_features}} is left empty).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Leave \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_features}} empty to stack every non\sphinxhyphen{}id feature automatically.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lengthen:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every selected value feature must share one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind (and, for numeric data,
the same scalar dtype and platform); mixing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} value feature with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
one in the same call is not supported, since they must concatenate into a single
homogeneous output column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any validity (null) mask on a stacked value feature is concatenated along with the
values, so missing cells in the source stay missing in the output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fresh\_cases = false}} deliberately produces a case axis with repeated labels (one
repeat per value\sphinxhyphen{}feature block) — pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default) unless you specifically
need to trace each output row back to its original case label.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A single, format\sphinxhyphen{}switched entry point that dispatches to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_txt()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}} based on a
runtime string, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}}. Useful when the file format isn’t known until runtime
(config\sphinxhyphen{}driven pipelines, a generic “import this file” code path) — otherwise, calling
the format\sphinxhyphen{}specific loader directly is clearer and avoids the string\sphinxhyphen{}matching layer
entirely.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Not every overload supports every format
Only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConfigEntry}}\sphinxhyphen{}based overloads dispatch across \sphinxstylestrong{all five} formats.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} overload and the positional (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_bad\_lines}}) overload only recognize \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} — passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}} to either of those two
overloads throws \sphinxstyleemphasis{“unsupported source type”}, even though the same string works fine
with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}\sphinxhyphen{}based overloads. This is a real asymmetry in the overload set, not
an oversight in this documentation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{source\_type} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The format selector, matched case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively. Recognized values:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}} (the last three
only via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConfigEntry}} overloads — see the caution above). Anything else
throws \sphinxstyleemphasis{“unsupported source type”}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Path to the file to read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline settings bundle. Works with all five recognized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}}
values — each format’s own loader (for example {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} overload) interprets the same key/value entries its dedicated loader would.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::ReadCsvOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A typed CSV\sphinxhyphen{}parsing options struct, for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} source types only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sep}, \sphinxstylestrong{ncases}, \sphinxstylestrong{usefeats}, \sphinxstylestrong{case\_col}, \sphinxstylestrong{on\_bad\_lines}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as the equivalent {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} positional parameters, for
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} source types only.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new, fully typed frame, exactly as if you had called the format\sphinxhyphen{}specific loader
directly with equivalent settings.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}} never invents its own parsing or type\sphinxhyphen{}inference logic — it is purely a
string\sphinxhyphen{}keyed dispatch to the format\sphinxhyphen{}specific static loaders. Reading the dispatched
method’s own documentation ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}},
and so on) tells you exactly what a given call will do.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} and positional overloads are CSV/TXT\sphinxhyphen{}only; use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}
overload if the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type}} might resolve to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}}
at runtime.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}} can never return a multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::LoadResult}} — even with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_type = "excel"}}, it always calls the single\sphinxhyphen{}frame {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}}
overload. For multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet loading, call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}} directly with its
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_names}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_indices}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullptr}} overloads.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s static constructor for delimited text files. It parses a
CSV (or any single\sphinxhyphen{}character\sphinxhyphen{}delimited text file) and returns a fully typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}:
numeric columns are parsed into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} with an inferred scalar type, text columns
become \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, and empty or malformed cells become missing values rather than empty
strings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The overload set trades off convenience against control:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv(filepath)}} alone is the “just read it” overload — comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, header
row present, every column and row loaded, malformed rows treated as an error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The positional overload (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_bad\_lines}}) is
for one\sphinxhyphen{}off loads where a handful of settings need to change but a whole config object
would be overkill.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} overloads are for reusable, named option bundles —
build the options once and pass the same object to several \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv}} calls, or store
it alongside a data pipeline definition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}} overloads are for headerless files or files where the source column that
should become the case axis is known up front.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All overloads perform the same parse\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}type\sphinxhyphen{}infer work under the hood; picking an
overload is about how you want to \sphinxstyleemphasis{express} the loader settings, not about different
parsing behavior.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Path to the delimited text file to read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sep} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Field delimiter. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}}} for standard CSV; pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}\textbackslash{}t\textquotesingle{}}} for TSV, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}|\textquotesingle{}}} for pipe\sphinxhyphen{}delimited
files, and so on.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ncases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::size\_t\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Maximum number of rows to read, useful for peeking at a large file without loading it in
full. Leave unset to read every row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{usefeats} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default
empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricts the load to a subset of columns by name, matched against the file’s header
row. Leave empty to load every column present in the file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_col} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Names a source column that should become the frame’s case axis instead of an
auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated integer index. The column is consumed from the regular feature set and
becomes the case label thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{on\_bad\_lines} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::BadLinePolicy}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Error}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
What to do when a row does not parse cleanly (wrong field count, for example):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Error}}: stop loading and raise immediately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Warn}}: emit a warning and continue, skipping the malformed row.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Skip}}: silently skip the malformed row.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline key/value settings bundle, for callers who prefer a single options
object over a long positional argument list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::ReadCsvOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A typed options struct covering the same settings as the positional overload
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_bad\_lines}}, and more), useful when the same
parsing configuration is reused across several files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{header} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV header mode: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"infer"}} reads the first row as feature names; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"none"}} treats the
file as headerless and auto\sphinxhyphen{}generates feature names (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feat\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feat\_1}}, …).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"none"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Name given to the restored case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column, for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}}\sphinxhyphen{}based overload.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{engine} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"auto"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Backend selector for the parser. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"auto"}} lets PlussMic choose the fastest available
engine for the file; pass an explicit engine name only when you need predictable,
non\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}detected routing.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new, fully typed frame built from the file’s contents. Numeric columns are typed
as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; text columns are typed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}; malformed or empty cells become
missing values rather than empty strings or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"nan"}} text.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Load a plain, comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated CSV with a header row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Given \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders.csv}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
order\PYGZus{}id,city,product,units,unit\PYGZus{}price
101,Accra,Laptop,2,1200
102,Accra,Headphones,5,45.5
103,Tema,Laptop,1,1150
104,Tema,Monitor,3,320
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
=====================================================
     | order\PYGZus{}id  city   product     units  unit\PYGZus{}price
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | 101       Accra  Laptop      2      1200      
1    | 102       Accra  Headphones  5      45.5      
2    | 103       Tema   Laptop      1      1150      
3    | 104       Tema   Monitor     3      320       
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 5 feat]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} are parsed as integer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} as a floating\sphinxhyphen{}point
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{product}} as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} — all inferred purely from the file’s
contents, with no schema declared up front.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Load only a subset of columns and cap the number of rows.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{preview}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{,}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{size\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{preview}} has only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} features, and stops after the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}
data rows, without reading (or even parsing) the rest of the file — useful for a quick
peek at a source file that may be much larger than you want to load in full.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}} to promote an existing column to the case axis.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{by\PYGZus{}order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{,}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} is consumed from the ordinary feature set and becomes the frame’s case label,
so the resulting frame has four features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{product}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}) with
case labels \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{101, 102, 103, 104}} instead of a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..3}} index.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Type inference happens per column, from the observed values in that column only —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv}} does not accept an explicit dtype schema. If a numeric\sphinxhyphen{}looking column
contains even one non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric value, expect it to be inferred as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} rather than
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; clean the source data or post\sphinxhyphen{}process with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}}}}}}} /
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cast::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cast()}}}}}}} if that happens unintentionally.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empty cells become missing values (visible as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} when the frame is printed and
reflected in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}}’s non\sphinxhyphen{}null counts), not the literal string \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"nan"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Excel loading (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}) can return several frames at once from a multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet
workbook, which is why its return type differs (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::LoadResult}}) from the
single\sphinxhyphen{}frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s static constructor for Excel workbooks — the one loader in this family
with genuinely different \sphinxstyleemphasis{return types} depending on the overload, because a workbook
can hold more than one sheet:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Single sheet} (no sheet argument, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_index}} named explicitly)
— returns a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, exactly like every other loader.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Several sheets at once} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullptr}} for “all sheets”, or an explicit list of sheet
names/indices) — returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::LoadResult}}, a tagged bundle holding
either a single frame or a whole \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Workbook}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::vector\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string, DataFrame\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}}) depending on which overload produced it.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Path to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xlsx}} workbook to read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sheet\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, single\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The worksheet to load, by name. Passing the literal string \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"none"}} here is rejected
with a message redirecting you to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullptr}} (all\sphinxhyphen{}sheets) overload instead — it’s
not a valid way to request every sheet.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sheet\_index} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, single\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The worksheet to load, by zero\sphinxhyphen{}based position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{header} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the sheet’s first row holds feature names.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sheet\_names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}},
multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Worksheets to load together, by name. An \sphinxstylestrong{empty} list is equivalent to passing
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullptr}} — both load every sheet in the workbook.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sheet\_indices} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::vector\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}},
multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Worksheets to load together, by zero\sphinxhyphen{}based position. Same empty\sphinxhyphen{}list\sphinxhyphen{}means\sphinxhyphen{}all\sphinxhyphen{}sheets
behavior as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_names}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{options}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::ReadExcelOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent settings expressed as a reusable config object, inline entries, or a typed
options struct — covering sheet selection, header row handling, and multi\sphinxhyphen{}row header
merging, for callers who want to configure everything in one object rather than a
chain of positional parameters.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} (single\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overloads)
One fully typed frame for the requested sheet.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::LoadResult}} (multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overloads)
A tagged bundle: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.is\_frame()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.is\_workbook()}} report which case applies,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dataframe()}} unwraps a single\sphinxhyphen{}frame result, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.workbook()}} returns the full
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::vector\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string, DataFrame\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}} for a multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet result, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sheets("Name")}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sheet\_by\_index(i)}} reach one sheet directly without
unwrapping the whole vector yourself.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requesting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name = "none"}} on the single\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overload throws, redirecting
you to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullptr}} overload — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"none"}} is not itself a magic value meaning “all
sheets” for that particular overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_names}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_indices}} list on the multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet overloads behaves
identically to the explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullptr}} (all\sphinxhyphen{}sheets) overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}} applies uniformly to every sheet loaded in a single call — there is no way
to set a different header mode per sheet within one multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}} (among all the loaders in this family) can return
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::LoadResult}} — every other loader always returns a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s static constructor for JSON files. The parser auto\sphinxhyphen{}detects one of two
layouts based on the JSON root’s shape:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Records} (a JSON array of objects, one object per row) — the more common shape,
and the one {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json()}}}}}}} writes by default.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Split} (a single JSON object with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}} array and a parallel \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"data"}}
array of row arrays) — a more compact alternative layout, also produced by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json()}}}}}}} when asked for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orient = "split"}}.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values are re\sphinxhyphen{}inferred the same way load\_csv() infers them
Even though JSON natively distinguishes numbers, strings, and booleans, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}
converts every cell to its string form internally and re\sphinxhyphen{}runs it through the exact
same numeric/text type\sphinxhyphen{}inference engine {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} uses — it does
not trust JSON’s own value tags directly. In practice this rarely matters (a JSON
number reads back as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, a JSON string as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}), but it means the same
edge cases that affect \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}’s inference (a column that’s “mostly numbers plus
one stray string” falling back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}) apply here too, even though the source file
had unambiguous per\sphinxhyphen{}value JSON types.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Path to the JSON file to read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline settings bundle, recognizing the same general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose keys
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}}, and so on) as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}
overload — the layout (records vs. split) is detected automatically from the file
itself and is not a setting you choose.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new, fully typed frame, with the same numeric/text type inference behavior as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Type inference happens the same way it does for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} — from
each column’s string\sphinxhyphen{}converted values, not from JSON’s own type tags. See the
caution above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A JSON root that is neither an array of objects nor a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"columns", "data"\}}} object
fails to parse.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

behavior.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s static constructor for Parquet files, read via Apache Arrow’s Parquet
C++ library.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{caution}{Caution:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parquet’s own schema is not trusted directly — values are re\sphinxhyphen{}inferred
Parquet embeds a real, strongly\sphinxhyphen{}typed columnar schema (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int64}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{utf8}}, and
so on). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}} reads that schema and the underlying columnar data via Arrow,
but then converts every value to its string form and re\sphinxhyphen{}runs it through the exact
same numeric/text type\sphinxhyphen{}inference engine {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} uses, rather than
adopting Arrow’s schema directly. For ordinary numeric and string columns this
round\sphinxhyphen{}trips cleanly, but it means Parquet’s own type precision (distinguishing
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int32}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int64}}, for example) is not preserved as\sphinxhyphen{}is — the resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
dtype comes from PlussMic’s own inference, not from the Parquet file’s schema.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires an Arrow + Parquet C++ build
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}} throws \sphinxstyleemphasis{“built without parquet\sphinxhyphen{}cpp support”} if PlussMic was
compiled without the optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PLUSSMIC\_HAS\_PARQUET\_CPP}} support — Parquet reading (and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet()}}}}}}} writing) is conditional on that dependency being
available at build time, unlike CSV/TXT/JSON support, which is always present.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Path to the Parquet file to read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline settings bundle, recognizing the same general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose keys
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}}, and so on) as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}
overload — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}} here restricts which Parquet columns are even read out of the
file via Arrow, rather than reading everything and discarding columns afterward.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new, fully typed frame, with the same numeric/text type inference behavior as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} — not Parquet’s own embedded schema.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires PlussMic to have been built with Arrow + Parquet C++ support; otherwise
every call throws immediately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dtypes come from PlussMic’s own string\sphinxhyphen{}based inference (the same engine
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} uses), not directly from Parquet’s embedded schema — see
the caution above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}} is pushed down to the Arrow column read, so unwanted columns are never
even decoded from disk, unlike a post\sphinxhyphen{}hoc {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} projection.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s static constructor for plain delimited text files that aren’t
necessarily comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated — the same underlying parser and type\sphinxhyphen{}inference machinery
as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}, read through a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConfigEntry}} settings bundle
instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}’s rich set of dedicated positional/typed overloads.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Path to the text file to read.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline settings bundle. Recognizes the same kind of keys \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} overload does (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}}, and so on) —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_txt()}} doesn’t default to a different delimiter on the read side; pass
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"sep", "\textbackslash{}t"\}}} explicitly for tab\sphinxhyphen{}separated input, the same as you would for
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new, fully typed frame, with the same numeric/text type inference behavior as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_txt()}} shares its type\sphinxhyphen{}inference engine with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} —
numeric\sphinxhyphen{}looking columns become \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, everything else becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, and empty
cells become missing values, exactly as documented there.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no dedicated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadTxtOptions}} struct or positional overload the way
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}}}}}} has — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConfigEntry}} overloads are the only
way to customize parsing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The corresponding writer, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_txt()}}}}}}}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{does} default to a tab
separator on the write side unless you override it — but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_txt()}}’s read side
has no such default; specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}} explicitly to match whatever delimiter the file
actually uses.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_csv}}}}}}}: the fuller explanation of the shared parsing

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_bad\_lines}}).

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::save\_txt}}}}}}}: the write\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{log}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies the natural logarithm (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln}}) elementwise to every numeric feature, leaving
non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) unchanged — the same
delegation pattern as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/abs::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{abs()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp()}}}}}}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}float numeric
features are upcast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}} first.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{caution}{Caution:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No domain check — negative or zero inputs produce NaN/\sphinxhyphen{}inf, not an error
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}} does not validate its input’s sign before computing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log(0)}} produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}inf}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log(negative)}} produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, following ordinary floating\sphinxhyphen{}point semantics — the
cell’s validity mask is untouched, so a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} payload from an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}domain input
still reports as a \sphinxstyleemphasis{valid} (non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) cell. If you need to guard against this,
check with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge()}}}}}}} before calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}}, rather than relying
on the result to flag the problem for you.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by its
natural logarithm. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Take the natural log of a numeric feature.

\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{c}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{log}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===========
     | x   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln(1) = 0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln(e) = 1}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln(e\textasciicircum{}2) = 2}} — the input values here are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\textasciicircum{}2}}, chosen so the result comes out to clean whole numbers.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are always left unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integer\sphinxhyphen{}typed features are upcast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}} before taking the log; the result is
always a floating\sphinxhyphen{}point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log(0)}} yields \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}inf}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log(negative)}} yields \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} — neither is converted to a
missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) cell. A pre\sphinxhyphen{}existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell in the input stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the
output, but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}} never introduces new nulls on its own.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}} is the inverse of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x.exp().log()}} reconstructs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} (up to
floating\sphinxhyphen{}point precision) for every input.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/log:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/exp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::exp}}}}}}}: the inverse operation.

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/gt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::gt}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ge::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ge}}}}}}}: guard against non\sphinxhyphen{}positive

\sphinxstylestrong{other}

positionally) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (one boolean thread applied identically to every

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lor:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires a genuine \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} scalar type on every participating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}’s note on casting first with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype(..., pluss::ScalarType::Bool)}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor(const DataFrame\&)}} matches positionally by feature name and case count only —
it does not align by case label. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} for the full explanation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ror::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ror()}}}}}}} computes the same cell values (OR is
commutative) and the same case labels and title too — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ror()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}} are fully
interchangeable. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} for the fuller explanation, including a
note on an earlier revision where this wasn’t the case.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ordering relation “less than”, returning a boolean\sphinxhyphen{}valued frame the same shape as
the source. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}} shares the same scalar/string/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} operand shapes as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}’s “What It Does” for the full explanation — plus one
extra parameter, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}}, that the equality/inequality methods don’t have.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
le() is implemented in terms of lt()
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}}}}}} has no independent implementation: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.le(other)}} is literally
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.lt(other, /* strict = */ false)}}. There is no separate “less than or equal”
code path — passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict = false}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}} directly produces the exact same result
as calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features only),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}). See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} for
the full breakdown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{strict} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Selects which relation is actually evaluated:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): strict “less than” (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}}) — a cell equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} reports
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: “less than or equal to” (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}=}}) — a cell equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.
This is exactly what calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}}}}}} does internally.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, where every feature holds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
according to whether that cell is less than (or, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict = false}}, less than
or equal to) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. A cell compared against a missing value on either side is
itself missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), matching {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.

reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for every case where the value equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{84}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{s1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{s3}} on both
features), since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{84 \textless{}= 84}} holds — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scores.le(84.0)}} would produce this identical
result.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt:notes}}\begin{itemize}

A cell compared against a missing value on either side is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}},

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{lxor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise logical XOR — the same overload shape, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}only requirement, and
positional (not case\sphinxhyphen{}label) matching as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}. See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}’s “What It
Does” for the full explanation of the two overloads and the constraints on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}.
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}}}}}}, XOR reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} exactly where the two
operands \sphinxstyleemphasis{disagree} — a useful “exactly one of these flags is set” check.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (same feature names in order, same case count, matched
positionally) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (one boolean thread applied identically to every
feature). See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} for the full breakdown.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every feature holding the logical XOR
of the source cell and the corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} value.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires a genuine \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} scalar type on every participating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}’s note on casting first with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype(..., pluss::ScalarType::Bool)}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor(const DataFrame\&)}} matches positionally by feature name and case count only —
it does not align by case label. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} for the full explanation.

\item {}

commutative) and the same case labels and title too — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rxor()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}} are
fully interchangeable. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} for the fuller explanation, including
a note on an earlier revision where this wasn’t the case.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::map}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map:dataframe-map}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map:signature}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} to every cell of the selected features, one scalar value at a time, and
returns a new frame with those features replaced. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} receives one cell as a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} and must return one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} back — it is skipped entirely for
missing cells (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} ever being called), and every
non\sphinxhyphen{}null cell in one feature’s column must map to the \sphinxstylestrong{same} output kind (you
cannot have \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} return a numeric value for one row and text for another row of the
same feature).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/transform::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform()}}}}}}}, which operates on a whole feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} at
once (so it can do things like a running total), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map()}} only ever sees one value at
a time — it is the right tool for a pure, independent per\sphinxhyphen{}cell computation.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}ThreadValue(const ThreadValue\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}cell callback. Extract the incoming scalar with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} (matching the feature’s kind), compute a new value, and wrap it back into
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} over a length\sphinxhyphen{}1 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (for example
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue(Thread(pluss::make\_series(\{result\})))}}). The output kind does not have to
match the input kind — mapping \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} cells to their string length (an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}
result) is a valid, kind\sphinxhyphen{}changing use of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} is applied to. Leave empty (the default) to apply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} to every
feature on the frame — note that this only makes sense if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} can handle every
feature’s kind; pass an explicit subset when different features need different
treatment.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with the selected features replaced by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}}’s output. Untargeted features are unchanged, and missing cells stay missing.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/map:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} is never invoked for a missing cell; the cell stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the output
without needing special\sphinxhyphen{}case handling inside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} itself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every non\sphinxhyphen{}null result within one feature must share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind}}; mixing
kinds within a single feature’s output throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::map: output kinds must be consistent"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Leaving \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} empty applies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} to literally every feature on the frame,
including features of different kinds — only do this when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} is written to handle
every kind present, typically by branching on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v.kind()}} inside the lambda.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating; it always returns a new frame.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every cell with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, leaving every other
cell untouched. This is the inverse of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} keeps or
drops entire \sphinxstylestrong{rows} based on a mask, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask()}} blanks out individual \sphinxstylestrong{cells}
across the selected features without removing any row, and every feature keeps its
original shape and case count.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean mask with one entry per case. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} nulls the corresponding row’s selected
cells; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (or a missing mask entry, treated the same as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}) leaves it alone.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is applied to. Leave empty (the default) to null out the
masked rows across \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the frame; pass a subset to restrict the
effect to just those columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is aligned to the frame’s case axis when it doesn’t already
match exactly — the same alignment mechanism used throughout the arithmetic and
comparison families (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} written into every selected
feature wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} was \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask()}} never changes the frame’s shape or case count — it only ever replaces
values with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, the same way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} never removes rows either.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A mask entry that is itself missing behaves like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the corresponding row is
left alone, not nulled “just in case.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating; it always returns a new frame.

\end{itemize}
