\subparagraph{DataFrame::prod}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:dataframe-prod}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to the product of its values, returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
whose entries line up with the frame’s numeric feature names — the same shape
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} returns, but multiplying instead of adding. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are
skipped entirely, the same rule every other single\sphinxhyphen{}statistic reducer in this family
follows.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) multiplies down each feature’s cases,
producing one product per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} multiplies across each row’s
features instead, producing one product per case — for example, multiplying a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}
column by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} column row\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}row to get each row’s line total.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects that reduction’s result:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values are excluded from the product entirely, as if
they were never part of the multiplication.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a single missing value poisons the entire reduction it participates in,
which comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or per case
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), holding the product of that reduction’s values.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Multiply every numeric feature’s values, skipping missing values (the
default).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{320.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{42.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{discount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  1.228251417e+12
     units  240
unit\PYGZus{}price  8.438976e+11
  discount  2.4e\PYGZhy{}06
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s missing observation (case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}) is excluded from the product, the same
way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}} treat that column’s missing value — the
product runs over the remaining five prices only. Note the scientific notation on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prod()}}’s outputs grow (or shrink) fast, and
the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{:.10g\}}} formatting every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} render uses switches to
scientific notation once a value’s magnitude crosses ten significant digits either way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Disable null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping to see a missing value propagate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{products\PYGZus{}strict}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  1.228251417e+12
     units  240
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} — the two features that each have
one missing value — come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entirely, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} are
unaffected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} to multiply across a row’s features instead of down a
feature’s cases — here, computing each order’s line total as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units * unit\_price}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}totals}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{prod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Feature}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}totals}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  2400
1  227.5
2  1150
3  960
4  168
5  2
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} show the expected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units * unit\_price}} line total. Case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} is missing, and with the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = true}}
the missing factor is simply excluded from that row’s product rather than poisoning
it, leaving only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) to multiply. Pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} as the second argument if a
missing price should invalidate the whole row’s total instead.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/prod:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prod()}}’s result is labeled by feature name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}) or by case index
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}), and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, not like a row sliced
from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither multiplied as an
error nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A product that would overflow or underflow \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} precision follows ordinary IEEE
754 behavior (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inf}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}}), the same as any other floating\sphinxhyphen{}point multiplication in
the library.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::ptypes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:dataframe-ptypes}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ptypes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DTypes}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the coarse payload family of every feature in the frame — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — without the concrete scalar type underneath. Where
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}}}}}}} tells you \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}float64\textgreater{}}} versus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}int64\textgreater{}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} only tells you it’s a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} at all. Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} when you’re
routing logic by payload family (numeric work needs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, text work needs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}},
and so on) and don’t need the extra precision \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}} provides.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::DTypes}} object rather
than a raw map — it supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contains(name)}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{at(name)}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator{[}{]}(name)}}, and range\sphinxhyphen{}based iteration over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(name, ptype)}} pairs,
and has its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}} for a quick printout.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DTypes}}
A feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}payload\sphinxhyphen{}family summary. Iterate it directly, or look up one
feature’s payload family with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes(){[}"feature\_name"{]}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes().at("feature\_name")}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Inspect payload families without the concrete scalar type.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{users}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{user\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{101.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{102.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{103.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signup\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{referral}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ad}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{referral}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{users}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ptypes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
features  dtype
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}  \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
user\PYGZus{}id  Series
signup\PYGZus{}note  Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user\_id}} regardless of whether it’s stored as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int64}} underneath — for that level of detail, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}}}}}}} instead. As with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}}, the row alignment above is not a
typo: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DTypes::operator\textless{}\textless{}}} prints a fixed header and separator, then each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name  ptype}}
pair with a plain two\sphinxhyphen{}space gap and no column\sphinxhyphen{}width padding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Look up one feature’s payload family directly.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{users}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ptypes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{contains}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signup\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signup\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZdq{}Note\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ptypes:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptypes()}} reports the \sphinxstyleemphasis{coarse} payload family only (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}). Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/dtypes::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtypes()}}}}}}} when you need the concrete scalar type
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}float64\textgreater{}}} vs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series\textless{}int64\textgreater{}}}) as well.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iteration order matches the frame’s current feature order, the same order
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} returns.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signatures}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rewrites one feature’s values only at the rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, leaving
every other row’s value on that feature untouched — the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature, mask\sphinxhyphen{}driven
sibling of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask()}}}}}}} (which nulls out cells rather than replacing them with
a chosen value). Where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} is itself a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} rather than a scalar, each masked
row is replaced by \sphinxstylestrong{that same row’s own value} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} — not one shared
replacement broadcast to every masked cell. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} returns a new frame;
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put\_()}}}}}}} is the in\sphinxhyphen{}place counterpart that mutates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} directly instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every value\sphinxhyphen{}type overload above also has a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}mask convenience
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put(feature, series\_mask, value)}}) that just wraps the mask in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} and
forwards to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}\sphinxhyphen{}mask overload — the two mask types behave identically.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to rewrite. Must already exist on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean row mask. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} rewrites the corresponding row on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
leaves that row’s existing value unchanged. A masked\sphinxhyphen{}missing mask entry behaves like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement. A scalar (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, string, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}}) is broadcast to every
masked row identically. A full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} instead supplies a \sphinxstylestrong{different} replacement
value per row — row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} replaces row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}, wherever
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is aligned to the frame’s case axis when it doesn’t already
match exactly, the same alignment mechanism used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame identical to the source, except \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s masked rows have been
replaced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, string, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}}) is the same replacement for
every masked row; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} supplies a different replacement per row,
taken from that row’s own position in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} may be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} overloads are pure
convenience wrappers with identical behavior.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} never changes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s kind; replacing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature requires a
string (or null) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}, and replacing a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature requires a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (or null) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The in\sphinxhyphen{}place counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}: rewrites one feature’s values at the
rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, mutating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} directly and returning a reference
to it, instead of returning a new frame. Every parameter and replacement rule is
identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} — see that page for the full breakdown of scalar\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
replacement semantics; this page only covers what differs about mutating in place.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to rewrite in place. Must already exist on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean row mask, identical in behavior to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement, identical in behavior to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} — a scalar
broadcasts to every masked row, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} supplies a different value per row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is aligned to the frame’s case axis, identical to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame\&}}
A reference to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}’s masked rows have been rewritten.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put\_()}} mutates and returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} by reference; it never allocates a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}} does.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} value that shares the same underlying columns (via a prior
copy) does not see this mutation — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::table::DataFrame}}’s copies are
value\sphinxhyphen{}like, not aliased references to shared state.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}} for the complete parameter and replacement\sphinxhyphen{}semantics
breakdown; every rule there (scalar vs. per\sphinxhyphen{}row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} replacement, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}mask
convenience overloads, kind constraints) applies identically here.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/put_:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::put}}}}}}}: the non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating counterpart, returning a new frame
instead of mutating in place.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/mask::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::mask}}}}}}}: nulls out masked cells outright, rather than
replacing them with a chosen value.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::query}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:dataframe-query}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{expression}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter rows with a boolean expression written against DataFrame feature names.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::query(...)}} is the string\sphinxhyphen{}expression row filter for PlussMic. It lets you write one compact predicate instead of building a boolean mask by hand, which is especially useful when you are exploring data interactively or translating logic from notebook\sphinxhyphen{}style workflows into C++.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression itself is a small language evaluated against feature names, so you can
write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"units \textgreater{}= 10 and region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}"}} instead of assembling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df{[}(df.units \textgreater{}= 10) \& (df.region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}){]}}} by hand. The C++ equivalent of the
boolean\sphinxhyphen{}mask style is {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} — reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}} when the predicate
reads more clearly as a single self\sphinxhyphen{}contained string, and for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} when the mask is
more naturally built up from existing C++ expressions or reused across calls.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expression Input

\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat the query string as code\sphinxhyphen{}like input owned by the developer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not pass untrusted raw user input directly into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::query(...)}} without validation or a safer higher\sphinxhyphen{}level policy layer around it.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{expression}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Boolean filter expression to evaluate against each row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Common patterns include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
numeric comparison: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{}= 10}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
string comparison: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
combined predicates: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{}= 10 and region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}feature comparison: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{} price}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
spaced feature names via backticks: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciigrave{}First Name\textasciigrave{} == \textquotesingle{}Laurel\textquotesingle{}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result must be a row\sphinxhyphen{}level truth decision.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A filtered frame containing only the rows where the expression evaluates to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The returned frame preserves:
\PYGZhy{} the original feature set,
\PYGZhy{} the original feature order,
\PYGZhy{} the original case labels for rows that survive the filter.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::filter: filter rows from an explicit boolean mask instead of a query string.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::where: row filter using a boolean mask that has already been computed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::case\_study: select rows by position, label, or mask when you do not want an expression parser.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/query:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression is evaluated row by row against the current frame. Feature names are available directly inside the query string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
String literals must be quoted. For example, write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region == \textquotesingle{}south\textquotesingle{}}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region == south}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}feature comparison is supported. For example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units \textgreater{} price}} compares the two features row by row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use backticks around feature names that contain spaces or punctuation, such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciigrave{}First Name\textasciigrave{} == \textquotesingle{}Laurel\textquotesingle{}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method is for row filtering. It does not rewrite values, create columns, or mutate the current frame in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expression is parsed and evaluated by PlussMic’s own small expression engine, not by
shelling out to an external interpreter — there is no dependency on Python, a SQL engine,
or any other runtime to use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}}. The patterns documented above (numeric and string
comparisons, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{and}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{or}} combinators, quoted literals, and backtick\sphinxhyphen{}quoted feature
names) are the supported core; if a more elaborate expression does not parse the way you
expect, fall back to building the mask explicitly with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}}, which
accepts any boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} you can construct in ordinary C++.

\subparagraph{DataFrame::radd}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:dataframe-radd}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{radd}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected (right\sphinxhyphen{}hand) form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}: computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other + frame}} instead
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame + other}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rsub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rfloordiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmod}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rpow}} are the reflected counterparts of the eight forward
arithmetic methods, all scalar\sphinxhyphen{}only (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double other}}) — there is no reflected
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} form, since swapping which side is the “frame”
is unambiguous once a scalar is the other operand.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For addition specifically, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.add(other)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.radd(other)}} produce the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{same} result, since addition is commutative — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}} mainly exists for symmetry
with the rest of the reflected family (where operand order genuinely changes the
result, such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rsub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub()}}}}}}}) and for call sites where “the scalar comes first”
reads more naturally.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar added to every numeric feature on the frame.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature increased by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All eight reflected methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rfloordiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmod}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rpow}}) only accept a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}; there is no reflected
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For commutative operations (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul}}), the reflected and forward forms always
agree. For non\sphinxhyphen{}commutative operations (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rfloordiv}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmod}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rpow}}), the reflected form computes a genuinely different result — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rsub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub()}}}}}}} for a worked example.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::rand}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rand}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rand}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}. Since logical AND is commutative,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.rand(other)}} is indistinguishable from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.land(other)}} in every observable
respect — same cell values, and (for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload) the same case labels
and title, both drawn from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame}} itself, exactly as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} documents.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Previously, the DataFrame overload inherited case labels from other
An earlier revision of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand(const DataFrame\&)}} computed the reflection as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other.land(*this)}}, which meant the result’s case labels and title came from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead of from the frame the method was called on — a real, verified quirk
that was documented here as a caution. That has since been fixed: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}} now zips
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} directly (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::rand()}} handling the per\sphinxhyphen{}cell operand
order internally), so the result’s structure always comes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} and every other method in this family. If you’re working against
an older build where this fix isn’t present, verify which behavior you’re actually
seeing before relying on either.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} — identical shape requirements to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}: same feature names in order and same case count for the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload; one boolean thread matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}} for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame holding the logical AND of each cell against the corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}
value, with case labels and title drawn from the frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}} was called on —
identical in every respect to what {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} would produce for the same
arguments.

\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Keep}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every numeric feature’s values with their rank among that feature’s other
values — the smallest value gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending = true}}, the default), the
next\sphinxhyphen{}smallest gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, and so on. The result is the same shape as the source frame;
ranks replace values in place, feature by feature, rather than being reduced to a single
summary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two things need a policy decision that plain sorting doesn’t: what happens when two
values are \sphinxstylestrong{tied}, and what happens to a \sphinxstylestrong{null}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rank()}} exposes both as explicit
parameters instead of picking a silent default you’d have to discover by testing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ties} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankTieRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How to resolve rank ties (equal values):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}}: tied values all receive the mean of the ranks they would have occupied
(two values tied for ranks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} both get \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.5}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lowest}}: tied values all receive the lowest of the ranks they would have occupied.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Highest}}: tied values all receive the highest of the ranks they would have occupied.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{First}}: ties are broken by original row order — whichever tied value appears first in
the frame gets the lower rank.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dense}}: like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lowest}}, but without leaving a gap in the rank sequence afterward (the
next distinct value always gets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{previous\_rank + 1}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{previous\_rank + count\_of\_ties}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankNullRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Keep}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How to rank missing values: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Keep}} leaves a null’s rank as null (it is excluded from
ranking entirely); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Top}} ranks nulls as if they were the smallest values; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bottom}} ranks
them as if they were the largest.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} ranks smallest\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}largest (smallest gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} reverses the order
(largest gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{percentage} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, each rank is divided by the number of ranked observations, giving a
percentile\sphinxhyphen{}style rank in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0, 1{]}}} instead of a raw integer\sphinxhyphen{}like rank.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature’s values replaced
by their rank under the requested policy. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rank()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with ranks; it does not add a new
column alongside the original. Keep the original values with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}}
first if you need both.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankNullRule::Keep}} (the default) means a row with a null in the ranked feature simply
has no rank there — it does not consume a rank position, so the remaining values still
rank as if that row didn’t exist for this feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentage = true}} is useful when you want a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1{]}}}\sphinxhyphen{}scaled competitive standing
(percentile rank) rather than a raw position number, without a separate division step.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rank:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sort\_values}}}}}}}: reorder rows by value, rather than
annotating each row with its rank in place.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/percentiles::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::percentiles}}}}}}}: a related but distinct question — the
value at a given percentile, rather than a value’s own rank.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::rdiv}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:dataframe-rdiv}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rdiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected (right\sphinxhyphen{}hand) form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}: computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other / frame}} instead
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame / other}}. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rmul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul()}}}}}}}, the reflected and forward forms
genuinely disagree here, since division is not commutative.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
rdiv() and rtruediv() are the same operation
Just like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}}}}}}} are verified\sphinxhyphen{}identical at the
forward level, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rtruediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}}}}}}} are the same reflected
operation under two names — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}} for the side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side confirmation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scalar that the frame’s values divide.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, holding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} divided by every numeric
feature’s value. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}} against plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} on the same data.

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{c}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reflected}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rdiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reflected}\PYG{p}{;}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
==================

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values.rdiv(10.0)}} computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 / x}} for every case: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 / 2 = 5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 / 3 ≈ 3.333333333}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 / 4 = 2.5}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{forward}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{div}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{forward}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===========
     | x   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
a    | 0.2 
b    | 0.3 
c    | 0.4 
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values.div(10.0)}} computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x / 10}} instead — an entirely different set of numbers,
since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame / other}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other / frame}} are reciprocal operations, not the same one.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv(other)}} computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other / frame}}; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div(other)}}}}}}} computes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame / other}}. The two only coincide when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame}}’s values and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} are equal.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}} are verified to be the same operation, mirroring the
forward \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}} identity.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only accepts a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/radd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}}}}}}} for why there is no
reflected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dividing by a frame value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} produces the usual floating\sphinxhyphen{}point division\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}zero
result (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inf}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, depending on the numerator), not an exception.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::div}}}}}}}: the forward form.

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes feature names without touching a single value, dtype, or case label. Two
distinct shapes are supported, and picking the right one matters:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Targeted rename} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_name}}, or a collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(old\_name, new\_name)}}
pairs): rename one or a few specific features by name, leaving every other feature’s
name untouched. This is the overload to reach for almost all the time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Full\sphinxhyphen{}axis replace} (a plain list of names, with no pairing): replace \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} feature
name at once, positionally, left to right. The list you pass must have exactly
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} entries, in the exact order the current features already appear — this
overload does not know or care what the old names were, it only knows position.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Mixing these up is the most common mistake: passing a short list intending a targeted
rename will instead try to rename \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} feature positionally (and fail or misname
things if the count doesn’t match). Use the pair\sphinxhyphen{}based overloads unless you genuinely
mean “replace the entire schema in one shot.”


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{old\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Existing feature name to rename, for the single\sphinxhyphen{}rename overload.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{new\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Replacement name for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{renames} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string\_view, std::string\_view\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::pair\textless{}std::string\_view, std::string\_view\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A collection of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(old\_name, new\_name)}} pairs, applied together. Features not named in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{renames}} keep their current name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}const char*\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A full replacement name list, applied \sphinxstylestrong{positionally} to every feature on the frame,
left to right. Must have exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} entries.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested names applied. Feature order, values, dtypes, and the
case axis are all unchanged — only names move.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The full\sphinxhyphen{}axis overload (a plain list, no pairing) requires the list length to match
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}} exactly. A shorter or longer list is a programming error, not something
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}} pads or truncates for you.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}} never changes values, dtypes, feature order, or case labels — it is a
pure schema\sphinxhyphen{}naming operation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For an in\sphinxhyphen{}place variant on a single feature, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}}}}}}} (note the
trailing underscore, the project\sphinxhyphen{}wide convention for mutating siblings of a
non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating method).

\subparagraph{DataFrame::rename\_}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:dataframe-rename}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rename\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{old\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The in\sphinxhyphen{}place counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}}’s targeted single\sphinxhyphen{}name overload:
renames exactly one feature, mutating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} directly and returning a reference to
it, rather than returning a new frame. Values, dtype, and case labels are untouched —
only the feature’s name changes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}, which offers several overloads (single pair, multiple pairs, or a
full positional\sphinxhyphen{}list replace), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} only supports the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature form —
there is no in\sphinxhyphen{}place equivalent of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}’s multi\sphinxhyphen{}pair or full\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}replace
overloads.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{old\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The existing feature name to rename. Must already exist on the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{new\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement name. Must not already be used by another feature on the frame
(unless it is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}}, which is a no\sphinxhyphen{}op).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame\&}}
A reference to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}} renamed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_name}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename_:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} throws if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name}} doesn’t exist, or if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_name}} collides with a
different, already\sphinxhyphen{}existing feature name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Renaming a feature to its own current name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{old\_name == new\_name}}) is a harmless
no\sphinxhyphen{}op.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For renaming several features at once, or replacing every feature name
positionally, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} only covers the
single\sphinxhyphen{}feature, in\sphinxhyphen{}place case.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Moves one or more named features into a new relative position, while every other
feature keeps its current relative order — without having to restate the frame’s
entire column list the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} reordering would. There are
two ways to describe a move:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A plain list of names (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder(\{"city"\})}}) moves those features together to the
\sphinxstylestrong{front}, preserving their relative order among themselves and the relative order
of everything else. This is shorthand for a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{placement = Front}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} (or several, applied left to right) supports front, back, before\sphinxhyphen{}an\sphinxhyphen{}
anchor, or after\sphinxhyphen{}an\sphinxhyphen{}anchor placement, and can select the features to move either by
an explicit name list or by a regex pattern matched against every feature name.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} in a multi\sphinxhyphen{}spec sequence sees the column order left behind by the
previous spec — later specs can reference columns by name regardless of where an
earlier spec moved them.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names to move together to the front, preserving their relative order among
themselves and the relative order of every untouched feature. Shorthand for a single
front\sphinxhyphen{}placement \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{spec} / \sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} / a range or list of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more move instructions, each built via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec::move(...)}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec::move\_regex(...)}} and a placement (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.first()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.last()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.before(anchor)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.after(anchor)}}). Several specs are applied in the exact order
given, each seeing the previous spec’s resulting order.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the moved feature(s) repositioned as described; every untouched
feature keeps its relative order (values, dtypes, and case labels are unchanged).

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reorder:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder(\{"a", "b"\})}} moves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"b"}} together to the front, preserving the
relative order of every other feature — it does not mean “replace the entire
feature order with just these two.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec::move\_regex(pattern)}} selects every feature whose name matches
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} (ECMAScript regex), instead of naming them explicitly — useful when
moving a family of similarly\sphinxhyphen{}named columns (for example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{move\_regex("\textasciicircum{}col\_2{[}1\sphinxhyphen{}4{]}\$")}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature named in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReorderSpec}} must exist exactly once across the frame; an
unknown name, a duplicate within one spec, or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{before}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{after}} anchor that is
itself one of the moved features throws.

\end{itemize}

one anchor, a lighter\sphinxhyphen{}weight alternative when only a single feature needs to move.

just reordering them.

reordering them.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::repeated}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:dataframe-repeated}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{repeated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flags \sphinxstylestrong{every} row that belongs to a group sharing the same composite key across
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} — including that group’s very first occurrence, not just the ones after
it. This is exactly {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated(features, false, false)}}}}}}} with its
display name changed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"repeated"}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} is what you reach for when you
want “is this row part of a repeated group at all,” rather than “is this row a
duplicate follower of an earlier one” (which is what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}’s default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}} answers instead).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which features form the composite key that defines a “group.” Leave empty (the
default) to compare whole rows across every feature.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, one entry per case, labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"repeated"}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} marks every
row belonging to a key that occurs more than once anywhere in the frame; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
marks a row whose key is unique.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{roster}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Compare against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}’s default follower\sphinxhyphen{}only semantics on the
same data.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{followers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{roster}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{student}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{followers}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  false
1  false
2  true
3  false
4  true
Name: duplicated, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}’s default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}}) marks only the \sphinxstylestrong{second and later}
occurrence of each repeated name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} at cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, the first
appearances) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} marks \sphinxstylestrong{all} of them, first appearance included. The two
methods answer genuinely different questions: “which rows are extras I could drop”
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}) versus “which rows belong to a group that repeats at all”
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}}).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} is literally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated(features, /*keep\_first=*/false, /*keep\_last=*/false)}} under a different display name — it never has its own
separate keep\sphinxhyphen{}policy parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing value in every selected feature is itself a valid “value” for grouping
purposes — two rows that are both missing on every selected feature count as
sharing a key, same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every selected feature name must exist on the frame; an unknown name throws.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/repeated:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::duplicated}}}}}}}: the keep\sphinxhyphen{}policy\sphinxhyphen{}driven sibling, for
marking only the extras after (or before) the first occurrence.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/drop_duplicates::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::drop\_duplicates}}}}}}}: removes duplicate rows outright
instead of just flagging them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::freq}}}}}}}: counts \sphinxstyleemphasis{how many times} each composite key occurs,
rather than flagging individual rows.

\end{itemize}



\sphinxstepscope

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finds a specific value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}) across compatible features and rewrites every matching
cell to a replacement value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}), returning the updated frame. The long overload list
looks intimidating, but it collapses into one rule: \sphinxstylestrong{the type of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} decides which
feature kind participates}. Pass a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} and only numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features are
searched; pass a string and only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} features are searched; pass a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} and only that temporal kind is searched. Features of any other kind are left
completely alone, the same way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}}}}}}} restrict themselves by dtype.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The other half of the rule concerns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}} (of type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}}), the
project’s null\sphinxhyphen{}sentinel constant: pass it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} to turn matched cells into missing
values instead of a replacement value, or pass it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} to replace \sphinxstylestrong{existing}
nulls with a concrete value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(pluss::null, 0.0)}} is a targeted, single\sphinxhyphen{}value
alternative to a broader {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(0.0)}}}}}}} call).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{from} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Note\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Timeline\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::TimeIndex\&}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value to search for. Its type selects which feature kind participates in the search;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}} searches for existing missing values instead of a concrete value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to} (same family of types as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement value written wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} matches. Pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}} to turn
matches into missing values instead of a concrete replacement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricts the search to an explicit feature subset. Leave empty to search every
compatible feature (every feature whose kind matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s type).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every matching cell rewritten to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}. Features that don’t match
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s type, and cells within compatible features that don’t match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s value,
are left exactly as they were.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:id3}}

===========================

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

1    | 102       42        
2    | 9103      1150
