\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} arguments are matched up positionally: every occurrence of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from{[}i{]}}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to{[}i{]}}}, for every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}, in a single pass over the frame. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{101}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{103}} are renumbered to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9101}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9103}} respectively; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{102}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{104}} never
appear in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}, so they pass through unchanged. This is the overload to reach for when
you have a whole lookup table of value substitutions rather than a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}
pair — build the two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} from a mapping and pass them straight through, instead of
writing one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} call per pair.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/replace:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s type is the whole dispatch rule: a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} never touches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} features, a
string never touches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features, and so on, regardless of what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} you
pass.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} narrows the search further, but never widens it beyond what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s
type already allows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} matches values exactly. It has no tolerance, rounding, or pattern\sphinxhyphen{}matching
behavior for numeric or string values — use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query()}}}}}}} or a mask built with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} for anything more elaborate than an exact\sphinxhyphen{}value swap.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating; it always returns a new frame.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::reshuffle}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:dataframe-reshuffle}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{reshuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{uint64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomly permutes either the case order (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}}, the default) or the feature
order (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}) of the frame, leaving the other axis and every value
untouched. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle(random\_state)}}}}}}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle(Axis::Case, random\_state)}} — the dedicated, more discoverable name for the case\sphinxhyphen{}axis case, which
is by far the more common one (train/test splits, breaking up any accidental
ordering before sampling, and so on).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} seeds the underlying random engine (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}}); passing the
same seed reproduces the same permutation on the same build, while omitting it draws
a fresh, non\sphinxhyphen{}reproducible permutation from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}} each call. Because
the exact permutation a given seed produces depends on the C++ standard library’s
own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}} implementation, this page verifies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}}’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{effect} — same
rows or features, same values, different order, reproducible given a seed — rather
than asserting one specific row order for one specific seed.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} permutes row order, keeping the feature order and every row’s own
values intact. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} permutes feature (column) order instead, keeping row
order and every feature’s own values intact.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{random\_state} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::uint64\_t\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A seed for reproducible shuffling. Omit it (the default) for a non\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic
shuffle seeded from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested axis permuted; the other axis and every
underlying value are unchanged.


\subparagraph{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} on the same build reproduces the same permutation;
it is not guaranteed to reproduce the same permutation across different platforms,
compilers, or standard library implementations, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}}’s exact
algorithm is implementation\sphinxhyphen{}defined.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} are mutually exclusive per call — a single call
only permutes one axis. Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle()}} twice (once per axis) to permute both.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}}}}}}} is the more discoverable, case\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}only convenience for
the common case; reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reshuffle(Axis::Feature, ...)}} directly when you
specifically need to permute column order instead.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/reshuffle:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shuffle::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::shuffle}}}}}}}: the case\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}only convenience wrapper around
this method.

permuting the full set.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

rather than a random permutation.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::rfloordiv}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:dataframe-rfloordiv}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rfloordiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected (right\sphinxhyphen{}hand) form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}}: computes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(other / frame)}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(frame / other)}}. Like the forward pair, this
is the one reflected arithmetic method whose result genuinely differs from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rdiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rtruediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rtruediv()}}}}}}} in value, not just in name — it always
rounds the quotient down after dividing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rfloordiv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ror:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}}}}}}. Since logical OR is commutative,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.ror(other)}} is indistinguishable from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.lor(other)}} in every observable
respect — same cell values, and (for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload) the same case labels
and title, both drawn from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame}} itself, exactly as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}}}}}} documents. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} for the full explanation, including a note on a previous revision
where the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload’s case labels came from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead — that has
since been fixed, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ror()}} shares the fix.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ror:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} — identical shape requirements to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ror:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame holding the logical OR of each cell against the corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}
value, with case labels and title drawn from the frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ror()}} was called on —
identical in every respect to what {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}}}}}} would produce for the same
arguments.

\subparagraph{DataFrame::round}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:dataframe-round}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{round}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{decimals}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rounds every numeric feature to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decimals}} decimal places, cell by cell. With the
default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decimals = 0}}, each value rounds to the nearest whole number. A null cell
stays null — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round()}} only ever changes an observed number’s precision, never invents
a value for a missing one.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{decimals} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of decimal places to keep. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} rounds to the nearest integer. A positive value
keeps that many digits after the decimal point (internally, the value is scaled by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10\textasciicircum{}decimals}}, rounded to the nearest whole number, then scaled back down).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/round:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature rounded to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decimals}} places. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) are left
exactly as they were.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rpow:notes}}\begin{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rxor:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}}. Since logical XOR is commutative,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.rxor(other)}} is indistinguishable from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.lxor(other)}} in every observable
respect — same cell values, and (for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload) the same case labels
and title, both drawn from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame}} itself, exactly as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}} documents.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} for the full explanation, including a note on a previous
revision where the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload’s case labels came from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead —
that has since been fixed, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rxor()}} shares the fix.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rxor:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} — identical shape requirements to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/rxor:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame holding the logical XOR of each cell against the corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}
value, with case labels and title drawn from the frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rxor()}} was called on —
identical in every respect to what {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}} would produce for the same
arguments.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a random subset of cases (or, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, a random subset of
features) from the frame — either a fixed count (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}) or a proportion of the axis
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}}). Internally this is built on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}: a set of positions is drawn
by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}} random\sphinxhyphen{}number engine, then those positions are taken in one
call, so the same shape guarantees \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}} makes (original case labels preserved,
feature order preserved) apply here too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A note on reproducibility: passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} seeds the engine so the \sphinxstylestrong{same
seed on the same build (same compiler and standard library) reproduces the same
draw}. The draw itself, however, is produced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}} / a uniform integer
distribution from the C++ standard library, and the exact sequence those algorithms
produce for a given seed is not fixed by the C++ standard — only the underlying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}} engine is fully specified. In practice this means a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}}
reproduces results reliably across runs on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{same} platform and toolchain, but the
specific rows two different compilers or standard library implementations draw for
the same seed are not guaranteed to match each other.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exact number of items to draw from the selected axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{frac} (floating\sphinxhyphen{}point)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The proportion of the selected axis to draw, computed as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round(frac * axis\_size)}}. Values greater than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} require \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} (there
aren’t enough distinct rows to draw more than the total without repeating some).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{replace} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the same position can be drawn more than once:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the default): every drawn position is distinct — equivalent to shuffling
the axis and taking the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}}\sphinxhyphen{}implied count).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: positions are drawn independently with replacement, so the same row (or
feature) can appear more than once in the result. Feature sampling
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis = Axis::Feature}}) does not support \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} — that combination is a
validation error.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which axis to sample from. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) draws rows. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}
draws columns instead, returning a frame with a random subset (or resampling, subject
to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace}} restriction above) of the original features, each with all of its
data intact.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{random\_state} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::uint64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
An explicit seed for the underlying random engine. Omit it (use one of the shorter
overloads) to seed from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}} instead, which draws fresh entropy each
call and is never reproducible run\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}run.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing the drawn subset, with the source frame’s feature order,
dtypes, and original case labels preserved for whichever rows/features were
selected.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Draw a fixed number of rows without a seed (result varies each run).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{three\PYGZus{}rows}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sample}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{three\PYGZus{}rows}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (one possible draw)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:output-one-possible-draw}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
======================
     | order\PYGZus{}id  units
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
1    | 102       5    
3    | 104       3    
5    | 106       2    
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result always has exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} rows, each a distinct case from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} (since
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace}} defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}), always rendered in the same box\sphinxhyphen{}table format any
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} prints in. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Which} three rows, and in what order, is genuinely random
without a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} — the table above is one possible draw, not a fixed result;
rerunning this exact code will draw a different set of rows almost every time, but it
will always be three distinct case labels pulled from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}}} with their
original \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} values intact.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}repeats}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} only has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} rows, but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} allows drawing more than that — case
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} and case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} each happen to appear twice above, and case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} and case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} also
repeat, since with\sphinxhyphen{}replacement sampling can draw the same row more than once. The
specific repeats and their order are random and will differ run to run; what is fixed
is the shape (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} rows) and that every value in the output traces back to one of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}}’s original \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} rows. Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}, requesting more rows than
exist is not possible for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} sampling.

===========================

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | 101       1200      
1    | 102       45.5      
2    | 103       1150      
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 2 feat]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac = 0.5}} over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} features draws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} of them — here, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}
happened to be chosen, but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} are equally likely candidates on
another run. What is fixed is the shape: the result always keeps all \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} cases for
whichever features were chosen, since sampling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} only decides which
\sphinxstyleemphasis{columns} participate, not which rows.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/sample:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample()}} is built on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}; a drawn position’s original case label
is preserved in the result, exactly as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}} would preserve it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} reproduces the same draw on the same compiler/standard\sphinxhyphen{}library
build, but is not guaranteed to reproduce identically across different platforms —
don’t rely on a specific seed producing byte\sphinxhyphen{}identical results in, say, CI running a
different toolchain than a developer’s laptop.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}} is not supported for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} sampling; every feature draw
is always without replacement.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}} values above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} require \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}, since there is no way to draw
more distinct items than the axis contains.

\end{itemize}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A single format\sphinxhyphen{}switched write entry point: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} picks which dedicated
writer actually runs, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as("csv", ...)}} behaves exactly like calling
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} with the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as("json", ...)}} like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json()}}}}}}}, and so on. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} is matched
case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}},
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}} — the exact same set of format names {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}}}}}} recognizes
on the read side, and every one of them is supported through this dispatcher (unlike
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}, whose non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} overloads only cover \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as()}}
has no such asymmetry — every format is reachable regardless of how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}} is
supplied).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Useful when the destination format is only known at runtime (for example, chosen from
a file extension or a user\sphinxhyphen{}facing dropdown) rather than hardcoded at the call site.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target\_type} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Format selector: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"json"}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"parquet"}}, matched case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively. Any other value throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PLUSS\_FAIL("DataFrame::save\_as: unsupported target type ...")}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Forwarded as\sphinxhyphen{}is to whichever dedicated writer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} selects — the recognized
keys are exactly that writer’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} keys (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json()}}}}}}}, or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet()}}}}}}} for the
per\sphinxhyphen{}format key lists).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} matching is case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}}
are accepted as interchangeable spellings — the same aliasing
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load(source\_type, ...)}}}}}}} use.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}}/positional overloads (which only support
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"csv"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"txt"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"text"}} and throw for the other three formats), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as()}} has no
such gap — every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config\_entries}} overload reaches all five formats.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An unrecognized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type}} throws immediately, before any file I/O is attempted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_as()}} cannot write a multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet Excel workbook — like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel()}}}}}}}, it writes exactly one sheet per call.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet}}}}}}},

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a delimited text file. The plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv(filepath)}} overload
covers the common case — comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, header row written, case labels \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} written
as their own column — while the fully positional overload exposes every formatting knob
CSV round\sphinxhyphen{}tripping tends to need: the delimiter, the missing\sphinxhyphen{}value marker, whether the
case axis should be exported as a real column, numeric formatting, quoting rules, line
endings, and text encoding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single detail worth deciding deliberately every time: \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}}. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
(the effective default via the filepath\sphinxhyphen{}only overload), the file contains only the
frame’s ordinary features — reloading it with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}} gives you back a frame with a
fresh, auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..N\sphinxhyphen{}1}} case index, not the original one. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the current
case axis is written out as its own leading column (named via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}}, or a default
name if you leave it unset), so a later \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv(..., case\_col = \textless{}that name\textgreater{})}} can
restore the exact case labels the frame had when it was saved.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{add\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the case axis is exported as its own column so case labels survive a
save/load round trip. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, only the ordinary features are written.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{header} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether to write feature names as the first line of the file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sep} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Field delimiter to write between values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{null\_rep} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The literal text written for a missing value. The default is an empty field; pass
something like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NA"}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} if the consuming system needs missing values to be
visually unambiguous rather than an empty CSV field.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_label} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Column name to use for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases=true}}. Leave unset
to use a default name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{float\_format} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fmt}}\sphinxhyphen{}style format string applied to every floating\sphinxhyphen{}point value written. Leave unset
to use the library’s default numeric formatting (enough significant digits to round\sphinxhyphen{}trip
typical values without excess trailing digits).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{quotechar} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}"\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Character used to quote fields that contain the delimiter, the quote character itself,
or a line break.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{doublequote} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, an embedded quote character inside a field is escaped by doubling it
(standard CSV quoting); when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, a different escaping convention is used instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{line\_terminator} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textbackslash{}n"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Line ending written between rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{decimal} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}.\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Decimal point character used when formatting floating\sphinxhyphen{}point values — set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}}} for
locales that expect a comma decimal separator (note this then requires a non\sphinxhyphen{}comma
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}, such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{};\textquotesingle{}}}, to keep fields unambiguous).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{encoding} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"utf\sphinxhyphen{}8"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Text encoding used when writing the file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{options}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::WriteCsvOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent settings expressed as a reusable config object, inline entries, or a typed
options struct, for callers who prefer not to spell out every positional parameter at
the call site.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing. Inspect the file on disk (or catch an
exception from the loader layer on a write failure) to confirm the result — there is
no in\sphinxhyphen{}memory object to print afterward.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Save with the simple, filepath\sphinxhyphen{}only overload.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}out.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_out.csv}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
order\PYGZus{}id,city,units
101,Accra,2
102,Tema,1
103,Kumasi,4
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column is written — reloading this file gives back a frame with a fresh
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2}} index rather than whatever case labels \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} had before saving (in this
example, they happen to coincide, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}} itself uses the default index).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Export the case axis as its own named column.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}case.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*add\PYGZus{}cases=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*header=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{,}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{c+cm}{/*null\PYGZus{}rep=*/}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*case\PYGZus{}label=*/}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{case\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_with\_case.csv}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
case\PYGZus{}id,order\PYGZus{}id,city,units
0,101,Accra,2
1,102,Tema,1
2,103,Kumasi,4
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading this file back with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_csv("orders\_with\_case.csv", \textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}, std::nullopt, std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}\{\}, std::string\{"case\_id"\})}}
restores \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_id}} as the case axis instead of leaving it as an ordinary feature.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv}} never mutates the frame it is called on — it is a pure side\sphinxhyphen{}effecting write.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing values are written as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null\_rep}} (an empty field by default), never as the
literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"nan"}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} unless you set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null\_rep}} to that string explicitly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float\_format}} when downstream tooling expects a fixed number of decimal places
(for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{:.2f\}"}} for currency\sphinxhyphen{}style output) instead of the default
significant\sphinxhyphen{}digits formatting.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a single worksheet of an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xlsx}} workbook. The sheet name defaults
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Sheet1"}} unless you supply one (via the positional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}} parameter, or the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}} field of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}). As with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}, the case axis
is \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} written as its own column unless \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} is turned on.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xlsx}} path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{sheet\_name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, positional overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Sheet1"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Name of the worksheet to write within the workbook.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{add\_cases} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the case axis is exported as its own leading column, named via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} (or a default name if left unset) — the same convention
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} uses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{header} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether to write feature names as the sheet’s first row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{null\_rep} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Literal text written for a missing cell. Default is an empty cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_label} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, default unset)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Column name for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases=true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{options}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::WriteExcelOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent settings expressed as a reusable config object, inline entries, or the typed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}} struct — recognizing the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} (also
accepted under the legacy alias \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}})/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null\_rep}} fields as the
positional overload.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Save with the default sheet name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Sheet1"}}), no case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}excel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}out.xlsx}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting workbook \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_out.xlsx}}, sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sheet1}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
| id  | city   | units |
| 101 | Accra  | 2     |
| 102 | Tema   | 1     |
| 103 | Kumasi | 4     |
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Save to a named sheet and export the case axis as its own column.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}excel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}case.xlsx}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Orders}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*add\PYGZus{}cases=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                   }\PYG{c+cm}{/*header=*/}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*null\PYGZus{}rep=*/}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*case\PYGZus{}label=*/}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{case\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting workbook \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_with\_case.xlsx}}, sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Orders}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
| case\PYGZus{}id | id  | city   | units |
| 0       | 101 | Accra  | 2     |
| 1       | 102 | Tema   | 1     |
| 2       | 103 | Kumasi | 4     |
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading this back with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_excel("orders\_with\_case.xlsx", "Orders")}} followed by treating
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_id}} as the case column (via a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadExcelOptions}} case\sphinxhyphen{}column setting)
restores the original case labels, the same way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv()}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}} pair does.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Save with a typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}} struct.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{WriteExcelOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sheet\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Regions}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}cases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}excel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders\PYGZus{}options.xlsx}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Resulting workbook \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders\_options.xlsx}}, sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Regions}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
| case | id  | city   | units |
| 0    | 101 | Accra  | 2     |
| 1    | 102 | Tema   | 1     |
| 2    | 103 | Kumasi | 4     |
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} wasn’t set here, the exported case column falls back to its default
name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}}).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only one sheet is written per call — there’s no multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet write overload the way
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_excel()}}}}}}} has multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet \sphinxstyleemphasis{read} overloads. Writing several
sheets into one workbook means saving to the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filepath}} multiple times with
different \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sheet\_name}}s and workbook\sphinxhyphen{}append handling managed at the file\sphinxhyphen{}format
level, not through a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::save\_excel()}} call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} mirror {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s convention exactly —
the case axis is opt\sphinxhyphen{}in, not written by default.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WriteExcelOptions}} accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} under the legacy field name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}} as well,
for compatibility with older call sites.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_excel}}}}}}}: the read\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart, including the
multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LoadResult}} return type this writer has no equivalent of.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::save\_csv}}}}}}}: the analogous CSV writer and the fuller
explanation of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} convention shared across all writers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_as::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::save\_as}}}}}}}: the format\sphinxhyphen{}switched entry point that can
dispatch to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel()}} via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_type = "excel"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xlsx"}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}json}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filepath}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Config}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{config}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{void}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a JSON file, in one of three layouts controlled by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orient}}
config key:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}}} (the default) — a JSON array of one object per case, each keyed by
feature name. This is also the layout {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}} reads most
naturally.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}}} — a single JSON object keyed by feature name, each value a JSON
array of that feature’s values across every case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"split"}}} — a single JSON object with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}} array of feature names and a
parallel \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"data"}} array of row arrays. This is the other layout
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}} recognizes on read.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output is pretty\sphinxhyphen{}printed with a 2\sphinxhyphen{}space indent by default; set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty=false}} for
compact, single\sphinxhyphen{}line output.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Recognized keys:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orient}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}}): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"split"}} — see “What It Does” above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): whether to add newlines and indentation.
Passing an integer instead of a bool also works — any value greater than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} is
treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indent}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json\_indent}}} (integer, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{8}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}): number of spaces
per indent level, when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty}} is on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{index}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}):
export the case axis as its own field/column, the same convention
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} uses.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indexlabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): field name
for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}} is enabled.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"records"}} is both the default write orientation and one of the two layouts
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_json::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}}}}}}} auto\sphinxhyphen{}detects on read; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"split"}} is the other.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"columns"}} is write\sphinxhyphen{}only — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_json()}} does not currently parse a bare
column\sphinxhyphen{}keyed object back into a frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pretty=false}} for compact output with no added whitespace, useful when file
size matters more than human readability.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}} follow the same convention as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} — export the case axis as its own field so a later
reload can restore it.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_json:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a Parquet file via Apache Arrow’s Parquet C++ library —
compact, columnar, typed storage, the write\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires an Arrow + Parquet C++ build
Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet()}} throws \sphinxstyleemphasis{“built without parquet\sphinxhyphen{}cpp support”}
if PlussMic was compiled without the optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PLUSSMIC\_HAS\_PARQUET\_CPP}} dependency.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination Parquet file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Recognized keys:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{index}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}):
export the case axis as its own column, matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}} convention.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indexlabel}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): column
name for the exported case\sphinxhyphen{}axis column when the flag above is enabled.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_parquet:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires PlussMic to have been built with Arrow + Parquet C++ support, exactly like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}}; otherwise every call throws immediately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselabel}} follow the same convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_cases}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_label}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_excel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel()}}}}}}}’s equivalent fields.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values are written using Arrow’s own Parquet type mapping from PlussMic’s inferred
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} dtypes — but recall from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_parquet::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_parquet()}}}}}}} that
reading the file back re\sphinxhyphen{}infers types from stringified values rather than trusting
the Parquet schema directly, so a save/load round trip is not guaranteed to preserve
the exact original precision (for example, a narrower integer width).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes the frame to a delimited text file — internally, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_txt()}} is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} with one difference: if the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}} doesn’t explicitly
set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delimiter}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}, the field delimiter defaults to a tab (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}\textbackslash{}t\textquotesingle{}}})
instead of a comma. Every other writing behavior (missing\sphinxhyphen{}value representation,
quoting, encoding) is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{filepath} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Destination file path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{config} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::loader::Config\&}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{config\_entries}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}pluss::loader::ConfigEntry\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A reusable or inline settings bundle, recognizing the same keys
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config}} overload does (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{addcases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nullrep}}, and so on).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{void}}
Performs the write and returns nothing.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_txt:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_txt()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/save_csv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}}}}}}} share the exact same writer; the only
difference is the tab\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}comma default delimiter, and only when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}} isn’t set
explicitly in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no dedicated positional overload the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv()}} has — use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}
for anything beyond the plain filepath\sphinxhyphen{}only call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The read\sphinxhyphen{}side counterpart, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/load_txt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_txt()}}}}}}}, does \sphinxstylestrong{not} default to a
tab separator — you must specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sep}} explicitly when reading a file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_txt()}}
wrote with its tab default.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::scan}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:dataframe-scan}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:signatures}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{scan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ScanStatistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statistic}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skip\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose running/cumulative\sphinxhyphen{}statistic engine behind
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumprod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}}}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}}}}}} — each of those four is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} with one fixed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Sum, ...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Product, ...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Minimum, ...)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax(...)}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Maximum, ...)}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} directly when you want to select the statistic dynamically (as a
variable rather than a fixed call name); reach for the four named convenience
methods otherwise, since they read more clearly at the call site.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which running statistic to compute down (or across) each numeric feature:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic::Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Product}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Direction to accumulate along. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) runs down each feature’s
cases; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} accumulates across a row’s features left to right instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls what happens once a null is encountered — identical semantics to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): a null produces a null only at that case; the running
statistic is preserved underneath it and resumes normally at the next observed
value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the first null poisons every case after it, all the way to the end of
that feature.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape as the source, with every numeric feature replaced by
its running \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{statistic}}. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are left unchanged.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{score}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/scan:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} \sphinxstylestrong{replaces} each numeric feature’s values with the running statistic; it
does not add a new column alongside the original.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features pass through completely unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic::Sum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Product}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}} are the only four supported
statistics; there is no running mean or running standard deviation available
through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}}.

\end{itemize}
