\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transform:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rewrites feature values by applying a user\sphinxhyphen{}supplied function, in several shapes
depending on which overload you reach for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame, thread\sphinxhyphen{}wise} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform(fn)}}): applies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} to \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} feature’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} independently, replacing each with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}}’s result. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}} overload is
the same thing spelled out explicitly — it requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} and throws
otherwise, pointing you at the row\sphinxhyphen{}wise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback overload for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Single feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform(feature, fn)}}): rewrites just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}. The
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback form receives that feature’s own values; the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback
form receives the \sphinxstyleemphasis{whole frame} so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} can derive the new column from other
features too — this form can also \sphinxstylestrong{create} a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new feature named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}
if it doesn’t already exist (it’s implemented via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Several features via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TransformSpec}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform(specs)}}): apply a different
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback to each of several named features in one call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Row\sphinxhyphen{}wise} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} only): the two least common overloads. The
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback form calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} once per case (each case observed as a
one\sphinxhyphen{}row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}) and expects a single scalar back, concatenating the results
into one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} — every returned value must share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind}}. The
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback form is the same per\sphinxhyphen{}case iteration but expects a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
back each time, controlled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape::Infer}} (the default) imposes
no consistency check at all; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Reduce}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Preserve}} require exactly one output row per
case; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Expand}} requires every case’s callback result to share the same case count
and feature schema.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transform:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The transform function. Its signature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread(const Thread\&)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread(const DataFrame\&)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue(const DataFrame\&)}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame(const DataFrame\&)}})
selects which overload is called. A returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} must match the frame’s case
count.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame overload, must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (throws otherwise). For the
row\sphinxhyphen{}wise overloads, must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (throws otherwise) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}} exists on these
signatures mainly to make the row\sphinxhyphen{}wise\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}feature\sphinxhyphen{}wise choice explicit at the call
site.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to rewrite (or create, for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback single\sphinxhyphen{}feature
overload).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}TransformSpec\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{feature, expr\}}} pairs, each naming one feature and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback
to apply to it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{shape} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infer}}, row\sphinxhyphen{}wise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback overload
only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls what consistency is required across every case’s callback result:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infer}} (no check), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Reduce}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Preserve}} (each result must be exactly one row;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Preserve}} additionally requires the same feature schema as the input),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Expand}} (every result must share the same case count and feature schema as each
other).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transform:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
(Most overloads) A new frame with the targeted feature(s) rewritten (or, for the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback single\sphinxhyphen{}feature and row\sphinxhyphen{}wise overloads, potentially added).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
(Row\sphinxhyphen{}wise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback overload) One entry per case, concatenated from
each case’s scalar result.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transform:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform(fn)}} (no feature name) always applies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} to every feature; use the
single\sphinxhyphen{}feature or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TransformSpec}} overloads to target specific features instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback overload can both \sphinxstylestrong{rewrite} an existing
feature and \sphinxstylestrong{create} a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new one, depending on whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} already
exists — it’s implemented directly via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/assign::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (whole\sphinxhyphen{}frame and single\sphinxhyphen{}feature overloads) must have the
same length as the frame’s case count, or the call throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the row\sphinxhyphen{}wise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}callback overload, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultShape::Infer}} (the
default) performs \sphinxstylestrong{no} shape consistency check across cases at all — reach for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Reduce}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Preserve}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Expand}} explicitly when you need that guarantee enforced.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::transpose}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transpose:dataframe-transpose}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transpose::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transpose:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{transpose}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transpose:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flips rows and features: each original \sphinxstylestrong{case} becomes a new \sphinxstylestrong{feature} (named
after that case’s original label), and each original \sphinxstylestrong{feature name} becomes a new
\sphinxstylestrong{case label}. Every value in the result is converted to its text representation —
transposing mixes together whatever types were in each row (numbers, strings, and so
on), and a single output column can no longer be a single\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} once it holds
values that used to live in different feature columns of different types. This makes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transpose()}} best suited for quick visual inspection of a small, wide\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}tall
swap — not as a step in a numeric pipeline, since every value becomes text and a
missing value becomes the literal string \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transpose:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, identical in behavior to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transpose:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A new frame where the original feature names are the case labels, and the
original case labels are the feature names, with every cell converted to text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The original two features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}) are now the row labels; the original
three cases (default labels \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) are now the feature names. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s
missing third value became the literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} — a text cell reading the word
“NULL”, not a typed missing value — because the result is text throughout. Note also
that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1200.0}} prints as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1200}}: whole\sphinxhyphen{}valued floats are rendered without a trailing
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.0}} in the transposed text form.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/transpose:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every cell in the result is text, regardless of the original column’s type — a
transposed frame is not meant for further numeric computation, only inspection.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing source cell becomes the literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} (the word, as a text cell),
not a typed missing value — this is different from every other reshaping method in
this reference, which preserve an actual missing cell instead of a text
representation of one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The new feature names come from the original case labels; if those labels would
collide as feature names (for example, duplicate case labels), they are
disambiguated automatically.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transpose()}} composes with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} exactly like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} do.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/truediv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The named\sphinxhyphen{}method form of elementwise division — and, verified against the underlying
numeric kernel, \sphinxstylestrong{the same operation as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}} shares the
exact same overload shape and alignment rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} and the rest of the
arithmetic family — see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s “What It Does” for the full explanation of the
scalar/frame/Thread operand shapes and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} parameters.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
truediv() and div() are the same operation
Both names route to the identical division kernel and produce identical results for
every input, including integer\sphinxhyphen{}typed features — neither one truncates or floors the
way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}} does. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}} exists as the more explicit name for
readers who want it clear this is ordinary (non\sphinxhyphen{}floor) division; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} is the
shorter alternative. There is no behavioral difference — pick whichever name reads
better at the call site.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/truediv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand operand, dividing the current frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (broadcast scalar),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} (aligned frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} (broadcast per
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}}, Thread overloads only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} (default) supplies one
value per feature; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} supplies one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same meaning as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters the dedicated time\sphinxhyphen{}series\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{numerics} accessor for the current frame —
period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period returns, differencing, lag/lead, rolling and expanding windows,
exponentially\sphinxhyphen{}weighted statistics, and more, one method per operation. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}}}}}}} (which requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} features), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} requires
\sphinxstylestrong{every feature currently on the frame to already be a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}} — narrow
to the numeric feature(s) first with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}}, the same idiom
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} use for their own kind requirement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions}}) optionally supplies an explicit time \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group}} (for
grouped/panel time\sphinxhyphen{}series operations), and an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor}}, letting the accessor’s window
and resampling methods reason about actual elapsed time rather than plain row
position. Omitting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} is equivalent to a default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions\{\}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page previews the accessor’s most common entry points. Every one of its methods
has its own dedicated, example\sphinxhyphen{}rich reference page — start at the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}} and
use its left sidebar to jump straight to any method (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expanding}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ewm}}, and more).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const TsOptions\&}}, optional)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, default undefined): an explicit time axis (typically a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}) to align duration\sphinxhyphen{}based windows against, instead of plain row order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsGroup}}, default empty): grouping keys for panel\sphinxhyphen{}style time series,
so window/lag operations don’t cross group boundaries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, default undefined): a reference point for anchored
resampling operations.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor}}
A lightweight accessor bound to the current (all\sphinxhyphen{}numeric) frame and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.
Every method on it returns a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}; the source frame is never mutated.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute a lag and a period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period difference on a numeric feature —
after selecting it first.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature on the frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} is called on must already be a numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; select the numeric feature(s) first with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} if
the source frame has other kinds mixed in.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.lag(periods)}} on a numeric feature behaves identically to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift(periods)}}}}}}} scoped to that same feature — both introduce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
at the vacated end.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} on a frame with no features at all, or a frame containing a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
feature, throws before constructing the accessor.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unify:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A relational, key\sphinxhyphen{}value join between this frame and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} — matching rows by the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{values} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left\_on}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right\_on}}, not by case label or row position. This is
distinct from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/join::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/align::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}}}}}},
which all match rows by \sphinxstylestrong{case\sphinxhyphen{}label value}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unify()}} matches by an arbitrary key
feature (or several), the same shape as a SQL \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JOIN}} or a pandas \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{merge()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right\_on}} defaults to reusing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left\_on}}’s names when left and right share the same
key column name(s); pass it explicitly when the two frames name their keys
differently.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unify:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{left\_on} / \sphinxstylestrong{right\_on}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Key feature name(s) on this frame / on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} used to match rows. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right\_on}}
defaults (empty) to reusing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left\_on}}’s names.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{right} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand frame to join against.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{how} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"common"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The join mode. Matching is case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive, and an empty string is treated the same
as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"common"}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"common"}} (aliases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"inner"}}): keep only rows whose key values match on both
sides.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"keep\_left"}} (aliases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"keep\sphinxhyphen{}left"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"left"}}): keep every row from this frame,
attaching a match from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} where one exists (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s columns
otherwise).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"keep\_right"}} (aliases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"keep\sphinxhyphen{}right"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"right"}}): the mirror image, keeping every
row from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"unite"}} (aliases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"outer"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"full"}}): keep the union of keys from both sides.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cross"}}: the cartesian product of every row in both frames; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left\_on}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right\_on}}
must both be empty for this mode.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"left\_only"}} (aliases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"left\sphinxhyphen{}only"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"left\_anti"}}): keep only this frame’s rows
whose key does \sphinxstylestrong{not} occur on the right — an anti\sphinxhyphen{}join.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"right\_only"}} (aliases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"right\sphinxhyphen{}only"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"right\_anti"}}): the mirror image anti\sphinxhyphen{}join,
keeping only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s unmatched rows.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing anything else throws with the message
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::unify: supported modes are \textquotesingle{}common\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}keep\_left\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}keep\_right\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}unite\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}cross\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}left\_only\textquotesingle{}, and \textquotesingle{}right\_only\textquotesingle{}"}}
(the canonical names only — the message itself doesn’t list the shorthand aliases
above, even though they’re all accepted).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{right\_suffix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_right"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Suffix appended to a right\sphinxhyphen{}hand, non\sphinxhyphen{}key feature name that would otherwise collide
with an existing left\sphinxhyphen{}hand feature name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{validate} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"many\_to\_many"}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
An optional key\sphinxhyphen{}cardinality check: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"many\_to\_many"}} (no constraint, the default),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"one\_to\_one"}} (each key must appear at most once on both sides), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"one\_to\_many"}}
(unique on the left, duplicates allowed on the right), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"many\_to\_one"}} (the
mirror image). A violated constraint throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unify:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"many\_to\_many"}} allows repeated keys on either side freely; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"one\_to\_one"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"one\_to\_many"}} (unique left required), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"many\_to\_one"}} (unique right required)
each enforce a cardinality constraint and throw the moment it’s violated.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unify:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unify()}} matches rows by key \sphinxstylestrong{value}, never by case label or row position —
this is the key distinction from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/join::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/align::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Repeated key values expand to every matching pair on the opposing side — a key
that appears twice on the left and three times on the right produces six paired
rows in the joined result (subject to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{how}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right\_suffix}} is only ever applied to right\sphinxhyphen{}hand, \sphinxstylestrong{non\sphinxhyphen{}key} feature names that
collide with an existing left\sphinxhyphen{}hand name — the shared key column itself is never
suffixed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result’s case labels are always a fresh default index, regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{how}} —
neither input frame’s case labels carry through.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unsqueeze:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wraps the current frame into a depth\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::table}}’s stacked,
multi\sphinxhyphen{}frame container — so it can participate in APIs that expect an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} rather
than a lone \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsqueeze()}} is literally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas(\{*this\})}}; the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth\_labels}} overload is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas(\{*this\}, depth\_labels)}}, additionally naming that
one depth layer.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unsqueeze:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{depth\_labels} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, one\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A single label naming the frame’s one depth layer. Must be defined and have exactly
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size() == 1}}, or the call throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unsqueeze:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}
A new atlas of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth() == 1}}, whose one frame (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.frame(0)}}) is exactly this
frame.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labeled\_atlas}} carries one depth label, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"train"}}, alongside its single frame —
useful when this frame is about to be combined with other unsqueezed frames into a
multi\sphinxhyphen{}depth atlas (say, one layer per dataset split) and each layer needs a name.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unsqueeze:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsqueeze()}} never copies or transforms the frame’s data — the atlas’s one layer
is exactly this frame, unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth\_labels}} overload requires exactly one label (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size() == 1}}); passing a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} of any other length throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::unsqueeze: depth labels must have size 1"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the natural entry point when an API expects an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} (for example,
multi\sphinxhyphen{}frame plotting or archival) but the data in hand is currently a single
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unstack:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pivots one named level out of a \sphinxstylestrong{multi\sphinxhyphen{}level case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis} so its distinct
values become new output columns — the (partial) inverse of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/stack::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stack()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unstack()}} requires the
frame to already have named case\sphinxhyphen{}label levels (built via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(\{...\}, true)}}}}}}}); the level named by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.label}} (or the
convenience overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}} argument) is the one that gets spread into columns,
while every \sphinxstyleemphasis{other} level stays as the row grouping key.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the new column names get prefixed by the source feature name depends on how
many ordinary features remain on the frame at the time of the call: with exactly one
remaining feature, the pivoted columns are named directly after the level’s distinct
values; with more than one, each gets prefixed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature + options.separator + value}} to keep them distinguishable.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unstack:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const UnstackOptions\&}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}): the case\sphinxhyphen{}label level to pivot into columns. Must
already exist on the frame’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): whether the \sphinxstyleemphasis{remaining} case\sphinxhyphen{}label level(s)
end up promoted back into the result’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) or kept as
ordinary columns instead (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): whether the pivoted column names are sorted
alphabetically before being added.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\_"}}): the separator between a source
feature name and a pivoted value, used only when more than one feature remains
(see above).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{label} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, convenience overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shorthand for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnstackOptions\{.label = label\}}} — every other option keeps its
default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop = true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort = true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator = "\_"}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unstack:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one row per distinct combination of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{remaining} case\sphinxhyphen{}label
level(s), and one column per distinct value of the pivoted \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/unstack:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unstack()}} requires the frame to already have named case\sphinxhyphen{}label level(s) — build
them first with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(\{...\}, true)}}}}}}}; it throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::unstack: current DataFrame has no case labels"}} otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(remaining\sphinxhyphen{}level combination, pivoted value)}} pair occurs more than once in
the source, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unstack()}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"duplicate cells found; aggregate before unstacking"}} rather than silently picking one — aggregate with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}} first if that’s the actual intent.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A remaining\sphinxhyphen{}level combination that never occurs for a given pivoted value produces
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell there, the same convention {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/pivot_table::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}}}}}} uses.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update:dataframe-update}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{update}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{overwrite}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A thin, case\sphinxhyphen{}label\sphinxhyphen{}matched wrapper over {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}}:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update(other, overwrite)}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine(other, \{.op = CombineOp::Update, .overwrite = overwrite, .cases = FrameMatchRule::KeepLeft\})}}. It refreshes this
frame’s existing feature values with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s values wherever their case labels
line up — but, unlike a general \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}} call, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update()}} never introduces a
feature that doesn’t already exist on this frame, and the result’s case labels are
always exactly this frame’s own (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FrameMatchRule::KeepLeft}}), regardless of what
extra case labels \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} might carry.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The frame supplying replacement values, matched to this frame by case label.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{overwrite} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether a non\sphinxhyphen{}null value in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} replaces a non\sphinxhyphen{}null value already present in
this frame. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, only cells that are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in this frame get filled from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}; existing non\sphinxhyphen{}null values are left untouched either way. (In both cases, a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} never erases an existing non\sphinxhyphen{}null value in this frame.)


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as this frame, with matching cases’
feature values refreshed from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}.

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 2 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result keeps exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}’s own case labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c2}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c3}}) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c4}} is dropped entirely, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update()}} always uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FrameMatchRule::KeepLeft}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c1}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{age}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30}}) has no counterpart in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}, so it’s untouched. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c2}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{age}}
was \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{26}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}, so it’s filled in. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c3}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{age}} was \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{28}}
in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{40}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}; with the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{overwrite = true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s
non\sphinxhyphen{}null value wins. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}} feature is ignored completely — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update()}}
never adds a feature that wasn’t already on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}, unlike a general
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}} call.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update(other, overwrite)}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine(other, \{.op = CombineOp::Update, .overwrite = overwrite, .cases = FrameMatchRule::KeepLeft\})}} — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine()}}}}}}} for the full generality this wraps.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only features that already exist on this frame are ever touched; anything unique
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} (like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}} above) is silently ignored.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result’s case labels are always exactly this frame’s own — cases unique to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} never appear in the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{overwrite = false}}, a cell already holding a non\sphinxhyphen{}null value in this frame is
never replaced, even if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} has a differing non\sphinxhyphen{}null value for that same case.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/update:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/combine::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::combine}}}}}}}: the general merge this method wraps a fixed
configuration of.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/unify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::unify}}}}}}}: a fundamentally different, key\sphinxhyphen{}value relational
join rather than a case\sphinxhyphen{}label\sphinxhyphen{}matched refresh.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrame::var}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:dataframe-var}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{axis}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduces every numeric feature to its variance, returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} whose entries line
up with the frame’s numeric feature names — the same shape {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}} returns,
without the final square root. Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features are skipped entirely rather than
coerced into a statistic that wouldn’t mean anything.

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default this is the \sphinxstylestrong{sample} variance: the sum of squared deviations from the mean
is divided by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}} overload exposes the same
two fields as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}’s structured overload — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} to switch to the population
variance, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} to require a minimum number of observations before a feature’s
result counts as valid.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reduction direction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Case}} (the default) reduces down each feature’s cases,
producing one variance per feature. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Axis::Feature}} reduces across each row’s features
instead, producing one value per case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Controls how a missing value affects that feature’s result:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing values are excluded from the computation entirely, so
the variance reflects only the observed values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a single missing value in a feature poisons that feature’s result, which comes
back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const StatisticOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A structured policy for the same reduction:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the delta\sphinxhyphen{}degrees\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}freedom subtracted from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}
in the divisor. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} (the default under either overload) is the sample variance;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} is the population variance, dividing by the full observed count instead of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the minimum number of non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations
a feature must have before it is assigned a real result at all; a feature with fewer
observed values than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One entry per participating numeric feature, labeled by feature name, holding that
feature’s variance.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute the sample variance, skipping missing values (the default).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{order\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{101}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{102}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{103}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{104}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{105}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{106}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{unit\PYGZus{}price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{320.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{42.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{discount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  3.5
     units  2.166666667
unit\PYGZus{}price  336993.25
  discount  0.00095
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each entry is exactly the corresponding entry in {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}}’s Example 1, squared —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{336993.25}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{580.5111971\textasciicircum{}2}}, for instance. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}}’s one missing observation
(case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}) is excluded from the computation, the same null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping rule every other
feature reduction in this table applies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Disable null\sphinxhyphen{}skipping to see a missing value propagate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  3.5
     units  2.166666667
unit\PYGZus{}price  NULL
  discount  NULL
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit\_price}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discount}} come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entirely, exactly
mirroring {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}}’s Example 2.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}} overload to compute the population variance
instead of the sample variance.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{population}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{population}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ddof}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread\PYGZus{}population}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Axis}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Case}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{population}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread\PYGZus{}population}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
  order\PYGZus{}id  2.916666667
     units  1.805555556
unit\PYGZus{}price  269594.6
  discount  0.00076
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every value is smaller than in Example 1, and each is the corresponding population
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}} value from that method’s own Example 3, squared. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} divides by the full
observed count rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}; use it when the data in hand is the entire
population of interest rather than a sample.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}’s result is labeled by feature name and prints like a small labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}},
not like a row sliced from the source frame.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features never appear in the result; they are neither computed as an error
nor silently coerced.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature with fewer than two observed values has an undefined sample variance and
reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, independent of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}} always agree up to a square root: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}’s result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}’s
result with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::sqrt}} applied element\sphinxhyphen{}wise, under matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/var:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::std}}}}}}}: the square root of this statistic, in the same units as the

\subparagraph{DataFrame::view}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:dataframe-view}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrame API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{view}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stop}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} row range wrapped in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, the same renderable
wrapper {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}}}}}} return. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view(start, stop)}} uses
the exact same slice normalization as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}} — both endpoints support
Python\sphinxhyphen{}style negative indices, both are clamped into range, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} is exclusive on
both ends, positive or negative. The only thing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}} adds on top of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}} is
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} toggle: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view(start, stop, render)}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(start, stop)}} dressed up in
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first case position to include. A negative value counts backward from the end of
the frame (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} is the last case), then the result is clamped into range — identical
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} handling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case position to stop before (exclusive), positive or negative — identical to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} handling. If the normalized \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} ends up before the normalized
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}, the result is an empty (zero\sphinxhyphen{}case) frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display toggle for the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, identical in behavior to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A view over a new frame holding the cases in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} and every feature of
the source frame, with the source frame’s original case labels preserved.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/view:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} handling is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}’s in every respect
— negative\sphinxhyphen{}index normalization, clamping, and an exclusive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}. The only
difference between the two methods is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} toggle and the fact that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}}
always returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} rather than a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case labels on the result are the source frame’s original labels, never renumbered
— same as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{render}} parameter works exactly as it does on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An exact alias for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where(bool\_mask, ...)}} literally
delegates to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter(bool\_mask, ...)}} for both the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} mask
overloads, keeping only the rows where the mask is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} and dropping the rest.
Note this is \sphinxstylestrong{not} numpy/pandas \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.where()}}’s replace\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}place semantics (which
keeps every row and only replaces individual masked\sphinxhyphen{}out \sphinxstyleemphasis{values}) — for that kind
of masked replacement within a single feature, reach for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}} instead.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A boolean mask whose length must equal the frame’s case count. Rows where the mask
is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} are kept; rows where it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) are dropped.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const AlignOptions\&}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}\sphinxhyphen{}mask overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alignment options controlling how a case\sphinxhyphen{}label\sphinxhyphen{}bearing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} mask is matched
against this frame’s own case labels before filtering.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing only the rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe/where:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}} is a pure alias for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} — anything documented there
(mask\sphinxhyphen{}length validation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}mask handling, case\sphinxhyphen{}label preservation) applies
identically here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is \sphinxstylestrong{not} numpy/pandas\sphinxhyphen{}style \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.where()}} replace semantics — it drops rows
rather than replacing individual masked values while keeping every row. Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/put::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put()}}}}}}} for masked, in\sphinxhyphen{}place\sphinxhyphen{}style value replacement within one feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kept rows retain their original case labels; the result is never re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed.

\end{itemize}

absolute value.

\subparagraph{Thread::add}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add:thread-add}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise addition. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} overload adds the same scalar to every value; the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload adds two threads together \sphinxstylestrong{positionally} — element \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} of the
result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(*this){[}i{]} + other{[}i{]}}} — and requires both threads to have the same
length. There is no case\sphinxhyphen{}label alignment the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} overload has; a length mismatch throws rather than padding with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} normally requires a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}backed thread, with one special case:
two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) threads support \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} too, and it means \sphinxstylestrong{string
concatenation}, not addition — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north\sphinxhyphen{}".add("store")}} behaves like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north\sphinxhyphen{}" + "store"}}, not a type error.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
add() is the canonical arithmetic\sphinxhyphen{}family reference
The rest of Thread’s arithmetic methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pow}}, and their reflected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{r}}\sphinxhyphen{}prefixed forms) all share this exact overload
shape, positional\sphinxhyphen{}matching rule, and length\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch behavior. Their own pages focus
on what’s different about each operator; this page covers the shared mechanics once.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value(s) to add. For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}
(or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, for concatenation).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise sum (or, for two
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} threads, the elementwise concatenation).

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload’s error message is prefixed with the exact call site
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::add(Thread)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sub(Thread)}}, and so on) — every method in this
family reports its own name, not a shared generic message.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mixing incompatible payload kinds (for example, adding a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread to
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} thread) throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::add(Thread): unsupported payload combination for operator \textquotesingle{}+\textquotesingle{} (Series vs Note)"}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} only accepts two numeric threads or two
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} threads, never a mix.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the calling thread carries display/case labels (set via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set()}}), the
result carries those same labels forward; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s labels (if any) are never
used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/radd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}}}}}}} is the reflected form — identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} for numbers
(addition is commutative), but the operand order flips for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} concatenation.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/add:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/radd::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::radd}}}}}}}: the reflected form.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sub}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/mul::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::mul}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::div}}}}}}}: the rest
of the arithmetic family, sharing this same overload shape.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::add}}}}}}}: the multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature counterpart, which adds
an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}}\sphinxhyphen{}based case\sphinxhyphen{}label\sphinxhyphen{}alignment overload that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::add()}} has no
equivalent of.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::align}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:thread-align}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{AlignOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Realign one thread to a target label thread using positional, case\sphinxhyphen{}label, or feature\sphinxhyphen{}label rules.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::align(...)}} is the typed column\sphinxhyphen{}level alignment surface behind many higher\sphinxhyphen{}level DataFrame operations. Use it when you are working with one extracted column directly and you need to reorder or relabel it against another label vector before comparison, arithmetic, export, or manual reconstruction.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target\_labels}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Target label vector that defines the output order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its interpretation depends on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.align}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Caselbl}}: treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_labels}} as the desired case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Feature}}: treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_labels}} as the desired feature\sphinxhyphen{}label axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}}: validate strict positional compatibility without doing label\sphinxhyphen{}based remapping.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alignment policy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignOptions}} exposes two public fields:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}: chooses the matching rule.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}}: strict positional alignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Caselbl}}: match by case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Feature}}: match by feature labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Both}}: not supported on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}: optional numeric fill scalar for newly introduced gaps.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
New thread whose values and label provenance reflect the requested alignment mode.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{} `AlignBy::Caselbl` gathers values by case label.
\PYGZhy{} `AlignBy::Feature` gathers one value per feature label.
\PYGZhy{} `AlignBy::Pos` keeps positional matching strict.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::align: frame\sphinxhyphen{}level alignment for several features at once.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::label: use label().set(…) to attach explicit labels before aligning by label.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/align:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Both}} is a DataFrame\sphinxhyphen{}oriented concept and is rejected for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} is omitted, unmatched target labels produce missing output entries. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} is provided, newly introduced numeric gaps are filled with that scalar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AlignBy::Pos}} does not broadcast. It expects compatible lengths and preserves the current thread’s value order and visible labels.

\subparagraph{Thread::all}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:thread-all}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skipnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns whether \sphinxstylestrong{every} entry in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — the
scalar universal\sphinxhyphen{}truth counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/any::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{any()}}}}}}}. Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; any other kind or dtype throws. With a validity mask
present, missing entries are excluded from consideration entirely (their
underlying stored value, whatever it happens to be, never contributes to the
result) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}} combined with a validity mask throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — every example
below uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} to print a clean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"true"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"false"}} instead of streaming
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
Must stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} when the thread has a validity mask — missing entries are
always excluded from the reduction when a mask is present. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull =     false}} together with a validity mask throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/all:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} only if every observed entry is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (an empty or
entirely\sphinxhyphen{}missing thread reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — vacuously, there’s no observed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} to disprove it).

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/any:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns whether \sphinxstylestrong{at least one} entry in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} —
a scalar existence test. Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; any other kind
or dtype throws. With a validity mask present, missing entries are excluded
from consideration entirely (their underlying stored value, whatever it happens
to be, never contributes to the result) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull = false}} combined with a
validity mask throws instead of attempting to define what “missing counts as
true or false” should mean.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — every example
below uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} to print a clean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"true"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"false"}} instead of streaming
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/any:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skipnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
Must stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} when the thread has a validity mask — missing entries are
always excluded from the reduction when a mask is present. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipnull =     false}} together with a validity mask throws.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/any:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if any observed entry is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} otherwise
(including for an all\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} or entirely\sphinxhyphen{}missing thread).

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/append:what-it-does}}

is a strict operation: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} must have the same {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/kind::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind()}}}}}}},

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{append()}} never coerces or promotes types to make two mismatched threads fit

followed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/append:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires identical \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind()}} between \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}; throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::append: payload kinds must match"}} otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads, also requires identical concrete scalar dtype
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::append: Series dtypes must match"}}) and platform
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::append: Series platforms must match"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validity masks combine correctly even when only one side has one — a side with
no explicit mask is treated as fully valid.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Also requires both threads to agree on whether they carry case labels at all
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::append: both Threads must either have case labels or both be unlabeled"}}); if both do, the labels are appended too.

\end{itemize}

It is especially useful for direct arithmetic chains, native Series reductions, or specialized kernels that already live below the table layer.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/as_series:notes}}
