This method returns the underlying payload reference. It does not automatically rewrap the result into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to call a Thread\sphinxhyphen{}only method after Series work, wrap the result back as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread(series\_result)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::astype(...)}} is the direct dtype\sphinxhyphen{}conversion surface on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. Use it when imported data need normalization, flags stored as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0/1}} should become booleans, or downstream kernels expect a more specific scalar dtype.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/astype:parameters}}

\sphinxstylestrong{dtype}

\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Bool}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Int64}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::ScalarType::Float64}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/astype:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the direct scalar\sphinxhyphen{}dtype conversion route. It is best for numeric Series\sphinxhyphen{}backed threads.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/astype:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}}}}}}: scanning right to left, whenever an
entry is missing and the entry immediately after it is (or has just become)
valid, it copies that value backward — so a run of consecutive missing entries
fills entirely from the single valid value following the run.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} caps how many consecutive missing positions get filled from a single
valid anchor per run; positions beyond the cap stay missing. A \sphinxstylestrong{trailing} run
of missing entries (nothing valid appears after it) never gets filled — there’s
no later value to borrow. Works across every payload kind (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — the latter delegates through its underlying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}’s note}}}}} on what counts as “missing” — for a
floating\sphinxhyphen{}point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} counts even without a validity mask.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})
Maximum number of consecutive missing positions to fill per run, counted from
the valid anchor backward. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means unlimited (fill the entire run). Must be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}, or it throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread with eligible missing positions filled. If the thread had no
validity mask and nothing was missing, the original thread is returned
unchanged. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit == 0}} is also a no\sphinxhyphen{}op.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Backward\sphinxhyphen{}fill every eligible missing position.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:id2}}

1  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} counts positions filled from the anchor backward per run — it resets
at every naturally valid entry, not per call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A trailing missing run (nothing valid follows it) always stays missing,
regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For floating\sphinxhyphen{}point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} counts as missing even without an explicit
validity mask.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}; anything else throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::bfill: limit must be \sphinxhyphen{}1 or \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Works on every payload kind, including \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} (via its underlying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}).

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bfill:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bottom:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} \sphinxstylestrong{smallest}\sphinxhyphen{}valued entries, sorted ascending, as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} —
the mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/top::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top()}}}}}}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size(){]}}}, the same
convention as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top()}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}}}}}} — a negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}
clamps to an empty result rather than throwing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bottom:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Number of smallest\sphinxhyphen{}valued entries to keep. Clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size(){]}}} — no
error for a negative or oversized value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s parameter description — auto\sphinxhyphen{}render\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}scope\sphinxhyphen{}exit
only.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bottom:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}}
A view over the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} smallest values, in ascending order, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s sorted
last.

\subparagraph{Thread::bounded}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:thread-bounded}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{bounded}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowBoundsFn}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bounds}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes a window statistic over the thread using \sphinxstylestrong{custom, per\sphinxhyphen{}row window
boundaries} you supply — the general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose escape hatch behind
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/weigh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weigh()}}}}}}} and the fixed\sphinxhyphen{}width rolling window methods on
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::ts()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeSeriesAccessor}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expanding()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{timed()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grouped()}} are all thin wrappers that compute their \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ends}}
internally and delegate to the same machinery this method exposes directly).
Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounded()}} when a fixed rolling width isn’t expressive enough and
each output row needs its own, independently\sphinxhyphen{}computed window.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}} is called once, given the thread’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} and the active
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowOptions}}, and must return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{starts, ends\}}} pair of equal\sphinxhyphen{}length
vectors — one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}} half\sphinxhyphen{}open interval per output row. Restricted to
numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; every other kind or dtype throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bounds} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const WindowBoundsFn\&}})
A callback \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(size, options) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} \{starts, ends\}}} producing one half\sphinxhyphen{}open
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}} window per output row. Must not be empty (a default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::function}}), or it throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})
Which statistic to compute inside each row’s window: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowOptions}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the smallest number of observed values inside a
window still considered valid. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the divisor
adjustment for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{centered}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closure}} are accepted but have no
effect here — your \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}} callback already fully determines each
window’s shape.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread the same length as the source, holding the requested
statistic evaluated over each row’s custom window.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{50.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:id1}}

0  NULL
1  15
2  25
3  35

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s window is just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1)}} — only one observed value, below
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 2}} — so it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Every later row has a genuine two\sphinxhyphen{}value
window: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15 = mean(10, 20)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25 = mean(20, 30)}}, and so on.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bounded:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}} must return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ends}} vectors the same length as the source
thread; each row’s window is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}}, half\sphinxhyphen{}open.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{centered}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closure}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} have no effect here, since your
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}} callback already fully controls each window’s shape — they only
matter for the fixed\sphinxhyphen{}width wrappers built on top of this method.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}} callback throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::bounded: bounds callback is empty"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return whether each element falls between two bounds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::btw(...)}} is the interval\sphinxhyphen{}membership surface on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. It supports scalar numeric bounds, scalar temporal/string bounds, and rowwise lower/upper threads. This makes it useful for grading bands, date windows, threshold rules, and per\sphinxhyphen{}row tolerance envelopes.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{a}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower scalar numeric bound for the numeric\sphinxhyphen{}scalar overloads.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{b}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Upper scalar numeric bound for the numeric\sphinxhyphen{}scalar overloads.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{lo}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower bound.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In scalar temporal/text overloads, this is one lower literal bound.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In rowwise overloads, this is the lower\sphinxhyphen{}bound thread used element by element.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{hi}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Upper bound.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In scalar temporal/text overloads, this is one upper literal bound.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In rowwise overloads, this is the upper\sphinxhyphen{}bound thread used element by element.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{inclusive}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shared boundary\sphinxhyphen{}closure shorthand.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: both boundaries are closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: both boundaries are open.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this when both sides should share the same closure rule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{include\_left}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the lower boundary is included.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: the lower boundary is closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the lower boundary is open.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{include\_right}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the upper boundary is included.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: the upper boundary is closed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: the upper boundary is open.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean thread containing one interval\sphinxhyphen{}membership result per element.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::ge and Thread::le: spell out the two comparisons manually when you want the lower and upper tests separately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame::filter: use the boolean result as a row mask inside a frame workflow.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The overload family supports three bound styles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
numeric scalar bounds,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
temporal/text scalar bounds,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
rowwise lower/upper threads.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When you use the two\sphinxhyphen{}boolean form, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_right}} independently control whether each boundary is closed or open.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The one\sphinxhyphen{}boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inclusive}} shorthand differs by overload family in the current API. The examples below show the actual behavior for each family, which is why this method deserves more careful reading than simpler comparison helpers.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/btw:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Use shared inclusion for scalar numeric bounds.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{btw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:signature}}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts a numeric thread into interval labels defined by explicit bin edges —
the one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional building block behind histogram\sphinxhyphen{}style feature engineering,
grading bands, and coarse segmentation. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}} must be strictly increasing and
supply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N + 1}} edges to define \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} buckets; each value is assigned the index
(or explicit label) of the bucket whose interval contains it. A value falling
outside every bucket’s interval (below the first edge, or above the last, given
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}} closure rules) becomes missing in the result,
rather than clamping into the nearest bucket or throwing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} controls interval closure: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = true}} (the default) makes each
interval \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(edge{[}i{]}, edge{[}i+1{]}{]}}} — closed on the right, open on the left — while
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = false}} makes it \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}edge{[}i{]}, edge{[}i+1{]})}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}} (only
relevant when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = true}}) additionally admits the exact lower bound of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{first} interval, so it behaves as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}edge{[}0{]}, edge{[}1{]}{]}}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(edge{[}0{]}, edge{[}1{]}{]}}} for that one interval only.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bins} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}double\textgreater{}}})
Strictly increasing interval edges — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N + 1}} edges define \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} buckets. Must
contain at least two edges, none of them \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, or it throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{labels} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}}, optional)
Explicit bucket labels, one per bucket. Left empty (the default) to use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ...}} as labels. If given, its length must equal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins.size() \sphinxhyphen{} 1}},
or it throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{right} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: each interval is right\sphinxhyphen{}closed, left\sphinxhyphen{}open (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(a, b{]}}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}:
left\sphinxhyphen{}closed, right\sphinxhyphen{}open (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}a, b)}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{include\_lowest} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = true}}, additionally admits the exact lower bound of the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{first} interval only. Has no additional effect when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = false}},
since the first interval is already left\sphinxhyphen{}closed in that case.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A numeric thread of bucket labels, the same length as the source, with a
missing entry wherever the source value falls outside every bucket’s
interval.

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

1  0
2  1
3  1
4  2

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bucket \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} covers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 20{]}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_lowest}} admits \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} itself, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}

Bucket \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} covers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(20, 40{]}}}, catching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30.0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{40.0}}. Example 3. A value outside every bucket’s interval becomes missing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}outlier}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{\PYGZhy{}5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{70.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}outlier}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{bucketize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{60.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  0
2  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5.0}} is below the first edge and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{70.0}} is above the last — both fall outside
every bucket’s interval and become missing, rather than clamping into the
nearest bucket.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N + 1}} bin edges are required to produce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} buckets.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bin edges must be strictly increasing and non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, or it throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::bucketize: bin edges must be strictly increasing"}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::bucketize: bin edges must not be NaN"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A value outside every interval becomes missing in the result — it is never
clamped into the nearest bucket.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; any other kind throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::bucketize is only valid for numeric Series payload"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}, when given, must have exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins.size() \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} entries,
or it throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::bucketize: labels size must equal bins.size() \sphinxhyphen{} 1"}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/bucketize:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::bucketize}}}}}}}: bucketize selected
numeric frame features while preserving the rest of the table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/btw::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::btw}}}}}}}: test interval membership directly, without
collapsing values into bucket labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/clip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::clip}}}}}}}: constrain values into a range instead of
labeling which sub\sphinxhyphen{}interval they fall in.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::casefold}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold:thread-casefold}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{casefold}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Produces a case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive\sphinxhyphen{}comparison form of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread’s text —
conceptually similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}, but intended specifically as a
normalization step \sphinxstylestrong{before equality comparison}, not as a display transform. True
Unicode case folding can differ from a simple lowercase mapping for certain
characters (the canonical example is German \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ß}}, which case\sphinxhyphen{}folds to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss}} rather
than lowercasing to itself).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This build’s actual behavior
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}}’s Unicode\sphinxhyphen{}aware folding is only active when this build links the
optional Unicode backend (GNU libunistring). Without it, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} falls back to
being functionally identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}. On plain ASCII input, the two
always produce the same result regardless of build configuration.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — calling it on a numeric or other kind of
thread throws.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the case\sphinxhyphen{}folded text.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/casefold:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}, whenever the goal is a case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive
\sphinxstyleemphasis{comparison} — even though the two produce identical output on ASCII text in every
build, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} states the intent explicitly and picks up full Unicode folding
automatically if this build’s Unicode support changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/casefold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor::casefold}}}}}}} for the
multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature counterpart and a worked comparison example.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Slices every cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread the same way Python slices a string —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(start, stop, step)}} mirrors \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{s{[}start:stop:step{]}}} exactly, including negative
indices (counted from the end) and a negative step (walking the string backwards).
Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. Each cell is split into individual characters
(Unicode codepoints, the same unit {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}} counts), the slice is
applied per\sphinxhyphen{}cell using that cell’s own length, and the selected characters are
rejoined into the output string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the slice bounds are evaluated per\sphinxhyphen{}cell using each cell’s own length, cells of
different lengths in the same thread can each keep a different \sphinxstyleemphasis{number} of characters
from the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(start, stop, step)}} call — exactly as it would if you ran the
equivalent Python slice separately over each string.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Index of the first character to include. Negative values count from the end of
the cell (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} is the last character). Out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range values are clamped, never
throw.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Index one past the last character to include (exclusive), or the point to stop
just before when walking backwards. When omitted, defaults to “the end of the
string” if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step \textgreater{} 0}}, or “all the way to the start” if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step \textless{} 0}} — i.e.,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(0)}} returns the whole cell and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(\sphinxhyphen{}1, std::nullopt, \sphinxhyphen{}1)}} reverses it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{step} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
Stride between characters. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} takes every character in order; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} takes every
other character; a negative step walks backwards. Must not be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(0, std::nullopt, 0)}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::chars: step cannot be zero"}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the sliced text.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples below share one input thread:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{hello world}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ab}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (before, shared by every example)}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:output-before-shared-by-every-example}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  hello world
1  Accra
2  ab
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A plain forward range: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(0, 5)}} keeps the first five characters of
each cell (or fewer, if the cell is shorter).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{chars}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  hello
1  Accra
2  ab
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row 0’s first five characters are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hello"}}. Row 1 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra"}}, exactly five
characters) comes back unchanged. Row 2 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ab"}}, only two characters) is also
unchanged — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} is clamped to the cell’s own length rather than padding or
erroring. Row 3 is invalid and stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. A negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} counts from the end: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(\sphinxhyphen{}5)}} keeps the last five
characters of each cell (with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} defaulted to “the end”).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{chars}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  world
1  Accra
2  ab
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row 0’s last five characters are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"world"}}. Row 1, exactly five characters long, is
unchanged (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5}} resolves to index 0). Row 2, only two characters long, is also
unchanged — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5}} clamps to index 0 once it’s out of range.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. A negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step}} walks backwards — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(\sphinxhyphen{}1, std::nullopt, \sphinxhyphen{}1)}} is the
idiomatic way to reverse a string with this method, exactly like Python’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{s{[}::\sphinxhyphen{}1{]}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{chars}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  dlrow olleh
1  arccA
2  ba
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every valid cell comes back fully reversed, character by character (including the
space in row 0, which reverses along with the letters around it).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step}} greater than 1 takes every Nth character — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(0, std::nullopt, 2)}} keeps every other character starting from the first.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{chars}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  hlowrd
1  Aca
2  a
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row 0 keeps characters at positions 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{h}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{o}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{w}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{r}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{d}}) —
the space at position 5 is skipped since it falls on an odd index. Row 2 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ab"}})
keeps just position 0 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a"}}); position 2 is past the end of a two\sphinxhyphen{}character string,
so the stride stops there.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 5. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step = 0}} throws — there’s no sensible stride of zero.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{try}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bad}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{chars}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{catch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{exception}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{what}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:id4}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::chars: step cannot be zero
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 6. A non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} thread throws.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numbers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{try}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bad}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numbers}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{chars}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{catch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{exception}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{msg}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{substr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{msg}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{find}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:id5}}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Slices by Unicode codepoint, the same unit {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}} counts.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} values are clamped rather than throwing — only
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step == 0}} throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bounds are evaluated per\sphinxhyphen{}cell against that cell’s own length, so a single call can
keep a different number of characters from cells of different lengths (Examples 1
and 2).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/chars:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::length}}}}}}}: the character count that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars()}}’s implicit
bounds (and any manual slicing math) are computed against.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/pad::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::pad}}}}}}}: the complementary operation — grow a cell to a target
width instead of slicing it down.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::split}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/partition::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::partition}}}}}}}: delimiter\sphinxhyphen{}based
ways to break a cell into pieces, instead of position\sphinxhyphen{}based.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::clip}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/clip:thread-clip}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/clip::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/clip:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{clip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/clip:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clamps every element into the closed interval \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}min\_value, max\_value{]}}} — a value
below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_value}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_value}}, a value above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_value}} becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_value}}, and everything in between is left untouched. Requires the thread to be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/clip:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})
The lower bound. Values below this are raised to it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{max\_value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})
The upper bound. Values above this are lowered to it.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/clip:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with every value clamped
into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}min\_value, max\_value{]}}}.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadCorrMethod}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{method}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadCorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Pearson}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{double}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the correlation between this thread and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, as a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}
(unlike most of the reduction family, this one doesn’t return a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}). Three methods are available:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}}} (the default): ordinary linear correlation — sensitive to the
actual shape of the relationship, not just its direction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Spearman}}}: rank correlation — correlates the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ranks} of the two
threads instead of their raw values, so it only cares whether the
relationship is monotonic, not whether it’s linear.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KendallTau}}}: rank\sphinxhyphen{}concordance correlation — a different, more
robust\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}outliers measure of monotonic association.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both threads must be numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, or it throws. If either thread has
explicit case labels, the two are first \sphinxstylestrong{aligned by case label} rather than
raw position — see the important callout below, since this changes the result
compared to a naive positional pairing. After alignment, missing/non\sphinxhyphen{}finite
entries in either thread are excluded pairwise (a position missing in \sphinxstyleemphasis{either}
thread drops that pair from both). If fewer than 2 valid pairs remain, or
either thread has zero variance across its valid pairs, the result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}
(never thrown).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
case\sphinxhyphen{}label alignment changes the result
If both threads carry explicit case labels, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}} (and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/covar::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{covar()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_with()}}}}}}}) pairs entries by
\sphinxstyleemphasis{matching label}, not by raw position — the same way two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} columns
with mismatched row order still combine correctly. Two threads of equal length
with no explicit labels pair positionally instead. Example 3 below shows how
different these two outcomes can be for the same underlying data.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})
The numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread to correlate with.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{method} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCorrMethod}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Spearman}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KendallTau}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}
The correlation coefficient in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} if there aren’t enough
valid pairs, or either side has zero variance.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Pearson correlation between two related numeric threads.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{35.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{45.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadCorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Pearson}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0.943119
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Spearman correlation is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} for a perfectly monotonic —
but nonlinear — relationship, where Pearson is not.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{9.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{16.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{25.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{// y = x\PYGZca{}2}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pearson}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadCorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Pearson}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spearman}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadCorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Spearman}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{pearson: }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pearson}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{, spearman: }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spearman}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pearson: 0.981105, spearman: 1
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pearson sees the curvature in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y = x\textasciicircum{}2}} and reports slightly less than
perfect correlation; Spearman only cares that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}} strictly increases whenever
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} does, so it reports a perfect \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Case\sphinxhyphen{}label alignment changes the result compared to raw positional
pairing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{caselbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{c}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{caselbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{c}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aligned}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{aligned}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
1
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Even though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s raw values are in a different order than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}’s,
matching them up by label (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a"}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"b"}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"b"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"c"}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"c"}}) reveals a perfect underlying relationship: label \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a"}} pairs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"b"}} pairs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"c"}} pairs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30}}. Comparing the same
two threads’ \sphinxstyleemphasis{raw positions} instead (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}) would give \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}0.5}} — label alignment is what makes this example correlate
perfectly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. Fewer than 2 valid pairs, or zero variance in either thread,
returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} rather than throwing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constant}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{varying}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constant}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{varying}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{isnan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If either thread carries explicit case labels, pairing is by matching label,
not raw position — see the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing or non\sphinxhyphen{}finite entries are excluded pairwise; a position missing in
either thread drops that pair from both.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} (never throws) for fewer than 2 valid pairs or zero variance
in either side.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::corr: both operands must be numeric Series"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::corr\_with}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with:thread-corr-with}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadCorrMethod}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{method}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadCorrMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Pearson}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the same correlation {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}} does, but returns it as a
scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} gated by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} instead of a raw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} — below
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} valid pairs, the result is marked \sphinxstyleemphasis{invalid} rather than returning
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} as a plain, unflagged value. Both threads must be numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; case
labels align the pairing exactly as they do for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
invalid whenever the underlying correlation isn’t finite
Beyond the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} gate, the result is also marked invalid whenever the
underlying {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}} computation itself doesn’t come out to a finite
number — for example, zero variance on either side (every observed value
tied, under any of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Spearman}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KendallTau}}) produces a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}
correlation, and that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} is caught and reflected in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}} rather than silently passing through as a “valid”
result. You never need to separately guard against a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} hiding behind a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} validity flag — check \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}} and trust it.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})
The numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread to correlate with.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{method} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCorrMethod}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pearson}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Spearman}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{KendallTau}} — same semantics as

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 1}}, or it throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::corr\_with: min\_count must be \textgreater{}= 1"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case\sphinxhyphen{}label alignment applies exactly as it does for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the important callout above: validity covers both the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} gate
and whether the underlying correlation itself came out finite, across all
three methods.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both threads must already share the same platform, or it throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::corr\_with: operands must share a platform"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::corr\_with: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/count:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts entries in the thread — but exactly \sphinxstyleemphasis{what} it counts depends on the
payload’s dtype:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} payload} (any numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}):
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}} returns the number of \sphinxstylestrong{non\sphinxhyphen{}missing entries}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_true}} must
stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for these payloads — passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} throws, since “count the
falses” has no meaning outside a boolean payload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payload}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_true}} switches what gets counted —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count(true)}} (the default) counts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} values, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count(false)}} counts
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} values. This is a genuinely different computation from the non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}
case, not just a filter on top of it: it counts by truth value, not by
missingness.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — every example
below uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}} to extract a clean integer instead of streaming the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/count:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{count\_true} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
For a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}: which truth value to count. For every other payload:
must stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the non\sphinxhyphen{}missing count); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/count:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} count.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/count:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} payloads, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}} is always the non\sphinxhyphen{}missing count — a
thread with no validity mask reports its full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} specifically, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_true}} switches between counting
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}s and counting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}s — a fundamentally different question from
missingness.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count(false)}} on any non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} payload throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::count(false) is only valid for Bool Series payload"}}.

\subparagraph{Thread::covar}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/covar:thread-covar}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/covar::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/covar:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{covar}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/covar:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the covariance between this thread and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, as a scalar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} — the unnormalized counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}}}}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}
is covariance divided by the product of the two standard deviations). Both
threads must be numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}. If either thread carries explicit case
labels, the two are aligned by matching label first — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}’s important callout}}}}} on how much this can change the
result. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}) controls the divisor, exactly like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}} overload: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} (the default)
gives the sample covariance (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} divisor); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} gives the
population covariance (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} divisor). Below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} valid pairs, the result
is marked \sphinxstyleemphasis{invalid} rather than thrown — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note}}}}} on checking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}} rather than
trusting the printed number in that case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}, this method requires both threads to already share the same
platform (CPU/CUDA/MPS) — there’s no automatic host\sphinxhyphen{}side conversion here.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/covar:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})
The numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread to compute covariance with.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the divisor is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} ddof}} over the valid pairs.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the smallest number of valid pairs still
considered valid; below it (and always below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof + 1}}), the result is
marked invalid.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/covar:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the covariance.

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/covar:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If either thread carries explicit case labels, pairing is by matching
label — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}’s callout}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} (the default) gives the sample covariance; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} gives the
population covariance.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} valid pairs, the result is marked invalid rather than
thrown.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both threads must already share the same platform, or it throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::covar: operands must share a platform"}} — unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr()}}, this
method doesn’t convert to a common host representation first.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::covar: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::csmax}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:thread-csmax}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{csmax}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the \sphinxstylestrong{case label} of the row holding the largest value in the thread
— not the value itself. The mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/csmin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmin()}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cs"}}
stands for case, so this is the “which row” answer (like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{idxmax}} elsewhere).
If the thread has no explicit case labels, that’s the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}based
position; if it does, it’s that label’s own value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ties keep the \sphinxstylestrong{first} occurrence — if two rows tie for the largest value, the
earlier row’s label is returned. Works on every payload kind. Missing entries
are skipped when scanning; an empty thread, or one where every entry is
missing, throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — the examples
below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}} (default integer labels) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} (explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
labels) instead of streaming the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar holding the case label of the maximum\sphinxhyphen{}valued row — an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}
position by default, or whatever payload kind the thread’s own case labels
use if explicit labels are set.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Without explicit case labels, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csmax()}} returns the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}based
position of the largest value.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{50.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{csmax}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}int}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
2
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50.0}} (the largest value) sits at position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} — the position, not the value.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{labeled}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{csmax}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}str}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmax:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} (still where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50.0}} lives) is now labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Cy"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
