{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmin:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{csmin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmin:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the \sphinxstylestrong{case label} of the row holding the smallest value in the thread
— not the value itself. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cs"}} stands for case: this is the “which row” answer
(like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{idxmin}} elsewhere), scanning every valid entry, comparing by the same
rule {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}}}}}}} uses, and returning
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl()}}}}}}} at the winning row’s position. If the thread has no
explicit case labels, that’s the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}based position; if it does (via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(...)}}}}}}} or the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl()}} mutator), it’s that label’s
own value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ties keep the \sphinxstylestrong{first} occurrence — if two rows tie for the smallest value,
the earlier row’s label is returned, not the later one. Works on every payload
kind (comparison is delegated to the same generic row\sphinxhyphen{}comparison logic
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} uses). Missing entries are skipped when scanning; an empty
thread, or one where every entry is missing, throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — the examples
below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}} (default integer labels) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} (explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
labels) instead of streaming the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmin:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/csmin:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar holding the case label of the minimum\sphinxhyphen{}valued row — an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}
position by default, or whatever payload kind the thread’s own case labels
use if explicit labels are set.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/cumsum:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the running (cumulative) sum down the thread — a thin wrapper for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(ScanStatistic::Sum, skip\_nulls)}}. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/scan::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::scan}}}}}}} for the
full mechanics shared by all four running\sphinxhyphen{}statistic methods, including exactly
how missing entries are handled under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}}, and why the throw message
for a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric thread reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::scan"}} rather than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::cumsum"}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/cumsum:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: a missing input position stays missing in the output, but later
positions’ running sums are unaffected. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a missing input position
makes every subsequent output position missing too. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/scan::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::scan}}}}}}} for the full explanation.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/cumsum:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A thread the same length as the source, holding the running sum at each
position.

\subparagraph{Thread::day}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/day:thread-day}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/day::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/day:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{day}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extract the day\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}month component from each temporal value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the calendar\sphinxhyphen{}field projection for timeline and time\sphinxhyphen{}index threads.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use it when your temporal thread already carries full timestamps but the downstream computation needs just the calendar day.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/day:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/day:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
Numeric thread containing the day component for each participating temporal entry.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/day:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{day()}} expects temporal payloads such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The validity mask is preserved while the calendar field is projected out.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result is a numeric thread, so you can immediately use it in comparison, grouping, bucketing, or arithmetic pipelines.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/day:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01T09:10:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}02\PYGZhy{}01T11:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}03\PYGZhy{}05T15:30:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{day}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Thread::defined}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/defined:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{defined}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{noexcept}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/defined:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} object currently owns a usable backing payload at all —
an object\sphinxhyphen{}level integrity check, not a data\sphinxhyphen{}level one. A default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread()}} is undefined: it has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
payload behind it, and calling almost any other method on it throws. This is a
different question from “does this thread have missing values” — a fully defined
thread can still hold \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cells; see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} for that question.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Almost every other method requires defined() == true
Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype()}}, or any transform/reduction on an undefined
thread throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread: undefined handle"}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} itself is one of the very
few methods safe to call unconditionally — it never throws, regardless of whether
the thread is defined.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/defined:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/defined:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} when the thread owns a backing payload and can participate in ordinary
operations; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for a default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed or moved\sphinxhyphen{}from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/defined:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A thread built from real data is defined.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/defined:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} never throws, even on an undefined thread — it’s the safe way to check
before calling anything else.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Object\sphinxhyphen{}level validity only: says nothing about whether individual cells are
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}}}}}} for that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A moved\sphinxhyphen{}from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::move}}) is also left undefined.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::describe}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:thread-describe}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{render}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadView}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a compact statistical summary of one thread, as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} whose case
labels are the names of the computed statistics. The exact statistics depend on
the payload kind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}}: the same eight statistics, in the same order, as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe()}}}}}}} computes per column —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}} (sample standard deviation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} denominator), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75\%}} (quantiles via linear interpolation between ranks), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max}}.
Internally this wraps the thread in a one\sphinxhyphen{}column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, calls its
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}, and extracts the single resulting column back out — so it’s the
exact per\sphinxhyphen{}column counterpart of that method, not a separately implemented
calculation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind}: a frequency\sphinxhyphen{}oriented summary instead — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}} (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing
entries), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unique}} (distinct non\sphinxhyphen{}missing values), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top}} (the most frequent
value, ties broken alphabetically), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} (that value’s count).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Anything else} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}, non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}): throws —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} has no defined summary for those payload kinds.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s parameter description — auto\sphinxhyphen{}render\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}scope\sphinxhyphen{}exit
only; has no effect on what an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} ...}} prints.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}}
A summary view with one entry per statistic, labeled by statistic name. It is
given a display name — the source thread’s own {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/display_name::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}}}}}}}
if it has one, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}} otherwise — so the render footer always reads
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Name: \{name\}, ptype: \{kind\}}} rather than the plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype: \{kind\}}} a default
thread shows.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Describe a numeric thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
count  4
 mean  25
  std  12.90994449
  min  10
  25\PYGZpc{}  17.5
  50\PYGZpc{}  25
  75\PYGZpc{}  32.5
  max  40

Name: value, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The leading label column is right\sphinxhyphen{}aligned to the widest label in play (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}},
five characters) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min}}, and each quartile line up one or two
spaces further in than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Missing values are excluded from every statistic, the same
per\sphinxhyphen{}column skip {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe()}}}}}}} uses.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
count  3
 mean  23.33333333
  std  15.27525232
  min  10
  25\PYGZpc{}  15
  50\PYGZpc{}  20
  75\PYGZpc{}  30
  max  40

Name: value, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} — the missing entry is dropped before any statistic
is computed, not treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or left to propagate a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} through the results.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Describe a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread — a frequency summary instead of

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

unique  3
   top  Accra
  freq  2

Name: value, ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}} are tied at two occurrences each; ties break

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::describe supports numeric Series and Note payloads
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric statistics match {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe()}}}}}}}
exactly — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std}} uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} (sample standard deviation), and quartiles use
linear interpolation between the two closest ranks, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}} coincides with the
median exactly, including for even\sphinxhyphen{}sized samples.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads, ties for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top}} break alphabetically by value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned view always has a display name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}} if the source thread
didn’t already have one), so the render footer reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Name: ..., ptype: ...}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} payloads; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}, and
non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} all throw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::describe supports numeric Series and Note payloads"}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/describe:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::describe}}}}}}}: the same summary computed

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} are drawn from.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::mean}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::std}}}}}}},

\subparagraph{Thread::display\_name}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name:thread-display-name}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{display\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return the display name attached to the current thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The display name is presentation metadata, useful for rendering and labeling, not for changing the underlying values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use it when you need the current human\sphinxhyphen{}facing label without reaching into renderer\sphinxhyphen{}specific code.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}
Current display name, if one has been attached.


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread::with\_display\_name, Thread::clear\_display\_name: attach or remove the metadata.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_labels()}}, this is metadata\sphinxhyphen{}only. Reading it does not mutate the thread or affect later numeric, text, or temporal operations.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/display_name:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Inspect the display name attached to a thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}display\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{scores}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{display\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

scores

\subparagraph{Thread::distinct}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:thread-distinct}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{distinct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the distinct values of the thread, one representative per value, in
\sphinxstylestrong{first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order} — not sorted. Grouping is done by each value’s string form
(the same conversion {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tally::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally()}}}}}}} uses), so this works on any payload
kind, not just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}. Unlike a sort\sphinxhyphen{}based dedup, the surviving representative
for each value is always the earliest occurrence, and the relative order of
distinct values in the output matches the order they first appeared in the
source thread.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing entries are excluded entirely from the
result.
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: at most one missing entry is kept, appearing at the position of
its first occurrence among the survivors.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread holding one representative of each distinct value, in
first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order. Shorter than (or equal in length to) the source thread.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Collect distinct values in first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{distinct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  Accra
1  Tema
2  Kumasi

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra"}}’s repeat at position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is dropped, but the survivors keep the order
they were first seen in — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}} before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Kumasi"}}, not alphabetical order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}} keeps a single representative missing entry.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{distinct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  Accra
1  NULL
2  Tema

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} survives (from its first occurrence at position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}), even
though the source had two missing entries.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Order is first\sphinxhyphen{}seen, never sorted — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}}}}}}} if
you want the distinct values in value order instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}} keeps at most one missing entry, not one per occurrence.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grouping is by each value’s string form, so this works across every payload
kind.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/distinct:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ndistinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::ndistinct}}}}}}}: the count of distinct values, without
the values themselves.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

counts, sorted by frequency instead of first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::duplicated}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/repeated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::repeated}}}}}}}:

\subparagraph{Thread::div}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:thread-div}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{div}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{div}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise division, following {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s shared mechanics (positional
matching, length\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch throw, no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}payload support). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} delegates to the
underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} library’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} algebra, which is a distinct code path from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}}}}}}} (which always promotes to floating point via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true\_divide()}}). For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed threads used throughout this reference, the
two produce identical results; the distinction can matter for integer\sphinxhyphen{}typed threads,
where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}’s exact type\sphinxhyphen{}preservation behavior comes from outside this repository
and isn’t asserted here — prefer {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}}}}}}} when you specifically want
guaranteed floating\sphinxhyphen{}point division regardless of input type.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The divisor(s). For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise quotient.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Divide every value by a scalar.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{div}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  2.5
1  5
2  7.5

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Divide two threads positionally.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{splits}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{9.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{div}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{splits}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  2.5
1  2.5
2  3.333333333

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30 / 9}} doesn’t divide evenly — the result is displayed to 10 significant digits
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.333333333}}), the same formatting every numeric thread uses.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the family\sphinxhyphen{}wide mechanics: positional matching and the
length\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch throw (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::div(Thread): positional operation requires identical lengths"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}payload special case, unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} data, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}}}}}}} always agree — reach for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}} when the underlying type might not be floating\sphinxhyphen{}point and you need
float division guaranteed.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/div:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/truediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::truediv}}}}}}}: the always\sphinxhyphen{}floating\sphinxhyphen{}point counterpart.

\subparagraph{Thread::dropnull}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull:thread-dropnull}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new, compacted thread containing only the entries \sphinxstylestrong{not} marked missing
by the validity mask. If the thread carries no validity mask at all, this is a
no\sphinxhyphen{}op — the thread is returned unchanged (there’s nothing to drop). Otherwise, it
gathers the indices of every valid entry and calls {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}} with them,
so the result is a genuinely shorter thread (no null holes left in place) rather
than the original length with gaps. The result never carries a leftover validity
mask, even if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}’s bookkeeping would otherwise attach one — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}
explicitly clears it, so a fully\sphinxhyphen{}valid result reports no mask at all.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
mask\sphinxhyphen{}driven, not NaN\sphinxhyphen{}driven
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}} inspects the thread’s validity mask only. A plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} inside a
numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} is not, by itself, “missing” to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}} unless that position
is also marked invalid in the mask — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} for the same
mask\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} distinction.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread holding only the valid entries, compacted (re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}),
with no validity mask attached.

\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No\sphinxhyphen{}op when there’s no validity mask — returns the thread unchanged, not a copy
with a fresh empty mask.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result is compacted: surviving entries are re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed, never left with holes
at their old positions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result never carries a leftover validity mask, even when every surviving
entry happens to be valid.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Driven entirely by the validity mask, not by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}/sentinel values inside the
payload — see the note above.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::dtype}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:thread-dtype}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the concrete dtype name of the underlying payload — one level more specific
than {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ptype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype()}}}}}}}’s broad family name. For a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread this is
the scalar type’s own name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"float64"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"bool"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"int64"}}, and so on); for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"utf8"}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"bytes"}}, for byte\sphinxhyphen{}string payloads); for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"datetime64{[}ns, \textless{}tz\textgreater{}{]}"}}, including the timezone.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}
The concrete dtype name, formatted per payload kind as described above.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ptype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype()}}}}}}}, which would report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Series"}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Note"}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Timeline"}} for
the same threads.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numeric}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{text}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dates}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}timeline}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numeric}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{text}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dates}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
float64
utf8
datetime64[ns, UTC]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dates}} was built from a UTC\sphinxhyphen{}suffixed (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}) timestamp string, so its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}
carries the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UTC}} timezone — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype()}} includes it directly in the string, unlike
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype()}}, which would just say \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Timeline"}} regardless of timezone.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/dtype:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads report their scalar type by name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"float64"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"bool"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"int64"}}, etc.) — the same names \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::dtypes()}} reports per feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"utf8"}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"bytes"}} for a byte\sphinxhyphen{}string payload).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"datetime64{[}ns, \textless{}tz\textgreater{}{]}"}}, including the
timezone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype()}} on an undefined thread throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread: undefined handle"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::duplicated}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:thread-duplicated}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a boolean thread, the same length as the source, marking which entries
are duplicate \sphinxstyleemphasis{followers} of an earlier (or later) occurrence — one designated
occurrence per distinct value is left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (the “survivor”), and every other
occurrence of that value is marked \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. Which occurrence survives is
controlled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}} (the default): the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} occurrence of each value is
the survivor; every later repeat is marked \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last = true}}: the \sphinxstyleemphasis{last} occurrence is the survivor instead; every
earlier repeat is marked \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} cannot both be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — that throws. A value that
appears only once is never marked, regardless of the policy. This method only
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reports} duplicate membership — it never removes or reorders anything itself;
pass the result to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} to actually drop the flagged rows.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_first} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
Treat each value’s first occurrence as the survivor (left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
Treat each value’s last occurrence as the survivor (left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}) instead.
Cannot be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} at the same time as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, same length as the source, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} at every non\sphinxhyphen{}survivor
duplicate position.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default policy — keep the first occurrence of each value.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{duplicated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  false
1  false
2  true
3  false
4  true

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Positions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra"}} and first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}}) stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}};
their later repeats at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} are flagged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Kumasi"}} (unique) is
never flagged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last = true}} flips which occurrence survives.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grouping is by each value’s string form, matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/distinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distinct()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tally::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally()}}}}}}}; works across every payload
kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A value occurring only once is never flagged, under either policy.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports membership only — combine with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} (or its
logical negation) to actually drop or keep duplicates.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first \&\& keep\_last}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::duplicated: keep\_first and keep\_last cannot both be true"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::encode}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:thread-encode}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{encode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{encoding}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{base64}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread with an encoded form of its raw
bytes, choosing between three schemes via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encoding}} argument: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}} (the
default), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}}. Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. Unlike most
methods in this family, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} doesn’t validate its argument against an enum —
any other string throws.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}}}: standard Base64 (RFC 4648), using the classic alphabet (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}) with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}} padding to a multiple of 4 output characters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}}}: lowercase hexadecimal, two characters per input byte (so the output is
always exactly twice as long as the input, in bytes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}}}: percent\sphinxhyphen{}encoding (RFC 3986) — letters, digits, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}}}
pass through unchanged; every other byte becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%XX}} with two \sphinxstylestrong{uppercase} hex
digits.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encode only — no decode()
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} exposes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} but no corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decode()}}. There’s no built\sphinxhyphen{}in way
to reverse the transform on a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{encoding} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}})
Which scheme to apply: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}}. Any other value throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::encode: encoding must be base64, hex, or url"}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the encoded text.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples below share one input thread containing a mix of plain text,
punctuation, and a space:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{payloads}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra Mall}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{50\PYGZpc{} off!}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{path/to/file}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{payloads}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (before, shared by every example)}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:output-before-shared-by-every-example}}

0  Accra Mall
1  50\PYGZpc{} off!
2  path/to/file
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. The default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} with no argument uses Base64.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{payloads}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{encode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

1  NTAlIG9mZiE=
2  cGF0aC90by9maWxl
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra Mall"}} is 10 bytes, needing 2 bytes of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}} padding to round up to a full
16\sphinxhyphen{}character block. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"50\% off!"}} is 8 bytes, one short of a multiple of 3, so it gets
a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"path/to/file"}} is 12 bytes — an exact multiple of 3 — so it encodes
cleanly with no padding at all.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"50\% off!"}} (8 bytes) becomes a 16\sphinxhyphen{}character hex string — always exactly twice as

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encodes raw bytes, not Unicode codepoints — for ASCII text, “bytes” and
“characters” coincide, but multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 characters encode as their full
multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte sequence, not as one unit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}} output is always lowercase; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}} percent\sphinxhyphen{}escapes use uppercase hex
digits — the two schemes intentionally differ in this convention, matching common
real\sphinxhyphen{}world usage of each format.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind (text in, text out) — unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}}, which
switches to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decode()}} exists — see the note above.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/encode:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::length}}}}}}}: count characters instead of encoding them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

escaping needs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} doesn’t cover.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ends:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread’s cells for a literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive suffix match,
replacing each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell’s text ends with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{suffix}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t. The mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/starts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts()}}}}}}}:
same single\sphinxhyphen{}overload, no\sphinxhyphen{}options shape, anchored at the end instead of the
beginning. Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ends:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{suffix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The literal text to check for at the end of each cell. An empty suffix matches every
non\sphinxhyphen{}null cell.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ends:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the
elementwise suffix check.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ends:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Check a filenames thread for a literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive suffix.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{files}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ends}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{.pdf}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ends:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  true
1  false
2  false

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"notes.PDF"}}) doesn’t match — the uppercase \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{".PDF"}} extension doesn’t
match lowercase \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{".pdf"}} under a case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive comparison.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive suffix matching by normalizing first.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ends:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  true
1  true
2  false

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lowercasing first folds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"notes.PDF"}} down to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"notes.pdf"}}, so row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} now matches
too — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ends()}} itself never gained a case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitivity option; the normalization
happens entirely in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} step ahead of it.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ends:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive, literal comparison only — no regex mode. See Example 2 for the
normalize\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}check pattern that works around this.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the thread’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/eq:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise equality, returning a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}
overload compares every value against the same scalar; the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload
compares two threads \sphinxstylestrong{positionally} (same length required, no case\sphinxhyphen{}label
alignment); the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} overload (with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} convenience
wrapper that just forwards to it) behaves differently depending on the calling
thread’s kind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
On a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread, it compares each string directly against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
On any other kind (a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, for example), it \sphinxstylestrong{stringifies}
each value first, then does a plain string comparison against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}. It does not
parse \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} as a number and compare numerically.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
eq() is the canonical comparison\sphinxhyphen{}family reference
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ne}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ge}} all share this exact overload shape and
positional\sphinxhyphen{}matching rule. Their own pages focus on what’s different about each
operator; this page covers the shared mechanics once. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}}
specifically for why the string\sphinxhyphen{}overload’s stringify\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}compare behavior matters
more for ordering operators than it does for equality.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/eq:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value to compare against. For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/eq:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise
equality result.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/eq:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The comparison family also accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads on the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload (comparing timestamps), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} on the same
overload (comparing strings) — this page focuses on the numeric case, which is
the most common.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mixing incompatible payload kinds on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload (for example, a numeric
thread against a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} thread) throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"unsupported payload combination"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every method in this family reports its own name in error messages
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::eq(Thread)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::lt(Thread)}}, and so on), not a shared generic one.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/exp:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies the elementwise natural exponential (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\textasciicircum{}x}}) — the inverse of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/log::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}}}}}}}. Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. A non\sphinxhyphen{}floating scalar
type (integer, bool) is promoted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} before the exponential is computed.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/exp:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/exp:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp(x)}} for each
element (promoted to a floating scalar type if the input was integral).

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extracts one or more regex capture groups from a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread into a new
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} — one feature per capture group. Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind,
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} must contain at least one capture group (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(...)}}), or the call throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A regular expression containing at least one capture group. Only the parenthesized
groups become output features — the rest of the pattern is used for matching only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, optional)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature names for the capture groups, one per group. Leave it empty to get
auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated names \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_1}}, and so on (in capture\sphinxhyphen{}group order); if
supplied, its length must exactly match the number of capture groups.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/extract:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature per capture group. Rows where the
pattern doesn’t match stay present, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every capture\sphinxhyphen{}group column.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Forward\sphinxhyphen{}fills missing entries by propagating the last observed value ahead of
each gap. Scanning left to right, whenever an entry is missing and the entry
immediately before it is (or has just become) valid, it copies that value
forward — so a run of several consecutive missing entries fills entirely from
the single valid value preceding the run, not independently per position.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
what counts as “missing” here
For a floating\sphinxhyphen{}point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}} treats a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} value as missing
even with no validity mask present — it doesn’t require an explicit mask entry,
unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}}, which look at the
mask only. This is intentional: fill methods exist to patch numeric gaps, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} is the natural in\sphinxhyphen{}band hole marker for floating\sphinxhyphen{}point data. If a validity
mask is also present, both signals combine — an entry is treated as missing if
either the mask marks it invalid or (for floats) it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} caps how many consecutive missing positions get filled from a single
valid anchor; positions beyond the cap stay missing. A \sphinxstylestrong{leading} run of missing
entries (nothing valid appears before it) never gets filled, no matter the limit
— there’s no earlier value to borrow. Works across every payload kind (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — the latter delegates through its underlying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})
Maximum number of consecutive missing positions to fill per run, counted from
the valid anchor forward. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means unlimited (fill the entire run). Must be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}, or it throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread with eligible missing positions filled. If the thread had no
validity mask and nothing was missing, the original thread is returned
unchanged. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit == 0}} is also a no\sphinxhyphen{}op.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Forward\sphinxhyphen{}fill every eligible missing position.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mf}{50.0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ffill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:output}}

1  10
2  10
3  40
4  50

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both missing positions borrow from the single valid value at position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} — the
run fills as a block, not by looking two steps back independently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = 1}} caps the fill to one position per run; the rest of the run

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{numeric\PYGZus{}limits}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{quiet\PYGZus{}NaN}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:id2}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} counts positions filled from the anchor forward per run — it resets at
every naturally valid entry, not per call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A leading missing run (nothing valid precedes it) always stays missing,
regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For floating\sphinxhyphen{}point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} counts as missing even without an explicit
validity mask — see the note above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}; anything else throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::ffill: limit must be \sphinxhyphen{}1 or \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Works on every payload kind, including \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} (via its underlying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}).

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ffill:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

value.

\end{itemize}
