\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}, leaving already\sphinxhyphen{}valid cells untouched. The
overload selects which payload kind is required: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} requires a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind
thread, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
overloads both accept either a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}\sphinxhyphen{} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind calling thread
symmetrically. This is the same operation {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/replace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(null\_t, to)}}}}}}}
delegates to internally when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value}
The replacement for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cells. Its C++ type selects the overload — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}
for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Timeline}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::TimeIndex}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads (either scalar type
works against either temporal thread kind). The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} overloads
require a scalar value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{numel() == 1}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size() == 1}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length and kind as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell replaced
by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}.

Example 4. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} overload works against a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread too — the

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overload selection is by the C++ type of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}, which also determines the
required payload kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(double)}} requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; message: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::fillnull(double) is only valid for Series payload"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(string\_view)}} requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}; message: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::fillnull(string) is only valid for Note payload"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(Timeline)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(TimeIndex)}} both accept either a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}\sphinxhyphen{} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind calling thread; messages: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::fillnull(Timeline) is only valid for Timeline/TimeIndex payload"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::fillnull(TimeIndex) is only valid for Timeline/TimeIndex payload"}}, respectively.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} overloads require a scalar (single\sphinxhyphen{}element) replacement
value, or throw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"...replacement value must be scalar"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A mutating sibling, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull_::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_()}}}}}}}, applies the same fill in place.

\end{itemize}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull_:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The mutating counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}: fills \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cells with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} and updates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} in place, returning a reference to it, instead of
returning a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. Copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write applies — if this thread’s storage is shared
with another \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shares\_payload\_with()}}}}}}}), the
mutation clones the storage first, so the other thread is unaffected.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the double overload is genuinely in\sphinxhyphen{}place
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} overload mutates the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} storage directly through the
copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write path. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} overloads are
implemented as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this = fillnull(value);}} — they call the functional
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}} and reassign the result to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}. The end result and
copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write behavior are the same either way; only the internal mechanism differs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull_:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value}
Same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}} — the replacement for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cells,
selecting the overload (and required payload kind) by its C++ type.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull_:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread\&}}
A reference to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, after the fill.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull_:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write: mutating a thread that shares storage with another detaches it
first, leaving the other thread untouched. See Example 2 and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shares\_payload\_with()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} overload mutates storage directly; the others reassign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}
via the functional {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}. See the note above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} overload’s error message includes the underscore:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::fillnull\_(double) is only valid for Series payload"}} — a detail that
differs from the functional form’s own message for the same overload.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/filter:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Series}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bool\PYGZus{}mask}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/filter:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keeps only the entries where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, dropping the rest — the classic
boolean\sphinxhyphen{}mask row filter, built on top of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}} converts
the mask to the list of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} positions, then takes them in order). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}}
must be a 1D, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}scalar\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}} with exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} elements.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/filter:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Series\&}})
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed, 1D \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}. Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} position is
kept, in original order; every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} position is dropped.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/filter:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread holding only the entries where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool\_mask}} was \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, in their
original relative order.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/floordiv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Floor division: computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor((*this) / other)}}, elementwise — always the
mathematical floor of the true (floating\sphinxhyphen{}point) quotient, not a truncation toward
zero. Follows {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s shared mechanics (positional matching,
length\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch throw, no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}payload support).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Floor, not truncation
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}} is defined as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(true\_divide(a, b))}}. For positive operands this
matches ordinary integer division; the distinction only shows up with negative
operands, which this reference deliberately avoids — the exact rounding convention
for negative divisors depends on the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} library and isn’t asserted
here.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/floordiv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The divisor(s). For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/floordiv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise floored quotient.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/floordiv:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amounts}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{floordiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

1  5
2  6
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(33 / 5) = floor(6.6) = 6}} — how many whole groups of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} fit into each amount.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/floordiv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the family\sphinxhyphen{}wide mechanics: positional matching and the

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fullmatch:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks each cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread against a regular expression, requiring
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} to match the \sphinxstylestrong{entire} cell’s text — not just a prefix, the way
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/matches::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}}}}}} does. Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fullmatch:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A regular expression (ECMAScript\sphinxhyphen{}flavored, via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/fullmatch:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the
elementwise full\sphinxhyphen{}match result.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ge:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

string overload stringifies numeric values before comparing lexicographically — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}} for a concrete example of why that can disagree with numeric
ordering.

\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/head:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} entries of the thread as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} — a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} subclass
(it inherits every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} method and renders identically via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}}) that
additionally carries a display title (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"head"}}) and an opt\sphinxhyphen{}in auto\sphinxhyphen{}render behavior
for interactive/terminal contexts. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is silently clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size(){]}}} —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} never throws for an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}, the same convention
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/top::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/bottom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bottom()}}}}}}} use.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
ThreadView is a Thread
Every method documented elsewhere in this reference — arithmetic, string ops,
reductions, everything — works directly on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} returned here, since it
publicly inherits from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} wrapper only adds a couple of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show()}} overloads and a distinct stream\sphinxhyphen{}insertion operator (which renders exactly
like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}’s own).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/head:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}})
Number of leading entries to keep. Values below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} clamp to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}; values above
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} clamp to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} — no error either way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the returned view may auto\sphinxhyphen{}render itself if it reaches the end of
its scope without being explicitly printed (a convenience for interactive/REPL
contexts). Has no effect on what an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} ...}} prints, which is
what every example on this page uses.

A view over the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} entries (or every entry, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \textgreater{}= size()}}).

\subparagraph{Thread::indicate}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate:thread-indicate}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{indicate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delimiter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{|}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Splits every cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delimiter}}, collects every distinct
non\sphinxhyphen{}empty token seen anywhere in the thread, and produces one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} column per
distinct token (“level”) — the classic one\sphinxhyphen{}hot / multi\sphinxhyphen{}label indicator (“dummy
variable”) encoding, for a text thread that holds delimiter\sphinxhyphen{}separated tags,
categories, or labels rather than a single value per cell. Requires the thread to be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. Column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\textless{}level\textgreater{}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for a row if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{level}} is one of that
row’s tokens, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} otherwise.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Levels are collected into a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::set\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, so the output columns always
appear in \sphinxstylestrong{sorted (alphabetical) order} — not first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order, and not any order
tied to the input data’s row sequence.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{danger}{Danger:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
indicate() never attaches a validity mask — invalid rows are just all\sphinxhyphen{}false, not NULL
Unlike every other method in this family, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}’s output columns carry \sphinxstylestrong{no
validity mask at all}. A row that was invalid on input doesn’t show \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the
indicator columns — it shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} in every one of them, exactly the same as a row
that’s genuinely valid but happens to match none of the levels. There is no way to
tell “this row is invalid” apart from “this row matched nothing” by looking at
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}’s output alone. See Example 1.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid row’s hidden text can still create a phantom output column
The set of levels is collected from \sphinxstylestrong{every row’s underlying text}, including rows
marked invalid — the delimiter split that builds the level set runs over the whole
thread before any validity check happens. An invalid cell whose hidden underlying
text contains a token no valid row ever uses still produces its own indicator column,
one that’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for every row in the entire result (since no valid row can ever
match it, and the invalid row itself is skipped when indicators are actually
computed). See Example 2 — this is the same category of surprise documented on
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}’s single\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter overload.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{delimiter} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"|"}})
The literal text to split each cell on before collecting tokens. Must not be
empty — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate("")}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::indicate: delimiter cannot be empty"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}})
Text prepended to each level to form its column name — with the default empty
prefix, a column is named exactly after the level text itself (e.g. a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"red"}}
token produces a column literally named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{red}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} feature per distinct non\sphinxhyphen{}empty token seen in the
thread, sorted alphabetically by token text, named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\textless{}level\textgreater{}}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output columns are sorted alphabetically by token text, not by first\sphinxhyphen{}appearance
order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No validity mask is attached to the result at all — invalid input rows show
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} everywhere, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. See the danger box above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The level set is collected from every row’s raw text regardless of validity, so an
invalid row can introduce an all\sphinxhyphen{}false phantom column. See the warning above and
Example 2.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delimiter}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::indicate: delimiter cannot be empty"}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/indicate:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::split}}}}}}}: the same underlying delimiter\sphinxhyphen{}split mechanic,
producing positional columns instead of one\sphinxhyphen{}hot level columns — and sharing the
same invalid\sphinxhyphen{}row\sphinxhyphen{}inflates\sphinxhyphen{}output quirk on its single\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::has}}}}}}}: test for a single specific substring instead of
enumerating every distinct delimited token.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/interp:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fills missing numeric values by \sphinxstylestrong{linear interpolation} between the nearest
valid value before and after each gap — unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}}}}}}/
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/bfill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}}}}}}}, which copy an edge value verbatim, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interp()}} computes a
value proportional to each missing position’s place within the gap. For a gap of
length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{g}} between a valid value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} at position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}} and a valid value
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} at position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p + g + 1}}, the missing entry at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p + k}} (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{g}}) becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left + (right \sphinxhyphen{} left) * (k / (g + 1))}} — an even linear ramp
between the two anchors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only \sphinxstylestrong{interior} gaps (bounded by a valid value on both sides) are filled. A
leading run of missing values (nothing valid before it) and a trailing run
(nothing valid after it) are left untouched — there’s no second anchor to
interpolate toward. Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads only; every other
kind throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/interp:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})
Maximum number of consecutive missing positions to fill per gap, counted from
the left anchor forward — the same convention as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ffill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means unlimited (fill the entire gap). Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}},
or it throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/interp:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread with eligible interior gaps interpolated. A thread with no
missing values, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit == 0}}, or an empty thread, is returned unchanged.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/interp:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interior gaps only — leading and trailing missing runs are never filled,
matching the “no anchor on one side” limitation of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ffill()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfill()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The interpolated value at a given position depends only on the gap’s two
anchors and that position’s place within the full gap — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} truncates
\sphinxstyleemphasis{how far} the fill reaches, not the values computed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}; anything else throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::interp: limit must be \sphinxhyphen{}1 or \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} only; any other payload kind throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::interp is only valid for numeric Series payload"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/invalid:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, marking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}
wherever a cell should be treated as unusable data. The exact meaning depends on
payload kind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, \sphinxstylestrong{or} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\(\pm\)Inf}} — the union of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} and the logical negation of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isfinite::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isfinite()}}}}}}}.
This is a strictly broader check than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} alone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Every other kind} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid()}} is exactly
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} — there’s no separate “not finite” concept for text or
temporal payloads, so the two checks coincide.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
invalid() is not isfinite()’s exact opposite for masked cells
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind threads, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isfinite::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isfinite()}}}}}}} are close to
opposites but computed slightly differently under the hood — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid()}} is built as
“not finite, or explicitly null,” which lands on the same result as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!isfinite()}}
for every practical case, but the two are documented separately here because they’re
implemented via genuinely different code paths, not simply negated from one another.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/invalid:parameters}}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/is_valid:what-it-does}}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}}}}}} check every position at once and

last element), and a thread with no validity mask attached at all is treated as
fully valid everywhere.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/is_valid:parameters}}

\sphinxstylestrong{row} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
The position to check. Negative values count from the end (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} is the last
row). Out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range values (after resolving negatives) throw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread: index out     of bounds"}}.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/isfinite:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, marking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}

valid (not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}). Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnan::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnan()}}}}}}}, which checks the numeric value alone, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isfinite()}} combines
the numeric check with the validity mask — a masked\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} here even
if its underlying stored value happens to be an ordinary finite number.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/isnan:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks the actual floating\sphinxhyphen{}point value — unaffected by, and independent of, the
validity mask that {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}} checks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A cell can be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} and still report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}, and vice versa (a
masked\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} value reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnan()}}).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::isnull}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/isnull:thread-isnull}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/isnull::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/isnull:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{isnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/isnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, marking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}
wherever the source thread is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} everywhere else. Works on every
payload kind — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — with no kind restriction,
unlike most of the payload\sphinxhyphen{}specific methods elsewhere in this API.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
isnull() checks the validity mask, not the numeric value
For a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} only looks at the thread’s validity mask — a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} value that’s still marked \sphinxstyleemphasis{valid} is reported \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}, not
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/isnan::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnan()}}}}}}} to check for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} specifically, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/invalid::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid()}}}}}}} to catch both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} and non\sphinxhyphen{}finite values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Inf}})
in one call. See Example 2.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} also folds in the payload’s own
internal validity signal (its own “not\sphinxhyphen{}a\sphinxhyphen{}time” sentinel), in addition to the
thread’s validity mask — so a timestamp that’s intrinsically invalid is reported as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} here even without an explicit mask entry.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isnan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/isnull:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadKind}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kind:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind}} enum value identifying which payload family a thread
currently stores: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (numeric/bool), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (text), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}. This is the typed enum form; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ptype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype()}}}}}}} returns the same
information as a human\sphinxhyphen{}readable string (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Series"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Note"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Timeline"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeIndex"}}) — use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind()}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{switch}}/comparison logic in C++ and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype()}} when
you just want to display or print the family name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every payload\sphinxhyphen{}kind\sphinxhyphen{}specific method (the string family, the temporal accessors, and
so on) checks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind()}} internally and throws when it doesn’t match — this is the
same check surfaced as, for example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::upper: expected Note payload"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}

One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind::Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind::Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind::Timeline}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind::TimeIndex}}.

\subparagraph{Thread::kurtosis}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:thread-kurtosis}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the sample excess kurtosis (bias\sphinxhyphen{}corrected) of every observed value in
a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread — a measure of tail weight relative to a normal
distribution: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for normal\sphinxhyphen{}like tails, positive for heavier (“fat”) tails,
negative for lighter tails. Rather than throwing on a too\sphinxhyphen{}small sample, this
method returns a result marked \sphinxstyleemphasis{invalid} whenever the observed count is below
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(4, min\_count)}} — kurtosis needs at least 4 observations regardless of
what you pass. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note}}}}} on why you should check
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}} rather than trust the printed number for an invalid
result.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If every observed value is identical (zero variance), the result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}
exactly, rather than the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infinity}} that dividing by a zero variance
would otherwise produce.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}})
The smallest observed count still considered valid. The effective floor is
always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(4, min\_count)}} — kurtosis needs at least 4 observations
regardless of what you pass here.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the sample excess
kurtosis.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A sample with a pronounced outlier — heavier tails than normal.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
4.27215
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Identical values produce exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flat}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kurtosis}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}valid}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
false
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The effective minimum observed count is always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(4, min\_count)}} — passing
a smaller \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} doesn’t lower the floor below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero variance (every observed value identical) yields \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} exactly, never
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Below the effective minimum count, the result is marked invalid rather than
thrown — see the caveat on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s page}}}}} about checking
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}} rather than trusting the printed number.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::kurtosis: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::label}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:thread-label}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadLabelAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Return the Thread label machinery for inspecting and manipulating 1D case labels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::label()}} is the 1D foundation for label handling. DataFrame label machinery is built above this because a DataFrame case axis is itself a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this surface for new code instead of reaching for lower\sphinxhyphen{}level case\sphinxhyphen{}label helpers directly:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().values()}} returns the current label values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().has()}} reports whether the thread is defined and can expose labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().set(labels)}} returns a copy with explicit labels attached.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().range()}} returns a copy with explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..n\sphinxhyphen{}1}} labels materialized.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().reset()}} returns a copy with explicit labels cleared.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().align(target, options)}} delegates to Thread alignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().unite(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intersect(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{symdiff(...)}} provide Index\sphinxhyphen{}style set operations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().find(targets)}} returns exact\sphinxhyphen{}match positions and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} for missing targets.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().pos(value)}} returns all matching positions for one label and throws when absent.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().slice(start, stop)}} returns an inclusive label\sphinxhyphen{}value slice.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().fillnull(...)}} returns a copy whose labels have missing values filled.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().isnull()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thread.label().notnull()}} inspect label missingness.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadLabelAccessor}}
Lightweight 1D label accessor bound to the source thread.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().values()}} returns default range labels when the thread has no explicit labels, matching the Pluss hybrid alignment model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().range()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().reset()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().align(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().fillnull(...)}} are non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating. They return new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().values()}} returns the frame’s case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread. Thread \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label()}} is where 1D relabeling and 1D label alignment live.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set operations preserve label payload dtype when the two label vectors are compatible: same Series dtype stays unchanged, mixed numeric Series labels upcast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}, Note labels stay Note, and Timeline/TimeIndex labels stay temporal. Incompatible mixed label payloads fall back to Note labels through comparable string keys.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/label:examples}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/land:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{land}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/land:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise logical AND. Unlike the arithmetic and comparison families, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} has
only one overload — there’s no scalar form, since a scalar boolean would just be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} applied uniformly, which reads more clearly as a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{if}}. Both
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} must be genuine \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} threads (not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}
numbers — cast first with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype(pluss::ScalarType::Bool)}} if needed), and must be
the same length; matching is purely positional.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
land() is the canonical logical\sphinxhyphen{}family reference
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor}} share this exact single\sphinxhyphen{}overload shape, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}only requirement,
and positional matching. Their own pages focus on what’s different about each
operator. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} for an important difference in how display labels
carry through the reflected forms of this family — genuinely different from the rest
of this reference’s reflected\sphinxhyphen{}method pairs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/land:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/land:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise
logical AND. Display labels (if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} has any set via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set()}}) carry
through onto the result.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/land:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matching is purely positional, the same as the arithmetic and comparison
families — there is no case\sphinxhyphen{}label alignment.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result’s display labels always come from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} (the object \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} was
called on), never from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/le:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise “less than or equal”, following {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s shared overload shape
and positional matching. Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}}, the string overload stringifies
numeric values before comparing — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt()}}}}}}} for why that can disagree with
numeric ordering.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/le:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/le:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise
“less than or equal” result.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/length:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{length}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/length:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread with its character count, as an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread — same row order, but the payload kind changes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}. Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts Unicode codepoints, not bytes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}} counts \sphinxstyleemphasis{characters} (Unicode codepoints), not raw UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 storage bytes.
For plain ASCII text the two are identical — but any character outside the ASCII
range (an accented letter, a currency symbol, an emoji) is encoded as more than one
byte in UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 while still counting as exactly one character.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/length:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/length:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}) thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding each
cell’s character count.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/length:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor::length}}}}}}} for the
multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature counterpart and a worked multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte\sphinxhyphen{}character example.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/log:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies the elementwise natural logarithm (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln}}). Requires the thread to be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. A non\sphinxhyphen{}floating scalar type (integer, bool) is promoted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}
before the logarithm is computed — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log()}} never throws on integer input purely for
being integer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Standard IEEE\sphinxhyphen{}754 domain behavior applies: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log(0.0)}} produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Inf}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log(negative)}} produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, rather than throwing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/log:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/log:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the natural log of
each element (promoted to a floating scalar type if the input was integral).

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{log}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/log:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integer/bool input is promoted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} automatically before computing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} cell on input stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} on output.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lower:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lowercases every character in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread’s cells — the classic
normalization step before a case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive comparison, a grouping key that
shouldn’t be split by casing accidents, or a lookup against a canonical lowercase
reference list. Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
ASCII vs. Unicode case mapping
On plain ASCII text, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} behaves exactly as you’d expect: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}} becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}}, everything else is untouched. Non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII case mapping depends on whether this
build links the optional Unicode backend (GNU libunistring).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lower:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lower:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with every character
lowercased; non\sphinxhyphen{}alphabetic characters (digits, punctuation, whitespace) are left
exactly as they were.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lower}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lower:output}}

1  tema

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise “less than”, following {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}’s shared overload shape and
positional matching. Unlike a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}} toggle you might expect from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/lt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::lt}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::lt()}} has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool strict}} parameter
at all — it’s always strict (use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/le::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le()}}}}}}} for the inclusive form).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The string overload compares text, not numbers
On a numeric thread, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt(std::string\_view)}} stringifies each value and does a plain
lexicographic string comparison against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} — it does \sphinxstylestrong{not} parse \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} as a
number. This can disagree sharply with numeric ordering: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"10"}} sorts \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"9"}}
lexicographically (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}1\textquotesingle{} \textless{} \textquotesingle{}9\textquotesingle{}}} as the first character), even though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 \textgreater{} 9}}
numerically. Example 3 below shows this concretely.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lt:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise
“less than” result.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{85.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numeric}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{9.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lexicographic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numeric}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lt:id2}}

1  false

Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lt("9")}} stringifies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{21.0}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"2"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"10"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"21"}} and

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lxor:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise logical XOR, following {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}’s shared mechanics: single
overload, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}only requirement, positional matching, and display labels carried
from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}. Unlike AND/OR, XOR reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} exactly where the two operands
\sphinxstylestrong{disagree}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lxor:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lxor:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise
logical XOR.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Bool}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lxor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/lxor:output}}

1  true

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

disagree, so XOR reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/matches:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks each cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread against a regular expression, replacing
each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}} is a \sphinxstylestrong{start\sphinxhyphen{}anchored search}, not a full\sphinxhyphen{}string
match: it reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} as soon as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} matches a \sphinxstyleemphasis{prefix} of the cell’s text
— anything left over after the match doesn’t matter. For a check that requires the
pattern to consume the entire string, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}}}}}}}. Requires the
thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/matches:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A regular expression (ECMAScript\sphinxhyphen{}flavored, via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex}}). Internally,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}} wraps it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciicircum{}(?:pattern)}} before searching.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/matches:returns}}

A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the
elementwise match result.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/matches:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A pattern matching only part of the string still counts as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{codes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SKU\PYGZhy{}1001}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SKU\PYGZhy{}42}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SKU\PYGZhy{}4}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{codes}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{matches}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SKU\PYGZhy{}[0\PYGZhy{}9]\PYGZob{}2\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/matches:output}}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"SKU\sphinxhyphen{}1001"}} matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} even though the pattern only asks for exactly two

\subparagraph{Thread::max}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max:thread-max}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the largest observed value in the thread, as a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} —
the mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}}}}}}, and just like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}, this works on
\sphinxstylestrong{every} payload kind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}}: the largest number.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind}: the alphabetically\sphinxhyphen{}last string.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}}: the latest timestamp.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing entries are excluded first (via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}} when a
validity mask is present). An empty thread, or one where every entry is
missing, throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — the examples
below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} for numeric results and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/temporal
results, rather than streaming the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar holding the largest observed value, in the source thread’s own
payload kind (a one\sphinxhyphen{}entry \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}).

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Largest value in a numeric thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/max:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Works on every payload kind — numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}, which are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing entries are excluded first, via the same mechanism as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty thread, or one where every entry is missing, throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::max on an empty (all\sphinxhyphen{}null) selection"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::mean}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:thread-mean}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the arithmetic mean of every observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing) value in a numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, as a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}. Missing entries are excluded before
the mean is computed — both from the sum and from the count used to divide it,
so a missing entry never drags the average toward zero. The computation is
carried out in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} on a non\sphinxhyphen{}CPU platform), regardless of
the source dtype, so an integer\sphinxhyphen{}dtype thread still produces a proper fractional
mean rather than a truncated integer result. Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads;
every other kind throws. An empty thread, or one where every entry is missing,
also throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — every example
below uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} to extract a clean number instead of streaming the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the mean of the observed
values.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Mean of a numeric thread with no missing entries.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
20
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mean:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always computed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (CPU) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} (off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU), regardless of the
source dtype — an integer thread’s mean is a proper fraction, not a truncated

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty thread, or one where every entry is missing, throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::mean on an empty (all\sphinxhyphen{}null) selection"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::mean is only valid for Series payload"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::median}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/median:thread-median}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/median::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/median:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{median}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/median:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the median of every observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing) value in a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
thread, as a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} — the middle value when the observed values
are sorted, less sensitive to outliers than {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}}. For an
even number of observed values, it’s the average of the two middle values
(the same linear\sphinxhyphen{}interpolation convention {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}’s}}}}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}}
quartile uses). Missing entries are excluded first, exactly like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}. The
computation is carried out in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU), regardless of
the source dtype. Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; every other kind throws. An
empty thread, or one where every entry is missing, also throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — every example
below uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} to extract a clean number instead of streaming the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/median:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/median:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the median of the
observed values.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/median:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{median}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

Example 2. Median of an even\sphinxhyphen{}length thread — the average of the two middle

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{9.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
