\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

source dtype.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::median is only valid for Series payload"}}.

\subparagraph{Thread::min}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min:thread-min}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the smallest observed value in the thread, as a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} —
and unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}}}}}}, this
works on \sphinxstylestrong{every} payload kind, not just numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}}: the smallest number.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind}: the alphabetically\sphinxhyphen{}first string.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}}: the earliest timestamp.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing entries are excluded first (via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}} when a
validity mask is present). An empty thread, or one where every entry is
missing, throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — the examples
below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} for numeric results and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/temporal
results, rather than streaming the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar holding the smallest observed value, in the source thread’s own
payload kind (a one\sphinxhyphen{}entry \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}).


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Smallest value in a numeric thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/min:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Works on every payload kind — numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}, which are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing entries are excluded first, via the same mechanism as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty thread, or one where every entry is missing, throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::min on an empty (all\sphinxhyphen{}null) selection"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::mod}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mod:thread-mod}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mod::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mod:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mod:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise remainder — the complement to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/floordiv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floordiv()}}}}}}}: for each
position, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{divisor * floordiv\_result + mod\_result}} reconstructs the original
dividend. Follows {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s shared mechanics (positional matching,
length\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch throw, no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}payload support).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Negative operands are deliberately not covered
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mod()}} delegates to the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} library’s own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{remainder()}} primitive,
which is not implemented in this repository — its exact sign convention for negative
dividends or divisors can’t be verified here. Every example on this page uses
positive operands only, where the convention is unambiguous.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mod:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The divisor(s). For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mod:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise remainder.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mod:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Remainder against a scalar divisor.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{amounts}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mod}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Thread::mode}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:thread-mode}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{drop\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns every value tied for the \sphinxstylestrong{most frequently observed} in the thread —
not just one. If several values are equally the most common, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode()}} returns
all of them, in ascending order (alphabetical for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, chronological for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}), rather than picking one arbitrarily. Works on numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} payloads.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls}} controls whether missing entries can compete for “most frequent”
at all:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}} (the default): missing entries never become part of the result,
no matter how many there are — only real, observed values compete.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}}: missing entries compete on equal footing with real values. If
“missing” turns out to be the single most frequent “value,” a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entry
is included in the result (appended after every tied real\sphinxhyphen{}value mode).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Throws if there are no values to consider at all (an empty thread, or one that
is entirely missing while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls = true}}).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{drop\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: missing entries are excluded from mode candidacy entirely.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: missing entries compete for “most frequent” like any other value.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread holding every value tied for most frequent, in ascending
order. Length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} if there’s a single mode, longer if there’s a tie.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:output}}

0  20

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}} occurs three times, more than any other value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. A tie returns every tied value, in ascending order.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tied}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tied}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

1  20

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}} occur twice; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30.0}} occurs once and doesn’t qualify.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mostly\PYGZus{}missing}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  10

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Three of the five entries are missing — more than any real value’s count — but
they’re excluded from competing at all, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}} (observed twice) wins.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls = false}} lets missing entries win, appearing as a

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Now missing (three occurrences) beats \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}}’s two, so the sole mode is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns every tied value, not just one — length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} only when there’s a
single unambiguous mode.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls = true}}, missing entries never compete, regardless of how
frequent they are.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_nulls = false}}, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entry appears in the result (after every
tied real\sphinxhyphen{}value mode) if missing is itself the single most frequent
“value.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::mode: no values"}} for an empty thread, or one with nothing
left to consider.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payload, restricted to numeric dtypes — a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::mode: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mode:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tally::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::tally}}}}}}}: the full frequency breakdown this method’s
“most frequent” answer is drawn from.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

single most frequent value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top}}) and its count (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}}) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode()}} returns
every tied top value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}} only the first alphabetically.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::median}}}}}}}: the middle value, a different measure of
central tendency for numeric data.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::mul}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:thread-mul}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mul}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mul}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise multiplication, following {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s shared mechanics. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mul()}}
has its own payload special case, parallel to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}concatenation
exception: multiplying a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread by a non\sphinxhyphen{}negative integral scalar
\sphinxstylestrong{repeats} each string that many times — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ab".mul(3.0)}} behaves like Python’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ab" * 3}}, giving \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ababab"}}. This only works for the scalar overload; there is no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}times\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} multiplication.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value(s) to multiply by. For a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} thread, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} must be a non\sphinxhyphen{}negative
integral value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.0}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.5}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread holding the elementwise product — or, for a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} thread multiplied
by a scalar, each string repeated that many times.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Multiply every value by a scalar.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mul}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  20
1  40
2  60

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Multiply two threads positionally.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boost}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mul}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{boost}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/mul:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  20
1  80
2  150
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ndistinct:what-it-does}}

Returns the number of distinct values in the thread, as a scalar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}. This is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distinct(dropnull).size()}} wrapped as a scalar
— the same grouping rule (each value’s string form) and the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull}}

differs (a count instead of the values themselves).

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — streaming the
result directly (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} out}}) prints its full diagnostic form, not a
bare number; both examples below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}} for a clean integer instead.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ndistinct:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing entries don’t count toward the distinct
total.
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a missing entry counts as one additional distinct “value” (all

individually).

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/normalize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies Unicode text normalization to every cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread,
choosing one of the four standard Unicode Normalization Forms via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{form}}. Requires
the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{enum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// Canonical Decomposition, followed by Canonical Composition}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// Canonical Decomposition}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFKC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// Compatibility Decomposition, followed by Canonical Composition}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFKD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// Compatibility Decomposition}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalization matters for text that might contain the same visible character
represented in more than one way — most commonly, a precomposed accented letter (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{é}}
as a single codepoint) versus a base letter plus a combining mark (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e}} + a combining
acute accent, two codepoints that render identically). Two byte\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}byte\sphinxhyphen{}different
strings can look identical and still compare unequal with a plain {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}};
running both through the same normalization form first makes such comparisons
consistent.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the optional Unicode backend (GNU libunistring) for anything beyond plain ASCII
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize()}}’s real behavior depends entirely on whether this build links
libunistring:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{With the backend}: all four forms are fully implemented via the standard
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uninorm\_normalize}} routine, correctly handling precomposed and decomposed Unicode
text.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Without the backend}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize()}} still accepts pure\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII input — and, since
plain ASCII has no combining marks, ligatures, or compatibility characters to
normalize in the first place, every form behaves as an identity transform and
returns the input unchanged (see Example 1). But any \sphinxstylestrong{non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII} input throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Note::normalize: non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII text requires a Unicode backend"}} — there is no
partial or best\sphinxhyphen{}effort fallback for non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII text.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Confirm this build’s Unicode support before relying on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize()}} for any text
that might contain non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII characters.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/normalize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{form} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnicodeForm}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnicodeForm::NFC}})
Which normalization form to apply: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFC}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFD}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFKC}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFKD}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/normalize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the normalized text.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/normalize:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Plain ASCII text under the default form (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFC}}) — a no\sphinxhyphen{}op, since ASCII has
nothing to normalize, and this behavior holds regardless of whether this build links
the Unicode backend.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Hello World}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ASCII text only}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output (before, identical to output after)}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/normalize:output-before-identical-to-output-after}}

0  Hello World
1  ASCII text only

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

The output is byte\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}byte identical to the input: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFC}} (like every other form, on
ASCII) has nothing to canonicalize when there are no combining marks or compatibility
characters present. The invalid third row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Explicitly requesting each of the four forms on the same ASCII input — all
four produce the identical result, since the distinctions between NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD
only matter for text containing decomposable or compatibility characters, none of
which plain ASCII has.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFD}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfkc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFKC}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfkd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFKD}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+c1}{// nfc, nfd, nfkc, and nfkd are all identical to titles here.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/normalize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All four \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnicodeForm}} values are identity transforms on pure ASCII text, with or
without the Unicode backend.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII input throws outright when this build lacks libunistring — there is no
partial fallback. See the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pad:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grows every cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread up to a target character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} by
adding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} characters, positioning the original text according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}.
Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{enum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{TextAlign}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Left}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Right}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Center}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Left}}} (the default): the original text is left\sphinxhyphen{}aligned — fill
characters are added on the \sphinxstylestrong{right}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Right}}}: the original text is right\sphinxhyphen{}aligned — fill characters are
added on the \sphinxstylestrong{left}. The classic use is zero\sphinxhyphen{}padding numeric\sphinxhyphen{}looking codes
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"7"}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"0007"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Center}}}: fill is split between both sides. When the amount needed is
odd, the \sphinxstylestrong{extra} fill character goes on the right (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left = needed / 2}}, integer
division; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = needed \sphinxhyphen{} left}}).

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
pad() only ever grows a cell, never shrinks it
If a cell is already at least \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} characters long, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad()}} leaves it completely
unchanged — there’s no truncation mode. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} is measured in Unicode codepoints,
the same unit {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}} counts.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pad:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{width} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
The target character width. Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad(\sphinxhyphen{}1)}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::pad:     width must be \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{align} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Left}})
Where the fill characters go: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}} pads on the right, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}} pads on the left,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Center}} splits the fill (extra character on the right for an odd amount).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fill} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{} \textquotesingle{}}})
The single character used to pad. Note this is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, not a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} — multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 fill sequences aren’t supported.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pad:returns}}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the padded text (or
left unchanged, for cells already at or beyond \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}}).

\subparagraph{Output (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Center}})}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pad:output-textalign-center}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  ..A...
1  ..BB..
2  .CCCC.
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"A"}} (1 character) needs 5 fill characters to reach width 6: all 5 on the right
under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}}, all 5 on the left under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}}, and split 2\sphinxhyphen{}left/3\sphinxhyphen{}right under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Center}}
(the odd character goes right). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"BB"}} needs 4 (split evenly, 2/2, since 4 is even).
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"CCCC"}} needs only 2 (split 1/1). Row 3 was invalid on input and stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} under
every alignment — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad()}} never manufactures text for an invalid cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. The practical, real\sphinxhyphen{}world use of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}} alignment: zero\sphinxhyphen{}padding
numeric\sphinxhyphen{}looking codes to a fixed width.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{zero\PYGZus{}padded}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ids}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{pad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TextAlign}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Right}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{0}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pad:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad()}} only grows; a cell already at or beyond \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} is returned unchanged,
never truncated.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} is measured in Unicode codepoints, the same unit {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}}
counts.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} is a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, not a string — no multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 fill characters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Center}}’s extra fill character (when the amount needed is odd) always goes on the
right.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width \textless{} 0}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::pad: width must be \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::partition}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/partition:thread-partition}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/partition::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/partition:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{separator}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{part}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/partition:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Splits every cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} occurrence of a literal
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}, always producing exactly \sphinxstylestrong{three} output columns: the text before the
separator, the separator itself, and the text after it. Requires the thread to be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. It’s a narrower, simpler cousin of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}} — always
literal (no regex), always stops at the first match, and always exactly three columns
regardless of the input.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing separator produces empty strings, not NULL
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}} doesn’t occur in a cell at all, that row’s middle and third columns
are set to the \sphinxstylestrong{empty string} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — the row itself is still valid, it
simply had nothing to split. This is a meaningfully different behavior from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}, where a row that produced fewer pieces than the widest row gets
genuine \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s in the missing columns. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition()}}’s validity for all three output
columns is copied directly from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{original row’s own validity} — a valid input row
is valid in all three output columns even when the separator wasn’t found; only a row
that was already invalid on input produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in all three. See Example 1.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/partition:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{separator} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The literal text to split on. Must not be empty — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition("")}} throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::partition: separator cannot be empty"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}})
Base name for the three output columns: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}} (before), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_1}} (the
separator, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}} if not found), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_2}} (after, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}} if not found).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/partition:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with exactly three features: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_2}}.

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{entries}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/partition:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always literal (no regex mode) and always stops at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} occurrence — for a
regex\sphinxhyphen{}aware or multi\sphinxhyphen{}way split, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always produces exactly three output columns, regardless of the input.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing separator yields empty strings in the second and third columns, not
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — see the important callout above. Only a row that was already invalid on
input produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in any of the three columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::partition: separator cannot be empty"}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/percentiles:thread-percentiles}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/percentiles::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/percentiles:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/percentiles:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the value at each requested fractional position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}} = minimum,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} = maximum, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}} = median) among the thread’s observed values, using the
same linear\sphinxhyphen{}interpolation\sphinxhyphen{}between\sphinxhyphen{}ranks convention as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}’s}}}}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25\%}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{50\%}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75\%}} rows and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}}}}}}. Missing entries are dropped first (via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/dropnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull()}}}}}}}). Returns a new thread — one entry per requested
point, in the order given — rather than a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}, so the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}} point (for example) computes exactly the same value
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}}}}}} would.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If there are no observed values at all (or fewer than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}), every
requested point comes back \sphinxstylestrong{missing} rather than throwing — the underlying
storage is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, but it’s marked invalid, so it renders and inspects as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}
like any other missing entry.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/percentiles:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{points} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}double\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0.25, 0.5, 0.75\}}})
The fractional positions to evaluate, each in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1{]}}}. Must be
non\sphinxhyphen{}empty, or it throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
The smallest number of observed values still considered valid. Below it,
every requested point comes back missing rather than throwing.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/percentiles:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, one entry per requested point (in the order given), holding
the interpolated value at each fractional position.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/percentiles:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}} point always matches {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/median::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{median()}}}}}}} exactly, and every
point matches the corresponding quartile row in
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/describe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}}}}}} when it happens to request \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.25}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.75}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No observed values (or a count below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}) produces a fully\sphinxhyphen{}missing
result, not a thrown error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{points}} must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty and every value in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1{]}}}, or it throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::percentiles: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pow:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise exponentiation, computed via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::pow}} after promoting both operands to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}. Follows {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}’s shared mechanics (positional matching,
length\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch throw, no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}payload support). This reference sticks to positive
bases and small exponents throughout — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::pow}}’s behavior for negative bases with
fractional exponents (which can produce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}) isn’t exercised here.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pow:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exponent(s). For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/pow:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise power.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/prod:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the product of every observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing) value in a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
thread, as a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} — the multiplicative counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}}. Missing entries are excluded before the product is computed,
not treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}. Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; every other kind throws. A
thread whose every entry is missing (or that is empty) also throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — streaming the
result directly prints its diagnostic form, not a bare number; use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}}
(as every example below does) for a clean scalar.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/prod:parameters}}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}

(or its promoted equivalent).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the broad payload family as a display string: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Series"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Note"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Timeline"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeIndex"}} — the same information {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/kind::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind()}}}}}}} returns as
a typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind}} enum, formatted for printing. This is the 1D analog of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ptypes()}}, which reports the same family names per feature.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ptype:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ptype:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Series"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Note"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Timeline"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeIndex"}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ptype:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype()}} is for dispatching or displaying by payload \sphinxstyleemphasis{family}. Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/dtype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype()}}}}}}} when you need the concrete storage detail within that
family (e.g. which numeric scalar type a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread holds).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ptype()}} on an undefined thread throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread: undefined handle"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/put:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes replacement values into positions selected by a boolean mask.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/put:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bool\_mask}
Boolean row mask. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} keeps or rewrites the corresponding row, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} leaves it out or leaves the original value unchanged depending on the method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value}
Replacement, fill, or write value used by mutation\sphinxhyphen{}style methods such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{put(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(...)}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(...)}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/put:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
Value produced by this call.

\subparagraph{Thread::radd}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}

\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{radd}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/radd:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}. For numbers, addition is commutative, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} produce identical results in every observable way. The
distinction only matters for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) threads, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} means
concatenation and concatenation order depends on which operand comes first —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}} reverses that order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/radd:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/radd:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
For numbers, identical to what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} would produce for the same arguments. For
two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} threads, the concatenation with the operand order reversed.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/radd:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{radd}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reflected}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{radd}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{base\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{forward}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reflected}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/radd:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For numeric threads, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}} exists purely for API symmetry with the rest of the
reflected family (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rmul}}, and so on) — there is no behavioral reason to
prefer it over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the shared mechanics every arithmetic method in this
family follows: positional matching, the length\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch throw, and the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}concatenation special case.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:thread-rand}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rand}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}. Logical AND is commutative, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} always compute the \sphinxstylestrong{same boolean values}. The display labels on the
result are a different story:

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
rand()’s result labels come from other, not from *this
Unlike the arithmetic family (where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radd()}} reuses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}’s exact metadata rules)
and unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::rand()}} (which always carries labels from the object it was
called on, matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} exactly), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::rand()}} is implemented as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} with the two operands swapped internally — which means the display labels
on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}’s result come from \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}}, not from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}. This is a real,
observable difference from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}, not just an API\sphinxhyphen{}symmetry alias.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed thread holding the same values {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}} would
produce for the same arguments — but with display labels carried from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}
instead of from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Same values as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}, but the row labels come from the other side.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Bool}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{                }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{p}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{q}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{r}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Bool}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{                 }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{forward}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{land}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reflected}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rand}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{forward}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reflected}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
p  true
q  false
r  false

ptype: Series
x  true
y  false
z  false

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The boolean values are identical in both outputs (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true, false, false}}) — only the
row labels differ: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}}’s labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p, q, r}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}} shows
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x, y, z}}), because internally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left.rand(right)}} computes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}\sphinxhyphen{}AND\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} supplying the metadata.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rand:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If neither thread has display labels set, this distinction is invisible — both
methods fall back to the same default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0, 1, 2, ...}} row index either way.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This label\sphinxhyphen{}carry difference is specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}; the equivalent
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::rand}}}}}}} was fixed in an earlier revision to
always carry metadata from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}} exactly. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::rand()}}
has no such fix — treat this page’s behavior as the current, verified source
truth rather than assuming symmetry with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} version.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::rank}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:thread-rank}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{RankTieRule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ties}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RankTieRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Average}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Keep}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{percentage}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assigns a numeric rank (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} = smallest, by default) to every entry, based on
its value relative to the rest of the thread. Ties — entries with equal
value — are resolved by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ties}}, and missing entries are handled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls}}.
Always returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) thread the same length as the
source, regardless of the source’s own dtype, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentage}}
ranks are inherently fractional. Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; every
other kind or dtype throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ties}} controls what rank a group of equal values receives:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}}} (the default): every tied entry gets the mean of the rank
positions the group spans (e.g. a 2\sphinxhyphen{}way tie for ranks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}\textendash{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} gives both
entries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.5}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lowest}}}: every tied entry gets the group’s lowest rank position.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Highest}}}: every tied entry gets the group’s highest rank position.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{First}}}: ties are broken by original order — the earlier\sphinxhyphen{}occurring entry
gets the lower rank number, so no two entries ever tie.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dense}}}: like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lowest}}, but the next distinct value’s rank always follows
immediately after (no rank numbers are skipped for the size of a tie group).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls}} controls what happens to missing entries:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Keep}}} (the default): missing entries are excluded from ranking
entirely, and their own output position is missing too.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Top}}}: missing entries participate in ranking and are treated as the
smallest (or largest, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending = false}}) possible value, so they receive
the lowest ranks. Every position gets a real (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing) rank.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bottom}}}: the mirror of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Top}} — missing entries rank last. Every
position gets a real rank.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ties} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankTieRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}})
How equal\sphinxhyphen{}valued entries share rank numbers: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lowest}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Highest}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{First}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dense}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RankNullRule}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Keep}})
How missing entries are handled: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Keep}} (exclude, stays missing), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Top}}
(ranks first), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bottom}} (ranks last).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} ranks the smallest value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} reverses it so the largest
value is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{percentage} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, divides every rank by the number of ranked entries, producing
a fraction in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0, 1{]}}} instead of a raw rank number.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) thread of ranks, the same length as the
source.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default ranking — smallest value gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, ties average their
rank positions.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  1.5
1  1.5
2  3.5
3  3.5

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}}s share ranks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}\textendash{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} (averaging to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.5}}); both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}}s share ranks
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}\textendash{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} (averaging to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.5}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ties = RankTieRule::First}} breaks ties by original order instead
of averaging — no two entries ever tie.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{RankTieRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{First}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  1
1  2
2  3
3  4

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}} (position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}) gets rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}; the second (position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}) gets
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} — purely by which one appeared first in the thread.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ties = RankTieRule::Dense}} doesn’t skip rank numbers for the size
of a tie group.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{RankTieRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Dense}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  1
1  1
2  2
3  2

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compare to Example 1: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Average}} jumped from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}} group (ranks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}\textendash{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}})
straight to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.5}} for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}} group; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dense}} instead moves to rank \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}
immediately, since it’s simply “the next distinct value” rather than “the next
unused rank position.”

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls = RankNullRule::Keep}} (the default) excludes missing entries
from ranking — they stay missing in the output too.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  1
1  NULL
2  2

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 5. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls = RankNullRule::Top}} gives the missing entry a real rank —
the lowest one, since it’s treated as smaller than every observed value.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{RankTieRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Average}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Top}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out5}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:id4}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  2
1  1
2  3

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every position now has a real rank — position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (the missing entry) ranks
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, ahead of both observed values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 6. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentage = true}} divides every rank by the total ranked count.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{clean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out6}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{clean}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{RankTieRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Average}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RankNullRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Keep}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out6}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:id5}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  0.25
1  0.5
2  0.75
3  1

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rank:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}}, regardless of the source dtype — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}}
through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} (or a fraction of that range with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentage = true}}), not
necessarily whole numbers once \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ties = Average}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{percentage = true}} is in
play.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls = Keep}} is the only mode where the output can itself contain missing
entries; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Top}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bottom}} always produce a fully\sphinxhyphen{}valid rank thread.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::rank: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sort\_values}}}}}}}: reorder by value directly, rather
