\subparagraph{Thread::rdiv}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:thread-rdiv}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rdiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rdiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}. Division is not commutative, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rdiv()}}
computes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other / (*this)}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(*this) / other}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread holding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other / (*this)}}, elementwise.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Divide a scalar by every value.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rdiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  0.4
1  0.2
2  0.1333333333

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4 / 10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4 / 20}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4 / 30}} — the opposite of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prices.div(4.0)}}}}}}}, which
would give \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.5, 5, 7.5}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Reflected against another thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{splits}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{9.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rdiv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{splits}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  0.4
1  0.4
2  0.3

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prices.rdiv(splits)}} computes exactly what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{splits.div(prices)}} would: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4 / 10}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{8 / 20}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9 / 30}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prices.rdiv(x)}} always equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x / prices}} — the mirror image of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}, not a synonym for it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the family\sphinxhyphen{}wide shared mechanics.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rdiv:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::div}}}}}}}: the forward form.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/rtruediv::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::rtruediv}}}}}}}: the always\sphinxhyphen{}floating\sphinxhyphen{}point reflected counterpart.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::repeated}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:thread-repeated}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{repeated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a boolean thread, the same length as the source, marking \sphinxstylestrong{every}
entry whose value occurs more than once — including the occurrence that
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}} would leave unmarked as the “survivor.” Where
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}} answers “which entries are extra copies to drop,” \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}}
answers “which entries belong to a repeated group at all.” For values \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}A, B, A, C, B{]}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}} marks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}true, true, true, false, true{]}}} — both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}}s and
both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}}s are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}} (unique) is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} — whereas \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}} with the
default policy would mark only the second \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} and second \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}false, false, true, false, true{]}}}).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, same length as the source, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} at every position
whose value occurs more than once anywhere in the thread.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Mark every member of a repeated value’s group.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Kumasi}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{repeated}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  true
1  true
2  true
3  false
4  true

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Accra"}} occurrences (positions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) and both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}} occurrences
(positions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}) are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Kumasi"}} (unique) is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grouping is by each value’s string form, matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/distinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distinct()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tally::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally()}}}}}}};
works across every payload kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Marks the whole repeated group, unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}, which leaves one
designated survivor per group unmarked.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/repeated:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::duplicated}}}}}}}: mark only the \sphinxstyleemphasis{extra} occurrences
under a keep\sphinxhyphen{}first/keep\sphinxhyphen{}last policy, leaving one survivor per group unmarked.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/distinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::distinct}}}}}}}: the deduplicated values themselves.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::filter}}}}}}}: apply the mask this method returns to
actually select the repeated rows.

\end{itemize}



\sphinxstepscope

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} covers two conceptually different operations that happen to share a name:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Text substring/regex replace} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to)}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to, TextOptions)}} — replaces occurrences of a substring or regex
pattern \sphinxstyleemphasis{within} each cell’s text. Requires a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread. This is the same
operation family as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}} and the rest of the string/text methods.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Whole\sphinxhyphen{}value replace} — every other overload — replaces cells whose \sphinxstylestrong{entire
value} exactly equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}, the way a lookup\sphinxhyphen{}table substitution works.
The C++ type of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} determines which payload kind participates: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}
pairs with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Note}} pairs with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind
thread (matching the \sphinxstylestrong{whole cell’s text}, not a substring), and scalar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::TimeIndex}} pair with temporal threads. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}}
scalar\sphinxhyphen{}wrapper overloads are typed convenience forms that unwrap to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}
overload; passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::null\_t}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} fills nulls (equivalent to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull()}}}}}}}), and passing it for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} nullifies matching cells.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{danger}{Danger:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
replace(Note, Note) is whole\sphinxhyphen{}cell exact match, not substring replace
It is easy to reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} on a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} thread and land on the wrong overload.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace("Tema", "Tamale")}} (two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} arguments) replaces the
\sphinxstylestrong{substring} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}} wherever it occurs inside each cell — a cell like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema West"}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tamale West"}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(pluss::make\_note(\{"Tema"\}), pluss::make\_note(\{"Tamale"\}))}} (two scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Note}} arguments) instead requires
the \sphinxstylestrong{entire cell} to equal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}} exactly — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema West"}} is left completely
unchanged, since it isn’t \sphinxstyleemphasis{equal to} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Tema"}}, only \sphinxstyleemphasis{contains} it. See Example 6 for
both side by side on the same data.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
replace(from, to) and replace(from, to, \{\}) are byte\sphinxhyphen{}identical
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} is left at its default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_sensitive = true}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = \sphinxhyphen{}1}}), the three\sphinxhyphen{}argument text overload takes a fast path straight to the
same underlying primitive the two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload uses. There is no behavioral
difference between the two spellings.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{from} / \sphinxstylestrong{to}
The value(s) participating in the replacement. Their C++ type selects which
overload (and which payload kind) applies — see What It Does above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, text overload only)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} as a regular expression instead
of literal text; supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$2}}, … backreferences in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, matching ignores case
(ASCII fold), but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} is inserted exactly as given. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}} (default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}): caps the number of replacements per cell; matches never overlap.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} is not used by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length and kind as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} (except a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to = pluss::null\_t}}
result, which nullifies matching cells rather than changing their kind).


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. The default text overload: literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive, unlimited
substring replacement.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cat and cat}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Cat there}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{no match}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{replace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cat}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{dog}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (before)}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:output-before}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  cat and cat
1  Cat there
2  no match
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  dog and dog
1  Cat there
2  no match
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both occurrences of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cat"}} in row 0 are replaced. Row 1’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Cat"}} (capital C)
doesn’t match the lowercase, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cat"}} needle, so it’s left untouched.
Row 3 is invalid and stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_sensitive = false}}: matching ignores case, but the replacement text
is still inserted literally as given.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cities}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{replace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cat}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{dog}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}sensitive}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  dog and dog
1  dog there
2  no match
3  NULL

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row 1’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Cat"}} now matches too (case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively) and is replaced with the literal
lowercase \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"dog"}} — the original capitalization of the matched text is discarded, not
preserved or transferred to the replacement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} caps replacements per cell, and matches never overlap.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{banana}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{aardvark}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{xyz}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{replace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{X}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  bXnXna
1  XXrdvark
2  xyz

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"banana"}} has three \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}s, but only the first two are replaced (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = 2}}), leaving
the trailing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"na"}} untouched. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"aardvark"}} has two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}s \sphinxstyleemphasis{adjacent} to each other at
the start — both get replaced, reaching the limit before the third \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} (inside
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"vark"}}) is ever considered. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"xyz"}} has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} at all, so it’s unchanged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. Regex mode with backreferences: swap the two sides of an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} using capture
groups.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/replace:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two unrelated operations share the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} name — substring/regex replace on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} text, and whole\sphinxhyphen{}value exact\sphinxhyphen{}match replace across any payload kind. See the
danger box above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to, \{\})}} (the text overloads) are the exact
same operation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Whole\sphinxhyphen{}value replace requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} scalar wrapper objects (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{numel() == 1}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size() == 1}}) — a multi\sphinxhyphen{}element \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Note}}/etc. throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(Timeline, Timeline)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(TimeIndex, TimeIndex)}} both accept
either a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}\sphinxhyphen{} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind calling thread — symmetric on both sides.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(null\_t, to)}} is equivalent to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull(to)}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, null\_t)}} nullifies cells matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} rather than changing the
thread’s kind.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/fillnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::fillnull}}}}}}}: fill nulls with a value directly — what

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor(100 / 33) = floor(3.03) = 3}} — how many whole \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{amounts}}\sphinxhyphen{}worth fit into a

The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}}}}}}. Logical OR is commutative, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ror()}} and

explanation and a worked example of this label\sphinxhyphen{}carry difference.

\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lor()}}}}}}}.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ror:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}

display labels carried from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/round:what-it-does}}

number). Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decimals != 0}}, the
implementation scales up by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10\textasciicircum{}decimals}}, rounds to the nearest whole number, then
scales back down — the same multiply/round/divide approach most numeric libraries
use for decimal rounding.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rxor:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rxor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rxor:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The reflected form of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}}. Logical XOR is commutative, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rxor()}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}} always compute the same boolean values — but, exactly like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} versus {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/land::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rxor()}}’s result carries display
labels from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead of from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/rand::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rand()}}}}}}} for the full
explanation and a worked example of this label\sphinxhyphen{}carry difference.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rxor:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/rxor:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
The same values {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lxor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lxor()}}}}}}} would produce for the same arguments, with
display labels carried from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sample:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a random subset of entries. There are two ways to size the draw — a count
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}) or a fraction of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}}, rounded to the nearest integer count) —
and each has a plain form (a fresh, non\sphinxhyphen{}reproducible random seed every call) and an
explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} form (reproducible on a given build — see the important
callout below).
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace}}} (the default): each position can be drawn at most once.
Requesting more than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} doesn’t throw — the draw silently caps at
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}, so you get every entry back (in shuffled order), never a repeat.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}}: positions can repeat, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}} may exceed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} freely — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac \textgreater{} 1.0}} is only accepted when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}, otherwise
it throws.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
random\_state reproduces results on a given build, not across toolchains
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample()}}’s underlying randomness comes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}} combined with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}} (without replacement) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::uniform\_int\_distribution}} (with
replacement). The C++ standard fixes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{statistical properties} of these
facilities but not their exact bit\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}bit algorithm, so the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}}
reliably reproduces the same draw \sphinxstyleemphasis{within one build} (same compiler, same standard
library), but is not guaranteed to reproduce the identical draw across different
compilers or standard library implementations. The example outputs below reflect
one particular build and are illustrative of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{shape} of the result, not a
cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform guarantee of the exact indices drawn.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sample:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Number of entries to draw. Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}. Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace}}, capped silently
at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{frac} (floating\sphinxhyphen{}point)
Fraction of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} to draw, rounded to the nearest integer count. Must be
finite and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}. A value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{} 1.0}} requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{random\_state} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::uint64\_t}}, optional)
Seed for the random number generator. Omitted (or the no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}}
overload) draws a fresh, non\sphinxhyphen{}reproducible seed each call via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{replace} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
Whether a position can be drawn more than once.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sample:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread holding the drawn entries, length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} (or the rounded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac *     size()}}, capped as described above when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = false}}).


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sample:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sample}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sample:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::sample: frac \PYGZgt{} 1 requires replace = true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sample:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace}}, a draw larger than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} caps at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} silently — never
throws, never duplicates.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac}} may exceed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} freely, and repeats are possible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frac \textgreater{} 1.0}} requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace = true}}, or it throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::sample: frac \textgreater{} 1 requires replace = true"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \textless{} 0}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::sample: n must be \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The overloads without an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} draw a fresh seed via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}} every call — never reproducible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the important callout above regarding cross\sphinxhyphen{}build reproducibility of a given
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::scan}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:thread-scan}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{scan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ScanStatistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statistic}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skip\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes a \sphinxstylestrong{running} (cumulative) statistic down the thread — the value at
each position reflects every observed entry up to and including it, not just
that position alone. {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/cumsum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/cumprod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/cummin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/cummax::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}}}}}} are thin wrappers around
this method for each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic}}; this page documents the shared mechanics
all four rely on. Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; every other kind or
dtype throws.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
the throw message always says “Thread::scan”
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}} each delegate straight to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan(...)}}, passing the literal string \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::scan"}} as the error context —
so calling any of the four wrapper methods on a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric thread throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::scan: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}, not a message naming
the specific method you actually called.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally, missing entries are first replaced with the operation’s
\sphinxstylestrong{identity element} before the running computation runs — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}
for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Product}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+\(\infty\)}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\(\infty\)}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}} — so a missing entry
never resets or corrupts the running value for the positions after it. What
happens to \sphinxstyleemphasis{that position’s own} output value is then controlled separately by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls = true}}} (the default): each output position’s validity
mirrors its \sphinxstyleemphasis{own} input position — a position that was missing in the input
stays missing in the output, but the running computation for every
\sphinxstylestrong{later} position still correctly includes whatever value came before it
(accumulated through the identity\sphinxhyphen{}substituted missing spot).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls = false}}}: once any position is missing, \sphinxstylestrong{every position
after it} becomes missing too — the missing entry “poisons” the running
computation forward, even though the identity\sphinxhyphen{}substituted arithmetic
underneath is still technically well\sphinxhyphen{}defined. This matches the common
spreadsheet/pandas convention that a running total is undefined once a gap
appears in the input, unless you explicitly ask to skip past it.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScanStatistic}})
Which running computation to perform: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Product}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{skip\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: a missing input position stays missing in the output, but later
positions’ running values are unaffected. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: a missing input
position makes every subsequent output position missing too.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A thread the same length as the source, holding the running statistic at
each position.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Running sum with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls = true}} (the default) — the missing
position stays missing, but the run continues correctly underneath it.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ScanStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Sum}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  10
1  NULL
2  40
3  80

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (missing) is hidden as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, but position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}’s running sum is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{40}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 + 30}}, correctly skipping the missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}}), and position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}’s is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{80}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 + 30 + 40}}) — the gap doesn’t reset or break the running total for
what follows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. The same input with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls = false}} — the missing position
poisons every position after it.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ScanStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Sum}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  10
1  NULL
2  NULL
3  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} (there was nothing to sum there), but now
positions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} are also \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — even though their underlying running
totals are the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{40}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{80}} computed in Example 1, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls = false}}
suppresses them because a gap appeared earlier in the run.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{catch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{exception}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{what}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/scan:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing entries are substituted with the operation’s identity element before
the running computation runs, so later positions’ values are always
arithmetically correct underneath — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls}} only controls which
positions are \sphinxstyleemphasis{displayed} as missing, not what gets computed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skip\_nulls = false}} propagates missingness forward from the first gap
onward, matching the common “undefined once a gap appears” convention.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::scan: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}} — this exact message,
regardless of whether you call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} directly or through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumsum()}}
/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cumprod()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummin()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cummax()}}.

\end{itemize}

fixed\sphinxhyphen{}statistic wrappers around this method.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/prod::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::prod}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::min}}}}}}},

\subparagraph{Thread::se}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se:thread-se}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{se}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ErrorTarget}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ErrorTarget}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the standard error of the mean — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(variance / count)}}, using the
same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}\sphinxhyphen{}adjusted variance {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var(options)}}}}}}} computes. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target}}
exists to select \sphinxstyleemphasis{what} the standard error is computed for, but only
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget::Mean}} is currently implemented; passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget::Median}}
throws rather than silently computing something else. Like the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}} overload of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}, this method returns a result marked
\sphinxstyleemphasis{invalid} (rather than throwing) when the observed count is below
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note}}}}} on why you should check
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}} rather than trust the printed number in that case.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})
Which statistic’s standard error to compute. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}} is currently
implemented; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Median}} throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the same divisor adjustment \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}} use.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the smallest observed count still considered
valid; below it, the result is marked invalid rather than thrown.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the standard error of
the mean.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Standard error of the mean, default options.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{se}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/se:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
1.29099
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(var() / count)}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(6.66667 / 4)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ErrorTarget::Median}} throws — it isn’t implemented.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shape:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{size(), 1\}}} — a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}\sphinxhyphen{}shaped view of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}’s dimensions, where a
thread is always exactly one “column” wide. This exists purely for API symmetry with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::shape()}} (which returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{nrows, nfeatures\}}}); the second element is
always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and carries no information \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} doesn’t already give directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shape:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shape:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::pair\textless{}std::int64\_t, std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{size(), 1\}}}.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shape:examples}}

\subparagraph{Thread::shares\_payload\_with}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:thread-shares-payload-with}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{shares\PYGZus{}payload\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{noexcept}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} objects point at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{exact same} underlying payload
storage — a pointer\sphinxhyphen{}identity check on the internal reference\sphinxhyphen{}counted handle, not a
value\sphinxhyphen{}equality check. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} uses copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write: copying a thread (via the copy
constructor or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator=}}) is cheap and initially shares storage with the original;
the first mutating operation on either copy clones the storage before writing, so the
two threads stop sharing from that point on. Every purely functional method (the vast
majority of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}’s API, which returns a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} rather than mutating in
place) never causes sharing between its input and its output — sharing only ever
comes from copying the same handle.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is not eq() or ==
Two threads holding identical values but built independently (e.g. two separate
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread(pluss::make\_series(\{1.0, 2.0\}))}} calls) are \sphinxstylestrong{not} sharing payload — they’re
distinct storage that happens to hold equal data. Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}} to compare
values.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})
The thread to compare storage identity against.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} currently point at the same backing storage;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} otherwise.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A freshly copied thread shares payload with its source.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{original}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{copy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{original}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{boolalpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{original}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shares\PYGZus{}payload\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{copy}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Two threads built independently from equal\sphinxhyphen{}looking data never share,
even though they’d compare equal with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{boolalpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shares\PYGZus{}payload\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
false
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. A thread never shares payload with itself in the trivial sense of being
compared post\sphinxhyphen{}mutation — mutating a copy detaches it from the original (copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{base}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{shared\PYGZus{}copy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{base}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{boolalpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{base}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shares\PYGZus{}payload\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{shared\PYGZus{}copy}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{shared\PYGZus{}copy}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{boolalpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{base}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shares\PYGZus{}payload\PYGZus{}with}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{shared\PYGZus{}copy}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

false
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before the mutating \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull\_()}} call, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shared\_copy}} still point at the
same storage. Calling the mutating method on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shared\_copy}} clones its storage first
(copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write), so afterward the two threads no longer share anything — and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}}
itself is left completely untouched by the mutation.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shares_payload_with:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pointer\sphinxhyphen{}identity on internal storage, not value equality — see the note above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{noexcept}}: never throws, even comparing against an undefined thread.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copying a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (copy constructor or copy\sphinxhyphen{}assignment) is what creates sharing;
every purely functional transform method returns freshly built storage instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The first mutating (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_}}\sphinxhyphen{}suffixed) call on either a shared thread or its copy
detaches that one from the shared storage; the other side is unaffected.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::shift}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:thread-shift}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shifts every value forward (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textgreater{} 0}}) or backward (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textless{} 0}}) by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} positions, keeping the thread the same length — positions that shift in
from beyond either edge become \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, and values shifted past the opposite edge
are dropped entirely (not wrapped around). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 0}} (or an empty thread) is a
no\sphinxhyphen{}op, returning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} unchanged.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
Number of positions to shift. Positive shifts values to later positions
(introducing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s at the start); negative shifts values to earlier positions
(introducing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s at the end).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with values shifted and the vacated
positions set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A positive shift moves values later; the leading positions become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  10
2  20
3  30

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{40.0}} (the last value) is dropped entirely — shifted past the end, not wrapped
back to the front.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. A negative shift moves values earlier; the trailing positions become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:id2}}

1  20
2  30

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}null}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out4}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  1
2  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} comes from row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s already\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} value moving into that
position, not from the shift itself vacating it.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shift:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values shifted past either edge are dropped, not wrapped around.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Vacated positions (and any already\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} positions that moved) are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in
the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 0}}, or shifting an empty thread, returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Works on every payload kind, not just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::shuffle}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:thread-shuffle}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{uint64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new thread with every entry in a random order — the same entries as the
original, just permuted. Internally this builds the index range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size())}},
seeds a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::mt19937\_64}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} (or from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}} if
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} is omitted), calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}}, and takes the result — so it’s
equivalent to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample(size(), random\_state, false)}}}}}}} but reads more
directly at the call site when you just want “reorder everything,” rather than
“draw a subset.”

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
random\_state reproduces results on a given build, not across toolchains
As with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shuffle()}} uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::shuffle}}, whose exact
output for a given seed is not fixed by the C++ standard — only its statistical
properties are. The same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} reliably reproduces the same permutation
\sphinxstyleemphasis{within one build} (same compiler, same standard library), but different
toolchains may legitimately produce a different permutation for the same seed. The
example output below reflects one particular build.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{random\_state} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::uint64\_t\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Seed for the random number generator. Omitted (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}}) draws a fresh,
non\sphinxhyphen{}reproducible seed each call via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::random\_device}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread of the same length and kind, with entries reordered.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Shuffle with a fixed seed, reproducible on this build.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{50.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (illustrative — see the important callout above)}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:output-illustrative-see-the-important-callout-above}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  40
1  10
2  50
3  20
4  30

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same five values, same length, just reordered — every original value appears
exactly once.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Two calls with the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} produce the same permutation on
a given build.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{99}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{99}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{a}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{b}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
1
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Omitting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} draws a fresh seed each call — two calls are
not guaranteed to (and in practice essentially never do) match.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{c}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shuffle}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+c1}{// c and d are each some permutation of \PYGZob{}10, 20, 30, 40, 50\PYGZcb{}, independently drawn}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample(size(), random\_state, false)}}, but expresses intent more
directly for “reorder everything” use.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same length and kind as the original; no entries are dropped or duplicated.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the important callout above regarding cross\sphinxhyphen{}build reproducibility of a given
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/shuffle:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sample}}}}}}}: draw a random subset (or the whole thread,

\subparagraph{Thread::size}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:thread-size}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the number of elements (rows) in the thread — the one dimension a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
has, regardless of payload kind. This is the same count {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shape::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shape()}}}}}}} reports
as its first element and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ncases::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}}}}}}} returns under a different name.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}
The element count. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for an empty (but still defined) thread.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A thread’s size is independent of payload kind.

\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{words}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:output}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} counts every element, including \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} ones — it’s not a
non\sphinxhyphen{}null count.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}nulls}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:id1}}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/size:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts every element, valid or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/count::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}}}}}} for a
non\sphinxhyphen{}null\sphinxhyphen{}only count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} on an undefined thread throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread: undefined handle"}} — see
