\subparagraph{Thread::skew}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:thread-skew}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the sample skewness (the adjusted Fisher\sphinxhyphen{}Pearson standardized third
moment) of every observed value in a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread — a measure of
asymmetry: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for a symmetric distribution, positive for a right\sphinxhyphen{}leaning tail,
negative for a left\sphinxhyphen{}leaning tail. Rather than throwing on a too\sphinxhyphen{}small sample,
this method returns a result marked \sphinxstyleemphasis{invalid} whenever the observed count is
below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(3, min\_count)}} — skewness is undefined below 3 observations, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} can only raise that floor, never lower it. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note}}}}} on why you should check \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}}
rather than trust the printed number for an invalid result.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If every observed value is identical (zero variance), the result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}
exactly, rather than the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infinity}} that dividing by a zero standard
deviation would otherwise produce.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}})
The smallest observed count still considered valid. The effective floor is
always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(3, min\_count)}} — skewness needs at least 3 observations
regardless of what you pass here.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the sample skewness.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A right\sphinxhyphen{}skewed sample — a small cluster of low values plus one
large outlier.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
2.0287
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Identical values produce exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flat}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Fewer than 3 observed values marks the result invalid rather than
throwing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{skew}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}valid}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
false
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/skew:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The effective minimum observed count is always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max(3, min\_count)}} — passing
a smaller \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} doesn’t lower the floor below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Zero variance (every observed value identical) yields \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} exactly, never
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Below the effective minimum count, the result is marked invalid rather than
thrown — see the caveat on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s page}}}}} about checking
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.thread().is\_valid(0)}} rather than trusting the printed number.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::skew: expected a real numeric Series Thread"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::slice}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:thread-slice}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stop}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a contiguous \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} slice as a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} —
compare {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/view::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}}}}}}}, which wraps this exact operation in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}}).
Python\sphinxhyphen{}slice semantics throughout: negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} count from the end, both
are clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size(){]}}}, and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} at or before the resolved \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}
produces an empty (not erroring) result. Internally implemented as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(\{start, start+1, ..., stop\sphinxhyphen{}1\})}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Inclusive starting position. Negative values count from the end.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Exclusive ending position. Negative values count from the end.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread over positions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}}, clamped into range.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A plain forward slice.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{50.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  20
1  30
2  40

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Negative indices count from the end.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  40
1  50

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. An inverted range (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop \textless{}= start}} after resolving negatives) is an
empty result, not an error.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/slice:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} count from the end (Python\sphinxhyphen{}slice convention).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both bounds are clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size(){]}}} — never throws for out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range
values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An inverted or empty resulting range produces a valid, zero\sphinxhyphen{}length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::sort\_values}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values:thread-sort-values}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nulls\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new thread with every entry reordered by value — the payload kind is
unchanged, only the order changes. The comparison key depends on what the thread
holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}}: sorted numerically. If there’s no validity mask, this is a
single stable argsort (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{descending = !ascending}}) followed by a
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}}}}}}}. If there \sphinxstyleemphasis{is} a validity mask, valid and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} positions
are argsorted separately (only the valid subset is compared), then concatenated
in the order \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}} dictates.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}}: sorted by epoch\sphinxhyphen{}nanosecond value via a stable sort,
with the same null\sphinxhyphen{}grouping logic applied.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, or a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}}: sorted lexicographically by string
key (each entry’s string form), with the same null\sphinxhyphen{}grouping logic applied.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In every case the sort is \sphinxstylestrong{stable} — entries that compare equal keep their
original relative order — and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entries are grouped to one end according to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}} rather than being compared to real values at all. A thread with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size() \textless{}= 1}} returns unchanged immediately.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} sorts smallest/earliest/alphabetically\sphinxhyphen{}first values first; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
reverses the comparison.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} places every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entry after all valid entries, regardless of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} places them before all valid entries instead.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sort_values:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always stable, across every payload kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entries are never compared against real values — they’re grouped
wholesale to one end per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size() \textless{}= 1}} short\sphinxhyphen{}circuits to the thread unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Backs both {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/top::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/bottom::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bottom()}}}}}}}, which take a prefix of
a descending or ascending \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values()}} call respectively.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/split:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Splits every cell of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread on a delimiter, expanding the result into
one output column per split position — column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part\_0}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}}) holds each
row’s first piece, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part\_1}} its second, and so on. Requires the thread to be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. There are two overloads with different delimiter semantics:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split(delimiter, limit, prefix)}}}: always a literal substring split (never
regex), with an optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} on how many splits to perform and a customizable
column\sphinxhyphen{}name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split(pattern, options)}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} is literal or regex depending on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}} caps the split count and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} names the
columns (the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}} struct used across the string/text family — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/replace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}}}}}}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both overloads produce ragged results: a row with fewer pieces than the widest row is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the extra columns, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} caps the number of splits performed (a split
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a/b/c"}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = 1}} yields two pieces, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}"a", "b/c"{]}}} — the remainder after
the capped split stays joined, it isn’t dropped further).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two overloads compute the output column count differently for invalid rows
The single\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter overload (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split(delimiter, limit, prefix)}}) determines the
output column count from \sphinxstylestrong{every} row’s underlying text — including rows marked
invalid — because it works from a raw, validity\sphinxhyphen{}unaware split computed once over the
whole thread. An invalid cell whose underlying stored text happens to contain many
delimiters can inflate the column count even though that row shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every one
of them. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(pattern, options)}} overload does not have this quirk: it only computes
each row’s split (and therefore only contributes to the column count) for rows that
are actually valid. See Example 4 for a side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side demonstration with identical data
under both overloads.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/split:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{delimiter} / \sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The literal delimiter (first overload) or literal/regex pattern (second overload,
depending on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}) to split on. An empty delimiter throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::split: delimiter cannot be empty"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, first overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})
Maximum number of splits to perform (producing at most \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit + 1}} pieces); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}
means unlimited.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, first overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}})
Base name for the output columns: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_1}}, …

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, second overload)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} as regex. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}}
(default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}): cap the number of splits. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}}):
base name for output columns. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} is \sphinxstylestrong{not} used by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/split:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_1}}, … feature per split position (as
many as the widest split needs). Rows with fewer pieces are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the extra
columns.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/split:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the calling thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty delimiter/pattern throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::split: delimiter cannot be empty"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} caps the \sphinxstyleemphasis{number of splits}, not the \sphinxstyleemphasis{number of output columns} directly —
the capped remainder stays joined in the last piece (Example 2).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two overloads compute the output width differently for invalid rows — see the
warning above and Example 4.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} has no effect on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}.

\end{itemize}

\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{starts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/starts:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread’s cells for a literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive prefix match,
replacing each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell’s text begins with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t. The payload kind changes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}). Requires the thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts()}} has exactly one overload and takes no options — always a plain,
case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive, literal check. There’s no regex mode; use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/matches::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}}}}}}
with a pattern anchored at the start for anything more flexible.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/starts:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The literal text to check for at the start of each cell. An empty prefix matches
every non\sphinxhyphen{}null cell.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/starts:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the
elementwise prefix check.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/std:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the standard deviation of every observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing) value in a
numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread — the square root of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}}’s result, with
the exact same overload split and failure\sphinxhyphen{}mode difference:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std(unbiased)}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = true}} (the default) computes the sample
standard deviation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} divisor underneath); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = false}} computes
the population standard deviation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} divisor). An empty thread, or one
where every entry is missing, \sphinxstylestrong{throws}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std(options)}}}: takes a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions\{ddof, min\_count\}}}. Instead of
throwing on an insufficient sample, this overload returns a result marked
\sphinxstyleemphasis{invalid} (see the important caveat below) when the observed count is below
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — every example
below uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} for a clean number, and the note there also covers the
“invalid \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} still prints a number” trap that Example 4 below runs
into.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/std:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unbiased} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: sample standard deviation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} divisor underneath). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}:
population standard deviation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} divisor underneath).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the divisor underneath is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} ddof}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}
(default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the smallest observed count still considered valid; below
it, the result is marked invalid rather than thrown.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/std:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the standard deviation.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/strip:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Trims characters from both ends of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread’s cells. Requires the
thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind. Two distinct trimming policies:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload}: trims the classic ASCII whitespace set — space, tab,
newline, carriage return, form feed, vertical tab — from both ends of each cell.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} overload}: trims by \sphinxstylestrong{character\sphinxhyphen{}set membership}, not by matching
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} as a literal prefix/suffix substring. Every leading character that appears
anywhere in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} is removed, one at a time, until a character not in the set is
reached; the same happens independently from the trailing end — the same
convention Python’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{str.strip(chars)}} uses.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/strip:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{chars} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}}\sphinxhyphen{}overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The set of characters to strip from each cell’s edges. Order doesn’t matter.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/strip:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with each cell’s text trimmed.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/strip:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. The default overload trims ASCII whitespace from both ends.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{skus}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{  SKU\PYGZhy{}1001}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}t}\PYG{l+s}{SKU\PYGZhy{}1002}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SKU\PYGZhy{}1003   }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sub}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sub}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sub:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise subtraction, following the same shared mechanics documented on
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}: the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} overload subtracts the same scalar from every value;
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload subtracts positionally and requires matching lengths.
Subtraction is not commutative, so — unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub()}} and its reflected form
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/rsub::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsub()}}}}}}} genuinely produce different results, even for plain numbers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}, there is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}payload special case for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sub()}} — subtracting one
string thread from another always throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sub:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value(s) to subtract. For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sub:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise difference.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sub:examples}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sub}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Thread::sum}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sum:thread-sum}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sum:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sum:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the sum of every observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing) value in a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
thread, as a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}. Missing entries are excluded before the sum
is computed, not treated as zero. Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; every other
kind throws, since “sum” has no defined meaning for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
data. A thread whose every entry is missing (or that is empty) also throws —
there is no meaningful sum of zero observations to return.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
printing a ThreadValue directly
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} wraps a one\sphinxhyphen{}element payload (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} here). Streaming it
directly — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} result}} — does \sphinxstylestrong{not} print a clean bare number: it
prints the full diagnostic form of the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}}, including its
shape, dtype, platform, and contiguity metadata ahead of the data. Example 2
below shows the raw form for reference, once, so you know what to expect if
you ever do stream a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To pull out a plain host\sphinxhyphen{}language scalar instead, reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} — but each of those commits you to a specific
native C++ type, so you need to already know (or assume) what the underlying
scalar is before calling one. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.host()}} sidesteps that: it returns a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue::HostAny}}, a small tagged union that already knows its own kind
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UInt}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Double}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{String}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Time}}), and streaming \sphinxstyleemphasis{it} —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} result.host()}} — prints a clean scalar with no cast or
type\sphinxhyphen{}picking required up front. Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.host()}} when you just want to
print or forward the value without committing to a type; reach for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} when you specifically need the value as
that native C++ type (e.g. to do further arithmetic on it). Every example on
this page (and across the rest of the reduction methods) uses one of those
four — see Example 3 below for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.host()}} specifically.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A related trap: some statistical methods (for example the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}}
overloads of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/var::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/std::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/se::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{se()}}}}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/skew::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skew()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/kurtosis::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kurtosis()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/corr_with::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_with()}}}}}}})
return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} marked \sphinxstyleemphasis{invalid} instead of throwing when there isn’t
enough data — but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_int()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_str()}} still hand back whatever
number the underlying arithmetic produced, with no indication it’s actually
meaningless. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} printing has no concept of
nullness at all — only the wrapping \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}’s own validity mask does. Check
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.thread().is\_valid(0)}} before trusting a result from one of those
methods.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sum:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sum:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar wrapping the sum, in the source \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}’s own numeric dtype (or
its promoted equivalent, following the same numeric promotion rules as the
underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series::sum()}}).


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/sum:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Sum a numeric thread, extracting a clean scalar with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; anything else throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::sum is only valid for Series payload"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the callout above for how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} prints — use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} (or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.host()}} if you don’t want to commit to a native type) for a clean
numeric result.

Returns the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} entries of the thread as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} — see

Number of trailing entries to keep. Clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size(){]}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

A view over the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} entries (or every entry, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \textgreater{}= size()}}), in their
original order.

\subparagraph{Thread::take}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/take:thread-take}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/take::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/take:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{take}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{span}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indices}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/take:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the entries at the given positions, in the order \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indices}} specifies —
positions may repeat and don’t need to be sorted, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}} can reorder,
duplicate, or subset in one call. Every kind\sphinxhyphen{}specific payload path
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) resolves indices the same way: negative
values count from the end, and an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range index (after resolving negatives)
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread: index out of bounds"}}. Both {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/filter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter()}}}}}}} are implemented as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take()}} calls with a computed index
list.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/take:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{indices} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::span\textless{}const std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}})
The positions to select, in the order they should appear in the result.
Repeats are allowed. Negative values count from the end; any index still
out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range after that resolution throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/take:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indices.size()}}, holding the selected entries in the
requested order.

\subparagraph{Thread::tally}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/tally:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/tally:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts how often each distinct value occurs and returns the counts as a small
two\sphinxhyphen{}column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}} (the distinct value, as text) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"count"}}
(an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} occurrence count) — sorted by count descending, with ties broken
alphabetically by the value’s own text. Every value’s string form (via the same
scalar\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}string conversion used across the library, so this works on any
payload kind, not just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}) becomes its grouping key.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the value\sphinxhyphen{}first counting tool for one thread: it answers “what are the
most common values in this column,” rather than “how many distinct values are
there” (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/ndistinct::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ndistinct()}}}}}}} for a plain count without the
per\sphinxhyphen{}value breakdown). {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/freq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::freq()}}}}}}} is built on top
of this method for the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature case.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/tally:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{top\_n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})
Keep only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} most frequent rows after sorting. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (the default)
keeps every distinct value observed. Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}}, or it throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} (the default): missing entries are excluded from the count
entirely — they contribute no row.
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: missing entries are grouped under the literal key \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} and
counted like any other value, competing for sort order and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} the
same as a real value would.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s parameter description — auto\sphinxhyphen{}render\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}scope\sphinxhyphen{}exit
only; has no effect on what an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} ...}} prints, since
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}} renders identically to a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/tally:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}
A two\sphinxhyphen{}feature frame — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"count"}} — with one row per distinct
value (subject to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}}), sorted most\sphinxhyphen{}frequent first and alphabetically on
ties.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/tally:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorting is always most\sphinxhyphen{}frequent first; ties break by ascending alphabetical
order of the value’s text, never by first\sphinxhyphen{}appearance order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n = 0}} keeps every distinct value; a positive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} truncates after
sorting, so it always keeps the most frequent entries. A negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}}
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::tally: top\_n must be \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}}, the literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} is just another candidate
key — it can tie, sort, and be truncated by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} like any real value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Works on every payload kind, since grouping is done by each value’s string
form, not by numeric equality.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Thread::titlecase}

\subparagraph{Signature}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/titlecase:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Capitalizes the first letter of every “word” in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread’s cells and
lowercases the rest — the classic display\sphinxhyphen{}formatting transform for names,
addresses, or titles typed in all\sphinxhyphen{}lowercase or inconsistent casing. Requires the
thread to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Word\sphinxhyphen{}boundary detection resets on \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} non\sphinxhyphen{}alphanumeric character
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{titlecase()}} decides where a new “word” starts the same way Python’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{str.title()}}
does: a word boundary is any position right after a non\sphinxhyphen{}alphanumeric character
(space, hyphen, apostrophe, digit\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}letter transitions — anything that isn’t a
letter or digit), not just whitespace. This means an apostrophe inside a contraction
resets the boundary too, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"don\textquotesingle{}t"}} titlecases to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Don\textquotesingle{}T"}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Don\textquotesingle{}t"}} — see
Example 2. This is a well\sphinxhyphen{}known quirk of this style of word\sphinxhyphen{}boundary detection, not
a bug specific to this implementation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/titlecase:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/titlecase:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with every cell’s text
title\sphinxhyphen{}cased.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/titlecase:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. The common case: clean, space\sphinxhyphen{}separated words title\sphinxhyphen{}case exactly as
expected.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{places}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{accra central market}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{east legon}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{north kaneshie}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{places}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{titlecase}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/titlecase:output}}

1  East Legon
2  North Kaneshie

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. The word\sphinxhyphen{}boundary quirk in action: apostrophes and hyphens reset the
“start of a word” detector.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{phrases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{don\PYGZsq{}t stop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{rock \PYGZsq{}n\PYGZsq{} roll}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{co\PYGZhy{}op bank}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{phrases}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{titlecase}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/titlecase:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  Don\PYGZsq{}T Stop
1  Rock \PYGZsq{}N\PYGZsq{} Roll
2  Co\PYGZhy{}Op Bank

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"don\textquotesingle{}t"}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Don\textquotesingle{}T"}}: the apostrophe is a non\sphinxhyphen{}alphanumeric character, so the
letter right after it (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t}}) is treated as the start of a new “word” and capitalized.
The same thing happens to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} between the two apostrophes in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"rock \textquotesingle{}n\textquotesingle{} roll"}},
and to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{o}} right after the hyphen in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"co\sphinxhyphen{}op"}}. There is no built\sphinxhyphen{}in way to make
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{titlecase()}} treat apostrophes or hyphens as internal\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}a\sphinxhyphen{}word — post\sphinxhyphen{}process the
result with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/replace::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}}}}}}} for known quirks that matter for a given
column.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/titlecase:notes}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Word\sphinxhyphen{}boundary detection resets on \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} non\sphinxhyphen{}alphanumeric character, not just
whitespace — see the warning above.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/truediv:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Elementwise division that always promotes to floating point first — internally,
both operands are converted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} and divided via the library’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true\_divide()}} primitive, regardless of what numeric type the source thread holds.
This is a stricter guarantee than {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/div::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}}}}}}, which delegates to the raw
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series::div()}} algebra and may not promote integer types the same way. For the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}}\sphinxhyphen{}typed examples used throughout this reference, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truediv()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{div()}}
produce identical results.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/truediv:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The divisor(s). For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, must be the same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/truediv:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, holding the elementwise quotient.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/truediv:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Divide every value by a scalar.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{truediv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/truediv:output}}

1  5
2  7.5

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{splits}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{9.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Signature}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TimeSeriesAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enters the dedicated time\sphinxhyphen{}series\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{numerics} accessor for this thread — period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}
period returns, differencing, lag/lead, rolling and expanding windows, exponentially\sphinxhyphen{}
weighted statistics, gap filling, resampling, and axis\sphinxhyphen{}aligned arithmetic, one method
per operation. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}}}}}}} (which requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} payloads),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} requires the thread to already be a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — cast it first with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/astype::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{astype()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/cast::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cast()}}}}}}} if it isn’t.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}}}}}}}, this overload takes no options — there’s
no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor}} concept for a single thread outside a frame, and duration\sphinxhyphen{}based
methods that need an explicit time axis (like the duration overload of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}})
simply take that axis as a direct argument instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page previews the accessor’s most common entry points. Every one of its methods
has its own dedicated, example\sphinxhyphen{}rich reference page — start at the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{TimeSeriesAccessor API Reference}}}}}} and use its
left sidebar to jump straight to any method (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expanding}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ewm}}, and more).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeSeriesAccessor}}
A lightweight accessor bound to this (numeric) thread. Every method on it returns a
new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeSeriesResample}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} for the block/resample methods);
the source thread is never mutated.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute a lag and a period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period difference on a numeric thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{15.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lagged}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lagged}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  10
2  20
3  15

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.lag(1)}} is equivalent to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift(1)}}}}}}}: each position now shows the previous
position’s value, with position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} becoming \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} since it has no predecessor.

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{changes}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:id1}}

1  10
2  \PYGZhy{}5
3  15

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
TimeSeriesAccessor::lag: source must be Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The check happens lazily, on the first method call against the accessor — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}}
itself never throws, since it just binds the thread without inspecting it.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The source thread must already be a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}; every accessor method throws
otherwise (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} itself doesn’t validate eagerly).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.lag(periods)}} on a numeric thread behaves identically to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift(periods)}}}}}}}
— both introduce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} at the vacated end.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions}} parameter here, unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}}}}}}}
— duration\sphinxhyphen{}aware methods take their time axis directly as an argument instead.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/ts:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::shift}}}}}}}: the lower\sphinxhyphen{}level positional shift \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts().lag()}} is built
on, without the time\sphinxhyphen{}series\sphinxhyphen{}accessor framing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::tl}}}}}}}: the equivalent dedicated accessor for calendar/timestamp
components on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} payloads, instead of numeric time\sphinxhyphen{}series values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/weigh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::weigh}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/bounded::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::bounded}}}}}}}: lower\sphinxhyphen{}level windowing

\subparagraph{Thread::upper}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper:thread-upper}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uppercases every character in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (string) thread’s cells — the mirror image
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}. Common uses include normalizing free\sphinxhyphen{}typed codes or
abbreviations before comparing or grouping by them. Requires the thread to be
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
ASCII vs. Unicode case mapping
Exactly the same caveat as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}: ASCII \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}} mapping is always
available; correct handling of accented or non\sphinxhyphen{}Latin uppercase mapping depends on
whether this build links the optional Unicode backend.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind thread, same length as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, with every character
uppercased; non\sphinxhyphen{}alphabetic characters are left exactly as they were.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Uppercase a text thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{codes}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{gh\PYGZhy{}001}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Gh\PYGZhy{}002}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{GH\PYGZhy{}003}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{codes}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{upper}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/upper:output}}

0  GH\PYGZhy{}001
1  GH\PYGZhy{}002
2  GH\PYGZhy{}003

ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"gh"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Gh"}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"GH"}} all normalize to the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"GH"}} — the hyphen and digits
are untouched throughout, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{upper()}} only ever changes letters.

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{catch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{exception}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{msg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{what}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\subparagraph{Thread::value}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/value:thread-value}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/value::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/value:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/value:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wraps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} — a lightweight box around a whole \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} that
adds typed scalar\sphinxhyphen{}extraction helpers (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_dbl()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_int()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_str()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{host()}})
and implicit conversions to the underlying payload types (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Series}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::TimeIndex}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value()}} itself does \sphinxstylestrong{not}
reduce or require a single\sphinxhyphen{}element thread — it wraps the thread as\sphinxhyphen{}is, at whatever
length it already has. The reduction methods ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}}}}}}, and the rest) also return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}, typically already
length\sphinxhyphen{}1 after their own reduction; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value()}} is the direct way to get the same box
type around a thread you already have, without any reduction step.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Scalar accessors require exactly one element
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_dbl()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_int()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_str()}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{host()}} all check that the wrapped thread has
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size() == 1}}, throwing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ThreadValue::host: Thread payload must contain exactly one value"}} otherwise. Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.value()}} on a multi\sphinxhyphen{}element thread is legal; calling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} on the result of that isn’t. See Example 3.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/value:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/value:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A box around \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}}, same length and kind as the source thread.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/value:examples}}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boxed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{single}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{boxed}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dbl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}

\subparagraph{Thread::var}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/var:thread-var}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/var::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/var:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unbiased}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{var}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ThreadValue}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/var:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the variance of every observed (non\sphinxhyphen{}missing) value in a numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread, as a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}. There are two overloads, and they
handle an insufficient sample differently:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var(unbiased)}}}: the simple form. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = true}} (the default)
computes the \sphinxstylestrong{sample} variance (dividing by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}, Bessel’s correction);
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = false}} computes the \sphinxstylestrong{population} variance (dividing by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}).
An empty thread, or one where every entry is missing, \sphinxstylestrong{throws}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{var(options)}}}: the general form, taking a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions\{ddof, min\_count\}}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (delta degrees of freedom) generalizes the divisor to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} ddof}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} matches
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = false}}, and any other non\sphinxhyphen{}negative value is accepted too.
Instead of throwing when the observed count is too small, this overload
\sphinxstylestrong{returns a missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) result} if the observed count is below
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (and always below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof + 1}}, since a divisor of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or less
would be undefined).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::sum}}’s note on printing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}}}}}} — every example
below uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_dbl()}} for a clean number instead of streaming the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}} directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/var:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unbiased} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: sample variance (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} divisor). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: population variance
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} divisor).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StatisticOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the divisor is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} ddof}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} (default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): the smallest observed count still considered valid; below it, the
result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} rather than a thrown error.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/var:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}
A scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float64}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Float32}} off\sphinxhyphen{}CPU) holding the variance.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/var:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}\sphinxhyphen{}form returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} instead of throwing —
choose whichever failure mode fits your code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}\sphinxhyphen{}form’s default) matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = true}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 0}} matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unbiased = false}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/view:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns an arbitrary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} positional window as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}} — the
general form {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}}}}}} are anchored special cases of.
Delegates directly to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/slice::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice()}}}}}}} internally, so it shares that method’s
Python\sphinxhyphen{}style negative\sphinxhyphen{}index and clamping behavior: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} support negative
indices (counted from the end), both are clamped into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, size(){]}}}, and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}
that ends up before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} produces an empty (not erroring) result.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/view:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Inclusive starting position. Negative values count from the end.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Exclusive ending position. Negative values count from the end.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{render} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}’s parameter description — auto\sphinxhyphen{}render\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}scope\sphinxhyphen{}exit
only.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/view:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}}
A view over positions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}}, clamped into range.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread/view:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A plain forward window.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{view}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
