\subparagraph{Thread::weigh}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:thread-weigh}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Thread API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{weigh}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{weights}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes a \sphinxstylestrong{weighted trailing window} statistic over the thread — like a
fixed\sphinxhyphen{}width rolling window, but instead of every position in the window
counting equally, each contributes according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights}}. The window width is
implicitly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights{[}0{]}}} applies to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{oldest} position in
each window and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.back()}} applies to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{most recent} (current)
position — the natural left\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}right reading order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Near the start of the thread, where a full window isn’t yet available, the
missing leading positions are treated as absent (contributing zero weight)
rather than zero\sphinxhyphen{}valued — so early rows still compute a properly normalized
weighted average over however many real positions are actually available,
they just do so over a \sphinxstyleemphasis{smaller} effective window. Missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) entries
within a window are excluded the same way.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
weights are ignored for Minimum/Maximum
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic::Minimum}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic::Maximum}}, the actual
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights}} \sphinxstyleemphasis{values} don’t affect the result at all — only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}}
does, since “weighted minimum/maximum” isn’t a well\sphinxhyphen{}defined idea. These two
statistics fall back to a plain (unweighted) rolling min/max over a window the
same width as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{weights} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}double\textgreater{}}})
The per\sphinxhyphen{}position weights, oldest to newest. Implicitly sets the window
width to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}}. Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty, or it throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})
Which statistic to compute inside each weighted window: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}} ignore the
weight values — see the note above).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
The smallest number of observed (weighted\sphinxhyphen{}eligible) positions in a window
still considered valid. Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{} 0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}= weights.size()}}, or it
throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread the same length as the source, holding the weighted
statistic at each position.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A weighted moving average — later (more recent) positions in each
window count for more.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{40.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{50.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{weigh}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  10
1  16
2  23.33333333
3  33.33333333
4  43.33333333

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} onward has a full 3\sphinxhyphen{}wide window (weights \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1, 2, 3}} applied to the
oldest, middle, and newest of the three values respectively): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10*1 + 20*2 + 30*3) / (1+2+3) = 140/6 ≈ 23.333}}. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} has only itself available (the
two leading window slots don’t exist yet), so it’s weighted only by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} (the
weight for “most recent”), normalizing to exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} has two
real values, weighted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} (the window’s last two weights): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10*2 + 20*3) / (2+3) = 80/5 = 16}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} can require a fuller window before a position counts as
valid.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{weigh}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  NULL
2  23.33333333
3  33.33333333
4  43.33333333

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 3}} (the full window width), positions \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} — which
only had \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} real values available, respectively — are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}} reports the weighted total directly, without normalizing by
the weight total.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{weigh}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Sum}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  30
1  80
2  140
3  200
4  260

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These are the same weighted sums computed for Example 1’s means — just not
divided by the weight total (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} for a full window).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread/weigh:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights{[}0{]}}} applies to the oldest position in each window, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.back()}}
to the most recent — the window width is always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Near the start of the thread, unavailable leading positions contribute zero
weight (not a zero value), so early results are still properly normalized
weighted averages over a smaller effective window.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}} ignore the actual weight values — see the important note
above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights}} must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty, or it throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::weigh: weights cannot be empty"}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} must be in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0, weights.size(){]}}}, or it throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::weigh: invalid min\_count"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads.

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{window}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadWindowOp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RollingMean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Nexus API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{nexus_api_reference:nexus-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the public \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} surface with usage\sphinxhyphen{}first examples generated
from the current table API.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} is a named, multi\sphinxhyphen{}table workspace built on top of {\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}}}}}}
— it holds a keyed collection of frames, layers on declared relationships between
them, and provides key/relationship auditing, join\sphinxhyphen{}graph pathfinding, a fluent query
builder ({\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_query_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NexusQuery}}}}}}}, returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from()}}), and
save/load persistence.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This reference is being built out in batches
Not every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} method has its own page yet. The sidebar and the list below only
include methods that are already documented — more are being added incrementally.
Construct a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus(\{\{"name", frame\}, ...\})}} (a vector or brace list of
name/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} pairs); there is no dedicated constructor page, the same as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s own constructors.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\paragraph{Using This Reference}
\label{\detokenize{nexus_api_reference:using-this-reference}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the left sidebar to open one method page at a time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each method page contains its own signatures, parameter details, notes, verified
outputs, and working previous/next navigation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This landing page stays intentionally short so the content panel is not one giant
scroll of every method.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Method Pages}
\label{\detokenize{nexus_api_reference:method-pages}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The sidebar lists methods alphabetically. You can also use the search box to jump
directly to a method name.


\paragraph{The Query Builder}
\label{\detokenize{nexus_api_reference:the-query-builder}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::from(table)}} returns a {\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_query_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NexusQuery}}}}}}}, a
separate fluent builder for walking the join graph from one anchor table
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.join()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.via()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.pick()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.drop()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.collect()}}). See its own reference page for
the full method\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}method breakdown.

\sphinxstepscope




\subparagraph{Nexus::apply}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply:nexus-apply}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{apply}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{key}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fn}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rewrites exactly one named table inside the workspace by passing that table
through a callback and replacing only that table with the callback result.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the targeted transformation surface for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}: when you know \sphinxstyleemphasis{which}
table should change and want every other table left alone, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply()}} is more
precise than {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The method is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating. It returns a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} whose table keys are the
same as the source workspace, with only the named table’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} payload
replaced by the callback result.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{key} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Name of the table to transform.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must not be empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must already exist in the workspace.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Determines \sphinxstyleemphasis{which} table is rewritten; it does not affect ordering.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}DataFrame(const DataFrame\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback that receives the current table and returns the replacement table.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Receives the current \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must return a \sphinxstylestrong{defined} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
May change the table’s row count, feature set, feature order, labels, and
values; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply()}} does not impose shape preservation.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace with the named table replaced by the callback result and all
other tables preserved as they were.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Table keys and table order are preserved; only one table payload changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback is free to change the target table’s shape. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply()}} does not
require row\sphinxhyphen{}count or feature\sphinxhyphen{}count stability.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Workspace metadata is preserved by table key, not by column signature. If the
callback removes columns that existing relationships, saved views, or declared
key metadata depend on, those higher\sphinxhyphen{}level structures may need manual review
afterward.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the “same callback on every table” variant, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::apply\_all}}}}}}}: run one callback across every table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::map\_frames}}}}}}}: the same broad idea with more
functional\sphinxhyphen{}programming\sphinxhyphen{}oriented naming.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/flow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::flow}}}}}}}: transform the whole workspace through one chainable
callback.

\end{itemize}



\sphinxstepscope




\subparagraph{Nexus::apply\_all}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all:nexus-apply-all}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{apply\PYGZus{}all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fn}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rewrites every table in the workspace by applying the same callback to each
table, returning a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} with the transformed tables under the original
keys.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}} is the broad “rewrite the whole workspace uniformly” counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply(key, fn)}}}}}}}. The callback sees each table independently; the
method itself preserves the workspace key set and key order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method overlaps intentionally with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}}}}}}}. Their
core transformation behavior is the same, but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}} reads more naturally
when your mental model is “apply one table\sphinxhyphen{}rewrite rule everywhere”, while
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}} reads more naturally when you are thinking in terms of functional
mapping.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}DataFrame(const DataFrame\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback applied to each table in the workspace.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Receives each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must return a \sphinxstylestrong{defined} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} for every table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
May change table shape; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}} does not require schema preservation.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace containing one transformed replacement table for every source
table, under the same keys and in the same order.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Table keys and their order are preserved exactly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback may change each table’s shape; there is no row\sphinxhyphen{}count or
feature\sphinxhyphen{}count contract imposed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply()}}}}}}}, this method preserves workspace metadata by table
key rather than by column signature. If your callback removes columns that
relationships or saved views depend on, review those structures afterward.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}}}}}}} are behaviorally near\sphinxhyphen{}twins;
the difference is mostly naming intent and, now, their method\sphinxhyphen{}specific error
messages.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::apply}}}}}}}: rewrite one named table instead of every table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::map\_frames}}}}}}}: the same workspace\sphinxhyphen{}wide rewrite idea with
functional naming.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/flow::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::flow}}}}}}}: transform the whole workspace with a callback that
receives the entire \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}, not one table at a time.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::deduce}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/deduce:nexus-deduce}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/deduce::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/deduce:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{deduce}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}confidence}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/deduce:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Scans the workspace for plausible relationship candidates and returns them as an
advisory \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deduce()}} does not create relationships, mutate the workspace, or validate that
the suggested joins are semantically correct for your domain. Its job is narrower:
surface “these two tables share a feature name that looks structurally joinable”
signals so you can inspect them before you declare anything with the relationship
APIs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The current implementation scores candidates from four pieces of evidence:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
shared feature name: base score \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.35}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
left feature is unique: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+0.20}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
right feature is unique: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+0.20}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
left feature is declared as a single\sphinxhyphen{}column key: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+0.125}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
right feature is declared as a single\sphinxhyphen{}column key: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+0.125}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result is capped at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}}. Composite key declarations do \sphinxstylestrong{not} count toward
the declared\sphinxhyphen{}key bonus here; the implementation only treats exact one\sphinxhyphen{}column key
declarations as evidence for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deduce()}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
deduce() is name\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}key\sphinxhyphen{}structure driven
In the current implementation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deduce()}} does not compare actual value overlap
between the two columns. It reasons from shared feature names, uniqueness, and
declared one\sphinxhyphen{}column keys.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/deduce:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_confidence} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimum score a candidate row must reach before it is included in the output.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be in the closed interval \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.0, 1.0{]}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower thresholds admit weaker suggestions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Higher thresholds filter the result down to only the strongest structural
matches.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values outside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.0, 1.0{]}}} throw immediately.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/deduce:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per surviving candidate relationship.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The output frame has these columns:

\PYGZhy{} `name`: a stable suggestion label in the shape `left\PYGZus{}right\PYGZus{}feature`
\PYGZhy{} `left`, `right`: the participating table names
\PYGZhy{} `left\PYGZus{}key`, `right\PYGZus{}key`: the shared feature name on each side
\PYGZhy{} `cardinality`: the inferred cardinality from the two uniqueness flags
\PYGZhy{} `left\PYGZus{}unique`, `right\PYGZus{}unique`: whether each side is unique by that feature
\PYGZhy{} `left\PYGZus{}declared`, `right\PYGZus{}declared`: whether each side declares that feature
  as a one\PYGZhy{}column primary or candidate key
\PYGZhy{} `confidence`: the computed score
\PYGZhy{} `basis`: a compact explanation string showing which evidence contributed
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/deduce:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deduce()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating and purely advisory.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
One table pair can produce multiple rows when several shared feature names look
structurally plausible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} column is feature\sphinxhyphen{}specific, so those multi\sphinxhyphen{}row pair suggestions stay
distinguishable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the default call path \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deduce()}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deduce(0.5)}} is cached in the current
implementation. Non\sphinxhyphen{}default thresholds recompute.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Existing declared relationships do not suppress suggestions. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deduce()}} is about
plausible structure, not “only relationships not already present”.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/defined:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} handle currently owns a usable backing workspace at all —
not whether it holds zero tables. Every ordinary constructor (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vector\textless{}pair\textless{}...\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}}
form and the brace\sphinxhyphen{}init form) produces a defined handle; the main way to end up with
an undefined one is moving from an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} has no public
default constructor of its own (unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}}}}}}, which
does).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
defined() is about handle existence, not table count
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} built from an empty table list is still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined() == true}} — it owns a
real, usable workspace that just happens to hold zero tables. For “does this
workspace hold any tables?”, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/empty::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty()}}}}}}} instead.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/defined:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/defined:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if the handle owns a usable backing workspace; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for a moved\sphinxhyphen{}from
handle.

\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/defined:id1}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{biz}} no longer owns the underlying workspace — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{moved\_out}} does. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} itself

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/defined:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Nexus: undefined handle
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}} (like nearly every other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} method) needs a real backing workspace
to read from. Checking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} first, as this page recommends, lets calling code
sidestep this throw entirely — useful after a move, or around any code path that
might have handed the workspace off elsewhere.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/defined:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{noexcept}} and cheap — it’s a pointer check, not a workspace scan.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/defined::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} has no public default
constructor — you cannot write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus nexus;}} and get an undefined handle directly.
Moving from an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} is the ordinary way to observe \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined() == false}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} constructed from an empty table list is defined but empty — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/empty::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty()}}}}}}} for that distinction.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/defined:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/unique::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::unique}}}}}}}: a related but different existence question — whether
this handle is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{sole} owner of its workspace, not whether it owns one at all.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/empty::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::empty}}}}}}}: whether a defined workspace holds zero tables.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::dloc}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/dloc:nexus-dloc}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/dloc::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/dloc:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{dloc}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{index}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/dloc:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An exact alias for the positional overload of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame()}}}}}}} —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dloc(index)}} calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame(index)}} internally and returns the identical result,
negative\sphinxhyphen{}index wraparound included. The name mirrors
{\hyperref[\detokenize{atlas_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::dloc}}}}}}}’s identically\sphinxhyphen{}named, identically\sphinxhyphen{}behaved
method, since both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} are depth\sphinxhyphen{}stacked collections addressed by
position along that “depth” axis.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/dloc:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{index} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The zero\sphinxhyphen{}based position to fetch. Negative values count back from the end. Throws if
out of bounds.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/dloc:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
The table at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{index}} — identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame(index)}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/dloc:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Purely a naming alternative to the positional overload of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame()}}}}}}} —
see that page for the full breakdown, including negative\sphinxhyphen{}index behavior and the
out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}bounds throw message.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no name\sphinxhyphen{}based \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dloc()}} overload — for a name\sphinxhyphen{}based lookup, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame(key)}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/get::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get(key)}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::frame}}}}}}}: the canonical method, with both the name\sphinxhyphen{}based and

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::drop}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:nexus-drop}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{drop}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{initializer\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a new workspace by removing the named tables you specify and carrying
forward every unmentioned table unchanged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} is the complement of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}}}}}}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} says “keep exactly these tables”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} says “remove exactly these tables”

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
That difference affects ordering. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} does \sphinxstylestrong{not} use request order to
build the output; instead, it preserves the original left\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}right order of every
table that survives.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like the other subset operations, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} carries forward table metadata for the
remaining tables and keeps only the relationships and saved views that still make
structural sense after the removal.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keys} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The table names to remove.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each key must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each key must be unique within the request.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each key must already exist in the source workspace.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty list is allowed and acts as a no\sphinxhyphen{}op.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace containing every source table except the ones named in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys}}, with the surviving tables kept in their original order.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Remove two named tables and preserve the original order of what
remains.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Surviving tables keep their original order. This is the key semantic difference
from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}}}}}}}, whose request list determines output order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Surviving table metadata is preserved.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Relationships and saved views are pruned to the subset still supported by the
remaining tables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want the result to contain \sphinxstyleemphasis{only} a named list of tables, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}}}}}}} instead.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/drop:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::select}}}}}}}: keep an explicit table list instead of removing
one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::tail}}}}}}}: drop by position from the front rather than by name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::keys}}}}}}}: inspect the remaining order after dropping tables.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::empty}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/empty:nexus-empty}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/empty::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/empty:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{empty}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/empty:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether the workspace holds zero tables — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if either the handle is
undefined at all, or it’s defined but was built from (or reduced to) an empty table
list. This is a strict superset of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/defined::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}}}}}}}: every undefined handle
is also empty, but a defined handle can be empty too.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/empty:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/empty:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if the handle is undefined, or defined with zero tables; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} if it
holds at least one table.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/empty:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

instead of a boolean.

\subparagraph{Nexus::flow}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow:nexus-flow}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{flow}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fn}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Passes the entire workspace through a callback and returns whatever valid \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
the callback produces.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}} is the broadest chainable transformation surface on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}}}}}}, or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}}}}}}}, it does not operate table\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}table. Instead, it
hands the whole workspace to your callback so the callback can decide whether to
select tables, rename tables, inject tables, drop tables, or compose several of
those operations together before returning the next workspace.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use it when you want to keep a fluent chain but need a short custom block of
logic in the middle.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}Nexus(const Nexus\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback that receives the current workspace and returns the next workspace.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Receives the current \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must return a \sphinxstylestrong{defined} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
May return the input unchanged, a derived subset, an expanded workspace, or any
other valid \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
Whatever valid workspace the callback returns.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged unless the callback explicitly returns a
modified copy derived from it.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback is not constrained to preserve any particular aspect of the
workspace. It can return a subset, a renamed workspace, an injected workspace,
or the input unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the callback works at the workspace level, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}} is the right tool
for logic that depends on multiple tables or on method composition, not just
on transforming one table body.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the callback’s logic is really “rewrite one table” or “rewrite every table”,
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply()}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}}}}}} usually communicates
intent more clearly than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flow()}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/flow:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::apply}}}}}}}: transform one named table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::apply\_all}}}}}}}: transform every table with one callback.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::map\_frames}}}}}}}: functional table\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}table mapping.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frame:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fetches one table out of the workspace, either by name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key}}) or by position
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{index}}) in {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frames()}}}}}}} order. Both overloads throw
if the table doesn’t exist — for a non\sphinxhyphen{}throwing alternative, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/get::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get(key)}}}}}}} (name\sphinxhyphen{}based only).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The positional overload supports negative indices Python\sphinxhyphen{}style: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means the last
table, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}} the second\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}last, and so on.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frame:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{key} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The table name to fetch. Throws if unknown.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{index} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The zero\sphinxhyphen{}based position to fetch. Negative values count back from the end. Throws if
out of bounds.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frame:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
The requested table.

which follows the same positional\sphinxhyphen{}access convention.

reference\sphinxhyphen{}counted), not a fresh deep copy of the table data.

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frames:signature}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frames:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns every table in the workspace as a plain vector of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, in the same
order as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/names::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frames(){[}i{]}}} is always the
table named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys(){[}i{]}}}. Useful for iterating over every table without knowing (or
caring about) their names, or for zipping the two vectors together.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frames:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frames:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::vector\textless{}DataFrame\textgreater{}\&}}
The tables, in workspace order.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/frames:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returned by reference — reading it doesn’t copy any table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Order always matches {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/names::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}}}}}} positionally.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To get one table by name (rather than iterating all of them), prefer
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame(key)}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/get::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get(key)}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::get}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/get:nexus-get}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/get::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/get:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{key}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/get:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fetches a table by name, the same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame(key)}}}}}}}, but returns
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}} for an unknown key instead of throwing. This is the non\sphinxhyphen{}throwing
counterpart to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame()}} — reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get()}} when a missing table is an expected,
handled case rather than a programming error.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/get:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{key} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The table name to look up.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/get:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}DataFrame\textgreater{}}}
The table if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key}} exists; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}} otherwise.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/get:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A present key returns the table wrapped in an engaged \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{optional}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/has:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether a table with the given name exists in the workspace, in constant
time (a hash\sphinxhyphen{}map lookup, not a linear scan of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}}). This is the
non\sphinxhyphen{}throwing way to check for a table’s presence before calling
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame(key)}}}}}}}, which throws for an unknown key.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/has:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{key} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The table name to look up.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/has:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if a table with this name exists; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} otherwise.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/has:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lookup is by exact name match — no pattern matching or case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitivity.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(key)}} over a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{try}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{catch}} around {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frame::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame(key)}}}}}}} when you
only need to know presence, not fetch the table itself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/get::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get(key)}}}}}}} combines both concerns in one call — it returns
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}DataFrame\textgreater{}}}, so a single call answers “does it exist” and “here it
is” together.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::head}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head:nexus-head}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new workspace containing only the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} tables of the current
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}, in their existing left\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}right order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} is the simplest way to trim a larger multi\sphinxhyphen{}table workspace down to an
exploratory prefix without renaming anything, recomputing anything, or mutating
the source handle. It is purely positional: the method does not inspect table
names or contents; it simply keeps the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} entries from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frames()}}}}}}} order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two behaviors matter most in practice:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is \sphinxstylestrong{clamped}, not treated as a strict validation boundary. Asking for
more tables than exist gives you the whole workspace, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or a negative
count gives you an empty workspace.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Surviving schema attachments are carried forward for retained tables. Table
metadata survives for the tables that remain, and relationships or saved views
survive only if they are still fully supported by the retained key set.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of leading tables to keep.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \textgreater{} ntables()}}: clamped to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}}, so the whole workspace is returned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n == 0}}: returns a defined but empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \textless{} 0}}: also clamps to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, so the result is again a defined but empty
workspace.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no bounds error here.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace containing the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} tables from the source workspace,
in the same order they originally appeared.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Order is preserved exactly. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head(2)}} does not sort or otherwise reinterpret
the workspace; it just keeps the first two current positions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Surviving per\sphinxhyphen{}table metadata is carried forward for retained tables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Relationships and saved views are filtered structurally: only those whose
referenced tables are all still present survive into the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the symmetric operation from the end of the workspace, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail(n)}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/head:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/tail::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::tail}}}}}}}: keep the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} tables instead of the first.

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::keys}}}}}}}: inspect the current table order that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} slices
from.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/inject:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Appends one or more tables to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} workspace and returns the expanded
workspace as a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject(...)}} is the main “grow this workspace” API when you want to stay
pipeline\sphinxhyphen{}friendly and non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating. Instead of editing the current workspace in
place, it gives you a new handle with the appended tables while leaving the
source \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} untouched. That makes it a natural fit for expression\sphinxhyphen{}style
construction:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{customers}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{customers}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{inject}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{orders}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{orders}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{inject}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{payments}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The four overloads split cleanly into two naming modes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Named injection}: you supply table names explicitly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Unnamed injection}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} manufactures names for you as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_0}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_2}}, and so on.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every overload appends. None of them replace an existing table in place. If the
target name already exists, the call throws rather than overwriting anything.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/inject:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{key} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The explicit name to assign to the injected table in the single\sphinxhyphen{}table named
overload.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must not be empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must not already exist in the workspace.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If it has the auto\sphinxhyphen{}key shape \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_N}}, it also advances the internal
auto\sphinxhyphen{}naming counter so later unnamed injections continue from there rather than
reusing an older number.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{frame} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The single table to append.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be defined.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The table is appended at the end of the workspace.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the unnamed overload, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} chooses the new key automatically.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Batch named injection. Each pair is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(table\_name, frame)}}.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tables are appended in the exact order you supply them.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each name must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each name must be unique relative to the existing workspace and the rest of
the batch.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} must be defined.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Batch unnamed injection.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each frame is appended in the exact order you supply it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each frame receives the next available auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated key.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} must be defined.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/inject:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace containing the original tables followed by the injected
tables.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Existing table order is preserved. New tables are always appended, never
inserted into the middle and never used to overwrite an existing key.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/inject:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject(...)}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating. The source \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} is left unchanged; the result
is a new handle.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
New tables are always appended at the end of the workspace. If you care about
the final table order, the order of the initializer list is the order that will
appear in {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frames()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unnamed injection uses auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated keys of the form \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_N}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicitly naming a table \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_N}} is not cosmetic only; it advances the
internal auto\sphinxhyphen{}key counter used by later unnamed injections.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject(...)}} never overwrites an existing table name. Duplicate keys are always
an error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you want to mutate an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} in place instead of receiving a new
one, the corresponding mutating surface is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject\_(...)}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::keys}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/keys:nexus-keys}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/keys:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/keys:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the table names in the workspace, in the same order they were constructed
(or last reordered by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}}/
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/inject::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}}}}}}}). This order is not alphabetical — it’s
positional, and it’s exactly the order {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frames()}}}}}}} uses too, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys(){[}i{]}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frames(){[}i{]}}} always describe the same table.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/keys:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/keys:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}\&}}
The table names, in workspace order.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/keys:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returned by reference — no copy is made just to read the names.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/names::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}}}}}} is an exact alias for this same method.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The order matches {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/frames::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frames()}}}}}}} positionally; use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/ntables::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}}}}}}} for the count without materializing the vector at all
(though in practice \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys().size()}} is just as cheap).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::map\_frames}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames:nexus-map-frames}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{map\PYGZus{}frames}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fn}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a new workspace by mapping each table through a callback and storing the
mapped result back under the same key.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Semantically, this is the functional\sphinxhyphen{}programming sibling of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}}}}}}. Both methods walk every table in the workspace and
replace each one with the callback result. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}} simply emphasizes the
“map each frame to a new frame” mental model more explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use it when you want the workspace\sphinxhyphen{}level equivalent of a table collection map:
same key set, same order, transformed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} payloads.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}DataFrame(const DataFrame\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback applied to each table.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Receives each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const}} reference.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must return a \sphinxstylestrong{defined} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
May change shape; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}} does not enforce row\sphinxhyphen{}count or feature\sphinxhyphen{}count
stability.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace containing one mapped replacement table for every source
table, under the same keys and in the same order.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/map_frames:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
It preserves workspace keys and order exactly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}}}}}}, it preserves workspace metadata by table
key rather than by transformed column signature. If the callback removes
columns used by higher\sphinxhyphen{}level schema structures, review those structures after
the transformation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map\_frames()}} when “map each frame to a new frame” is the clearest
mental model. Choose {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/apply_all::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all()}}}}}}} when “apply one rule
everywhere” reads more naturally at the call site.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/names:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An exact alias for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}} calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}} internally and
returns the identical reference. Both names exist because a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} workspace reads
naturally either as a dictionary (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}, paralleling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(key)}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get(key)}}) or as
a named collection of tables (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}, paralleling how
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::features()}}}}}}} names columns). Pick whichever
reads better at the call site — there is no behavioral difference.

\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/names:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/names:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}\&}}
The table names, in workspace order — identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keys()}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/ntables:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}} needs a defined handle — calling it on an undefined (e.g. moved\sphinxhyphen{}from)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Nexus: undefined handle"}}, same as most other methods. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/defined::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{defined()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/size::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}}}}}} is a pure alias, provided for STL\sphinxhyphen{}style familiarity.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/profile:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{profile}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/profile:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a table\sphinxhyphen{}level diagnostics frame for the entire workspace.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/summary::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary()}}}}}}} answers “what tables are here and how large are they?”,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{profile()}} answers the next layer of questions:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
how complete is each table’s metadata?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
does a declared primary key look healthy?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
how connected is this table to the relationship graph?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
what is the table’s null burden and time\sphinxhyphen{}field declaration?

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output is one row per workspace table. Relationships do not get their own rows
here; for the mixed table\sphinxhyphen{}plus\sphinxhyphen{}relationship command\sphinxhyphen{}center view, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/scan::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/profile:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/profile:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per table, with these columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{} `table`: table key
\PYGZhy{} `rows`, `cols`: row and feature counts
\PYGZhy{} `null\PYGZus{}cells`, `null\PYGZus{}frac`: total missing cells and the fraction of all cells
\PYGZhy{} `meta\PYGZus{}score`: count of populated metadata fields among `grain`,
  `primary\PYGZus{}key`, `candidate\PYGZus{}keys`, `time\PYGZus{}field`, `case\PYGZus{}labels`, `source`,
  `provenance`, and `note`
\PYGZhy{} `meta\PYGZus{}ready`: `true` only when `grain` and `primary\PYGZus{}key` are both present
\PYGZhy{} `primary\PYGZus{}key`: declared primary\PYGZhy{}key signature, or empty when none exists
\PYGZhy{} `key\PYGZus{}missing\PYGZus{}rows`, `key\PYGZus{}duplicate\PYGZus{}rows`: health of the declared primary key
\PYGZhy{} `links`, `left\PYGZus{}links`, `right\PYGZus{}links`: relationship\PYGZhy{}graph connection counts
\PYGZhy{} `time\PYGZus{}field`: declared time field, if any
\PYGZhy{} `fingerprint`: short per\PYGZhy{}table fingerprint
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For tables with no declared primary key, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key\_missing\_rows}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key\_duplicate\_rows}} are emitted as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} sentinels rather than guessed values.
