\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/profile:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{profile()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The current implementation caches the result until the workspace schema or table
contents change.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic key health is computed only for the declared primary key, not for every
candidate feature that looks interesting.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{links}} counts all adjacent relationships for the table, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left\_links}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right\_links}} split that count by direction in the declared graph.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::rename}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:nexus-rename}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{rename}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{from}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{to}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes one table key inside the workspace and returns the resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}},
without altering table order or table contents.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a schema\sphinxhyphen{}level naming operation, not a data transformation. The table
itself stays exactly where it was in the workspace; only its key changes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}} is deeper than a plain string substitution, though. Internally, it
also updates the schema objects that refer to table names:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the table key list

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stored table metadata

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
declared relationships whose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left\_table}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right\_table}} matched the old key

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
saved join plans that reference the old table name

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
That means the operation is intended to preserve the workspace’s internal
consistency, not just make the visible key list look nicer.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{from} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Existing table key to rename.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must not be empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must already exist in the workspace.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Replacement key.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must not be empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must differ from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Must not already exist in the workspace.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If it has the auto\sphinxhyphen{}key shape \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_N}}, it advances the internal auto\sphinxhyphen{}name
counter so later unnamed {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/inject::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject()}}}}}}} calls continue from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N + 1}}
rather than reusing lower numbers.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace with the renamed table key applied.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Table order, table contents, and every unaffected table key remain unchanged.
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Nexus::rename: source key cannot be empty
Nexus::rename: target key cannot be empty
Nexus::rename: source and target keys must differ
Nexus::rename: unknown key \PYGZsq{}missing\PYGZsq{}
Nexus::rename: target key already exists \PYGZsq{}payments\PYGZsq{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The renamed table stays in the same position in the workspace; only the key
changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Table metadata keyed by the old name is moved to the new name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Relationships and saved join plans that reference the old table name are
rewritten to reference the new one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} matches the auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated naming convention \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_N}}, later unnamed
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/inject::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject()}}}}}}} calls continue from the next number after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The mutating sibling is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}}, but this page documents the non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating
pipeline\sphinxhyphen{}friendly form.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/rename:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/inject::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::inject}}}}}}}: add new tables, including unnamed auto\sphinxhyphen{}keyed
tables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::keys}}}}}}}: inspect the renamed key list.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::select}}}}}}}: project and reorder tables without renaming them.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::scan}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/scan:nexus-scan}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/scan::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/scan:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{scan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/scan:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a unified diagnostics table that mixes table rows and relationship rows in
one place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the closest thing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} has to a command\sphinxhyphen{}center overview. Table rows tell
you how declared primary keys and metadata look. Relationship rows tell you whether
the declared join structure is actually holding up under missing keys, duplicate
keys, and orphan pressure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/profile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{profile()}}}}}}}, which stays table\sphinxhyphen{}only, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} is intentionally
heterogeneous: some rows describe tables, others describe relationships, and the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind}} column tells you which is which.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/scan:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/scan:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per table plus one row per declared relationship.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The output columns are:

\PYGZhy{} `kind`: `\PYGZdq{}table\PYGZdq{}` or `\PYGZdq{}relationship\PYGZdq{}`
\PYGZhy{} `name`: table name or relationship name
\PYGZhy{} `left`, `right`: row anchors; for table rows, `left` repeats the table name
\PYGZhy{} `key\PYGZus{}signature`: primary\PYGZhy{}key or relationship\PYGZhy{}key signature
\PYGZhy{} `rows`, `cols`: populated for table rows, `\PYGZhy{}1` for relationship rows
\PYGZhy{} `left\PYGZus{}missing\PYGZus{}rows`, `right\PYGZus{}missing\PYGZus{}rows`
\PYGZhy{} `left\PYGZus{}duplicate\PYGZus{}rows`, `right\PYGZus{}duplicate\PYGZus{}rows`
\PYGZhy{} `left\PYGZus{}orphans`, `right\PYGZus{}orphans`
\PYGZhy{} `valid`
\PYGZhy{} `declared\PYGZus{}status`, `computed\PYGZus{}status`
\PYGZhy{} `meta\PYGZus{}score`, `meta\PYGZus{}ready`
\PYGZhy{} `confidence`
\PYGZhy{} `note`
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The most important distinction is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{declared\_status}} vs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{computed\_status}}:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{declared\_status}} is what the relationship says it is, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{computed\_status}} is
what the current data actually supports.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/scan:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The current implementation caches the default result until the workspace changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Table rows and relationship rows intentionally share the same frame even though
some columns are only meaningful for one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For relationship rows, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rows}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cols}} are set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} because the row is not
describing a materialized table.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Nexus::select}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select:nexus-select}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{select}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{initializer\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a new workspace containing exactly the named tables you request, in the
exact order you request them.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This makes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} more than a simple filter. It is both:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a \sphinxstylestrong{projection} operation, because it drops every unmentioned table, and

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a \sphinxstylestrong{reordering} operation, because the result follows the request list rather
than the source workspace’s original order.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
That second point is the easy one to miss. If the source workspace is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{customers, orders, payments, refunds}}, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select(\{"payments", "customers"\})}}
does not preserve source order among the survivors; it intentionally returns
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{payments, customers}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like the other subset\sphinxhyphen{}building methods, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} carries forward metadata for
surviving tables and keeps only the relationships and saved views that remain
valid on the selected key set.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keys} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The table names to keep.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each key must be non\sphinxhyphen{}empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each key must be unique within the request itself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each key must already exist in the source workspace.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Request order becomes output order.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty list is allowed and produces a defined but empty workspace.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace containing exactly the requested tables, in request order.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Request order controls output order. This is the key semantic difference from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}}}}}}}, which preserves the original order of survivors.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Surviving table metadata is preserved.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Relationships and saved views are pruned to the subset that remains fully
supported by the selected tables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you naturally think in terms of “remove these few tables” rather than “keep
exactly these tables”, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}}}}}}} is often the shorter expression.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/select:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::drop}}}}}}}: remove named tables and keep everything else.

\item {}

list.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::keys}}}}}}}: inspect the final order after projection.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/size:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An exact synonym for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/ntables::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}} calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}}
internally and returns precisely the same value. It exists purely for readers coming
from STL\sphinxhyphen{}container\sphinxhyphen{}style naming conventions (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.size()}}), alongside the more
domain\sphinxhyphen{}specific \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}} name used everywhere else in this reference (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nfeatures()}}, and so on, on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/ncases::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}}}}}}).

\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/size:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/size:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}
The number of tables currently in the workspace — identical to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/ntables::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ntables()}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{Nexus::summary}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/summary:nexus-summary}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/summary::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/summary:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{summary}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/summary:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the compact table inventory for the workspace.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary()}} is intentionally small. It answers only three questions:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
what is each table called?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
how many rows does it have?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
how many features does it have?

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
That narrow scope is deliberate. If you need metadata completeness, declared\sphinxhyphen{}key
health, or relationship diagnostics, step up to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/profile::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{profile()}}}}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/scan::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scan()}}}}}}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary()}} stays focused on table identity and size.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/summary:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/summary:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per table, with exactly these columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZhy{} `table`
\PYGZhy{} `ncases`
\PYGZhy{} `nfeatures`
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result follows the current workspace order exactly.

\subparagraph{Nexus::tail}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail:nexus-tail}}\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to Nexus API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{tail}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Nexus}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new workspace containing only the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} tables of the current
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}, preserving their existing relative order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} is the mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}}}}}}: where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}} keeps a
prefix, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} keeps a suffix. It is still positional, still non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating, and
still simple to reason about: table names and contents do not affect which
tables survive; only the current workspace order does.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}, this method carries forward surviving schema attachments for the
kept tables. Per\sphinxhyphen{}table metadata is preserved for tables that remain, while
relationships and saved views survive only when every table they depend on is
still present in the suffix.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of trailing tables to keep.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \textgreater{} ntables()}}: clamped down to the full workspace size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n == 0}}: returns a defined but empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \textless{} 0}}: clamps to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, again yielding an empty workspace.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range exception here.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}}
A new workspace containing the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} tables from the source workspace, in
the same order they originally appeared.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
The source `Nexus` is unchanged.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating; the source workspace keeps all of its tables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result keeps the original relative order of the retained suffix. For
example, the last two tables are returned as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"payments", "refunds"}}, not in
reverse.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Per\sphinxhyphen{}table metadata survives for retained tables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Relationships and saved views are kept only when their required tables are all
still present after the suffix slice.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a prefix slice instead, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head(n)}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/tail:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/head::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::head}}}}}}}: keep the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} tables instead of the last.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::drop}}}}}}}: remove explicitly named tables instead of slicing by
position.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/keys::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::keys}}}}}}}: inspect the order \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}} slices from.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Signature}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Nexus}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{noexcept}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/unique:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports whether this \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} handle is the \sphinxstylestrong{sole} owner of its underlying
workspace — a copy\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}write signal, not a data question. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} handles are cheap to
copy (copying just bumps a reference count); the actual table data is only cloned the
moment a mutating method (any trailing\sphinxhyphen{}underscore method, like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inject\_()}}) is called on a handle that
isn’t the sole owner. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unique()}} lets you observe that bookkeeping directly.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/unique:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/unique:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if no other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} handle currently shares this workspace; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} if at
least one other handle does.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/unique:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
true true
true false true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_()}} is a mutating (trailing\sphinxhyphen{}underscore) method. Since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shared}} wasn’t the
sole owner when it was called, the workspace was cloned first — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shared}} now points
at its own independent copy, renamed as requested, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{biz}} still has its
original, untouched \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"orders"}} table. Both handles are sole owners again after the
clone.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/nexus/unique:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copying a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} handle (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{auto shared = biz;}}) never copies table data up front —
it shares the same workspace and increments a reference count, which is why
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unique()}} immediately becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} on both sides.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The clone only happens lazily, inside a mutating (trailing\sphinxhyphen{}underscore) method, and
only if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unique()}} was already \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} at that moment — mutating a handle that’s
already the sole owner never clones.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating methods (no trailing underscore, like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/nexus/select::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select()}}}}}}}) always return a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus}} and never touch
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unique()}} on the original handle at all.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the public \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NexusQuery}} surface — the fluent join\sphinxhyphen{}graph query
builder returned by {\hyperref[\detokenize{nexus_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nexus::from(table)}}}}}}}.

\end{sphinxadmonition}


\paragraph{What It Is}
\label{\detokenize{nexus_query_api_reference:what-it-is}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nexus.from("table\_name")}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NexusQuery}} anchored at that table.
From there, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.join(other)}} (optionally with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JoinSpec}}) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.via(other, how)}}
extends the walk across the join graph, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.pick()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.drop()}} narrow the result
columns, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.name()}} labels the result, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.collect()}} executes the accumulated plan
and returns the joined {\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}}}}}}.

\sphinxstepscope

Outputs on this page are exercised by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plussmic\_table\_statistics\_window\_tests}}. Built\sphinxhyphen{}in numeric work stays in Series kernels; scalar and case callbacks are explicit UDF boundaries.

\subsubsection{Time\sphinxhyphen{}Series Accessor Guide}
\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:time-series-accessor-guide}}\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} surface for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}.
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} for numeric time\sphinxhyphen{}series values. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tl()}} for datetime/timeline
values.


\paragraph{API Signature}
\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:api-signature}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTsAccessor}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::ts() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} TimeSeriesAccessor}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::ts() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTsAccessor}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compatibility overloads still accept feature names, but preferred public code is
selection\sphinxhyphen{}first: select the value feature(s), then call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} with no feature
names.


\paragraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}} after selecting numeric value features when you want transforms returned as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.\\
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::ts()}} when you want transforms returned as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} for one column.
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::ts()}} when you want the same transform delegated to every frame in an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Preferred selection\sphinxhyphen{}first style:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{volume}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{daily}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{resample}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{D}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{roll}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seven\PYGZus{}day}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{7D}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Text\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}datetime parsing is an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cast(...)}}, then timeline operations
belong on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} surface:

\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadCastTarget}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Timeline}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadCastOptions}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{format}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZpc{}Y\PYGZhy{}\PYGZpc{}m\PYGZhy{}\PYGZpc{}d}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{            }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{invalid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ParseInvalid}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Null}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date\PYGZus{}text}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{years}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dates}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{year}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}} is called with no feature arguments, every feature in the
current frame must be a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}. A mixed frame throws a Pluss error.
This keeps surface application intentional:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ok}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{volume}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+c1}{// df.ts().rolling(5) throws if df also contains text or timeline columns.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Inputs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For cases\sphinxhyphen{}based time\sphinxhyphen{}axis methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{asfreq}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\_to}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reindex\_time}}), the frame cases must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}. Use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set("date")}} first.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overloads that accept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} are retained for compatibility.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor}} methods return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeSeriesAccessor}} methods return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{labels, values\}}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample}}).

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{time_series_accessor_guide:common-pitfall}}

\subsubsection{Timeline (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{tl}}) and Batched DataFrame Operations}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:timeline-tl-and-batched-dataframe-operations}}\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page covers the Pluss\sphinxhyphen{}native timeline surface and the batched numeric
delegation path added for multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature DataFrame operations.


\paragraph{API Signature}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:api-signature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::tl() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} ThreadTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl(feature: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl(features: initializer\_list\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl(features: RangeView\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{} = \{\}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::tl(feature: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::tl(features: initializer\_list\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTimelineAccessor}}\\
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::tl(features: RangeView\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{} = \{\}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} AtlasTimelineAccessor}}


\paragraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} is the datetime/timeline surface. It is separate from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}}
extracts and transforms datetime payloads, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} remains the time\sphinxhyphen{}series
analytics surface for returns, lag/lead, rolling blocks, resampling, and
alignment.


\paragraph{Inputs}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:inputs}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}}: one Timeline or TimeIndex feature name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}: zero or more Timeline/TimeIndex feature names. Empty selection
is valid only after an intentional selection where every feature in the
current frame is Timeline/TimeIndex, for example
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{"event\_time"\}).tl()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}: calendar/time unit accepted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} rounding methods, such as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}, or compatible CodeH units.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}}: signed number of frequency steps to shift.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}}: shift/period frequency such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"month"}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"year"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimelineLocalizeOptions}}: option struct with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tz}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.fold}}, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.nonexistent}} fields.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:output}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thread\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DataFrame\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} with selected features replaced
by the transformed result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Atlas\sphinxhyphen{}level \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tl()}} returns an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} after applying the DataFrame operation
to each frame.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Options}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:options}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit}} controls epoch extraction:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Nanos}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Micros}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Millis}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Seconds}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimelineLocalizeOptions}} supports C++20 designated initializers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{TimelineLocalizeOptions}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{UTC}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fold}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{nonexistent}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{raise}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:examples}}

\subparagraph{Example 1: Thread timeline extraction}
\label{\detokenize{timeline_batched_api_reference:example-1-thread-timeline-extraction}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{years}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{event\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{year}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{event\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{iso}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{seconds}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{event\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{epoch}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{TimeUnit}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Seconds}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Expected output:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{years}} is a numeric Thread containing calendar years.

\item {}

\subsubsection{Hierarchical Cases}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:hierarchical-cases}}\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hierarchical cases are PlussMic’s structured case\sphinxhyphen{}axis engine. They are the
Pluss\sphinxhyphen{}native equivalent of a pandas MultiIndex on rows, but the public language
uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case hierarchy is stored as typed case\sphinxhyphen{}label metadata. Display labels may
look like joined strings, but operations use the structured case\sphinxhyphen{}label payloads.


\paragraph{API Signature}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:api-signature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().set(options: SetLabelOptions) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().set(feature\_name: string\_view, drop\_feature: bool = true) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().set(feature\_names: initializer\_list\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}, drop\_features: bool = true, separator: string\_view = "\textbackslash{}x1F") \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().has() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} bool}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().names() \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} vector\textless{}string\textgreater{}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().part(name: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} Thread}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().part(position: int64) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} Thread}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::case\_study(pick: CasePick) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().sort(options: SortLabelOptions) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::group\_by(keys: LabelGroup, specs: RangeView\textless{}GroupSpec\textgreater{}, dropnull\_keys: bool = true, render: bool = false) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrameView}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().rename(renames: RangeView\textless{}LabelRename\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().order(names: RangeView\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().drop(names: RangeView\textless{}string\_view\textgreater{}) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().reset(options: ResetLabelOptions) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::unstack(label: string\_view) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} DataFrame}}


\paragraph{Options}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:options}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SetLabelOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}: features promoted into structured case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: removes promoted features from the ordinary feature axis when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verify}}: checks for duplicate full structured keys when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort}}: sorts by the selected case labels after construction when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}: display\sphinxhyphen{}label separator only; structured operations do not depend on it.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CasePick}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: select by one named case label.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbls}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}: select by several named case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key}}: select by the full structured key in case\sphinxhyphen{}label order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: drops matched case labels after selection when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SortCaselblOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbls}}: case\sphinxhyphen{}label names used for typed stable sorting. Empty means sort by the flat case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}}: sort direction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}}: null ordering.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LabelGroup}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl}}: group by one case label.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbls}}: group by several case labels.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResetLabelOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: discards case labels when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}: replacement feature names for materialized case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}}: fallback name prefix when case\sphinxhyphen{}label names are empty.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnstackOptions}}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{caselbl}}: case label moved into feature names.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}: drops remaining case\sphinxhyphen{}label materialization from ordinary features after rebuilding the case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort}}: sorts unstacked feature labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}: joins value\sphinxhyphen{}feature names and unstacked labels when several value features exist.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{hierarchical_cases:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A hierarchical case axis is typed. Numeric case labels remain numeric, text case labels remain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, and timeline case labels remain temporal.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(...)}}, transforms, and feature reordering preserve case\sphinxhyphen{}label metadata.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_study(CasePick)}} supports partial\sphinxhyphen{}label and full\sphinxhyphen{}key lookup.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by(LabelGroup\{...\})}} groups by case labels without requiring those labels to exist as ordinary features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unstack(...)}} rejects duplicate output cells. Aggregate first when multiple rows map to the same output cell.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stack(...)}} moves feature names into the case hierarchy and preserves homogeneous typed values.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{DataFrameSqlAccessor API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:dataframesqlaccessor-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the public SQL accessor returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sql()}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sql(SqlOptions)}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The table is named df, not self
Every statement addresses the frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql()}} was called on as \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}}} —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT ... FROM df ...}}. There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self}} keyword; if you’ve seen \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FROM self}}
in older notes or examples, that name never existed in the implementation and
will fail to resolve.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic’s embedded SQL is a small, deliberately limited dialect, not a general
SQL engine: one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}}, an optional single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{INNER JOIN}}, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WHERE}} clause that
is itself just a {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/query::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::query}}}}}}} expression, at
most one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY}} key, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LIMIT}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OFFSET}}. There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GROUP BY}}, no
aggregate functions, no subqueries, no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UNION}}, no multi\sphinxhyphen{}column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY}}, and
no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LEFT JOIN}} (the parser explicitly rejects it — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:notes-execute}]{\sphinxcrossref{Notes}}}). Anything beyond that grammar is a parse error, not a
silent best\sphinxhyphen{}effort interpretation.


\paragraph{How To Use This Page}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:how-to-use-this-page}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Methods are grouped alphabetically so you can jump quickly from the left rail.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each method section starts with the public signature(s), then explains what
the method does, how each parameter changes behavior, and what the call
returns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples build on one running dataset (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}}, and a second frame
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{managers}} for the JOIN examples) so you can compare outputs directly
instead of re\sphinxhyphen{}reading a new setup every time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each example is followed immediately by verified output hand\sphinxhyphen{}traced against
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSql.cpp}}, so the result shape is visible before you move to the
next one.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{E}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:e}}

\subparagraph{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{execute}}}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:execute}}

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameSqlAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statement}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Renders any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{name\}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@name\}}} template placeholders into the statement text,
parses the result as a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}} statement (or reuses a cached parse —
see the plan\sphinxhyphen{}cache note below), executes it against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}} (the frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sql()}}
was called on) and any additional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sources}}, and returns the projected rows as
a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}. Execution proceeds in a fixed pipeline: resolve \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FROM}}
source \(\rightarrow\) apply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JOIN}} (if any) \(\rightarrow\) apply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WHERE}} (if any) \(\rightarrow\) apply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY}} (if
any) \(\rightarrow\) apply the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}} projection \(\rightarrow\) apply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OFFSET}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LIMIT}} \(\rightarrow\) apply
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_result\_rows}} truncation. Resource limits (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_intermediate\_rows}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{memory\_budget\_mb}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{timeout\_ms}}) are checked at every one of those stages,
not just at the end.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statement} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The SQL text. Supported grammar:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
SELECT \PYGZlt{}* | col[, col ...][ AS alias]\PYGZgt{}
FROM \PYGZlt{}source\PYGZgt{}[ AS alias]
[INNER JOIN \PYGZlt{}source\PYGZgt{}[ AS alias] ON \PYGZlt{}left\PYGZgt{} = \PYGZlt{}right\PYGZgt{}]
[WHERE \PYGZlt{}query()\PYGZhy{}expression\PYGZgt{}]
[ORDER BY \PYGZlt{}one column\PYGZgt{} [ASC|DESC] [NULLS FIRST|LAST]]
[LIMIT \PYGZlt{}n\PYGZgt{}]
[OFFSET \PYGZlt{}n\PYGZgt{}]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}} (the calling frame) or a name bound via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions::sources}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}left\textgreater{}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}right\textgreater{}}} in a JOIN’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ON}} clause are bare or
dotted (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alias.column}}) identifiers separated by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}} with spaces around it —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region = m.region}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region=m.region}} (the tokenizer only splits on
whitespace/quotes/punctuation, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}} glued to its neighbors becomes one
unparsable word). At least one side of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ON}} must reference the joined
source’s own alias/name.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new, freshly materialized frame — the projected, filtered, ordered,
sliced result. Row case labels are whatever the last case\sphinxhyphen{}label\sphinxhyphen{}affecting
stage produced (see the per\sphinxhyphen{}example notes below; a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WHERE}} keeps the
original labels of the surviving rows, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JOIN}} always resets to a fresh
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..n\sphinxhyphen{}1}} index, per {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/unify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unify}}}}}}}).

not renumbered), because a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WHERE}} with no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JOIN}} never touches the case
axis.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}} is projected out under the name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{amount}}, but the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY sales}}
clause still refers to the underlying column — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY amount}} would fail
here since the projection hasn’t happened yet when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY}} runs (ordering
happens before the final \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT}} projection in the pipeline). Case labels
travel with their rows through the sort (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} now leads, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id 5}} had the
highest \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders.sql(...)}} is only a \sphinxstyleemphasis{handle} — the query still has to reference \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}}
(directly, or transitively via a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JOIN}}) somewhere. Querying only a bound
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sources}} entry with no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}} in sight is rejected outright, even though the
bound frame is perfectly queryable on its own via its \sphinxstyleemphasis{own} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sql()}} call.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:notes}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:notes-execute}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LEFT JOIN}} is parsed but explicitly rejected —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::sql().execute: LEFT JOIN is not supported yet (use INNER JOIN)"}}.
There is no working substitute inside SQL text; drop to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/unify::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::unify}}}}}}} directly (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{how = "keep\_left"}})
if you need it, then continue in SQL against the result via a bound source.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ORDER BY}} accepts exactly one column; there is no multi\sphinxhyphen{}column tiebreaker
and no expression, only a bare (optionally qualified) identifier plus
optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ASC}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DESC}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULLS FIRST}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULLS LAST}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions::result\_mode = ResultMode::Chunked}} currently has \sphinxstylestrong{no
execution effect} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute()}} still returns a fully materialized
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} either way, and merely emits a diagnostic warning noting the
request was ignored. There is no streaming/chunked execution path yet.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Diagnostics (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diagnostics\_explain}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diagnostics\_profile}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diagnostics\_trace\_tokens}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diagnostics\_trace\_plan}}) never appear in the
returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}} — they are emitted through
PlussMic’s internal warning log (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::codem::warn}}), a side channel
separate from the result value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{enable\_plan\_cache}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) memoizes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{parsed plan} keyed by the
exact rendered statement text (after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@\}}} substitution) — a statement
re\sphinxhyphen{}rendered to the same text skips re\sphinxhyphen{}parsing automatically, with no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} required. This is why \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}} (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{its reference page}}}}}) offers no
extra parsing\sphinxhyphen{}performance win beyond what repeated identical SQL text
already gets for free — its value is purely the ergonomics of not
re\sphinxhyphen{}typing/re\sphinxhyphen{}templating the same statement text at every call site.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The primary table name is always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}}, case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitively. Passing anything
else as the un\sphinxhyphen{}joined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FROM}} source only works if it’s a name bound via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions::sources}}.

\end{itemize}




\paragraph{P}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:p}}

\subparagraph{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{prepare}}}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:prepare}}

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:id9}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameSqlAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{prepare}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statement}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameSqlPrepared}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:id10}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stores the given statement text verbatim, together with a copy of this
accessor’s current frame and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}}, inside a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}}
value. \sphinxstylestrong{No parsing or validation happens at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} time} — the text is
only tokenized/parsed the first time it’s actually rendered and executed (via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared::execute(...)}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} exists purely so a
statement’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{text} can be built once and reused across several calls with
different scalar/identifier bindings, without retyping (or re\sphinxhyphen{}templating) it
each time.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:id11}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statement} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The (optionally parameterized) SQL text to store. May contain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{name\}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@name\}}} placeholders exactly like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute()}}’s argument — they’re just not
resolved until the prepared value is actually executed.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:id12}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}}
A reusable handle bound to this frame, this accessor’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}}, and
the given statement text. See its own
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{API reference}}}}} for the three
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute()}} overloads it exposes.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:id13}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Prepare a plain, unparameterized statement and run it with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared::execute()}} — no placeholders, no bindings, just a
stored statement you can re\sphinxhyphen{}run without retyping it.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:id16}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} never throws on a malformed or under\sphinxhyphen{}parameterized template by
itself — every check (unknown placeholder keys, missing required params,
unused params under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reject\_unused\_params}}, the SQL grammar itself) happens
inside the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute()}} call that follows, every time it’s called.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The captured \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sources}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collision\_policy}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{missing\_param\_policy}}, resource limits, and so on) come from \sphinxstylestrong{whichever
accessor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} was called on} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.sql(options).prepare(stmt)}}
bakes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} in as the base for every future execution; only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identifier\_params}} can still be layered on per\sphinxhyphen{}call, via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared::execute(...)}}’s arguments.

\end{itemize}



\sphinxstepscope




\subsubsection{DataFrameSqlPrepared API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference:dataframesqlprepared-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the reusable prepared\sphinxhyphen{}statement handle returned by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference:prepare}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlAccessor::prepare()}}}}}}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::prep\_sql()}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The table is named df, not self
Exactly like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlAccessor::execute()}}, a prepared statement addresses
its bound frame as \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT ... FROM df ...}}. There is no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}} bundles three things captured once, at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}}
time: the statement \sphinxstylestrong{text} (with any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{name\}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@name\}}} placeholders left
unresolved), a copy of the source \sphinxstylestrong{frame}, and a copy of the accessor’s
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}}} at that moment (its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sources}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collision\_policy}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{missing\_param\_policy}}, resource limits, and so on). Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute(...)}}
call layers fresh \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identifier\_params}} on top of that captured base —
it never mutates the prepared value itself, so the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}}
can be executed any number of times, with different bindings each time,
without rebuilding anything.


\paragraph{How To Use This Page}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference:how-to-use-this-page}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The three \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute()}} overloads are grouped together below since they’re
all one conceptual operation with progressively more binding power.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples reuse the same running dataset as the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlAccessor}} reference}}}}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{orders}}, plus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{managers}} for the JOIN example) so results are directly
comparable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each example is followed immediately by verified output hand\sphinxhyphen{}traced against
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSql.cpp}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Renders the captured statement text (substituting any supplied \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}/
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identifier\_params}} into its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{name\}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@name\}}} placeholders, on top of
whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identifier\_params}} were already present in the base
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} time), parses it, and runs it exactly like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlAccessor::execute()}} would — same pipeline, same resource
limits, same plan cache. The zero\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload is for statements with no
placeholders (or ones fully satisfied by base\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}} params already).
The one\sphinxhyphen{}map overload adds scalar bindings for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{name\}}} placeholders. The
two\sphinxhyphen{}map overload adds both scalar and identifier (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@name\}}}) bindings in the
same call.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{params} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::unordered\_map\textless{}std::string, DataFrame::SqlOptions::SqlParam\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Scalar values merged into the base \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions::params}} for this call only —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlParam}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::variant\textless{}std::nullptr\_t, bool, std::int64\_t, double, std::string\textgreater{}}}. Each entry overrides any base param of the same key.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{identifier\_params} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::unordered\_map\textless{}std::string, std::string\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Column/identifier names merged into the base \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions::identifier\_params}}
for this call only, resolved into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@name\}}} placeholders as backtick\sphinxhyphen{}quoted
identifiers.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
The same result \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlAccessor::execute(rendered\_statement)}} would
produce, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rendered\_statement}} is the prepared text after this
call’s placeholder substitution.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} happily stored \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"SELECT id FROM df WHERE region = \{region\}"}}
verbatim with no complaint — the placeholder is only discovered, and only
enforced against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MissingParamPolicy}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Error}} by default, the throw seen

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_sql_prepared_api_reference:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute(...)}} overload takes a private copy of the base \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}}
before merging in that call’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identifier\_params}} — the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}} value itself is never mutated, so it’s always safe to
call repeatedly, from multiple places, with different bindings each time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The automatic SQL plan cache (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions::enable\_plan\_cache}}, default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, keyed by exact rendered statement text) already avoids re\sphinxhyphen{}parsing
identical statement text on repeated calls, with no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} involved at
all. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlPrepared}}’s real value is therefore ergonomic — reusing a
statement’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{text} without retyping/re\sphinxhyphen{}templating it — not a parsing
speed\sphinxhyphen{}up the plan cache wasn’t already giving you.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{missing\_param\_policy}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reject\_unused\_params}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collision\_policy}},
resource limits, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sources}} all come from the base \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SqlOptions}} captured
at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prepare()}} time (i.e. whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sql(options)}} was called
with before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.prepare(...)}}). None of them can be changed per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute(...)}}
call — only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identifier\_params}} can.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_sql_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameSqlAccessor}} reference}}}}}
for the full SQL grammar, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case}} pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}column, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LEFT JOIN}}’s rejection,
and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResultMode::Chunked}} no\sphinxhyphen{}op gotcha — everything documented there for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute(statement)}} applies identically once the statement is rendered
here.

\end{itemize}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameNoteAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{casefold}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/casefold:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Produces a case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive\sphinxhyphen{}comparison form of every selected text feature’s
cells — conceptually similar to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}, but intended
specifically as a normalization step \sphinxstyleemphasis{before equality comparison}, not as a
display transform. The distinction matters in full Unicode case handling:
true Unicode case folding can differ from a simple lowercase mapping for
certain characters (the canonical example is German \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ß}}, which case\sphinxhyphen{}folds to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss}} rather than lowercasing to itself) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} is the method that’s
supposed to get that right, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} is not.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This build’s actual behavior
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}}’s Unicode\sphinxhyphen{}aware folding (handling cases like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ß}} \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss}}) is
only active when this build links the optional Unicode backend (GNU
libunistring). Without it, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} falls back to being \sphinxstylestrong{functionally
identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}} — same output, same ASCII\sphinxhyphen{}only
guarantees. On plain ASCII input, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} always produce
the same result regardless of build configuration, since ASCII case mapping
has no folding\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}lowering distinction to begin with. Confirm your build’s
Unicode support before relying on the two methods actually diverging.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like every method on this accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} applies to \sphinxstylestrong{every feature
the accessor was built with} in one call — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}} for
the shared mechanic and how null cells pass through unaffected.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}

this accessor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}, whenever the goal is a
case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive \sphinxstyleemphasis{comparison} — even though the two currently produce
identical output on ASCII text in every build, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}} states the
intent explicitly and is the one that picks up full Unicode folding
automatically if this build’s Unicode backend changes.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/chars:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Slices every selected text feature’s cells the same way Python slices a
string — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(start, stop, step)}} mirrors \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{s{[}start:stop:step{]}}} exactly,
including negative indices (counted from the end) and a negative step
(walking the string backwards). Each cell is split into individual
characters (Unicode codepoints, same unit {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}} counts
in), the slice is applied per\sphinxhyphen{}cell using that cell’s own length, and the
selected characters are rejoined into the output string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the slice bounds are evaluated per\sphinxhyphen{}cell using each cell’s own
length, cells of different lengths in the same feature can each keep a
different \sphinxstyleemphasis{number} of characters from the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(start, stop, step)}}
call — exactly as it would if you ran the equivalent Python slice
separately over each string.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/chars:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
Index of the first character to include. Negative values count from the
end of the cell (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} is the last character). Out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range values are
clamped, never throw.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Index one past the last character to include (exclusive), or the point
to stop just before when walking backwards. When omitted, defaults to
“the end of the string” if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step \textgreater{} 0}}, or “all the way to the start” if
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step \textless{} 0}} — i.e., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(0)}} returns the whole cell and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(\sphinxhyphen{}1,     std::nullopt, \sphinxhyphen{}1)}} reverses it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{step} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
Stride between characters. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} takes every character in order; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}
takes every other character; a negative step walks backwards. Must not
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars(0, std::nullopt, 0)}} throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::chars: step cannot be zero"}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/chars:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text replaced by the sliced
substring.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/chars:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Slices by Unicode codepoint, the same unit {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}}
counts — see that page’s caveat about codepoints vs. raw UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 storage
bytes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} values are clamped rather than throwing —
only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step == 0}} throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bounds are evaluated per\sphinxhyphen{}cell against that cell’s own length, so a single
call can keep a different number of characters from cells of different
lengths (Examples 1 and 2).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\end{itemize}
