\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping occurrences of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} in every selected text
feature’s cells, replacing each cell with an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} — the feature’s
payload kind changes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{danger}{Danger:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload defaults to REGEX mode, not literal
This is the single easiest mistake to make on this accessor.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count(pattern)}} with no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} is \sphinxstylestrong{not} the literal\sphinxhyphen{}text search you
might expect from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}}’s single\sphinxhyphen{}argument default — internally
it calls the two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{.regex = true\}}}. That means any
regex metacharacter in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{]}}}, and so on) is interpreted as a pattern instruction, not a literal
character. Counting literal periods, parentheses, or other punctuation with
the single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload will silently produce the wrong number — see
Example 1, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count(".")}} counts \sphinxstyleemphasis{every character} in each cell, not
the count of literal dots. Pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{.regex = false\}}} explicitly (or escape
the pattern) whenever the search text might contain characters regex would
interpret specially.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload takes an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, letting you
choose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_sensitive}} independently, and cap the count with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}, meaning unlimited):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{struct}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{TextOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{regex}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}sensitive}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{part}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// unused by count()}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Matches never overlap: once a match is found, scanning resumes right after
it, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count("aa")}} on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"aaaa"}} reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The text to count — a regular expression pattern under the
single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload (see the warning above), or literal/regex text
under the two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload depending on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload only)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} as a regex instead
of literal text.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): ASCII\sphinxhyphen{}fold both sides before
comparing (literal mode) or compile with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex::icase}} (regex
mode) when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}): stop counting once this many matches
have been found; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means no cap.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature replaced by an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} Series
of match counts.

that changed is whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} was left at its (very different)

\sphinxAtStartPar

both are reported as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} — counting stops the moment the limit is reached,
rather than continuing and clamping the final number.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{.regex = true\}}} — see the
danger callout above. This is the opposite default from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}}’s single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload, which defaults to literal
mode.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matches are always non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping: after a match, scanning resumes
immediately past it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output (evaluated internally as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}
but re\sphinxhyphen{}masked to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} before returning).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} is part of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}} but has no effect on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}
— it’s only meaningful to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameNoteAccessor::encode}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/encode:dataframenoteaccessor-encode}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/encode::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/encode:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected text feature’s cells with an encoded form of their
raw bytes, choosing between three schemes via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encoding}} argument:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}} (the default), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}}. Unlike most methods on this
accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} doesn’t validate its argument against an enum — any
other string throws.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}}}: standard Base64 (RFC 4648), using the classic alphabet
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}) with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}} padding to a multiple of 4
output characters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}}}: lowercase hexadecimal, two characters per input byte (so the
output is always exactly twice as long as the input, in bytes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}}}: percent\sphinxhyphen{}encoding (RFC 3986) — letters, digits, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}}} pass through unchanged; every other byte becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%XX}} with two \sphinxstylestrong{uppercase} hex digits.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encode only — no decode() on this accessor
This accessor exposes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{encode()}} but no corresponding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decode()}}. There’s
no built\sphinxhyphen{}in way to reverse the transform through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor}}
itself.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/encode:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{encoding} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}})
Which scheme to apply: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"base64"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}}. Any other value
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::encode: encoding must be base64, hex, or url"}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/encode:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text replaced by its encoded
form.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/encode:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Encodes raw bytes, not Unicode codepoints — for ASCII text, “bytes” and
“characters” coincide, but multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 characters encode as their
full multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte sequence, not as one unit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hex"}} output is always lowercase; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"url"}} percent\sphinxhyphen{}escapes use uppercase
hex digits — the two schemes intentionally differ in this convention,
matching common real\sphinxhyphen{}world usage of each format.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind but stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (text in, text out) —
unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}}, which switches to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decode()}} exists on this accessor — see the note above.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/ends:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks every selected text feature’s cells for a literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive
suffix match, replacing each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell’s
text ends with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{suffix}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t. This is the mirror image
of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/starts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts()}}}}}}}: same single\sphinxhyphen{}overload, no\sphinxhyphen{}options shape, just
anchored at the end of the string instead of the beginning. As with every
boolean\sphinxhyphen{}producing method on this accessor, the feature’s payload kind
changes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ends()}} has exactly one overload — always literal, always case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive,
no regex mode. For a case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive or pattern\sphinxhyphen{}based suffix check, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}} with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}} and a trailing anchor (e.g.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has("suffix\$", \{.regex = true\})}}), or normalize case first with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/casefold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/ends:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{suffix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The literal text to check for at the end of each cell. An empty suffix
matches every non\sphinxhyphen{}null cell (every string ends with the empty string).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/ends:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature replaced by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} Series:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell ends with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{suffix}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/ends:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive, literal comparison only — no regex mode, no
case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitivity toggle. See Example 2 for the normalize\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}check
pattern that works around this.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pairs naturally with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::filter()}} (via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.features(name)}} to pull
the single\sphinxhyphen{}column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} result out) to keep only matching rows — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/starts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts()}}}}}}}’s Example 2 for the pattern.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameNoteAccessor::extract}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract:dataframenoteaccessor-extract}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{msharp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Of}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{names}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Searches every cell of the \sphinxstylestrong{single selected text feature} for the first
match of a regular expression \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}, and expands each capture group
into its own output column — one column per group, in group order. It’s
the capture\sphinxhyphen{}group counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}: where
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}} collects every match’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{entire} matched text, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}}
takes apart the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} match into its named or numbered pieces.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
extract() requires exactly one selected feature
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition()}}}}}}},
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}} operates on exactly one
column. Calling it through an accessor built from more than one feature
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::note().extract requires one feature"}}. Build the
accessor from a single feature: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{"code"\}).note().extract(...)}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} must contain at least one capture group — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract("no groups here")}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::extract: pattern needs a capture group"}}. The
search is unanchored (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex\_search}}, like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}}’s regex mode,
not a whole\sphinxhyphen{}cell {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}}}}}}}) and only the \sphinxstylestrong{first}
match in each cell is used; if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} could match more than once,
everything after the first match is ignored for that row.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Naming the output columns.} By default, columns are named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_0}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_1}}, … in capture\sphinxhyphen{}group order. Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} overrides this —
but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names.size()}} must exactly equal the number of capture groups in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}, or the call throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::extract: names must match capture groups"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Optional groups that don’t participate.} A capture group inside an
optional construct (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(...)?}}, one alternative of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, and so on) can
match successfully overall while that particular group captures nothing.
When that happens, the group’s cell for that row is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — genuinely
different from that row simply not matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} at all, but
indistinguishable from it in the output alone (both show as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}). See
Example 2.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
A regular expression pattern (ECMAScript syntax) containing at least
one capture group \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(...)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Column names for each capture group, in order. Leave empty for the
default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_1}}, … naming, or supply exactly one name
per capture group.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the selected column replaced by one column per
capture group in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}. A row where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} didn’t match at all
is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every group column; a row where it matched but a
particular optional group didn’t participate is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in just that
group’s column.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the accessor to be built from exactly \sphinxstylestrong{one} feature — see the
important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses an unanchored search (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex\_search}}) and only the \sphinxstylestrong{first} match
per cell — a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} that could match multiple times in a cell still
only produces one row’s worth of group values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} must contain at least one capture group; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}, if given,
must have exactly one entry per group.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A row with no match at all is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every output column; a row that
matched but left one particular optional group empty is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in just
that column — see Example 2.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall:dataframenoteaccessor-findall}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finds every match of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} in each cell of the \sphinxstylestrong{single selected text
feature} and expands the result into one output column per match position
— column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_0}} holds each row’s first match, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_1}} its second, and
so on. Rows with fewer matches than another row simply have \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the
columns beyond their own match count; the number of output columns is
however many matches the \sphinxstyleemphasis{most\sphinxhyphen{}matching} row produced.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
findall() requires exactly one selected feature
Unlike most methods on this accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}} (like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}}}}}})
operates on exactly one column, not “every feature the accessor was built
with.” Calling it through an accessor built from more than one feature — e.g.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{"a", "b"\}).note().findall(...)}} — throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::note().findall requires one feature"}}. Build the accessor with
a single feature name for these methods:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{"city"\}).note().findall(...)}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{danger}{Danger:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload defaults to regex mode, same gotcha as count()
Exactly like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}}}}}}, the single\sphinxhyphen{}argument \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall(pattern)}}
defaults internally to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{.regex = true\}}} — a literal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"."}} is interpreted
as “match any character,” not a literal period. See Example 1, where the
default call splits every cell into one match per \sphinxstyleemphasis{character}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output DataFrame keeps the original frame’s row labels and title —
only the single selected column is replaced, by the expanded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_N}}
columns.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
A regular expression pattern under the single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload (always
regex mode — see the danger box above), or literal/regex text under the
two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload depending on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload only)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} as regex instead of
literal text.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive matching
when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}): cap the number of matches collected per
row (and therefore an upper bound on the number of output columns).
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} is \sphinxstylestrong{not} used by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}} — output columns are
always named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_1}}, and so on, regardless of what
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} is set to. (Contrast {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}}}}}}, which do honor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}}.)


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the selected column replaced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_1}},
… columns (as many as the row with the most matches needed), keeping
every other feature and the original row labels untouched. A row with
fewer matches than the column count has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the extra columns.

(three matches) sets the output at three \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_N}} columns, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hi"}}’s

collapses to a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_0}} column that’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} everywhere except that
one row.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the accessor to be built from exactly \sphinxstylestrong{one} feature — see the
important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{.regex = true\}}} — the same
gotcha documented on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output columns are always named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_1}}, … —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} has no effect here (contrast {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}} /
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}}}}}}, which do use it).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of output columns equals the largest per\sphinxhyphen{}row match count
(after any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} is applied); rows with fewer matches get \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the
extra columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid input cell contributes zero matches (all its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match\_N}} cells
are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}), the same as a cell with genuinely no matches — there is no
way to distinguish “invalid row” from “row that matched nothing” in the
output alone.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tests every selected text feature’s cells against a regular expression,
requiring the pattern to match the \sphinxstylestrong{entire} cell (start to end), and
replaces each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch(pattern)}} is not a separate
implementation — it’s defined purely as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches(pattern, true)}}; see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}}}}}} for the full explanation of how this whole\sphinxhyphen{}cell
mode differs from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}’s default start\sphinxhyphen{}anchored\sphinxhyphen{}only behavior.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent to matches(pattern, true)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch(pattern)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches(pattern, true)}} are two ways to write
literally the same call. Reach for whichever reads more clearly at the call
site — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}} states the “must match completely” intent more
directly, while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches(pattern, true)}} is convenient when the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full}} flag
is itself a variable.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
A regular expression pattern (ECMAScript syntax, via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex}}) that
must match the cell’s entire text to report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature replaced by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} Series:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell’s entire text matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}
otherwise.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Purely \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches(pattern, true)}} under the hood — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}}}}}} for the shared mechanics (validity passthrough,
regex compilation, error behavior).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciicircum{}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$}} anchors in the pattern are redundant (but harmless) here, since
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}} already requires the whole cell to match.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid regex pattern throws at call time (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::fullmatch: invalid regular expression: ..."}}).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks every selected text feature’s cells for the presence of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{needle}}
anywhere in the cell, replacing each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}. It’s the general
substring/pattern search on this accessor — where {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/starts::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts()}}}}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/ends::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ends()}}}}}}} only check the two ends of the string, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}} looks
everywhere, and it can be switched between a plain literal search and a
regular\sphinxhyphen{}expression search via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}} (namespace\sphinxhyphen{}scope in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread.h}}, used unqualified) has four
fields, though only two matter to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{struct}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{TextOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{regex}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}sensitive}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{// unused by has()}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{part}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// unused by has()}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
That default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}) makes a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(needle)}} call a \sphinxstylestrong{literal,
case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive substring search} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{needle}} is matched character\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}character,
not compiled as a pattern.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different from count()/findall()’s single\sphinxhyphen{}argument default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(needle)}} with no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} searches \sphinxstyleemphasis{literally}. This is easy to
confuse with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}, whose
single\sphinxhyphen{}argument overloads default internally to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{.regex = true\}}} instead —
so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(pattern)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count(pattern)}} treat the exact same string
differently unless you pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} explicitly. If a pattern with regex
metacharacters (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, and so on) doesn’t seem to be
matching under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}, this default is the first thing to check — pass
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{.regex = true\}}} explicitly to search by pattern instead of literal text.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex = true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{needle}} is compiled as an ECMAScript regular
expression (via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex}}) and each cell is tested with a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex\_search}} — a \sphinxstyleemphasis{contains} semantics, matching anywhere in the cell, not
anchored to the whole string (contrast {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}}}}}}}, which
requires the whole cell to match).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_sensitive = false}} works in both modes: for literal search it
ASCII\sphinxhyphen{}folds both the needle and the haystack before comparing; for regex
search it compiles the pattern with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex::icase}} flag.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{needle} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The text to search for — a literal substring by default, or a regular
expression pattern when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{needle}} as a regex pattern
instead of literal text.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, the search
ignores case (ASCII fold for literal mode, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex::icase}} for
regex mode).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature replaced by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} Series:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell contains a match, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions\{\}}} means literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive — unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}, whose single\sphinxhyphen{}argument
overloads default to regex mode. See the warning above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex = true}} uses \sphinxstyleemphasis{contains} semantics (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex\_search}}, matches
anywhere in the cell) — for a whole\sphinxhyphen{}cell match use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}}}}}}}, and for a start\sphinxhyphen{}anchored pattern use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid pattern under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex = true}} throws at the point
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}} is called (regex compilation is validated eagerly).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{+w}{                                 }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Splits every cell of the \sphinxstylestrong{single selected text feature} on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delimiter}},
collects every distinct non\sphinxhyphen{}empty token seen anywhere in the column, and
produces one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} column per distinct token (“level”) — the classic
one\sphinxhyphen{}hot / multi\sphinxhyphen{}label indicator (“dummy variable”) encoding, for a text
column that holds delimiter\sphinxhyphen{}separated tags, categories, or labels rather
than a single value per cell. Column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\textless{}level\textgreater{}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for a row
if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{level}} is one of that row’s tokens, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} otherwise.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Levels are collected into a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::set\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}, so the output columns
always appear in \sphinxstylestrong{sorted (alphabetical) order} — not first\sphinxhyphen{}seen order,
and not any order tied to the input data’s row sequence.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
indicate() requires exactly one selected feature
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}}}}}}},
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}} operates on exactly one
column — calling it through a multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature accessor throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::note().indicate requires one feature"}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{danger}{Danger:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
indicate() never attaches a validity mask — invalid rows are just all\sphinxhyphen{}false, not NULL
Unlike every other method on this accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}’s output columns
carry \sphinxstylestrong{no validity mask at all}. A row that was invalid on input doesn’t
show \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the indicator columns — it shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} in every one of
them, exactly the same as a row that’s genuinely valid but happens to match
none of the levels. There is no way to tell “this row is invalid” apart
from “this row matched nothing” by looking at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}’s output alone.
See Example 1.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid row’s hidden text can still create a phantom output column
The set of levels is collected from \sphinxstylestrong{every row’s underlying text},
including rows marked invalid — the delimiter split that builds the level
set runs over the whole column before any validity check happens. An
invalid cell whose hidden underlying text contains a token no valid row
ever uses still produces its own indicator column, one that’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for
every row in the entire result (since no valid row can ever match it, and
the invalid row itself is skipped when indicators are actually computed).
See Example 2 — this is the same category of surprise documented on
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}’s single\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter overload.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{delimiter} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"|"}})
The literal text to split each cell on before collecting tokens. Must
not be empty — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate("")}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::indicate: delimiter     cannot be empty"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}})
Text prepended to each level to form its column name — with the
default empty prefix, a column is named exactly after the level text
itself (e.g. a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"red"}} token produces a column literally named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{red}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the selected column replaced by one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} column per
distinct non\sphinxhyphen{}empty token seen in the column, sorted alphabetically by
token text, named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\textless{}level\textgreater{}}}.

ever mention. It still produces a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{know\_mars}} column, one that reads

never say \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mars"}}), and row 3 itself is skipped when indicators are
computed (since it’s invalid), so the column simply exists as inert
padding. Without looking at the raw construction data, there would be no
way to know \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{know\_mars}} came from an invisible invalid cell rather than
from a genuinely rare but real tag.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the accessor to be built from exactly \sphinxstylestrong{one} feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output columns are sorted alphabetically by token text, not by
first\sphinxhyphen{}appearance order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No validity mask is attached to the result at all — invalid input rows
show \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} everywhere, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. See the danger box above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The level set is collected from every row’s raw text regardless of
validity, so an invalid row can introduce an all\sphinxhyphen{}false phantom column.
See the warning above and Example 2.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delimiter}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::indicate: delimiter cannot be empty"}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor::split}}}}}}}: the same underlying
delimiter\sphinxhyphen{}split mechanic, producing positional columns instead of

\subparagraph{DataFrameNoteAccessor::length}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length:dataframenoteaccessor-length}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameNoteAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{length}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected text feature with its character count, as an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — same feature name, same row order, but the feature’s payload kind
changes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}. Unlike most of this accessor’s methods,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}} doesn’t return text at all.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts Unicode codepoints, not bytes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}} counts \sphinxstyleemphasis{characters} (Unicode codepoints), not raw UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 storage
bytes. For plain ASCII text the two are identical, so this distinction is
invisible — but any character outside the ASCII range (an accented letter, a
currency symbol, an emoji, and so on) is encoded as more than one byte in
UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 while still counting as exactly one character. See Example 2.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature replaced by its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}
character count; every other feature is left unchanged.


\subparagraph{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}’ first row is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Price: \texteuro{}50"}} (the Euro sign, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}xE2\textbackslash{}x82\textbackslash{}xAC}} in UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8
— three storage bytes) followed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"50"}}: 10 characters total (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{r}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, a space, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\texteuro{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}), even though the underlying byte
count is 12. The third row, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Fee: £5"}}, has the two\sphinxhyphen{}byte Pound sign (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{£}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}xC2\textbackslash{}xA3}}) and comes to 7 characters against 8 storage bytes. The middle
row, pure ASCII, has an identical character and byte count (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}} either way)
— it’s included as a control case showing where the two measures agree.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A related renderer quirk
The plain\sphinxhyphen{}text table renderer used throughout these docs pads and aligns
table cells by raw byte length, not by character count, when it lays out a
column’s width — a cosmetic\sphinxhyphen{}only detail unrelated to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}’s own
result, but worth knowing if a column containing multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 text ever
looks slightly misaligned when printed.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}}) — chain
a numeric operation (comparison, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/bucketize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bucketize()}}}}}}},
arithmetic) directly onto the result if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts Unicode codepoints, not raw UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 storage bytes — see the caveat and
Example 2 above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output, same as every other method on
this accessor.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lowercases every character in every selected text feature’s cells, returning
a new frame — the classic normalization step before a case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive
comparison, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_by()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by()}} key that shouldn’t be split by
casing accidents, or a lookup against a canonical lowercase reference list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like every method on this accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} applies to \sphinxstylestrong{every feature the
accessor was built with} in one call — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}} for the
full explanation of that shared mechanic (including the two ways to reach
the accessor) and how null cells pass through unaffected.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
ASCII vs. Unicode case mapping
On plain ASCII text, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} behaves exactly as you’d expect: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}
becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}}, everything else is untouched. Non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII (accented Latin,
Cyrillic, Greek, and so on) case mapping depends on whether this build was
linked against the optional Unicode backend (GNU libunistring); when it
isn’t, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} only recognizes ASCII letters and leaves non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII bytes as
they are (or, depending on build configuration, rejects them). Confirm your
build’s Unicode support before relying on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} for non\sphinxhyphen{}Latin or
accented text.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text lowercased; every
non\sphinxhyphen{}alphabetic character (digits, punctuation, whitespace) is left
exactly as it was.

The left\sphinxhyphen{}only half of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}}: trims characters from the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{start} of every selected text feature’s cells, leaving the trailing end
completely untouched. Same two policies as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar

only — every leading character that’s a member of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} is peeled off,

Everything else about how the accessor applies an operation — to every
selected feature in one call, leaving null cells null, and reachable either

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tests every selected text feature’s cells against a regular expression,
replacing each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full}} flag switches between two
different anchoring behaviors:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full = false}}} (the default): the pattern is anchored to the \sphinxstylestrong{start}
of the cell only — internally, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} is wrapped as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textasciicircum{}(?:" + pattern + ")"}} and searched with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex\_search}}. A match at the
beginning is enough; anything after the matched portion is ignored. This
is \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} a full\sphinxhyphen{}string match, despite the method name — a pattern that
matches only the first few characters of a longer cell still reports
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full = true}}}: the pattern must match the \sphinxstylestrong{entire} cell,
start to end (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex\_match}} semantics) — equivalent to calling
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch(pattern)}}}}}}} directly. In fact, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}} is
implemented as nothing more than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches(pattern, true)}}.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
matches() without full=true is a start\sphinxhyphen{}anchored search, not a whole\sphinxhyphen{}cell match
The default call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches(pattern)}} only requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} to match
starting at position 0 — it does \sphinxstylestrong{not} require the match to consume the
whole cell. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches("A{[}0\sphinxhyphen{}9{]}+")}} against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"A123XYZ"}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, because
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"A123"}} matches starting at the beginning even though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"XYZ"}} is left
over. If a whole\sphinxhyphen{}cell match is what’s actually needed, pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full = true}}
or call {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}}}}}}} — see Example 1 for the contrast.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
A regular expression pattern (ECMAScript syntax, via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{full} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}: match anchored at the start only. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}: the pattern must
match the entire cell — identical to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch(pattern)}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature replaced by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} Series:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell matches, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full = false}} (the default) is a start\sphinxhyphen{}anchored \sphinxstyleemphasis{search}, not a
whole\sphinxhyphen{}string match — see the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{full = true}} is identical to calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}}}}}}}
directly; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}} is implemented purely in terms of this call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid regex pattern throws at call time, before any row is
evaluated.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor::findall}}}}}}} / {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}}}}}}}:
return the matched text itself, instead of just a boolean.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameNoteAccessor::normalize}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:dataframenoteaccessor-normalize}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameNoteAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{form}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFC}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies Unicode text normalization to every selected feature’s cells,
choosing one of the four standard Unicode Normalization Forms via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{form}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{enum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// Canonical Decomposition, followed by Canonical Composition}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// Canonical Decomposition}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFKC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// Compatibility Decomposition, followed by Canonical Composition}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{NFKD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// Compatibility Decomposition}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalization matters for text that might contain the same visible
character represented in more than one way — most commonly, a precomposed
accented letter (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{é}} as a single codepoint) versus a base letter plus a
combining mark (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e}} + a combining acute accent, two codepoints that render
identically). Two byte\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}byte\sphinxhyphen{}different strings can look identical and
still compare unequal with a plain {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/eq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eq()}}}}}}}; running
both through the same normalization form first makes such comparisons
consistent.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the optional Unicode backend (GNU libunistring) for anything beyond plain ASCII
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize()}}’s real behavior depends entirely on whether this build links
libunistring:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{With the backend}: all four forms are fully implemented via the
standard \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uninorm\_normalize}} routine, correctly handling precomposed and
decomposed Unicode text.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Without the backend}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize()}} still accepts pure\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII input —
and, since plain ASCII has no combining marks, ligatures, or
compatibility characters to normalize in the first place, every form
behaves as an identity transform and returns the input unchanged (see
Example 1). But any \sphinxstylestrong{non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII} input throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Note::normalize: non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII text requires a Unicode backend"}} — there is
no partial or best\sphinxhyphen{}effort fallback for non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII text.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Confirm this build’s Unicode support before relying on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize()}} for
any text that might contain non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII characters.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{form} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnicodeForm}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnicodeForm::NFC}})
Which normalization form to apply: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFC}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFD}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFKC}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFKD}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text normalized to the
requested form.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Plain ASCII text under the default form (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFC}}) — a no\sphinxhyphen{}op,
since ASCII has nothing to normalize, and this behavior holds regardless
of whether this build links the Unicode backend.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{title}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Hello World}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ASCII text only}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out1}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (before, identical to output after)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:output-before-identical-to-output-after}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
======================
     | title          
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | Hello World    
1    | ASCII text only
2    | NULL           
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[3 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output is byte\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}byte identical to the input: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NFC}} (like every
other form, on ASCII) has nothing to canonicalize when there are no
combining marks or compatibility characters present. The invalid third row
stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, same as every other method on this accessor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Explicitly requesting each of the four forms on the same ASCII
input — all four produce the identical result, since the distinctions
between NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD only matter for text containing decomposable or
compatibility characters, none of which plain ASCII has.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFC}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFD}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfkc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFKC}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nfkd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{titles}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{UnicodeForm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NFKD}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+c1}{// nfc, nfd, nfkc, and nfkd are all identical to titles here.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII input without the Unicode backend throws — shown here
as the documented failure mode rather than a specific transformed value,
since the exact behavior depends on this build’s optional dependency (see
the important callout above).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{accented}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{word}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{caf}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}xC3}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}xA9}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZdq{}café\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{try}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{accented}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{catch}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{exception}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{what}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output (build without the Unicode backend)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:output-build-without-the-unicode-backend}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Note::normalize: non\PYGZhy{}ASCII text requires a Unicode backend
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A build with libunistring linked would instead perform genuine Unicode
normalization on this input rather than throwing — but the exact
byte\sphinxhyphen{}level output in that case isn’t asserted here, since it depends on a
build\sphinxhyphen{}time optional dependency rather than anything guaranteed by the
public API alone.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/normalize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All four \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnicodeForm}} values are identity transforms on pure ASCII
text, with or without the Unicode backend.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII input throws outright when this build lacks libunistring —
there is no partial fallback. See the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies to every feature the accessor was built with, in one call — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}}’s Notes for the mechanics shared by every method on
this accessor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameNoteAccessor::pad}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/pad:dataframenoteaccessor-pad}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/pad::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/pad:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameNoteAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pad}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{width}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                            }\PYG{n}{TextAlign}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{align}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TextAlign}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Left}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                            }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fill}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/pad:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grows every selected text feature’s cells up to a target character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}}
by adding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} characters, positioning the original text according to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{enum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{TextAlign}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Left}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Right}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Center}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Left}}} (the default): the original text is left\sphinxhyphen{}aligned —
fill characters are added on the \sphinxstylestrong{right}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Right}}}: the original text is right\sphinxhyphen{}aligned — fill
characters are added on the \sphinxstylestrong{left}. The classic use is zero\sphinxhyphen{}padding
numeric\sphinxhyphen{}looking codes (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"7"}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"0007"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Center}}}: fill is split between both sides. When the
amount needed is odd, the \sphinxstylestrong{extra} fill character goes on the right
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left = needed / 2}}, integer division; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right = needed \sphinxhyphen{} left}}).

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
pad() only ever grows a cell, never shrinks it
If a cell is already at least \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} characters long, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad()}} leaves it
completely unchanged — there’s no truncation mode. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} is measured in
Unicode codepoints, the same unit {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}} counts (see that
page’s caveat about codepoints vs. raw UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 storage bytes).
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Padding is invisible in a rendered table when fill is a space
The default fill character is a space, and the plain\sphinxhyphen{}text table renderer
used throughout these docs \sphinxstyleemphasis{also} right\sphinxhyphen{}pads cells to align columns — so a
space\sphinxhyphen{}padded cell and the renderer’s own column\sphinxhyphen{}alignment padding look
identical side by side. The examples below use a visible fill character
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}}) for the alignment demonstrations so the padding itself is visible in
the rendered table; the practical zero\sphinxhyphen{}padding example (Example 2) uses
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{}0\textquotesingle{}}}, which is visible for the same reason.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/pad:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{width} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})
The target character width. Must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}= 0}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad(\sphinxhyphen{}1)}} throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::pad: width must be \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{align} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextAlign::Left}})
Where the fill characters go: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}} pads on the right, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}} pads
on the left, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Center}} splits the fill (extra character on the right
for an odd amount).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fill} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textquotesingle{} \textquotesingle{}}})
The single character used to pad. Note this is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, not a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} — multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 fill sequences aren’t supported.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/pad:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text padded to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}}
characters (or left unchanged, for cells already at or beyond that
width).


\subparagraph{Examples}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/pad:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pad()}} only grows; a cell already at or beyond \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} is returned
unchanged, never truncated.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} is measured in Unicode codepoints, the same unit
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/length::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length()}}}}}}} counts.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} is a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char}}, not a string — no multi\sphinxhyphen{}byte UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 fill
characters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Center}}’s extra fill character (when the amount needed is odd) always
goes on the right.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A space fill (the default) is visually indistinguishable from the
rendered table’s own column\sphinxhyphen{}alignment padding — see the tip above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width \textless{} 0}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::pad: width must be \textgreater{}= 0"}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition:dataframenoteaccessor-partition}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}
