\PYG{+w}{                                  }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prefix}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{part}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Splits every cell of the \sphinxstylestrong{single selected text feature} at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first}
occurrence of a literal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}, always producing exactly \sphinxstylestrong{three}
output columns: the text before the separator, the separator itself, and
the text after it. It’s a narrower, simpler cousin of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}
— always literal (no regex), always stops at the first match, and always
exactly three columns regardless of the input.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
partition() requires exactly one selected feature
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}}}}}}},
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition()}} operates on exactly one
column — calling it through a multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature accessor throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::note().partition requires one feature"}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing separator produces empty strings, not NULL
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}} doesn’t occur in a cell at all, that row’s middle and
third columns are set to the \sphinxstylestrong{empty string} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — the row
itself is still valid, it simply had nothing to split. This is a
meaningfully different behavior from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}, where a row that produced fewer pieces than the
widest row gets genuine \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s in the missing columns. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition()}}’s
validity for all three output columns is copied directly from the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{original row’s own validity} — a valid input row is valid in all three
output columns even when the separator wasn’t found; only a row that was
already invalid on input produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in all three. See Example 1.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{separator} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The literal text to split on. Must not be empty — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition("")}}
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::partition: separator cannot be empty"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}})

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_1}} (the separator, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{""}} if not found), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_2}}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the accessor to be built from exactly \sphinxstylestrong{one} feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always literal (no regex mode) and always stops at the \sphinxstyleemphasis{first}
occurrence — for a regex\sphinxhyphen{}aware or multi\sphinxhyphen{}way split, use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}}}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always produces exactly three output columns, regardless of the input.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A missing separator yields empty strings in the second and third
columns, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — see the important callout above. Only a row that
was already invalid on input produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in any of the three
columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::partition: separator cannot be empty"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/replace:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces occurrences of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} in every selected text feature’s
cells, returning a new frame. Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/count::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}}}}}}, the two\sphinxhyphen{}argument
overload’s default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}) is a \sphinxstylestrong{literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive, unlimited}
replace — but unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}, this default matches what the
single\sphinxhyphen{}argument\sphinxhyphen{}style call actually does, so there’s no regex\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}default
surprise here: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to, \{\})}} are exactly
the same call.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Verified fast path: replace(from, to) and replace(from, to, \{\}) are byte\sphinxhyphen{}identical
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} is left at its default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex = false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_sensitive = true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = \sphinxhyphen{}1}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}} takes a fast path straight to the
underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note::replace}} primitive — the same code path the
two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload uses. There is no behavioral difference between the
two spellings; the two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload exists purely for convenience
when no options are needed.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} controls three independent things:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} as a regular
expression instead of literal text. Regex replacement text (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}})
supports ECMAScript\sphinxhyphen{}style backreferences (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$2}}, …) to capture
groups in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}): when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, matching
ignores case (ASCII fold), but the replacement text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} is inserted
exactly as given — case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive \sphinxstyleemphasis{matching} doesn’t mean
case\sphinxhyphen{}preserving \sphinxstyleemphasis{replacement}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}): caps the number of replacements per
cell; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means unlimited. Matches are always non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping — after a
replacement, scanning resumes right after the inserted \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} text, not
back inside it.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} is not used by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/replace:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{from} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The literal text or regex pattern to search for. An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} under
literal mode is a no\sphinxhyphen{}op (the cell is returned unchanged).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The replacement text. Under regex mode, may contain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$2}}, …
backreferences to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}}’s capture groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload only)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}} as described
above.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/replace:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text transformed by the
replacement.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(\textbackslash{}w+)@(\textbackslash{}w+)}} captures the text before and after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\$2\#\$1"}} swaps them
around a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#}}. Row 2 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"invalid"}}) has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} at all, so the pattern doesn’t
match and the text is returned unchanged — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regex\_replace}} leaves
non\sphinxhyphen{}matching text exactly as it was, it never errors on a cell with zero
matches.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/replace:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace(from, to, \{\})}} are the exact same
operation — see the note above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} under literal mode is a no\sphinxhyphen{}op (returns the cell
unchanged); this check happens before any matching is attempted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matches never overlap: after a replacement, scanning resumes
immediately past the inserted \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} text.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_sensitive = false}} affects matching only — the replacement text is
always inserted exactly as given, never case\sphinxhyphen{}adjusted to match what was
found.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Regex mode supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$2}}, … backreferences in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} has no effect on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replace()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/rstrip:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}only half of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}}: trims characters from the \sphinxstyleemphasis{end}
of every selected text feature’s cells, leaving the leading edge completely
untouched. Same two policies as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lstrip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lstrip()}}}}}}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload}: trims the classic ASCII whitespace set (space,
tab, newline, carriage return, form feed, vertical tab) from the right edge
only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} overload}: trims by character\sphinxhyphen{}set membership from the right
edge only — every trailing character that’s a member of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} is peeled
off, one at a time, until a character outside the set is reached. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}} for the full explanation of why this is
set\sphinxhyphen{}membership, not literal substring matching.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Everything else — applying to every selected feature in one call, leaving
null cells null, and the two ways to reach the accessor — is identical to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}}; see that page for the full explanation.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/rstrip:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{chars} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}}\sphinxhyphen{}overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The set of characters to strip from each cell’s right edge only.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/rstrip:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text right\sphinxhyphen{}trimmed; the leading
edge of every cell is preserved byte\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}byte.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Splits every cell of the \sphinxstylestrong{single selected text feature} on a delimiter,
expanding the result into one output column per split position — column
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part\_0}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}}) holds each row’s first piece, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part\_1}} its
second, and so on, the same column\sphinxhyphen{}expansion shape {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}}}}}}} use. There are two overloads with different
delimiter semantics:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split(delimiter, limit, prefix)}}}: always a literal substring split
(never regex), with an optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} on how many splits to perform
and a customizable column\sphinxhyphen{}name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split(pattern, options)}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} is literal or regex depending on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}} caps the split count and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} names the columns (both fields of the same
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}} struct used throughout this accessor).

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
split() requires exactly one selected feature
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/findall::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/extract::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{extract()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/partition::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition()}}}}}}},
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/indicate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{indicate()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}} operates on exactly one column —
calling it through a multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature accessor throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::note().split requires one feature"}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both overloads produce ragged results the same way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{findall()}} does: a row
with fewer pieces than the widest row is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the extra columns, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} caps the number of splits performed (a split of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a/b/c"}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit = 1}} yields two pieces, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}"a", "b/c"{]}}} — the remainder after the
capped split stays joined, it isn’t dropped).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two overloads compute the output column count differently for invalid rows
The single\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter overload (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split(delimiter, limit, prefix)}}) determines
the output column count from \sphinxstylestrong{every} row’s underlying text — including
rows the caller marked invalid — because it works from a raw, validity\sphinxhyphen{}unaware
split computed once over the whole column. A constructed\sphinxhyphen{}invalid cell whose
underlying stored text happens to contain many delimiters can inflate the
column count even though that row shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every one of them. The
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(pattern, options)}} overload does not have this quirk: it only computes
each row’s split (and therefore only contributes to the column count) for
rows that are actually valid. See Example 4 for a side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side
demonstration with identical data under both overloads.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{delimiter} / \sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The literal delimiter (first overload) or literal/regex pattern (second
overload, depending on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}}) to split on. An empty delimiter
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::split: delimiter cannot be empty"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{limit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, first overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}})
Maximum number of splits to perform (producing at most \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit + 1}}
pieces); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} means unlimited.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, first overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}})
Base name for the output columns: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_1}}, …

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}}, second overload)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.regex}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): treat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} as regex.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.limit}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}): cap the number of splits.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.prefix}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"part"}}): base name for output columns.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} is \sphinxstylestrong{not} used by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the selected column replaced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_0}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}prefix\textgreater{}\_1}}, … columns (as many as the widest split needs), keeping
every other feature and the original row labels. Rows with fewer
pieces are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in the extra columns.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/split:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires the accessor to be built from exactly \sphinxstylestrong{one} feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty delimiter/pattern throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Thread::split: delimiter cannot be empty"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} caps the \sphinxstyleemphasis{number of splits}, not the \sphinxstyleemphasis{number of output columns}
directly — the capped remainder stays joined in the last piece (Example 2).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two overloads compute the output width differently for invalid
rows — see the warning above and Example 4.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.case\_sensitive}} has no effect on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{split()}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/starts:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks every selected text feature’s cells for a literal, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive
prefix match, replacing each cell with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell’s
text begins with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t. The feature’s payload
kind changes from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}), same as every other
boolean\sphinxhyphen{}producing method on this accessor ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/fullmatch::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fullmatch()}}}}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{starts()}} has exactly one overload and takes no options — it is always a
plain, case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive, literal substring\sphinxhyphen{}at\sphinxhyphen{}position\sphinxhyphen{}0 check. There’s no
regex mode and no case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive toggle; for either of those, use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}} with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}} and an anchoring pattern (e.g.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has("\textasciicircum{}prefix", \{.regex = true\})}}), or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/matches::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches()}}}}}}} with a
regex pattern anchored at the start.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/starts:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The literal text to check for at the start of each cell. An empty
prefix matches every non\sphinxhyphen{}null cell (every string starts with the empty
string).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/starts:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature replaced by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} Series:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the cell starts with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it doesn’t.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/starts:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Case\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive, literal comparison only — no regex mode, no
case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitivity toggle. Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TextOptions}} (or a
prior {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/casefold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{casefold()}}}}}}} normalization
step) for anything more flexible.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes the feature’s payload kind from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output — it evaluates to neither \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}
nor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pairs naturally with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::filter()}} to keep only rows matching a
prefix (Example 2).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameNoteAccessor::strip}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip:dataframenoteaccessor-strip}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_note_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameNoteAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameNoteAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{strip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chars}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Trims characters from both ends of every selected text feature, cell by cell,
returning a new frame. There are two distinct trimming policies depending on
which overload you call:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload}: trims the classic ASCII whitespace set — space,
tab (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}t}}), newline (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}n}}), carriage return (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}r}}), form feed (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}f}}), and
vertical tab (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}v}}) — from both the start and end of each cell.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} overload}: trims by \sphinxstyleemphasis{character\sphinxhyphen{}set membership}, not by matching
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} as a literal prefix/suffix substring. Every leading character that
appears anywhere in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} is removed, one at a time, until a character not
in the set is reached; the same happens independently from the trailing
end. This is the same convention Python’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{str.strip(chars)}} uses — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}}
is a bag of characters to peel off, not a string to match.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every method on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}} included — applies to
\sphinxstylestrong{every feature the accessor was built with}, not just one. When reached the
ordinary way, through {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/note::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::note()}}}}}}}, that means
every feature on the (already all\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}) frame the accessor was constructed
from. A cell that is already null on the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} stays null;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}} never turns a missing cell into an empty string or vice versa.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A second way to reach the accessor: construct it directly
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor}}’s constructor — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor(DataFrame frame, std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{} features)}} — is public. Besides the usual
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.features(\{"city"\}).note()}} route (which requires the \sphinxstyleemphasis{entire} frame
to already be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind), you can construct the accessor directly with an
explicit feature list against a frame that still has other, non\sphinxhyphen{}text columns
mixed in — see Example 3. Every other accessor method inherits this same
alternate construction path; it isn’t repeated on every method’s page.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{chars} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}}\sphinxhyphen{}overload only)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The set of characters to strip from each cell’s edges. Order doesn’t matter,
and duplicates have no effect — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ab"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"ba"}} strip identically.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text trimmed; every other
feature (when reached via direct construction against a mixed frame) is
left completely unchanged.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mixed.note()}} directly would have thrown immediately, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mixed}} still has
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} feature (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}). Constructing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameNoteAccessor(mixed, \{"city"\})}} explicitly sidesteps that check: only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} is touched, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}
passes through completely untouched, and the frame never needs to be narrowed
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first. Naming a feature that
doesn’t exist on the frame at all (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"price"}}) throws once an actual operation
is called on it, not at construction time — the constructor itself performs no
validation.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chars}} overload’s “set of characters” semantics apply to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lstrip()}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rstrip()}} identically — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lstrip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lstrip}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/rstrip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rstrip}}}}}}}
for the one\sphinxhyphen{}sided versions of everything shown here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every accessor method — not just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}} — applies to every feature the
accessor was built with, whether that’s “every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} feature on the frame”
(via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.note()}}) or an explicit subset (via direct construction, Example 3).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A null cell on input stays null on output; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}} never fabricates or
discards nullity.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/titlecase:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Capitalizes the first letter of every “word” in every selected text
feature’s cells and lowercases the rest — the classic display\sphinxhyphen{}formatting
transform for names, addresses, or titles typed in all\sphinxhyphen{}lowercase or
inconsistent casing.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Word\sphinxhyphen{}boundary detection resets on \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} non\sphinxhyphen{}alphanumeric character
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{titlecase()}} decides where a new “word” starts the same way Python’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{str.title()}} does: a word boundary is any position right after a
non\sphinxhyphen{}alphanumeric character (space, hyphen, apostrophe, digit\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}letter
transitions, punctuation — anything that isn’t a letter or digit), not just
whitespace. This means an apostrophe inside a contraction resets the
boundary too, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"don\textquotesingle{}t"}} titlecases to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Don\textquotesingle{}T"}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Don\textquotesingle{}t"}} — see
Example 2. This is a well\sphinxhyphen{}known quirk of this style of word\sphinxhyphen{}boundary
detection, not a bug specific to this implementation, but it’s worth knowing
before running \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{titlecase()}} over free\sphinxhyphen{}text data that contains contractions,
hyphenated words, or embedded digits.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like every method on this accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{titlecase()}} applies to \sphinxstylestrong{every feature
the accessor was built with} in one call — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}} for
the shared mechanic and how null cells pass through unaffected.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/upper:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uppercases every character in every selected text feature’s cells, returning
a new frame — the mirror image of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}. Common uses include
normalizing free\sphinxhyphen{}typed codes or abbreviations (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"gh"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Gh"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"GH"}} all
becoming \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"GH"}}) before comparing or grouping by them, or matching a display
convention that expects codes in all caps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like every method on this accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{upper()}} applies to \sphinxstylestrong{every feature the
accessor was built with} in one call — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/strip::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strip()}}}}}}} for the
full explanation of that shared mechanic and how null cells pass through
unaffected.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
ASCII vs. Unicode case mapping
Exactly the same caveat as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/lower::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}}}}}}}: on ASCII text, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}
mapping is unambiguous and always available; correct handling of accented or
non\sphinxhyphen{}Latin uppercase mapping depends on whether this build links the optional
Unicode backend (GNU libunistring).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/upper:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-note/upper:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every selected feature’s text uppercased; every
non\sphinxhyphen{}alphabetic character is left exactly as it was.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::ceil}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:dataframetimelineaccessor-ceil}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_timeline_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTimelineAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ceil}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unit}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with each row rounded
\sphinxstyleemphasis{up} to the nearest \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} boundary, in local wall time — same feature name,
still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"S"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"s"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sec"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}} (second), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"m"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}
(minute), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"h"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}} (hour), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"d"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}} (day). Cannot be
empty.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/ceil:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature ceiled to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Days}}); passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Weeks}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Months}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}} throws, since
those units only make sense as a calendar\sphinxhyphen{}relative distance between two
timestamps — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{span()}}}}}}} for that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}, not a sentinel epoch value.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::floor}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:dataframetimelineaccessor-floor}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_timeline_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTimelineAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{floor}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{unit}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with each row rounded
\sphinxstyleemphasis{down} to the nearest \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} boundary, in local wall time — same feature
name, still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"S"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"s"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sec"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}} (second), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"m"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}
(minute), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"h"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}} (hour), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"d"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}} (day). Cannot be
empty. Sub\sphinxhyphen{}day units coarser than these (weeks, months) aren’t supported.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flooring happens in \sphinxstylestrong{local wall time} (per the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}’s current
timezone), then maps back — so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor("D")}} aligns to local midnight, not
necessarily UTC midnight, if the timezone isn’t \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} cannot be empty, and only accepts the fixed clock units listed above
— there’s no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"W"}} (week) or calendar\sphinxhyphen{}month unit here; see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/period::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{period()}}}}}}} for month/year truncation instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} (displays as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}) regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/fmt:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with a custom text
representation built from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}, as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — same feature
name, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/fmt:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strftime}}\sphinxhyphen{}style format string. Recognized tokens: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%Y}} (4\sphinxhyphen{}digit year),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%m}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%d}} (2\sphinxhyphen{}digit month/day), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%H}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%M}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%S}} (2\sphinxhyphen{}digit hour/minute/second),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%f}} (9\sphinxhyphen{}digit zero\sphinxhyphen{}padded nanoseconds), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%z}} (UTC offset as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+HH:MM}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}HH:MM}}
— never a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%a}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%A}} (abbreviated/full weekday name), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%b}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%B}}
(abbreviated/full month name), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%\%}} (a literal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}}). Any other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}}
sequence, or any character outside a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}} token, is copied through literally.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/fmt:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature replaced by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} Series
holding each row’s text rendered per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}, regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/index:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{require\_sorted = true}}, calling this on an \sphinxstyleemphasis{unsorted}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} (or one containing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}}) throws immediately — sort with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/sort_values::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::sort\_values}}}}}}} (or an equivalent)
first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{require\_sorted = false}} skips that check entirely — use it only when you
already know the data’s order doesn’t matter for what comes next, since
downstream duration\sphinxhyphen{}based operations generally \sphinxstyleemphasis{do} assume a monotonic
axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature that’s already \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind is returned as\sphinxhyphen{}is, regardless of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{require\_sorted}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::isnat}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/isnat:dataframetimelineaccessor-isnat}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/isnat::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_timeline_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTimelineAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/isnat:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{isnat}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/isnat:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with a boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
flagging whether the row is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} (missing timestamp) — same feature name,
same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/isnat:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/isnat:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature replaced by a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bool}} Series:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where the row is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} otherwise.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reinterprets every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{current} clock
reading as a naive local wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock time in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.tz}}, and converts it to
the true UTC instant that local reading corresponds to — same feature name,
still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order. \sphinxstylestrong{This changes the
underlying instant} (unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}}, which only relabels display).
The row is then displayed under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.tz}}, so its wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock text looks
unchanged even though the instant it now represents has shifted.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const TimelineLocalizeOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}}; must be one of the four supported names — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}}’s Notes — and cannot be empty), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}; during the
one\sphinxhyphen{}hour daylight\sphinxhyphen{}saving \sphinxstyleemphasis{fall\sphinxhyphen{}back} overlap, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold = 0}} resolves to the
daylight offset and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold = 1}} resolves to the standard offset), and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nonexistent}} (only the literal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"shift\_forward"}} is recognized as a real
handling mode; any other value — including the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"raise"}} — throws
when a row’s local reading falls in the daylight\sphinxhyphen{}saving \sphinxstyleemphasis{spring\sphinxhyphen{}forward} gap,
a wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock reading that never actually occurred).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature’s underlying instant
recomputed as if its prior reading were local time in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.tz}}.

(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+1:00}}), so the underlying instant moves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3,600}} seconds \sphinxstyleemphasis{earlier} — the
opposite direction from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{America/New\_York}} examples above, since London’s
offset is positive rather than negative.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{localize()}} changes the underlying instant; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}} never
does.} Reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{localize()}} only when the current ticks are naive local
readings that have never been anchored to a real instant; reach for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}
when the ticks are already correct and you just want a different display
timezone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.tz}} only accepts the same four names as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}} — anything else
throws — and cannot be empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fold}} only matters for the one hour of wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock time that repeats during
a fall\sphinxhyphen{}back transition; outside that window it has no effect.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nonexistent}} only recognizes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"shift\_forward"}} as an actual handling
strategy; every other value (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"raise"}} included) throws for a
spring\sphinxhyphen{}forward\sphinxhyphen{}gap reading, regardless of what the string itself says.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/period:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{period()}} doesn’t move by a count of
periods — it always snaps down to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start} of the row’s own current
period (there’s no way to ask for, say, the start of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{next} month
directly; combine with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift()}}}}}}} for that).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}} truncation is equivalent to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/floor::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor()}}}}}}} with the corresponding unit; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"year"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"month"}} go
further than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor()}} supports (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{floor()}} has no calendar\sphinxhyphen{}unit option).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} cannot be empty, and an unrecognized string throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} (displays as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}).

\end{itemize}

quarter (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}), as a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — same feature name, same row order.

quarter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with each row rounded
to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{nearest} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} boundary, in local wall time — same feature name,
still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/round:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"S"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"s"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sec"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}} (second), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"m"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}
(minute), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"H"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"h"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}} (hour), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"d"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}} (day). Cannot be
empty.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/round:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature rounded to the nearest
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/shift:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with each row shifted
forward (or backward, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} is negative) by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods * freq}} — same
feature name, still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order.
Month/year shifts are calendar\sphinxhyphen{}aware: a day\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}month that doesn’t exist in
the target month is clamped down to that month’s last valid day (never
rolls over into the next month).

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/shift:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How many \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} units to shift by. Positive moves forward in time, negative
moves backward.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{freq} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"y"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"yr"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"year"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"years"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"annual"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mo"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mth"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"month"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"months"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"d"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"day"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"days"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"h"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hr"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hour"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"hours"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"t"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minute"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"minutes"}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"s"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sec"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"seconds"}} (case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive). Cannot be empty.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/shift:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Timeline::shift: unsupported frequency
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"week"}} isn’t one of the accepted year/month/day/hour/minute/second
frequency groups, so the call throws instead of picking a nearby unit.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/shift:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} accepts calendar units (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{years}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{months}}) and fixed units
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{days}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hours}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minutes}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seconds}}) — there’s no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"week"}} frequency.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calendar\sphinxhyphen{}unit shifts (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{years}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{months}}) clamp the day\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}month rather than
overflowing into a later month; fixed\sphinxhyphen{}unit shifts (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{days}} and finer) are
exact elapsed\sphinxhyphen{}time arithmetic with no clamping concern.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} cannot be empty, and an unrecognized string throws
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Timeline::shift: unsupported frequency"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/shift:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/period::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::period}}}}}}}: truncate to the \sphinxstyleemphasis{start}
of a calendar period instead of shifting by a fixed number of them.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with the elapsed
distance between it and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.unit}} (or plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}}) — same
feature name, now a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} can be another \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
(paired feature\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}feature, by matching name), a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, or a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Timeline}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fixed\sphinxhyphen{}duration units (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nanos}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Micros}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Millis}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Seconds}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Days}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Weeks}}) are
plain elapsed\sphinxhyphen{}time differences. Calendar units (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Months}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}}) count
completed calendar periods or crossed calendar boundaries, per
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.mode}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}} counts business days per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.calendar}}
(default: Monday\sphinxhyphen{}Friday, no holidays).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::Timeline\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand timestamp(s). For the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} overload, every selected
feature name on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} must also exist on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}; each is paired by name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const TimelineSpanOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unit}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit::Days}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Complete}} — fully elapsed calendar
units, default; or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Boundary}} — crossed calendar labels; only affects
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Months}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DayOfMonth}} — strict day\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}month completion,
default; or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MonthEnd}} — treat matching month\sphinxhyphen{}end dates as equivalent),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{signed\_result}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — negative when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} precedes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}};
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} returns the absolute magnitude), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{calendar}} (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessCalendar}},
only used for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{unit} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeUnit}}, convenience overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shorthand for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimelineSpanOptions\{.unit = unit\}}} with every other option left
at its default.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature replaced by an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} Series
of elapsed distances to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Timeline::span: calendar/business spans require matching timezones; convert first
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{self}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} was relabeled to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"America/New\_York"}} — for a
calendar unit like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Months}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}}), both sides must share
the same timezone before the span can be computed; convert one side with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}} first. Fixed\sphinxhyphen{}duration units (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Days}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Seconds}}, and so on, as
in Example 1) have no such requirement.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/span:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calendar units (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Months}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}} require \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*this}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} to share the same timezone — mismatched timezones throw; convert
one side with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}}}}}} first.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anchor = TimelineSpanAnchor::MonthEnd}} changes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Complete}}\sphinxhyphen{}mode completion
so that two month\sphinxhyphen{}end dates (e.g. January 31st and February 29th in a leap
year) count as equivalent, rather than requiring an exact day\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}month
match.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}} uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.calendar}} (default: Monday\sphinxhyphen{}Friday, no
holidays); built\sphinxhyphen{}in presets include \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessCalendar::monfri()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usa\_federal(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{canada\_federal(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uk\_bank(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target2(...)}},
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nyse(...)}}. Holidays are local epoch\sphinxhyphen{}day labels (e.g. from
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tl().epoch(TimeUnit::Days)}}), not epoch nanoseconds. See the manual’s
“Timeline spans” section for worked \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessDays}} examples.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{signed\_result = false}} returns the absolute magnitude instead of a
direction\sphinxhyphen{}sensitive (possibly negative) value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If either side is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} for a row, that row’s span displays as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::time}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/time:dataframetimelineaccessor-time}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/time::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_timeline_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTimelineAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/time:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{time}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/time:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature with just its
time\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}day portion — the date is reset to the Unix epoch day
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1970\sphinxhyphen{}01\sphinxhyphen{}01}}), and the clock time is kept, in local wall time — same
feature name, still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row order.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/time:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/time:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature’s date portion reset to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1970\sphinxhyphen{}01\sphinxhyphen{}01}}, keeping only the time\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}day.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/time:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result is still a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} (not a plain string or
numeric type) with a fixed date component — it’s meant for comparing or
grouping by time\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}day, not as a display format. Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/fmt::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fmt("\%H:\%M:\%S")}}}}}}} if you want a bare text time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Operates in \sphinxstylestrong{local wall time}, per the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}’s current timezone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} (displays as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}).

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::tz}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:dataframetimelineaccessor-tz}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_timeline_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTimelineAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{tz}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{name}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{display} timezone
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} — same feature name, still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row
order. \sphinxstylestrong{The underlying instant is unchanged} — only the timezone used to
compute local calendar fields (year/month/day/hour, and box\sphinxhyphen{}table display)
shifts.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The target timezone. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}} (also the empty string), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"America/Edmonton"}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"America/New\_York"}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Europe/London"}} are recognized (case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive);
any other name throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature’s display timezone switched
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}}.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Unknown timezone: Asia/Tokyo (currently supported: UTC, America/Edmonton, America/New\PYGZus{}York, Europe/London)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Asia/Tokyo"}} is a real IANA zone name, but this project only ships rules
for the four zones listed in the error — there’s no general tzdata lookup
backing it.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only four timezone names are supported: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}} (or empty string),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"America/Edmonton"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"America/New\_York"}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Europe/London"}} — any
other name (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Asia/Tokyo"}}) throws. There is no general IANA tzdata
lookup.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}} never changes the underlying instant} — it only relabels which
timezone is used to interpret it for display and field extraction (like
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/hour::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hour()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/year::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{year()}}}}}}}). Use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/localize::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{localize()}}}}}}}
if your data is naive local wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock text that needs to be \sphinxstyleemphasis{anchored} to
a real instant for the first time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::utc}}}}}}}: shorthand for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz("UTC")}}.

ticks as local time in a timezone, shifting the underlying instant —

\subparagraph{DataFrameTimelineAccessor::utc}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc:dataframetimelineaccessor-utc}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_timeline_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTimelineAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTimelineAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{utc}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every selected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature’s display timezone
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}} — same feature name, still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind, same row
order. Exactly equivalent to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/tz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz("UTC")}}}}}}}; like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tz()}}, the
underlying instant never changes, only the timezone used to display it and
compute local calendar fields.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each selected time feature’s display timezone switched
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"UTC"}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/utc:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

chaining \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tz(name).utc()}} always round\sphinxhyphen{}trips back to the original
displayed values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}}.

\end{itemize}
