\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-timeline/week:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Follows the ISO\sphinxhyphen{}8601 definition: weeks start on Monday, and week \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is the
week containing the year’s first Thursday. Because of this, dates in very
late December or very early January can report a week number that belongs
to the neighboring calendar year (e.g. December 31st can report week \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} of
the following ISO year) — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{week()}} alone doesn’t disambiguate which ISO
year that week number belongs to.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::tl()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature on the calling frame to already
be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind — narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if needed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} row (or one already null on the underlying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}) displays as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{align}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{new\PYGZus{}label}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fill}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/align:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reindexes every feature onto an entirely new set of case labels, matching each
target label to a row of the current case labels \sphinxstylestrong{by value}, not by position.
When a target label appears more than once, its occurrences are matched in
order against the source’s occurrences of that same label (first target
occurrence to first source occurrence, second to second, and so on); a target
occurrence beyond the number of matching source rows — or a label absent from
the source entirely — comes back with no match.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unmatched cells are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} for every feature. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} is supplied, unmatched
cells in \sphinxstylestrong{numeric (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}})} features are replaced by that constant instead
— non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) stay \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} regardless
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}, since there’s no numeric value to substitute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Equivalent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.align(DataFrame::AlignSpec\{.label = new\_label{[}, .fill = fill{]}\})}} with every feature selected.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/align:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{new\_label} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new case labels to reindex onto. Becomes the result’s case labels exactly,
including any repeats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fill} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}double\textgreater{}}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A constant substituted into unmatched cells of numeric features only. Leave
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}} (the other overload) to leave unmatched cells \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} everywhere.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/align:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new\_label}} as its case labels, and every feature
reindexed by label\sphinxhyphen{}value match.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/align:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matching is purely by label \sphinxstylestrong{value}, occurrence\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}occurrence — not by the
source’s row position or any sort order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} never reaches non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features; an unmatched \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} cell is always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the DataFrame\sphinxhyphen{}wide counterpart to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::align\_to}}}}}}}, which performs
the analogous reindex for time axes using tick\sphinxhyphen{}based matching modes instead of
plain value equality.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/cast:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Casts the case labels to a different \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastTarget}} payload family
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) — every structured level if the
frame has any, or the flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread otherwise. Feature columns are
untouched. Casting a numeric\sphinxhyphen{}looking \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} axis (like case labels written as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"1"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"2"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"10"}}) to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} doesn’t just relabel the same text — it
changes how later operations like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/sort::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort()}}}}}}} or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/monotonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{monotonic()}}}}}}} compare rows, from lexicographic (string) order
to numeric order.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/cast:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastTarget}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The destination payload kind: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const ThreadCastOptions\&}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Full cast controls: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{series\_dtype}} (target numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScalarType}} when casting to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{format}} (parse/format pattern for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} targets),
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParseInvalid::Raise}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{::Null}} for unparseable values).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{series\_dtype} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}pluss::codem::ScalarType\textgreater{}}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shorthand for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastOptions\{.series\_dtype = series\_dtype\}}} — the target

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/cast:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Casting a structured (multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) frame casts \sphinxstylestrong{every} level to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} casts can fail to parse; use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadCastOptions\{.invalid = ParseInvalid::Null\}}} to turn unparseable values
into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} instead of throwing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because every column in the ASCII table renderer is left\sphinxhyphen{}justified regardless
of its underlying type, a cast between text\sphinxhyphen{}like and numeric representations
of the same digits is often invisible in the printed table — only later
comparisons (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{monotonic()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align()}}) reveal the difference.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameLabelAccessor::codes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/codes:dataframelabelaccessor-codes}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/codes::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_label_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameLabelAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/codes:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{codes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/codes:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Factorizes the case labels into integer codes, in first\sphinxhyphen{}occurrence order (the
first distinct value seen gets code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, the next new value gets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, and so
on). For a structured (multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) frame, each level is factorized
\sphinxstylestrong{independently}, producing one integer column per level. For an unstructured
frame, the whole flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread is factorized into a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}}
column.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/codes:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One column per case\sphinxhyphen{}label level (or a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}} column if
unstructured), each holding that level’s factorized codes; case labels on
the result match the source’s own case labels.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/codes:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Codes are per\sphinxhyphen{}level for structured frames; there is no shared numbering
across levels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result’s own case labels are the source’s case labels, unchanged — only
the feature columns differ.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameLabelAccessor::depth}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/depth:dataframelabelaccessor-depth}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/depth::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_label_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameLabelAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/depth:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{depth}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/depth:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the \sphinxstylestrong{lexsort depth} of the case labels: how many of the leading
levels, taken together in their current order, are already sorted ascending
(nulls last). For an unstructured frame, this is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} if the flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label
thread itself is sorted ascending, else \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}. For a structured frame, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth()}}
checks longer and longer level prefixes — level 0 alone, then levels 0\textendash{}1
together, then 0\textendash{}2, and so on — stopping at the first prefix that isn’t
jointly sorted.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/depth:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}
The number of leading levels that are jointly sorted ascending; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} if even
the first level isn’t sorted (or the frame is unstructured and not sorted).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region}} alone is still sorted, so the 1\sphinxhyphen{}level prefix passes. But within the
first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region}} group, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NYC"}} comes before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Boston"}} — jointly, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(region, city)}} is not sorted — so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth()}} stops at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} rather than reaching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/depth:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth()}} checks the levels \sphinxstylestrong{in their current order} (as returned by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}}}}}}); {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order()}}}}}}} or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swap()}}}}}}} can
change which prefixes are checked, and therefore the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every level comparison uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last = true}}; there’s no parameter to
change this.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For an unstructured frame, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth()}} is equivalent to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{monotonic(true, false, true) ? 1 : 0}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff:dataframelabelaccessor-diff}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_label_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameLabelAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{diff}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Treats the case labels and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} as two sets of values, and returns the
labels that appear in this accessor’s case labels but \sphinxstylestrong{not} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} (a
set difference: “mine minus yours”) — deduplicated, in first\sphinxhyphen{}occurrence order.
This is not the numeric row\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}row difference some other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff}} methods in the
library compute; it’s a set operation over label \sphinxstyleemphasis{values}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values to subtract. Can be any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, not necessarily another frame’s
case labels.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
The distinct case\sphinxhyphen{}label values with no match in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, in first\sphinxhyphen{}occurrence
order, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"diff"}}.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  east
Name: diff, ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case labels hold three distinct values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"east"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"west"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north"}},
ignoring the repeated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"east"}}); removing everything found in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"west"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north"}}) leaves just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"east"}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Order is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left minus right}}: swap the operands and you generally get a
different (and possibly non\sphinxhyphen{}empty where this was empty) result — unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/symdiff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{symdiff()}}}}}}}, which is symmetric.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Duplicates within either operand are collapsed; the result never repeats a
value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the two operands share a common representable dtype (same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
scalar type, both numeric, or the same non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} kind on the same
platform), the result preserves that dtype; otherwise it falls back to a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} of each value’s string form.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/distinct:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns the unique case\sphinxhyphen{}label values, in first\sphinxhyphen{}occurrence order. With
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}}, a single \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} is kept (at the position of its first
occurrence) if any case label is null; with the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = true}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} is excluded entirely.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/distinct:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether to exclude a null case label from the result. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, at most one
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} entry is kept.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/distinct:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
The distinct case\sphinxhyphen{}label values, in first\sphinxhyphen{}occurrence order.

\subparagraph{Output (distinct(false))}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/distinct:output-distinct-false}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  10
1  NULL
2  20
ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = true}}, the two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} case labels are excluded
entirely, leaving only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull = false}}, a single
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} is kept — at the position of its \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} occurrence (row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, before
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}} first appears at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) — even though it occurs twice in the source.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/distinct:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This operates on the flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread as a whole, even on a structured
(multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) frame — it does not distinguish per level. Use
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/levels::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{levels()}}}}}}} for per\sphinxhyphen{}level distinct values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result carries no display labels of its own; it prints with a plain
default integer index.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/drop:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Has two entirely different behaviors depending on how it’s called:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}\sphinxhyphen{}only overloads, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(options)}} with both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated}} left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}}: drop \sphinxstylestrong{case\sphinxhyphen{}label levels} by name from a
structured (multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) frame — not rows. The remaining levels are
rejoined into a new flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread. Feature columns are untouched.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(options)}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated = true}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated = true}}}: drop
\sphinxstylestrong{rows} instead, filtering out whichever rows {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}}
or {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/repeated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}}}}}}} (restricted to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.names}}, if given)
would mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. This mode requires structured labels only if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.names}}
is non\sphinxhyphen{}empty; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.names}} empty, it keys off the full flat case
label.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/drop:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (name\sphinxhyphen{}only overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The level name(s) to remove. Requires a structured frame; every name must
match an existing level.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame::LabelDropOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} (level names, or row\sphinxhyphen{}filter key names — see above), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated}} (switch to row\sphinxhyphen{}filter mode; mutually exclusive), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} (which occurrence \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated}}\sphinxhyphen{}mode row\sphinxhyphen{}filtering spares).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/drop:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
Either the same rows with fewer case\sphinxhyphen{}label levels, or the same levels with
fewer rows, depending on which mode was used.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/drop:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated}} cannot both be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} on the same call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In level\sphinxhyphen{}drop mode, dropping every level leaves the frame with default
integer case labels (like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/reset::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset(..., drop=true)}}}}}}}, but without
touching feature columns either way).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In row\sphinxhyphen{}filter mode with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.names}} non\sphinxhyphen{}empty, those names key the
filter but the printed case\sphinxhyphen{}label column still shows the \sphinxstylestrong{full} flat case
label, not just the selected level(s) — matching
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated(names)}}}}}}}’s own display behavior.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Marks each row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if its case\sphinxhyphen{}label key has already appeared earlier (or,
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last = true}}, will appear later) among the rows sharing that key —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for the first (or, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}}, the last) occurrence of every
distinct key, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for any key that never repeats at all. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}
given, the key is built from just those levels of a structured frame (still
requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_axis\_}} to be defined); without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}, the key is the full
flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label value.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (name\sphinxhyphen{}only overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Level names to key the duplicate check on, instead of the full case label.
Requires a structured frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_first} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the first occurrence of each repeated key is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (not marked
duplicate); every later occurrence is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{last} occurrence is spared instead; every earlier one is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. Cannot be combined with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = true}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean thread, one entry per row, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"duplicated"}},
displayed against the case label(s) it was computed from.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated:id3}}

Thread::duplicated: keep\PYGZus{}first and keep\PYGZus{}last cannot both be true
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sparing both the first \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} the last occurrence isn’t a coherent request, so
it throws rather than picking one silently. Note that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} defaults
to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — passing only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last = true}} positionally (without also
setting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first = false}}, as Example 3 does) hits this same throw.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_first}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_last}} cannot both be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The displayed labels alongside the result are always the frame’s full case
labels, even when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} restricts which levels build the duplicate key.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/repeated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repeated()}}}}}}}, a key that occurs more than once still
has exactly one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} row (its spared occurrence) here.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/fillnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replaces every null case label with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} and returns the filled case\sphinxhyphen{}label
\sphinxstylestrong{values} — it does \sphinxstylestrong{not} apply the fill back to the frame automatically.
To actually change the frame’s case labels, pass the result to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pick the overload matching the case labels’ own kind: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} for a numeric
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}) axis, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} for their respective temporal kinds.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/fillnull:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The replacement for every null case label, typed to match the case labels’
own kind.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/fillnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
The case\sphinxhyphen{}label values with nulls replaced — not yet applied back to the
frame.

\subparagraph{Output (filled values, not yet applied)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/fillnull:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01
1  2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}02
2  2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}03
ptype: Timeline
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The empty string in the constructor produced a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaT}} middle label, displayed
as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull}} replaces it with the single supplied \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Timeline}}
value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2024\sphinxhyphen{}01\sphinxhyphen{}02}}. As in Example 1, this is still just the filled values —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{readings}} itself needs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{readings.label().set(filled)}} to actually change.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/fillnull:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns values only; chain into {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}} to actually update the
frame’s case labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose the overload matching the case labels’ \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadKind}} — passing a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} axis (or vice versa) doesn’t fit any overload and won’t
compile.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}} overloads work the same way as
Example 1’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} overload, just for a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind axis instead of a
numeric one — pass the replacement text directly, e.g.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{readings.label().fillnull("unknown")}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::TimeIndex}} overload behaves identically to Example 2’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::Timeline}} overload — the same fill mechanics apply to either
temporal kind.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/fillnull:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameLabelAccessor::isnull}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/notnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameLabelAccessor::notnull}}}}}}}: check which case labels are
null before (or instead of) filling them.

\item {}

\subparagraph{DataFrameLabelAccessor::find}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:dataframelabelaccessor-find}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_label_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameLabelAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{find}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{targets}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each value in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{targets}}, looks up the position of its \sphinxstylestrong{first} occurrence
among the case labels — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} if that value never appears. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/pos::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pos()}}}}}}}, which returns every match for a single value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{find()}}
returns exactly one position (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}) per target, for potentially many
targets at once.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{targets} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values to look up, in the order you want positions back.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
One \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} position per target (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} if not found), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"find"}}, displayed against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{targets}} themselves.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{200.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{150.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{90.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{labeled}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{find}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{targets}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
 west  1
north  3
south  \PYGZhy{}1
Name: find, ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"west"}} first appears at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north"}} at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"south"}} never
appears in the case labels at all, so it comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"east"}}’s repeat at

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the \sphinxstylestrong{first} matching position is ever returned per target, even if
the case labels have more than one match.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result is displayed against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{targets}}, not against this accessor’s own
case labels — so a target with no match still gets a row, labeled by that
target value, holding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}}.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/pos::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameLabelAccessor::pos}}}}}}}: all matching positions for a single
value, rather than the first match for each of several targets.

instead of individual lookups.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameLabelAccessor::freq}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/freq:dataframelabelaccessor-freq}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/freq::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_label_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameLabelAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/freq:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{freq}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/freq:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Counts how many times each distinct case\sphinxhyphen{}label value occurs, and returns those
counts sorted by frequency descending (ties broken by the value itself,
ascending) — displayed against the value each count belongs to. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}}
optionally caps the result to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} most frequent values; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (the
default) keeps every distinct value.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/freq:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{top\_n} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Maximum number of distinct values to keep, ordered by descending count. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}
means no cap — keep every distinct value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dropnull} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether to exclude a null case label from the tally.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/freq:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} counts, one per distinct case\sphinxhyphen{}label value, sorted descending by
count (ties broken ascending by value), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"freq"}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/freq:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The tie\sphinxhyphen{}break is on the value’s own string form, always ascending —
independent of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull}} settings.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{top\_n}} truncates \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} sorting, so it always keeps the most frequent
values, never an arbitrary prefix of the unsorted data.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/has:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two unrelated questions share this name:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}} (no arguments) answers a structural question: does this frame
have \sphinxstylestrong{structured} (named, multi\sphinxhyphen{}level\sphinxhyphen{}capable) case labels at all — i.e.,
were they built via a route like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(feature\_name)}}}}}}} rather than
left as the default integer index or a raw axis from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(const Thread\&)}}}}}}}?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(value)}}} / \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(values)}}} answer an elementwise membership
question: for each row, does its case label equal \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} (single\sphinxhyphen{}value
overloads), or match \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}} (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload, an “is one
of” test)?

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/has:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A single value to test each case label against, elementwise.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{values} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A collection of values; each row is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} if its case label matches \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} of
them.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/has:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
(No\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload) Whether the frame’s case labels are structured.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
(Value\sphinxhyphen{}taking overloads) A boolean thread, one entry per row, displayed
against the case labels, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"has"}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/has:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The no\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload is purely structural — it says nothing about
whether any particular value is present.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has(values)}} is an elementwise “is one of” test across the whole \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values}}
collection, not a single membership question about the frame as a whole.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/levels:what-it-does}}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/levels:notes}}\begin{itemize}

would still print as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}}; only the trailing padding is blank.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

of the source frame’s own case labels.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/map:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}} to every case label individually and replaces the case labels
with the results. Only works on an \sphinxstylestrong{unstructured} frame (no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_axis\_}} —
i.e. not one built by promoting a named feature via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(feature\_name)}}}}}}});
calling it on a structured, multi\sphinxhyphen{}level frame throws, since there’s no single
flat thread to map over. Map an individual level via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/part::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part(name)}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}} it back instead.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/map:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const std::function\textless{}ThreadValue(const ThreadValue\&)\textgreater{}\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A callback receiving one case label at a time (wrapped in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadValue}}) and
returning its replacement.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/map:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the same features, and case labels replaced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fn}}’s
output.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/monotonic:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checks whether the flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label thread is sorted, according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strict}}. This always compares the full case label as one sequence — for
a structured (multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) frame it does \sphinxstylestrong{not} check per\sphinxhyphen{}level sortedness;
use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/depth::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth()}}}}}}} for that.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/monotonic:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Check ascending order if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, descending if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{strict} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, equal adjacent case labels fail the check (strictly increasing/
decreasing); if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, equal adjacent values are allowed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Where a null case label is expected to sort relative to real values.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/monotonic:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}
Whether the case labels satisfy the requested order.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The no\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload lists the current case\sphinxhyphen{}label level names, in level
order — empty if the frame isn’t structured. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}\sphinxhyphen{}taking overloads
\sphinxstylestrong{rename} every level in one call: you must supply exactly one new name per
existing level, positionally, and the result is exactly
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}} applied with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{old\_name, new\_name\}}} pairs built from
that positional pairing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (renaming overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
One replacement name per existing level, in level order. Must match the
current level count exactly.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{}}}
(No\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload) The current level names, in order; empty if
unstructured.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}\sphinxhyphen{}taking overloads) A new frame with every level renamed.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The renaming overloads require \sphinxstylestrong{exactly} one name per existing level — you
can’t rename a subset; use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/rename::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename()}}}}}}} for that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
On an unstructured frame, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}} (no arguments) returns an empty vector,
and the renaming overloads have nothing to operate on.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/notnull:signature}}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/notnull:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Marks each row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} where its case label is a genuine (non\sphinxhyphen{}null) value,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} where it’s null — the exact logical negation of
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/isnull::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/notnull:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean thread, one entry per row, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"notnull"}}, displayed
against the case labels themselves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_label_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameLabelAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signatures}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order:signatures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{order}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{initializer\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{names}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reorders the case\sphinxhyphen{}label \sphinxstylestrong{levels} (not rows) to match \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}, which must
name every existing level exactly once. Values within each level are
untouched — only which level comes first, second, and so on in the composite
label changes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The composite display string is rebuilt from the new level order using
whatever separator (custom or default) was used when the levels were
originally created via {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}} — the separator is preserved across
reordering.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every current level name, in the new order you want them combined in.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the same rows and values, its case\sphinxhyphen{}label levels reordered.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Swap the order of a 2\sphinxhyphen{}level structured frame’s levels.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This reorders \sphinxstylestrong{levels}, not rows — row order and every feature column are
untouched.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A custom separator passed to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set()}}}}}}} survives \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order()}} (and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swap()}}}}}}}, which is built on it): the displayed composite label
keeps using whichever separator the levels were created with.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} must include every current level exactly once; a partial or
duplicated list throws.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/part:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads a single case\sphinxhyphen{}label level’s own values, by name or by position, from a
structured (multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) frame. Requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}} to be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}; calling this on
an unstructured frame throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/part:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{name} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The level’s name, as returned by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{position} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The level’s position (0\sphinxhyphen{}based; negative counts back from the end).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/part:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
That level’s own values — not the composite case label, just this one
level’s contribution to it.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/part:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Throws if the frame isn’t structured (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}) — there’s no level
to read from a flat or default case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} carries no display labels of its own; it prints with a
plain default integer index, same as any other freestanding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/pos:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns \sphinxstylestrong{every} position where the case label equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}. Throws if
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}} never occurs. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{find()}}}}}}}, which returns only the first
match for each of several targets, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pos()}} returns \sphinxstyleemphasis{all} matches for a single
target.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/pos:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char*}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The value to locate every occurrence of.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/pos:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Int64}} positions where the case label equals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}, one entry per
match, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"pos"}}, plain default integer index.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/rename:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Renames one or more case\sphinxhyphen{}label levels by explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{from, to\}}} pairs. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}}}}}}’s renaming overloads, you don’t have to rename every
level — just the ones you list. Requires a structured (multi\sphinxhyphen{}level) frame;
values, row order, and the displayed composite label text are all unaffected —
only the level \sphinxstyleemphasis{names} returned by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/names::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names()}}}}}}} (and usable with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/part::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part(name)}}}}}}}) change.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/rename:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{renames} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of\textless{}DataFrame::LabelRename\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}DataFrame::LabelRename\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
One or more \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{from, to\}}} pairs — each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{from}} must name an existing level, and
no two renames may target the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/rename:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the named levels renamed; values and row order unchanged.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/repeated:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Marks every row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} whose case\sphinxhyphen{}label key occurs more than once anywhere in
the frame — including its \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} occurrence, unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/duplicated::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicated()}}}}}}}, which spares one occurrence (by default, the
first). A key that never repeats is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} everywhere it appears. With
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}, the key is built from just those levels of a structured frame
(requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_axis\_}} to be defined); without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}, the key is the full
flat case\sphinxhyphen{}label value.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/repeated:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{names} (name\sphinxhyphen{}only overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Level names to key the repeat check on, instead of the full case label.
Requires a structured frame.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/repeated:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A boolean thread, one entry per row, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{display\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"repeated"}},
displayed against the case label(s) it was computed from.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/repeated:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/reset:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clears the case labels back to the default integer index. Unless dropped, the
old case\sphinxhyphen{}label values are first materialized back as ordinary feature
column(s). By default — with no name supplied — each level’s own name is
kept (matching pandas’ \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset\_index()}}, which preserves a named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Index}}’s
name); pass an explicit name only when you want to override it.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/reset:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}, empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The name to give the restored feature column. Left empty (the default), each
level keeps its own name (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"level\_"}} + its position, if the level itself
has no name). Pass a non\sphinxhyphen{}empty string to override that name — valid only when
there’s exactly one case\sphinxhyphen{}label level (or an unstructured axis).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame::ResetLabelOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}} (discard the old values entirely instead of restoring them as
features), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} (one name per level, positionally — leave \sphinxstylestrong{empty} to keep
each level’s own name instead of overriding it), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}} (fallback prefix
for any level that has no name of its own).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/reset:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with default integer case labels, and (unless \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}}) the old
case\sphinxhyphen{}label values restored as feature column(s).

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/reset:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset()}} with no arguments keeps each level’s own name (or falls
back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"level\_"}} + position for an unnamed level) — this matches pandas’
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset\_index()}}, which preserves a named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Index}}’s name. Pass a non\sphinxhyphen{}empty
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} string only when you want to override that name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset(DataFrame::ResetLabelOptions\{\})}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.names}} left empty is
equivalent to the no\sphinxhyphen{}argument single\sphinxhyphen{}string overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
On a structured frame, if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.names}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}empty it must have exactly
one entry per level.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop = true}}, the old case\sphinxhyphen{}label values are discarded — there’s no way
to recover them afterward.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two entirely different mechanisms share this name:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(const Thread\&)}}} replaces the case labels directly with an arbitrary
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} — no structure is created; {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/has::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has()}}}}}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} afterward.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The feature\sphinxhyphen{}name overloads} (single name, multiple names, or the full
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SetLabelOptions}}) promote one or more existing features to \sphinxstylestrong{structured}
case labels — a real \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_axis\_}} with one named level per promoted feature.
With more than one feature, the levels are joined into a composite display
string using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}} (default: an unprintable “unit separator”
character). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_feature(s)}} controls whether the promoted feature(s) also
disappear from the ordinary feature columns.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
drop defaults to true — pandas set\_index() semantics, not “keep everything”
Promoting a feature to the case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis \sphinxstylestrong{removes it from the frame’s ordinary
columns by default}, exactly like pandas’ \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_index(keys, drop=True)}}. Pass
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_feature(s) = false}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SetLabelOptions\{.drop = false\}}}) explicitly if you want the
promoted feature to remain accessible as a regular column \sphinxstyleemphasis{in addition to} becoming the
case label. This mirrors {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/unstack::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unstack()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UnstackOptions::drop}},
which also defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}; it is the opposite of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/reset::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResetLabelOptions::drop}}, which defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} (reset’s job is to \sphinxstyleemphasis{materialize} the
label back into a column, so keeping it there by default is the natural counterpart).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{labels} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Replacement case labels, used as\sphinxhyphen{}is. Does not create structured levels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_name} / \sphinxstylestrong{feature\_names} (feature\sphinxhyphen{}name overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The existing feature(s) to promote to case labels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{drop\_feature} / \sphinxstylestrong{drop\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the promoted feature(s) are removed from the ordinary feature columns
after promotion. Defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — see the important callout above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{separator} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textbackslash{}x1F"}}, multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The string joining each level’s value into the composite display label. Only
affects the \sphinxstyleemphasis{displayed} text — {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/part::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{part(name)}}}}}}} always reads the
level’s own values regardless of separator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame::SetLabelOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The full form: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, same as above), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}}, plus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort}}
(immediately sort rows by the new case labels) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verify}} (throw if the new case labels
aren’t unique).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the requested case labels.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/set:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_feature}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_features}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SetLabelOptions.drop}} all default to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — promoting a
feature to the case\sphinxhyphen{}label axis removes it from the ordinary columns unless you pass
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} explicitly. See the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the feature\sphinxhyphen{}name overloads create a structured \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_axis\_}};
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set(const Thread\&)}} never does, no matter what, and has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}} concept since it isn’t
sourced from an existing column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}} only affects the displayed composite string. It’s preserved
across operations that rebuild that string from the levels — including
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swap()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/drop::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop()}}}}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/cast::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cast()}}}}}}} — so a custom separator sticks once set.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SetLabelOptions.verify = true}} throws if the resulting case labels aren’t
unique; without it, duplicates are allowed freely. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verify}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop}} are independent.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/slice:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two different slicing conventions:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(int64\_t, int64\_t)}}} is a plain \sphinxstylestrong{positional} slice of the case
labels — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{exclusive}, standard half\sphinxhyphen{}open \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, stop)}} indexing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(string\_view, string\_view)}}} is a \sphinxstylestrong{label\sphinxhyphen{}value} slice: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}
matches the case labels’ \sphinxstyleemphasis{first} occurrence of that value, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} matches
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{last} occurrence of its value — and the returned range is inclusive of
both ends. If either value never occurs, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}’s position ends up after
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}’s, it throws.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both overloads return the sliced case\sphinxhyphen{}label \sphinxstylestrong{values} as a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} —
not a filtered \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/slice:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} / \sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, positional overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Positions bounding the slice; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} is exclusive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{start} / \sphinxstylestrong{stop} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, label\sphinxhyphen{}value overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Case\sphinxhyphen{}label values bounding the slice; the range runs from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}’s first
occurrence through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}’s \sphinxstylestrong{last} occurrence, inclusive.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/slice:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
The sliced case\sphinxhyphen{}label values, plain default integer index.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/slice:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::label().slice: start label not found
Thread::label().slice: stop label not found
Thread::label().slice: start label occurs after stop label
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"missing"}} never occurs as either bound, so each throws its own not\sphinxhyphen{}found
message depending on which argument it was passed as. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north"}} (row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}) and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"east"}} (last occurrence at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}) both exist, but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north"}}’s position
comes \sphinxstyleemphasis{after} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"east"}}’s last occurrence, so the range is empty/backwards and
throws instead of silently returning nothing.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/slice:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The label\sphinxhyphen{}value overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} bound is the \sphinxstylestrong{last}, not first,
occurrence of that value — a subtlety worth checking carefully when the
slice value itself repeats, as in Example 2.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both overloads return values only, not a filtered frame — pair with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/pos::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pos()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/find::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{find()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/take::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::take}}}}}}} if you need the corresponding rows
instead.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/sort:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reorders every row by case label. The simple overload compares the \sphinxstylestrong{flat}
case label as a single sequence (the same comparison
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/monotonic::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{monotonic()}}}}}}} uses) — on a structured, multi\sphinxhyphen{}level frame, this
sorts by the composite \sphinxstyleemphasis{displayed} string, not level\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}level. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort(options)}}
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.names}} given instead sorts \sphinxstylestrong{lexicographically by those named
levels}, in the order you list them — a real per\sphinxhyphen{}level sort, independent of
how the composite string happens to be joined.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/sort:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sort ascending if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, descending if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Where null case labels sort relative to real values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame::SortLabelOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} (level names to sort by, in priority order — leave empty to fall back
to the flat comparison), plus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ascending}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/sort:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the same rows, reordered by case label.

\subparagraph{Output (city\_first — per\sphinxhyphen{}level order, city ahead of region)}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/sort:output-city-first-per-level-order-city-ahead-of-region}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===================
            | sales
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
east/Boston | 10   
west/LA     | 30   
east/NYC    | 20   
west/SF     | 40   
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The composite label is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"region/city"}}, so the plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort()}} above sorts by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{region}} first (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{east}} before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{west}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} only breaks ties within it.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort(SortLabelOptions\{.names = \{"city", "region"\}\})}} instead sorts by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}}
first regardless of level order in the composite string — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Boston" \textless{} "LA" \textless{} "NYC" \textless{} "SF"}} puts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{west/LA}} right after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{east/Boston}}, ahead of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{east/NYC}}, which the flat composite sort would never produce.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/sort:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simple overload compares the flat, displayed case\sphinxhyphen{}label string on a
structured frame — if the composite join could ever be ambiguous (rare with
the default separator, more of a concern with a custom one), prefer
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort(SortLabelOptions\{.names = \{...\}\})}} for an unambiguous, per\sphinxhyphen{}level sort.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorting is stable: rows with equal case labels retain their original
relative order.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameLabelAccessor::swap}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap:dataframelabelaccessor-swap}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_label_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameLabelAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameLabelAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{swap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Swaps the positions of two case\sphinxhyphen{}label levels, by name — a convenience for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order()}} with just those two levels’ positions exchanged and every other
level left where it was. Requires a structured frame with both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} as existing level names; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} must differ.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order()}}}}}}} (which this method is built on), the composite
display string is rebuilt using whichever separator (custom or default) was
used when the levels were originally created.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{left} / \sphinxstylestrong{right} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two level names to exchange. Must both exist, and must differ from each
other.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with the same rows and values, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}}’s level
positions swapped.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/swap:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

results — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swap}} is purely a convenience for that common case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{left}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} must both be existing level names and must differ, or the
call throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same separator behavior as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/order::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order()}}}}}}}: a custom separator is
preserved.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"symdiff"}}.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/symdiff:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  east
1  north
2  south
Name: symdiff, ptype: Note
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"west"}} is shared by both sides, so it’s excluded; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"east"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"north"}} are
only on the left, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"south"}} only on the right — all three make it into the
result, left\sphinxhyphen{}side values first.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/symdiff:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-label/diff::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{symdiff()}} is symmetric: swapping the operands
produces the same set of values (order may differ).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Duplicates on either side are collapsed; the result never repeats a value.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/match:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameFeatureAxisAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{match}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
