\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/match:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Selects every feature whose \sphinxstylestrong{name} matches \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}}, an ECMAScript regular
expression, searched (not required to match the whole name) against each
feature name. Case labels and row order are preserved unchanged.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/match:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pattern} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
An ECMAScript\sphinxhyphen{}flavored regular expression, checked against each feature name
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::regex\_search}} — a partial match anywhere in the name is enough
unless you anchor with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciicircum{}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$}} yourself.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/match:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with only the matching features; same case labels and rows as
the source. Throws if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} isn’t a valid regular expression.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/match:notes}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

be found somewhere in the name unless you anchor it yourself with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciicircum{}}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An invalid regular expression throws immediately, before any matching is
attempted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pattern}} that matches nothing returns a frame with zero features but the
same case labels and row count.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/note:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Selects every feature whose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} (text) — dropping numeric
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}) and temporal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) features. Case labels and row
order are preserved unchanged.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/note:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features; same case labels and rows
as the source.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/prefix:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prepends \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix}} to \sphinxstylestrong{every} feature name on the frame. Values, case labels,
and row order are all unaffected — only the names change.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/prefix:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{prefix} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/prefix:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with every feature renamed to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prefix + original\_name}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/prefix:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{DataFrameFeatureAxisAccessor::series}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/series:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameFeatureAxisAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/series:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Selects every feature whose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (numeric or boolean) —
dropping text (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}) and temporal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) features. Case
labels and row order are preserved unchanged.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-feataxis/series:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features; same case labels and
rows as the source.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsAccessor::add}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TsAlignMode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TsAlignMode}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Exact}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} to every bound feature, first aligning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows onto this
accessor’s own time axis according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}. For each bound feature name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}
must have a same\sphinxhyphen{}named feature; that feature’s values are aligned onto this
accessor’s axis (producing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever no match is found), then added
elementwise to the bound feature’s own values.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand frame. Must contain a feature with the same name as every feature
currently bound on this accessor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows are matched onto this accessor’s time axis:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}}: only rows whose axis tick matches exactly are paired; everything
else is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}}: each row is paired with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s most recent value at or before
its own tick (a “carry the last known value forward” match).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}}: each row is paired with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s next value at or after its own
tick.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}}}: each row is paired with whichever of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s values is closest in
time, before or after.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as this accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its sum with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s aligned values.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add:notes}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The result’s case labels are always this accessor’s own axis — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows
that don’t get matched (under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}) or contribute (under
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}}) never introduce new rows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every bound feature must have a same\sphinxhyphen{}named counterpart on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, or the call
throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}} are shown fully worked above; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}} follow

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reindexes every bound feature onto an entirely new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_axis}}, matching each
target row to a row of this accessor’s own time axis according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}}: a target tick is matched only to a source row with the exact same
tick; anything unmatched is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}}: each target tick takes the most recent source value at or before
it (a “last known value” lookup).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}}: each target tick takes the next source value at or after it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}}}: each target tick takes whichever source value is closest in time,
before or after.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} overloads additionally run {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_gaps()}}}}}}} on
the result afterward, using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}} (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsReindexFill}} value) to pick the gap\sphinxhyphen{}fill
strategy — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsReindexFill::None}} skips this fill step entirely, leaving any
still\sphinxhyphen{}unmatched cells as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{target\_axis} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new time axis (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}) to reindex onto. Becomes the result’s
case labels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The matching strategy described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fill} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsReindexFill}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The post\sphinxhyphen{}alignment gap\sphinxhyphen{}fill strategy: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}} (no fill), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Zero}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Constant}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{constant} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}double\textgreater{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fill value when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill == TsReindexFill::Constant}}. Required in that case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{time\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, two overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
An explicit feature name supplying this accessor’s own source time axis, instead
of using its case labels or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_axis}} as its case labels, and every bound feature
reindexed according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to:id2}}

DataFrameTsAccessor::align\PYGZus{}to: constant fill requires a value
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsReindexFill::Constant}} needs an
actual value to fill with, so omitting it throws rather than silently falling
back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}} is the mirror image of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}} — each gap takes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{next}
available value instead of the last one — and is what
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/bfill::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsResampler::bfill()}}}}}}} is built on
(deliberately the opposite naming: forward\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{fill} means “carry backward\sphinxhyphen{}looking
values forward,” so it maps to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode::Backward}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}} picks whichever neighbor (before or after) is chronologically closer,
breaking ties toward the earlier one; it underlies
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/nearest::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsResampler::nearest()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} overloads are a convenience for immediately gap\sphinxhyphen{}filling the
reindexed result — equivalent to calling the 2\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload and then
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_gaps()}}}}}}} yourself, except \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsReindexFill::None}} (a value not
present on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GapFillMode}}) explicitly means “don’t fill at all.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/insert_gaps::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::insert\_gaps}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsResampler::asfreq}}}}}}} are both
thin wrappers over this method with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode::Exact}} and a regular
frequency\sphinxhyphen{}derived \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_axis}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts(options)}} auto\sphinxhyphen{}bind only the numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} columns on
the calling frame; a named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} column meant for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} is simply skipped rather than rejected, so a frame can carry
both value features and a named time\sphinxhyphen{}axis column at once (Example 2).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} overloads consume that column purely as an alignment key —
it does not appear in the output, which instead takes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target\_axis}} as its
new case labels, exactly like the case\sphinxhyphen{}labels\sphinxhyphen{}only overloads.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/asfreq:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}}s every bound feature onto the regular grid implied by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} to combine any bucket that contains more than one
source observation, then immediately runs {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_gaps()}}}}}}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_mode}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} over the resampled result. Since
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}} already produces one row per bucket in the regular
grid — including empty ones, which come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — the only thing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{asfreq()}}
adds on top is filling those \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s in a single call.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/asfreq:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{asfreq()}} is exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample(freq/options, op)}} followed by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_gaps(fill\_mode, constant)}} on every bound feature — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}} for the underlying bucketing rules.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op = Last}} differs from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}}’s own default
behavior of requiring an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{asfreq()}} picks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Last}} to match the
common “most recent observation stands for the period” convention.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_mode = GapFillMode::Zero}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Constant}} fill \sphinxstylestrong{every} empty bucket
unconditionally; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}} only fill gaps that have a qualifying
neighbor in that direction — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_gaps()}}}}}}} for the full
behavior.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/bounded:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The most general window primitive: instead of a fixed trailing size
({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}), a growing size ({\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expanding()}}}}}}}), or a
duration, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounded()}} takes a callback that computes each row’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}}
window bounds directly, given the case count and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}. This lets you express
window shapes none of the other accessor methods can — for example, a window that
deliberately excludes the current row.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/bounded:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bounds} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const WindowBoundsFn\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A callback \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(std::int64\_t size, const WindowOptions\& options) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} pair\textless{}vector\textless{}int64\_t\textgreater{}, vector\textless{}int64\_t\textgreater{}\textgreater{}}}
returning one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}} pair per row. Must not be empty.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The statistic computed over each row’s custom window — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}
for the full set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const WindowOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Passed through to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}} unchanged, and used for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} when
evaluating the statistic — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/bounded:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its custom\sphinxhyphen{}bounded window statistic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s window is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 0)}} — empty, since there’s nothing before it — so with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 1}} it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s window is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1)}}, just \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load{[}0{]} = 10}}. Row
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}’s window is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 2)}}, the mean of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}}. Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}’s window is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 3)}}, the mean of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}}. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expanding()}}}}}}}, each row’s window here never includes its own value
— useful for leave\sphinxhyphen{}one\sphinxhyphen{}out baselines or detecting how far a row deviates from
everything observed strictly before it.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrameTsAccessor::bounded: bounds callback is empty
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::function}} holds no callable target; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounded()}}
checks for that up front rather than crashing when it tries to invoke \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/bounded:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounds}} is called once per \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounded()}} invocation (not once per row) and must
return one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, end)}} pair per row, each satisfying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0 \textless{}= start \textless{}= end \textless{}= size}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} still apply to whatever window each row ends up
with, exactly as in {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}} — an empty or too\sphinxhyphen{}small window
still produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} rather than an error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the primitive {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expanding()}}}}}}},
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/grouped::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grouped()}}}}}}} are all built from with a fixed bounds strategy;
reach for it directly only when none of those shapes fit.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/calendar:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extracts calendar components from a time axis into their own numeric/text
columns: year, month, day, hour, and a formatted weekday string. The no\sphinxhyphen{}argument
overload uses this accessor’s own time axis (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}} if set, otherwise
its case labels, which must be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}); the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} overload
instead reads an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature by name and prefixes each
output column with that feature’s name.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/calendar:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{time\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The name of an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature to extract components from,
instead of this accessor’s own axis.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/calendar:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with five columns — year, month, day, hour, and a formatted
weekday string — one row per case on the source axis.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/calendar:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{axis\_weekday}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{time\_feature\}\_weekday}} is a formatted \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"YYYY\sphinxhyphen{}MM\sphinxhyphen{}DD (Abbreviated weekday)"}} string, not a bare weekday name or numeric code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The no\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload requires a genuine time axis — either an explicit
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}}, or case labels that are already \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — and
throws otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike most other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} accessor methods, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{calendar()}}’s output columns are
unrelated to whichever numeric feature(s) happen to be bound — it only ever
reads the time axis itself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts(options)}} auto\sphinxhyphen{}bind only the numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} columns on
the calling frame as this accessor’s value features; any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
(or other non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric) column is simply skipped rather than rejected, which is
what makes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}}\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}name overload reachable in Example 2 above —
a frame can carry both value features and a named time\sphinxhyphen{}axis column at once.

\end{itemize}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{diff}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/diff:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the absolute period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period change of every bound feature:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = x{[}i{]} \sphinxhyphen{} base{[}i{]}}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} (a lag when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textgreater{} 0}}, a lead when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textless{} 0}}). A cell is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is missing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 0}} produces all zeros rather than throwing.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/diff:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The shift distance used to build the comparison base. Positive shifts compare each
row against an earlier one (a lag); negative shifts compare against a later one (a
lead).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/diff:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period absolute difference.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/div:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Divides every bound feature by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, first aligning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows onto this
accessor’s own time axis according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}} — the exact same alignment model as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, with division in place of addition. For each bound feature
name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} must have a same\sphinxhyphen{}named feature; that feature’s values are aligned
onto this accessor’s axis (producing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever no match is found), then
divided elementwise into the bound feature’s own values.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/div:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand frame (the divisor). Must contain a feature with the same name as
every feature currently bound on this accessor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows are matched onto this accessor’s time axis — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the full description of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/div:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as this accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its quotient with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s aligned values.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/div:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result’s case labels are always this accessor’s own axis — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the full notes on alignment and matching behavior, which
apply identically here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every bound feature must have a same\sphinxhyphen{}named counterpart on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, or the call
throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Division by an aligned zero follows ordinary floating\sphinxhyphen{}point division rules
(producing infinity or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, displayed accordingly), not a special \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} case.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An exponentially weighted moving statistic: each row’s output blends every prior
row (and itself), with weight decaying geometrically the further back a row is.
Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic::Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} are supported. With smoothing factor
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta = 1 \sphinxhyphen{} alpha}}, row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}’s weight for an observation \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{j}} rows back is
proportional to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta\textasciicircum{}j}} — larger \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} forgets the past faster.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adjusted}} selects between two well\sphinxhyphen{}known formulations:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adjusted = true}}} (the default): each row’s mean is a normalized weighted
average, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum(x{[}k{]} * beta\textasciicircum{}(i\sphinxhyphen{}k)) / sum(beta\textasciicircum{}(i\sphinxhyphen{}k))}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}. This
is well\sphinxhyphen{}defined from the very first row.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adjusted = false}}}: the classic recursive form, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y{[}0{]} = x{[}0{]}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y{[}i{]} = beta * y{[}i\sphinxhyphen{}1{]} + alpha * x{[}i{]}}}. This form requires the input to have no
nulls at all (throws otherwise).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{alpha} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Smoothing factor in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0, 1{]}}}. Larger values weight recent observations more
heavily.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} — any other value throws.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{adjusted} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Selects the normalized\sphinxhyphen{}weighted\sphinxhyphen{}average form (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) versus the classic recursive
form (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}), described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bias\_corrected} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} only: whether to apply a finite\sphinxhyphen{}sample bias correction to the
exponentially weighted variance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimum non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations seen so far required for a row’s output to be
non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ignore\_nulls} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, a null observation is skipped entirely when computing decay weights
(as if it were never in the series), rather than contributing a gap in the decay
schedule.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its exponentially weighted statistic.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
==================
     | load       
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | 10         
1    | 10         
2    | 13.33333333
3    | 22.85714286
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s null contributes no value either way, and both forms report \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} —
the running average carried over from row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, since a null row never
resets or invalidates the decay (it’s still \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count.ge(min\_count)}}\sphinxhyphen{}valid, just
unchanged from its predecessor). The two forms diverge starting at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}:
with the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ignore\_nulls = false}}, row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is still treated as being
\sphinxstyleemphasis{two} decay\sphinxhyphen{}steps behind row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (the gap itself counts toward the decay
distance), giving it less relative weight (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{14}}); with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ignore\_nulls = true}},
the null row is skipped entirely when counting decay distance, so row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is
treated as only \sphinxstyleemphasis{one} step behind row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, giving it more relative weight
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{13.333}}) — and the same pattern carries through to row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adjusted = true}} (default) form, used in Example 1, tolerates nulls instead.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::decay: only Mean, Var, and Std are supported
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}} has other members used elsewhere (by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}
and friends), but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ewm()}} only implements these three — anything else is
rejected rather than silently falling back to one of them.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adjusted = false}} requires the source feature to have no null values at all —
it throws immediately otherwise (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adjusted = true}} tolerates nulls, subject to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ignore\_nulls}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha = 1.0}} degenerates to returning the input unchanged (each row weighs only
itself).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bias\_corrected}} only affects \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, applying a correction factor akin to
Bessel’s correction for exponentially weighted variance; it has no effect on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::expanding}}}}}}}: an equally\sphinxhyphen{}weighted “everything
so far” statistic, as opposed to this method’s exponentially decaying weights.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/weigh::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::weigh}}}}}}}: a fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size window with an explicit,
caller\sphinxhyphen{}supplied weight kernel instead of a geometric decay.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsAccessor::expanding}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding:dataframetsaccessor-expanding}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{expanding}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{statistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{StatisticOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The same trailing\sphinxhyphen{}window engine as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}, except the window
always starts at row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and grows to include every row up to and including the
current one — equivalent to calling \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling(ncases(), statistic, \{...\})}} with a
window size at least as large as the whole series.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The statistic computed over each row’s growing window — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}
for the full set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const StatisticOptions\&}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): delta degrees of freedom for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): minimum non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations
required for a row’s output to be non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its expanding statistic.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/expanding:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expanding()}} is exactly {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}} with a window as large as the
whole series — every row’s output reflects every prior row (plus itself),
never a fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size trailing subset.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} still require the growing window’s observation count to exceed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result keeps the accessor’s original case labels; nothing is dropped or
re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fills missing (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}) values in every bound feature according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}} (the default): each gap is filled with the nearest preceding
non\sphinxhyphen{}null value (a “last observation carried forward” fill).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}}: each gap is filled with the nearest following non\sphinxhyphen{}null value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Zero}}}: every gap is filled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Constant}}}: every gap is filled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} (which must be supplied, or
the call throws).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A gap with no qualifying neighbor in the requested direction (for example, leading
nulls under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}, or trailing nulls under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}) remains \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. This
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GapFillMode}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::subsp::stats::ts::GapFillMode}}) has exactly these four
values — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Zero}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Constant}} — and no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}}/no\sphinxhyphen{}op member;
don’t confuse it with the unrelated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsReindexFill}} enum used by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\_to()}}}}}}}, which does have a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}} value.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GapFillMode}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fill strategy, described above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{constant} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}double\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fill value for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GapFillMode::Constant}}. Required (and only meaningful) when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode == Constant}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
gaps filled according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}}.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GapFillMode::Constant}} needs an actual
fill value, so omitting it throws instead of silently falling back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}}
(that’s what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GapFillMode::Zero}} is for).


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/fill_gaps:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}} gaps with no qualifying neighbor in that direction (leading
nulls under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}, trailing nulls under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}) remain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — neither
mode manufactures a value from nothing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Constant}} requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constant}} to be supplied; calling it without one throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Zero}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Constant}} fill \sphinxstylestrong{every} gap unconditionally, regardless of its position,
unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}’s directional dependency.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/grouped:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The same fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size trailing rolling statistic as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling(window, statistic, options)}}}}}}}, but computed \sphinxstylestrong{independently
within each group}, using each group’s own rows in their original relative order
(not resorted by group). A row’s window never reaches across a group boundary.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{no\sphinxhyphen{}argument\sphinxhyphen{}group overload} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grouped(window, statistic, options)}})
requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.group}} to already be set (via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{...\}).ts(\{.group = ...\})}}) and throws otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} overload} looks up an existing feature \sphinxstyleemphasis{by name} on the
exact frame \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} was called on — since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} requires every feature on that
frame to already be numeric, this only works if the group column is itself
numeric (or if it wasn’t dropped by an earlier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.features(\{...\})}} narrowing
step). In practice, the \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{groups}}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} overload} below is the more
reliable choice whenever the grouping key is non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric, since it lets you
extract that key \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} narrowing to the numeric value feature(s).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{groups}} overload} takes an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} of grouping keys, one per
case, matching the frame’s case count, independent of whichever features are
currently bound to the accessor.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/grouped:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{window} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The trailing window size, in rows, applied independently within each group.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The statistic computed over each window — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}} for the
full set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const WindowOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Same fields as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}’s fixed\sphinxhyphen{}window overload: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{centered}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closure}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{group\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The name of an existing feature on the frame whose values define the groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{groups} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const Thread\&}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
An explicit per\sphinxhyphen{}case grouping key; must be defined and match the frame’s case
count.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/grouped:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its grouped rolling statistic.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/grouped:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rows are grouped by matching key value, using each group’s original row order —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{grouped()}} does not sort or otherwise reorder cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every group’s rolling computation uses the exact same
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}\sphinxhyphen{}style partial\sphinxhyphen{}window and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}} semantics,
just scoped to that group’s own rows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The no\sphinxhyphen{}argument\sphinxhyphen{}group overload is the one to reach for when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.group}} was
already set once (via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts(\{.group = ...\})}}) and several grouped operations will
reuse it without repeating the group argument each time.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/insert_gaps:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a regular grid of ticks (using the same frequency bucketing as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}}) spanning this accessor’s own time range, then
reindexes every bound feature onto that grid with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode::Exact}} — a thin
wrapper over {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\_to()}}}}}}}. Any tick in the grid that has no exact
match in the source data comes back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}; unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/asfreq::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{asfreq()}}}}}}}, no
aggregation and no gap\sphinxhyphen{}filling happen here — this method only ever inserts
missing rows, it never combines or fills them.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/insert_gaps:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{freq} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bucket frequency defining the regular grid — same calendar/frequency string
convention as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{step} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A frequency multiplier, exactly as in {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{time\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, one overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
An explicit feature name supplying the time axis, instead of this accessor’s case
labels or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/insert_gaps:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one row per tick of the regular grid, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever the
source data had no exact match.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/insert_gaps:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{insert\_gaps(freq, step)}} is exactly
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\_to(bins.labels, TsAlignMode::Exact)}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}} comes from the same
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample\_bins}}\sphinxhyphen{}style bucketing {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}} uses — see that
method for the full frequency\sphinxhyphen{}string grammar.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No aggregation happens here even if a bucket somehow contained more than one
source tick at the exact same instant — use {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}}}}}} if
values need combining.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts(options)}} auto\sphinxhyphen{}bind only the numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} columns on
the calling frame; a named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} column meant for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} is simply skipped rather than rejected, so a frame can carry
both value features and a named time\sphinxhyphen{}axis column at once (Example 2).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} overload consumes that column purely as an alignment key —
it does not appear in the output, which instead takes the regular grid as its
new case labels.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsAccessor::lag}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag:dataframetsaccessor-lag}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shifts every bound feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} rows forward: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = x{[}i \sphinxhyphen{} periods{]}}} where
that index is in bounds, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} otherwise. A negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} delegates to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lead::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lead()}}}}}}} with the sign flipped.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of rows to shift forward. Negative values behave as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lead::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lead(\sphinxhyphen{}periods)}}}}}}} instead.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature lagged by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} rows.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Lag a numeric feature by one row.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag_block:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes several {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag()}}}}}}} shifts of the accessor’s (single) bound feature
at once, each as its own output column named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"lag" + \textless{}lag value\textgreater{}}}. Requires at
least one lag, and requires exactly one feature to be bound (since every output
column is derived from that one feature’s raw values).

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag_block:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{lags} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The lag distances to compute, in the order given. Must not be empty.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag_block:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one column per requested lag (named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"lag1"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"lag2"}}, and so
on), same case labels as the accessor’s bound feature.

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag1}} is the same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag(1)}}}}}}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}NULL, 10, 20, 15{]}}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag2}} is
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag(2)}}}}}}}: each row now shows the value from two rows earlier, so both
cases \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (which have no row two positions back) are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} shows
case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}, and case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} shows case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag_block:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each requested lag becomes its own output column, letting you compare several lag
depths of the same feature side by side in one call, rather than calling
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag()}}}}}}} repeatedly and combining the results yourself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output columns are always named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"lag" + \textless{}value\textgreater{}}} — there’s no way to customize
the column names from this method directly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires exactly one bound feature; narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if the source frame has more than
one.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag_block:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::lag}}}}}}}: the single\sphinxhyphen{}lag building block this method

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling_block::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::rolling\_block}}}}}}}: the equivalent “several
at once” pattern for rolling window statistics instead of lags.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/log_returns:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the logarithmic period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period change of every bound feature:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = ln(x{[}i{]} / base{[}i{]})}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} (a lag when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textgreater{} 0}}, a lead when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textless{} 0}}). A cell is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is missing or non\sphinxhyphen{}finite, \sphinxstylestrong{or either value is not strictly positive} —
unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/returns::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}}}}}}}, a zero or negative value anywhere in the
comparison always yields \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, since the logarithm would otherwise be undefined.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/log_returns:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The shift distance used to build the comparison base. Positive shifts compare each
row against an earlier one (a lag); negative shifts compare against a later one (a
lead). Must not be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or the call throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/log_returns:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period log return.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/log_returns:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/returns::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log\_returns()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{both} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} to be strictly greater than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}; a zero or negative value in either
produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} rather than an error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Log returns are additive across periods (the sum of consecutive one\sphinxhyphen{}period log
returns equals the multi\sphinxhyphen{}period log return), which plain fractional
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/returns::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}}}}}}} are not — a common reason to prefer this method for
compounding analysis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result keeps the accessor’s original case labels; nothing is dropped or
re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{mul}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TsAlignMode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TsAlignMode}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Exact}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/mul:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplies every bound feature by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}, first aligning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows onto this
accessor’s own time axis according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}} — the exact same alignment model as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, with multiplication in place of addition. For each bound feature
name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} must have a same\sphinxhyphen{}named feature; that feature’s values are aligned
onto this accessor’s axis (producing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever no match is found), then
multiplied elementwise with the bound feature’s own values.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/mul:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand frame. Must contain a feature with the same name as every feature
currently bound on this accessor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows are matched onto this accessor’s time axis — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the full description of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/mul:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as this accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its product with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s aligned values.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buckets every bound feature into regular calendar/duration periods (like every
day, every 6 hours, every week) and aggregates each bucket. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq}} supports
fixed units (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{H}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}, optionally prefixed with a multiplier like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"6H"}}), calendar\sphinxhyphen{}aware \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{W}} (weekly), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}} (monthly), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Y}} (yearly) buckets.
Every bucket in the regular grid between the data’s minimum and maximum tick
appears in the result — including ones with zero source observations, which come
back as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{First}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Last}}) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}).
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Without an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}} (returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsResampler}}): a lazy, chainable form —
call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mean()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sum()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.min()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.max()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.first()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.last()}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.count()}} on the result to actually aggregate, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.asfreq()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ffill()}}/
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.bfill()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.nearest()}} to reindex instead of aggregate.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{With an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}} (returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} directly): equivalent to calling the
matching method on the chainable form in one step.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{freq} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}) / \sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const pluss::TimeIndex::ResampleOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bucket frequency. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} additionally exposes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closed}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{origin}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StartDay}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Start}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Epoch}}), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset\_nanos}} for finer control than a bare
frequency string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{step} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A frequency multiplier — for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step = 6}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freq = "H"}} produces 6\sphinxhyphen{}hour
buckets.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{op} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ResampleOp}}, overloads that return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} directly)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The aggregation applied to each bucket: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{First}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Last}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{time\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, four overloads)

\sphinxAtStartPar
An explicit feature name supplying the time axis, instead of this accessor’s case
labels or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsResampler}}
(No\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} overloads) A chainable accessor; nothing is aggregated until one of
its own methods is called.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}\sphinxhyphen{}taking overloads) The aggregated result directly, one row per bucket.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every bucket in the contiguous grid from the data’s minimum to maximum tick
appears in the result, even ones with zero observations — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}} never
silently skips empty periods (that’s exactly what makes it useful for finding
gaps, alongside {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/insert_gaps::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{insert\_gaps()}}}}}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}} on an empty bucket produce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{First}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Last}}
produce \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bucket boundaries default to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closed = Left}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label = Left}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{origin = StartDay}} — the first bucket starts at midnight (in the axis’s own time zone) on
the day of the earliest observation, and each period is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}start, start + freq)}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::ts()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts(options)}} auto\sphinxhyphen{}bind only the numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} columns on
the calling frame; a named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} column meant for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} is simply skipped rather than rejected, so a frame can carry
both value features and a named time\sphinxhyphen{}axis column at once (Example 3).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_feature}} overloads consume that column purely as an alignment key —
it does not appear in the output, which instead takes the resample bucket
labels as its new case labels.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/returns:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the fractional period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period change of every bound feature:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = x{[}i{]} / base{[}i{]} \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} (a lag when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textgreater{} 0}}, a lead when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textless{} 0}}). A cell is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is missing, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or either value is non\sphinxhyphen{}finite.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/returns:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The shift distance used to build the comparison base. Positive shifts compare each
row against an earlier one (a lag); negative shifts compare against a later one (a
lead). Must not be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or the call throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/returns:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period fractional return.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/returns:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}} operates independently, feature by feature — every bound feature is
shifted and divided against its own prior (or later) values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} value of exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} always produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}}, since
the fractional change would otherwise be undefined or infinite.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result keeps the accessor’s original case labels; nothing is dropped or
re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed.

\end{itemize}
