\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes a \sphinxstylestrong{trailing rolling window statistic} over every bound feature, in one
of three shapes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fixed row count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling(window, statistic, options)}}): each row’s window is
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window}} rows ending at (and including) that row. The very first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}
rows use whatever’s available rather than waiting for a full window — row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s
window is just itself, row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s is rows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..1}}, and so on, until row
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} and beyond see a full window. A row’s output is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} only if the
number of non\sphinxhyphen{}null values it can see falls below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.min\_count}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Calendar duration} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling(duration, statistic, options, closure)}}): the same
trailing\sphinxhyphen{}window idea, but each row’s window spans a fixed span of time (like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"2D"}}) looked up against the accessor’s time axis, rather than a fixed row count.
This overload requires the frame’s case labels (or an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}})
to already be a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Structured specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling(specs, keep\_input)}}): delegates to a private
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::window(specs, keep\_input)}} helper (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor}} is declared
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{friend}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, so it can call it even though it isn’t part of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s own public interface) — each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowSpec}} names one feature, one
fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size window, and one of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingSum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingMean}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingMin}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingMax}},
producing one output column per spec (auto\sphinxhyphen{}named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{feature\}\_\{op\}\_\{window\}"}}
when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{spec.output}} is empty).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{window} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, fixed\sphinxhyphen{}window overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The trailing window size, in rows. Must be positive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The statistic computed over each window: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sem}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Skew}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kurtosis}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const WindowOptions\&}}, fixed\sphinxhyphen{}window overload)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): minimum non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations
required for a row’s output to be non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}): delta degrees of freedom for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{centered}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}): whether the window is centered on the
row instead of trailing it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closure}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowClosure}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}}): which end(s) of the window are
inclusive.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{duration} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A duration string (for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"2D"}}) defining each row’s time\sphinxhyphen{}based window width.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{closure} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowClosure}}, calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which end of the time window is inclusive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}DataFrame::WindowSpec\textgreater{}}}, structured overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{output, feature, op, window, min\_periods\}}} records, each describing one
fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size rolling column to compute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_input} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, structured overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the original features are kept alongside the newly computed columns
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) or dropped in favor of just the computed columns (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with each targeted feature replaced (fixed\sphinxhyphen{}window and
calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overloads) or a frame combining originals and/or computed
columns (structured overload).

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{load}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
===========
     | load
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | 10  
1    | 15  
2    | 17.5
3    | 22.5
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 1}}, row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} doesn’t wait for a full 2\sphinxhyphen{}row window —
its output is just itself (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}). Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} sees a full window (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10, 20}}, mean
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}}); row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} sees \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(20, 15)}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{17.5}}; row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} sees \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(15, 30)}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{22.5}}. This
differs from libraries whose rolling default requires a full window before
producing a value — here, that behavior only kicks in if you raise
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.min\_count}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. The same window with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic::Std}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} bites at
row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rolled\PYGZus{}std}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{load}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Std}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rolled\PYGZus{}std}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

==================
     | load       
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | NULL       
1    | 7.071067812
2    | 3.535533906
3    | 10.60660172
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s window has only 1 observation, and the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} requires more
than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} observation for a defined variance/std, so it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} even though
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 1}} alone would have allowed it. Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} computes the sample standard
deviation of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10, 20)}}; row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(20, 15)}}; row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(15, 30)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar

     | load       
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 1 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window = 3}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{centered = true}}, row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s window is rows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..1}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10, 20}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}}, clipped at the series start); row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is rows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..2}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10, 20, 15}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}}); row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is rows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1..3}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20, 15, 30}} \(\rightarrow\)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{21.667}}); row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} is rows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2..3}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15, 30}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{22.5}}, clipped at the end) — each
window is centered on its row rather than trailing it, so both edges of the
series see a truncated window instead of just the leading one.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling:id3}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::moving: window must be \PYGZgt{} 0

\sphinxAtStartPar
A window of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (or negative) has no meaningful trailing span, so it’s
rejected outright.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fixed\sphinxhyphen{}window overload’s default options (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = 1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{centered = false}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closure = Right}}) mean the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} rows use a growing partial window
rather than becoming \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count = window}} to require a full window
everywhere instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} additionally require the window’s observation count to exceed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof}}
(default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}), independent of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overload needs a genuine time axis — either the frame’s own
case labels are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}, or an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}} supplies
one — and is not covered by a worked example here since it depends on frequency
and calendar conventions outside this reference’s current verified scope.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The structured \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{specs}} overload only supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}} (via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadWindowOp}}), not the full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}} set the other two overloads
support.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/grouped::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::grouped}}}}}}}: the same fixed\sphinxhyphen{}window statistic,
computed independently per group instead of over the whole feature.

\item {}

growing from the start of the series instead of a fixed size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling_block::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::rolling\_block}}}}}}}: computing several
window sizes and statistics of the same feature at once, each as its own output
column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

overload under a different public name.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsAccessor::rolling\_block}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling_block:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes several rolling\sphinxhyphen{}window statistics, over several window sizes, of the
accessor’s (single) bound feature in one call — each combination becomes its own
output column, named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"roll\_\{stat\}\_w\{window\}"}} (for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"roll\_mean\_w2"}}).
Requires exactly one feature to be bound.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling_block:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{windows} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}std::int64\_t\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The window sizes to compute, in the order given. Must not be empty.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const TsRollingBlockOptions\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which statistics to compute for every window size, and the shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_mean}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_std}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_min}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_max}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_sum}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_var}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling_block:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame with one column per requested \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(window, included statistic)}}
combination, same case labels as the accessor’s bound feature.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling_block:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(window, statistic)}} combination becomes its own column — with several
window sizes and several enabled statistics, the output can grow quickly
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{windows.size() * (number of enabled statistics)}} columns).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Column names are fixed to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"roll\_\{stat\}\_w\{window\}"}} pattern and aren’t
customizable from this method directly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods}} (default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}) is shared across every window size and statistic in
the call — there’s no way to vary it per window size in one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling\_block()}}
call.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires exactly one bound feature; narrow with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/features::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features()}}}}}}} first if the source frame has more than
one.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling_block:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::rolling}}}}}}}: the single\sphinxhyphen{}window, single\sphinxhyphen{}statistic

\item {}

pattern for lags instead of rolling statistics.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsAccessor::sort}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sort:dataframetsaccessor-sort}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sort::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sort:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sort}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nulls\PYGZus{}last}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sort:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reorders every bound feature’s rows into chronological order along the accessor’s
time axis. That axis is either an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}} (if supplied when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ts()}} was called), or — when no explicit axis is set — the frame’s own case
labels, which must already be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} kind (this method throws
otherwise). The result carries the same time axis, now sorted, as its case labels.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sort:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ascending} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sort chronologically forward (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) or backward (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nulls\_last} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether undefined axis positions sort after (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) or before (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}) every
defined position.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sort:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame containing the accessor’s bound features, reordered into
chronological order along the time axis, with that axis as its case labels.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sort:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With no explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}}, this method requires the frame’s own case
labels to already be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} — it throws if they’re a plain
numeric or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} index instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is distinct from {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe/label::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label().sort()}}}}}}},
which sorts by whatever kind the case labels happen to be; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts().sort()}} is
specifically the time\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}aware entry point within the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts()}} accessor.

\end{itemize}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sub}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TsAlignMode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{TsAlignMode}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Exact}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sub:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Subtracts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} from every bound feature, first aligning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows onto
this accessor’s own time axis according to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode}} — the exact same alignment model
as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}}, with subtraction in place of addition. For each bound feature
name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}} must have a same\sphinxhyphen{}named feature; that feature’s values are aligned
onto this accessor’s axis (producing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever no match is found), then
subtracted elementwise from the bound feature’s own values.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sub:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{other} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const DataFrame\&}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The right\sphinxhyphen{}hand frame. Must contain a feature with the same name as every feature
currently bound on this accessor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
How \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s rows are matched onto this accessor’s time axis — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/add::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add()}}}}}}} for the full description of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Backward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Forward}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nearest}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/sub:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as this accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its difference against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other}}’s aligned values.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/weigh:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A trailing rolling statistic where each position in the window is scaled by an
explicit weight instead of contributing equally. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}} fixes the window
size; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights{[}0{]}}} applies to the oldest row in the window and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.back()}}
applies to the current row. Rows at the very start of the series see a
partially\sphinxhyphen{}filled window — the missing (not\sphinxhyphen{}yet\sphinxhyphen{}reached) positions simply don’t
contribute, and the remaining weights are \sphinxstylestrong{not renormalized to add up to their
original total} beyond dividing by whatever weight total is actually present, so
early rows are naturally computed from fewer, more\sphinxhyphen{}recent weights.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic::Minimum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}} ignore the weight \sphinxstyleemphasis{magnitudes} entirely (only
the window width \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}} matters) and fall back to the same trailing
extremum {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}} computes.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/weigh:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{weights} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}double\textgreater{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}position weight kernel, oldest\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}newest. Must not be empty.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{statistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}}. (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sem}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Skew}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kurtosis}} are not
supported by this method.)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_count} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimum non\sphinxhyphen{}null, in\sphinxhyphen{}window observations required for a row’s output to be
non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Must be between \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/weigh:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its weighted rolling statistic.

as plain {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling(2, Minimum)}}}}}}}.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/weigh:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Thread::weigh: weights cannot be empty
Thread::weigh: invalid min\PYGZus{}count
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty weight kernel has no window width to speak of, so it’s rejected
outright. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_count}} must be between \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}} inclusive; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}
exceeds the 2\sphinxhyphen{}element kernel’s own size, so that throws too.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/weigh:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike an unweighted {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}, the weights let recent
observations count more (or less) than older ones within the same window — a
common building block for smoothing filters distinct from
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ewm()}}}}}}}’s continuously\sphinxhyphen{}decaying kernel.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Minimum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Maximum}} only use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weights.size()}} as the window width; the actual
weight values are ignored for those two statistics.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result keeps the accessor’s original case labels; nothing is dropped or
re\sphinxhyphen{}indexed.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/weigh:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::rolling}}}}}}}: the unweighted (equal\sphinxhyphen{}contribution)
trailing window statistic this method generalizes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/ewm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::ewm}}}}}}}: a different, continuously\sphinxhyphen{}decaying weighting
scheme rather than a fixed, explicit kernel.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/bounded::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::bounded}}}}}}}: fully custom window bounds instead
of a fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size weighted kernel.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{window}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{duration}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowClosure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{closure}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{WindowClosure}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/window:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two unrelated shapes share this name:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Structured specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window(specs, keep\_input)}}): delegates to a private
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::window(specs, keep\_input)}} helper (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor}} is declared
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{friend}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, so it can reach it even though it isn’t part of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}’s own public interface) — each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::WindowSpec}} names one
feature, a fixed window size, one of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingSum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingMean}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingMin}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RollingMax}}, and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods}},
producing one computed output column per spec. When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{spec.output}} is empty, the
column is auto\sphinxhyphen{}named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{feature\}\_\{op\}\_\{window\}"}} (for example
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"load\_rollmean\_2"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Calendar duration} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window(duration, closure)}}): enters a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}} scoped to a fixed time span (like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"2D"}}) against the
accessor’s time axis, whose own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}
methods then compute grouped, duration\sphinxhyphen{}bucketed aggregates. This overload
requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.group}} to already be set and a genuine time axis (the
frame’s case labels already \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}, or an explicit
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.axis}}).

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/window:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{specs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::RangeView\textless{}DataFrame::WindowSpec\textgreater{}}}, structured overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{output, feature, op, window, min\_periods\}}} records, each describing one
fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size rolling column to compute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{keep\_input} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bool}}, structured overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Whether the original features are kept alongside the newly computed columns
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}) or dropped in favor of just the computed columns (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{duration} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overload)

\sphinxAtStartPar
A duration string (for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"2D"}}) defining the fixed time span each bucket in
the resulting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}} spans.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{closure} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowClosure}}, calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overload, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Which end of each time bucket is inclusive.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/window:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
(Structured overload) A frame combining the original and/or newly computed
rolling columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}}
(Calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overload) An accessor exposing duration\sphinxhyphen{}bucketed
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/window:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The structured\sphinxhyphen{}specs overload only supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}} (via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadWindowOp}}), not the full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowStatistic}} set
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}’s other overloads support.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The calendar\sphinxhyphen{}duration overload’s output depends on frequency and calendar
bucketing conventions outside this reference’s current verified scope, so it
isn’t covered by a worked example here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window(specs, keep\_input)}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling(specs, keep\_input)}}}}}}} (the
structured\sphinxhyphen{}specs overload of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}) are the exact same operation under two
names.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/zscore_rolling:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes a trailing rolling z\sphinxhyphen{}score for every bound feature:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = (x{[}i{]} \sphinxhyphen{} rolling\_mean{[}i{]}) / rolling\_std{[}i{]}}}, where the rolling mean and
standard deviation are the same trailing\sphinxhyphen{}window statistics
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}} computes (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}}, partial windows honored). A cell is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}}, the rolling mean, or the rolling standard deviation is undefined,
or if the rolling standard deviation’s magnitude doesn’t exceed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{epsilon}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/zscore_rolling:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{window} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The trailing window size, in rows, used for both the rolling mean and rolling
standard deviation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{min\_periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimum non\sphinxhyphen{}null observations required in the window for both the mean and
standard deviation to be defined.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{epsilon} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1e\sphinxhyphen{}12}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
The minimum rolling standard deviation magnitude treated as non\sphinxhyphen{}zero; a smaller
magnitude produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} rather than dividing by (near) zero.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/zscore_rolling:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
A new frame, same shape and case labels as the accessor’s bound features, with
each feature replaced by its rolling z\sphinxhyphen{}score.

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[4 cs x 1 feat]

\sphinxAtStartPar
Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s window has only 1 observation, so its rolling standard deviation is
undefined (the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ddof = 1}} requires more than 1 observation) and the
z\sphinxhyphen{}score is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s window is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10, 20)}}: mean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}}, std ≈ \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7.0711}}, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z = (20 \sphinxhyphen{} 15) / 7.0711 ≈ 0.7071}}. Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}’s window is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(20, 15)}}: mean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{17.5}},
std ≈ \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3.5355}}, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z = (15 \sphinxhyphen{} 17.5) / 3.5355 ≈ \sphinxhyphen{}0.7071}}. Row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}’s window is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(15, 30)}}: mean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{22.5}}, std ≈ \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.6066}}, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z = (30 \sphinxhyphen{} 22.5) / 10.6066 ≈ 0.7071}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/zscore_rolling:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{zscore\_rolling()}} is built directly from the same {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling()}}}}}}}
mean/std computation — every partial\sphinxhyphen{}window and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods}} behavior
documented there applies identically here for both the numerator and
denominator.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{epsilon}} guards only against a (near\sphinxhyphen{})zero rolling standard deviation, not
against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} or the rolling mean being undefined — either of those still
produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{epsilon}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/zscore_rolling:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/rolling::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::rolling}}}}}}}: the underlying rolling mean/std this

\item {}

by relative order rather than a rolling distributional statistic.

\end{itemize}

\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/count:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes, \sphinxstylestrong{once per group}, the number of observations of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} over
the trailing duration\sphinxhyphen{}length window ending at that group’s own most recent
time\sphinxhyphen{}axis value (or an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.anchor}}, if one was set) — the same
per\sphinxhyphen{}group trailing window {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} uses, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}} in place of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}.
Unlike the other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}} methods, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} doesn’t need
to be numeric for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}}, since it only counts observations rather than
combining their values.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/count:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to count observations of. May be omitted only if exactly one feature
is currently bound on the accessor.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/count:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per distinct group, with a group\sphinxhyphen{}key column (or columns) and a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"count\_" + value\_feature}} column.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count()}} only tallies how many observations fall in the window — it never
reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}}’s actual text values, so there’s no numeric requirement on it
the way there is for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max()}}.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/max:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes, \sphinxstylestrong{once per group}, the maximum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} over the trailing
duration\sphinxhyphen{}length window ending at that group’s own most recent time\sphinxhyphen{}axis value (or
an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.anchor}}, if one was set) — the same per\sphinxhyphen{}group trailing
window {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} uses, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}} in place of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} for the full setup requirements (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.group}}, window
closure, anchoring).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/max:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to maximize. May be omitted only if exactly one feature is currently
bound on the accessor.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/max:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per distinct group, with a group\sphinxhyphen{}key column (or columns) and a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"max\_" + value\_feature}} column.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/mean:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes, \sphinxstylestrong{once per group}, the mean of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} over the trailing
duration\sphinxhyphen{}length window ending at that group’s own most recent time\sphinxhyphen{}axis value (or
an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.anchor}}, if one was set) — the same per\sphinxhyphen{}group trailing
window {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} uses, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}} in place of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} for the full setup requirements (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.group}}, window
closure, anchoring).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/mean:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to average. May be omitted only if exactly one feature is currently
bound on the accessor.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/mean:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per distinct group, with a group\sphinxhyphen{}key column (or columns) and a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"mean\_" + value\_feature}} column.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/min:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes, \sphinxstylestrong{once per group}, the minimum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} over the trailing
duration\sphinxhyphen{}length window ending at that group’s own most recent time\sphinxhyphen{}axis value (or
an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.anchor}}, if one was set) — the same per\sphinxhyphen{}group trailing
window {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} uses, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}} in place of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}} for the full setup requirements (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.group}}, window
closure, anchoring).


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/min:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to minimize. May be omitted only if exactly one feature is currently
bound on the accessor.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/min:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per distinct group, with a group\sphinxhyphen{}key column (or columns) and a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"min\_" + value\_feature}} column.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor::sum}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum:dataframetswindowaccessor-sum}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_window_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsWindowAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{value\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes, \sphinxstylestrong{once per group}, the sum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} over the trailing
duration\sphinxhyphen{}length window ending at that group’s own most recent time\sphinxhyphen{}axis value (or
an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.anchor}}, if one was set). This is a per\sphinxhyphen{}group trailing
aggregate — not a resample\sphinxhyphen{}style bucketing — so the result has exactly one row
per distinct group, not one row per original observation.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, default empty)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature to sum. May be omitted only if exactly one feature is currently bound
on the accessor, in which case that feature is used automatically.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per distinct group, with a group\sphinxhyphen{}key column (or columns) and a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sum\_" + value\_feature}} column.

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrameTsAccessor::window: TsOptions.group is required
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The check happens as soon as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.window(...)}} builds the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsWindowAccessor}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}} (or any other aggregate) never even
gets a chance to run without a group already set via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{...\}).ts(\{.group = df.features("group\_col")\})}}.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-window/sum:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.group}} to already be set (via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features(\{...\}).ts(\{.group = df.features("group\_col")\})}}, extracting the
group column \sphinxstyleemphasis{before} narrowing to the numeric value feature, exactly as shown
above) — the accessor throws at construction otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The window is right\sphinxhyphen{}closed by default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WindowClosure::Right}}, set via
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/window::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closure}} parameter): it excludes the
anchor\sphinxhyphen{}minus\sphinxhyphen{}duration boundary itself and includes the anchor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With no explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsOptions.anchor}}, each group’s own anchor is that group’s
\sphinxstyleemphasis{own} maximum time\sphinxhyphen{}axis value — different groups can anchor to different
instants.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsResampler::asfreq}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq:dataframetsresampler-asfreq}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_resampler_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsResampler API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsResampler}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{asfreq}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fill\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reindexes the original (unaggregated) rows onto the regular grid produced by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}, using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode::Exact}}}}}}} tick matching — a grid tick
keeps its source value only if a source observation lands on that exact tick;
otherwise it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. This is unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/sum::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}}}}}}/etc.,
which aggregate every observation \sphinxstyleemphasis{within} each bucket; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{asfreq()}} only ever
keeps a value that already sat precisely on a bucket boundary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_value}} is supplied, every grid tick that did \sphinxstylestrong{not} get an exact match
is replaced by that single constant instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — the same constant for
every gap, regardless of position.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fill\_value} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}double\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
A constant substituted for every non\sphinxhyphen{}exact\sphinxhyphen{}match grid tick. Leave as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}} to keep those ticks \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per tick in the regular grid, with only exact matches (or the
supplied \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fill\_value}}) populated.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/asfreq:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsResampler::bfill}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/bfill:dataframetsresampler-bfill}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/bfill::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_resampler_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsResampler API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/bfill:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsResampler}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{bfill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/bfill:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reindexes the original (unaggregated) rows onto the regular grid produced by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}, using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode::Forward}}}}}}} tick matching — each grid
tick takes the value of the next source observation at or after it (the
standard “backward\sphinxhyphen{}fill” reindex, so named because values flow backward in
time to fill earlier gaps). A tick with no eligible later observation produces
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/bfill:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per tick in the regular grid, each carrying back the next known
value at or after that tick.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsResampler::count}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/count:dataframetsresampler-count}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/count::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_resampler_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsResampler API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/count:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsResampler}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/count:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregates every bucket built by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}
with the number of observations it holds. Equivalent to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{accessor.resample(freq/options, ResampleOp::Count)}}. A bucket with zero
observations produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/count:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per bucket in the regular grid, each feature replaced by its bucket’s
observation count.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsResampler::ffill}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/ffill:dataframetsresampler-ffill}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/ffill::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_resampler_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsResampler API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/ffill:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsResampler}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ffill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/ffill:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reindexes the original (unaggregated) rows onto the regular grid produced by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}, using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode::Backward}}}}}}} tick matching — each grid
tick takes the value of the most recent source observation at or before it (the
standard “forward\sphinxhyphen{}fill” reindex). A tick with no eligible prior observation
produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/ffill:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per tick in the regular grid, each carrying forward the last known
value at or before that tick.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/first:dataframetsresampler-first}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/first::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_resampler_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsResampler API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/first:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsResampler}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/first:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregates every bucket built by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}
with its earliest observation (in original tick order). Equivalent to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{accessor.resample(freq/options, ResampleOp::First)}}. A bucket with zero
observations produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/first:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per bucket in the regular grid, each feature replaced by the value
of its bucket’s earliest observation.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/last:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregates every bucket built by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}
with its latest observation (in original tick order). Equivalent to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{accessor.resample(freq/options, ResampleOp::Last)}}. A bucket with zero
observations produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/last:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per bucket in the regular grid, each feature replaced by the value
of its bucket’s latest observation.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsResampler::nearest}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/nearest:dataframetsresampler-nearest}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/nearest::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_resampler_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsResampler API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/nearest:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsResampler}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nearest}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/nearest:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reindexes the original (unaggregated) rows onto the regular grid produced by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}, using
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/align_to::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TsAlignMode::Nearest}}}}}}} tick matching — each grid
tick takes the value of whichever source observation is closest to it in time
(ties break toward the earlier candidate). A tick with no source observations
at all produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/nearest:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per tick in the regular grid, each taking the closest source
observation’s value.

\subparagraph{DataFrameTsResampler::sum}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/sum:dataframetsresampler-sum}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/sum::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_ts_resampler_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFrameTsResampler API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/sum:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrameTsResampler}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/sum:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregates every bucket built by {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts/resample::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameTsAccessor::resample()}}}}}}}
with the sum of its observations. Equivalent to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{accessor.resample(freq/options, ResampleOp::Sum)}}. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/mean::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/max::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/first::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{first()}}}}}}}, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/last::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{last()}}}}}}}, a bucket with zero observations produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-ts-resample/sum:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}
One row per bucket in the regular grid, each feature replaced by its bucket
sum.

\subparagraph{TimeSeriesAccessor::diff}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:timeseriesaccessor-diff}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to TimeSeriesAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{TimeSeriesAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{diff}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the absolute period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period change of the bound thread:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = x{[}i{]} \sphinxhyphen{} base{[}i{]}}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} (a lag when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textgreater{} 0}}, a lead when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textless{} 0}}). A position is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is missing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 0}} produces an all\sphinxhyphen{}zero result rather than
throwing. Restricted to a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread; anything else throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
The shift distance used to build the comparison base. Positive shifts compare
each position against an earlier one (a lag); negative shifts compare against
a later one (a lead).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as the bound source, holding the period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period
absolute difference.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute the one\sphinxhyphen{}period difference of a numeric thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{15.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{diff}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  10
2  \PYGZhy{}5
3  15

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} has no prior position, so it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20 \sphinxhyphen{} 10 = 10}}; position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15 \sphinxhyphen{} 20 = \sphinxhyphen{}5}}; position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30 \sphinxhyphen{} 15 = 15}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 0}} produces an all\sphinxhyphen{}zero result rather than throwing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{diff}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  0
1  0
2  0
3  0

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike a hand\sphinxhyphen{}rolled {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift()}}}}}}}\sphinxhyphen{}based approach, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff()}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

1  NULL
2  NULL
3  10

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}1{]}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}}) itself is masked\sphinxhyphen{}missing. Position

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/diff:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike a {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift()}}}}}}}\sphinxhyphen{}based approach you might build by hand,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff()}} handles \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 0}} explicitly by returning all zeros (an identity
comparison) rather than a thread of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A pre\sphinxhyphen{}existing missing entry in the source thread is honored — it produces
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every difference that would otherwise reference it, not just the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}s the shift itself introduces at the vacated end. See Example 3.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} thread
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeSeriesAccessor::diff: source must be Series"}}; a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeSeriesAccessor::diff: source Series must be numeric"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{TimeSeriesAccessor::lag}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:timeseriesaccessor-lag}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to TimeSeriesAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{TimeSeriesAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shifts the bound thread \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} positions forward: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = x{[}i \sphinxhyphen{} periods{]}}} where
that index is in bounds, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} otherwise. A negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} delegates to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lead()}}}}}}} with the sign flipped — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag(\sphinxhyphen{}periods)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lead(periods)}} are the
same operation. Restricted to a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread; anything else throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
The number of positions to shift forward. Negative values behave as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lead(\sphinxhyphen{}periods)}}}}}}} instead.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as the bound source, shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} positions.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Lag a numeric thread by one position.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{15.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  10
2  20
3  15

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each position now shows the previous position’s value: position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} shows position
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}, position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} shows position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}, and so on. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} has no
predecessor, so it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. This is the same operation
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread/shift::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread::shift(periods)}}}}}}} performs.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out3}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag:id1}}

1  15
2  30

\subparagraph{TimeSeriesAccessor::lead}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead:timeseriesaccessor-lead}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to TimeSeriesAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{TimeSeriesAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{lead}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shifts the bound thread \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} positions backward: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = x{[}i + periods{]}}} where
that index is in bounds, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} otherwise. A negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} delegates to
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag()}}}}}}} with the sign flipped — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lead(\sphinxhyphen{}periods)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag(periods)}} are the
same operation. Restricted to a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread; anything else throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
The number of positions to shift backward. Negative values behave as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag(\sphinxhyphen{}periods)}}}}}}} instead.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as the bound source, led by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} positions.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Lead a numeric thread by one position.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lead}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}

\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/lead:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  20
1  15
2  30
3  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each position now shows the next position’s value: position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} shows position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}, position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} shows position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15}}, and so on. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} has no
successor, so it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} lands at the opposite end from
