\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}gap}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lead}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{TimeSeriesAccessor::log\_returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns:timeseriesaccessor-log-returns}}\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{thread_ts_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to TimeSeriesAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the logarithmic period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period change of the bound thread:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = ln(x{[}i{]} / base{[}i{]})}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} (a lag when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textgreater{} 0}}, a lead when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textless{} 0}}). A position is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is missing or non\sphinxhyphen{}finite, \sphinxstylestrong{or either value is not strictly positive} —
unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}}}}}}}, a zero or negative value anywhere in the
comparison always yields \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, since the logarithm would otherwise be undefined.
Restricted to a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread; anything else throws.

\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
The shift distance used to build the comparison base. Positive shifts compare
each position against an earlier one (a lag); negative shifts compare against
a later one (a lead). Must not be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or the call throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as the bound source, holding the period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period
log return.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  0.6931471806
2  \PYGZhy{}0.2876820725
3  0.6931471806

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} has no prior position, so it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln(20 / 10) = ln(2) ≈ 0.6931}}; position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln(15 / 20) = ln(0.75) ≈ \sphinxhyphen{}0.2877}};
position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln(30 / 15) = ln(2) ≈ 0.6931}} — the same log return as position
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, since both moves double the value, whereas {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}}}}}}} would
report the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} fractional return for both but a different one for the
halving case.

\subparagraph{Output}

0  NULL
1  \PYGZhy{}1.5
2  \PYGZhy{}5

ptype: Series
0  NULL
1  NULL
2  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}} only requires the base to be nonzero — position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5}} vs. base
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}) is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5/10 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = \sphinxhyphen{}1.5}}, and position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}} vs. base \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5}}) is

requires \sphinxstylestrong{both} sides to be strictly positive; since every comparison here
involves the negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}5}}, all three positions come back \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}.

subsp::stats::ts::log\PYGZus{}returns: periods cannot be zero

\sphinxAtStartPar
Comparing each position against itself isn’t a meaningful log return, so

output.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log\_returns()}} requires \sphinxstylestrong{both} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} to be strictly greater than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}; a zero or negative value in either
produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} rather than an error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Log returns are additive across periods (the sum of consecutive one\sphinxhyphen{}period log
returns equals the multi\sphinxhyphen{}period log return), which plain fractional
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returns()}}}}}}} are not — a common reason to prefer this method for
compounding analysis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A pre\sphinxhyphen{}existing missing entry in the source thread is honored — it produces
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every log return that would otherwise reference it. See Example 3.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} must not be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or it throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"subsp::stats::ts::log\_returns: periods cannot be zero"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} thread
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeSeriesAccessor::log\_returns: source must be Series"}}; a
non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeSeriesAccessor::log\_returns: source Series must be numeric"}}.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/log_returns:see-also}}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{TimeSeriesAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{returns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{periods}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the fractional period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period change of the bound thread:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out{[}i{]} = x{[}i{]} / base{[}i{]} \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} (a lag when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textgreater{} 0}}, a lead when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods \textless{} 0}}). A position is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} wherever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is missing, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base{[}i{]}}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or either value is non\sphinxhyphen{}finite. Restricted
to a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} thread; anything else throws.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{periods} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}})
The shift distance used to build the comparison base. Positive shifts compare
each position against an earlier one (a lag); negative shifts compare against
a later one (a lead). Must not be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or the call throws.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}
A new thread, same length as the bound source, holding the period\sphinxhyphen{}over\sphinxhyphen{}period
fractional return.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Compute the one\sphinxhyphen{}period return of a numeric thread.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{15.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{returns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  NULL
1  1
2  \PYGZhy{}0.25
3  1

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} has no prior position to compare against, so it’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}. Position
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20 / 10 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = 1}} (a 100\% increase); position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15 / 20 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = \sphinxhyphen{}0.25}}
(a 25\% decrease); position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30 / 15 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = 1}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Pass a negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}}, comparing each position against a \sphinxstyleemphasis{later}
one (a lead) instead of an earlier one.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}lead}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{load}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{returns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}lead}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
0  \PYGZhy{}0.5
1  0.3333333333
2  \PYGZhy{}0.5
3  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = \sphinxhyphen{}1}}, each position’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{next} position instead of
the previous one: position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10 / 20 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = \sphinxhyphen{}0.5}}; position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20 / 15 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = 0.3333}}; position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{15 / 30 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = \sphinxhyphen{}0.5}}. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} has no

Example 1’s default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods = 1}}), where it was position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} that had no prior
position.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{delta}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{returns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out2}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:id2}}

0  NULL
1  \PYGZhy{}1
2  NULL

ptype: Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x = 0}}, base \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{= 10}}) is an ordinary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0 / 10 \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = \sphinxhyphen{}1}}. Position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x = 20}}, base \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{= 0}}) has a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} of exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} — rather than dividing by zero,

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. A pre\sphinxhyphen{}existing missing entry in the source thread propagates into

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/thread-ts/returns:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{base}} value of exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} always produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x{[}i{]}}},
since the fractional change would otherwise be undefined or infinite.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A pre\sphinxhyphen{}existing missing entry in the source thread is honored — it produces
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} in every return that would otherwise reference it. See Example 4.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} must not be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, or it throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"subsp::stats::ts::returns: periods cannot be zero"}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restricted to numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payloads; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} thread
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeSeriesAccessor::returns: source must be Series"}}; a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"TimeSeriesAccessor::returns: source Series must be numeric"}}.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{catalog_api_reference:id307}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combines two catalogs by matching rows on a key stream.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{catalog_api_reference:id308}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

Second frame, thread, or scalar operand supplied for binary combination, comparison, alignment, or join\sphinxhyphen{}style work.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Supported values:
\PYGZhy{} `common`: Keep only rows whose key values match on both sides.
\PYGZhy{} `keep\PYGZus{}left`: Preserve left keys and attach right\PYGZhy{}hand matches where they exist.
\PYGZhy{} `keep\PYGZus{}right`: Preserve right keys and attach left\PYGZhy{}hand matches where they exist.
\PYGZhy{} `unite`: Keep the stable union of keys from both frames.
\PYGZhy{} `cross`: Create the cartesian product; key feature arguments must be empty.
\PYGZhy{} `left\PYGZus{}only`: Keep left rows whose keys do not occur on the right.
\PYGZhy{} `right\PYGZus{}only`: Keep right rows whose keys do not occur on the left.

\subparagraph{Practical Behavior}
\label{\detokenize{registry_api_reference:practical-behavior}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply(...)}} rewrites one slot or a selected slot set; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_all(...)}} rewrites every slot.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The transform must return a defined slot.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the underscore form when you want the mutation in place.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:aisle-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the full public \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}} surface for depth\sphinxhyphen{}stacked registries.


\paragraph{How To Use This Page}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:how-to-use-this-page}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Methods are grouped alphabetically so you can jump quickly from the left rail.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each method page section starts with the public signatures, then explains what the method does, how each parameter changes behavior, and what the call returns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overloaded methods include several examples so you can see the supported call shapes instead of reverse\sphinxhyphen{}engineering them from signatures alone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each example is followed immediately by verified output captured from the current compiled examples so the result shape is visible before you move to the next overload.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{A}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:a}}

\subparagraph{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{apply\_slot}}}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:apply-slot}}

\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:signature}}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Applies a slot transform to one named key inside every registry and returns the updated aisle.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{key}
Name of the target slot or stream.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{fn}
Callback function used by this overload. The callable signature shown in the type tells you what input is provided and what you must return.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}}
Value produced by this call.

\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

depth1 \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Registry(ids \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Slot([Series(3), Series(4)]))
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Practical Behavior}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:practical-behavior}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{apply\_slot(key, fn)}} walks every registry in the aisle and rewrites that slot only where it exists.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Registries that do not have the requested key are left unchanged.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{Bridge Behavior}
\label{\detokenize{aisle_api_reference:bridge-behavior}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_kindle()}} converts the aisle into the Archive model.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this when the next workflow is archive/catalog based rather than bundle based.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{DataFramePlotAccessor API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_plot_api_reference:dataframeplotaccessor-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe_plot_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the public 2D plotting accessor returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::plot()}}.


\paragraph{Using This Reference}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_plot_api_reference:using-this-reference}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the left sidebar to open one method page at a time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each method page contains its own signatures, parameter details, notes, and working previous/next navigation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This landing page stays intentionally short so the content panel is not one giant scroll of every method.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every method returns a Studio, not a DataFrame
None of these methods print a table or draw anything to the console. Each one builds and
returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} figure object from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}} plotting library — nothing is
rendered until you call one of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}’s own methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_svg(path)}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_png(path)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_pdf(path)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_svg()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pdf()}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} has no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}}, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} figure}} does not compile — see each page’s examples for the
actual pattern.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subparagraph{DataFramePlotAccessor::act}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act:dataframeplotaccessor-act}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_plot_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFramePlotAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{act}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ActPlotOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pl}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Studio}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws an autocorrelation plot for one numeric feature: for each lag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} up to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag}}, computes the Pearson correlation between the series and itself shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}}
positions, and draws one vertical spike per lag at that correlation value. This is a
standard diagnostic for spotting periodicity or serial dependence in a sequence — a spike
that stays well outside the confidence band at a given lag suggests the series at that lag
is not just noise.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}} is one of three closely related single\sphinxhyphen{}feature diagnostic plots on this accessor,
alongside {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag()}}}}}}} (a single lag’s scatter, rather than every lag’s correlation)
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bootstrap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bootstrap()}}}}}}} (a resampling\sphinxhyphen{}based diagnostic, unrelated to lags). All
three share the same feature\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rule: the named feature must resolve to exactly one
numeric (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind) feature, validated via the accessor’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{numeric\_feature\_names(frame\_, \{feature\}, where)}} call — passing a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric feature name
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textless{}where\textgreater{}: feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{} is not a numeric Series"}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
include\_zero\_lag is always false here — lag 0 (always 1.0) is never shown
Internally, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}} delegates to the same autocorrelation machinery used elsewhere in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flash}} layer, but always with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_zero\_lag = false}}. The lag\sphinxhyphen{}0
autocorrelation of any series with itself is trivially \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} and isn’t informative, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}’s spikes always start at lag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, never lag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least three data points are required
The underlying autocorrelation computation needs at least three points to be meaningful; a
feature with fewer than three rows throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"flash::acfplot requires at least three points"}}
even though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ActPlotOptions}} itself has no explicit minimum\sphinxhyphen{}row\sphinxhyphen{}count field.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The single numeric feature to autocorrelate against its own lagged copies. Must resolve
to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature — see the shared\sphinxhyphen{}diagnostics note above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ActPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct ActPlotOptions \{       std::int64\_t max\_lag\{40\};       bool show\_confidence\_band\{true\};       double confidence\_level\{0.95\};       float trace\_width\{1.2F\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag}} is clamped internally to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1, n \sphinxhyphen{} 1{]}}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is the feature’s row count, so
requesting a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag}} larger than the data supports doesn’t throw — it’s silently
capped. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_confidence\_band}} draws two horizontal reference lines at
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\(\pm\)z / sqrt(n)}}, where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}} is the z\sphinxhyphen{}score for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{confidence\_level}} (using the same lookup
table as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci\_enabled}} whiskers: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.99 \(\rightarrow\) 2.575829}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.98 \(\rightarrow\)     2.326348}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.95 \(\rightarrow\) 1.959964}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.90 \(\rightarrow\) 1.644854}}, anything else \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\(\rightarrow\) 1.281552}}). A spike
that crosses outside this band at a given lag is a rough visual cue that the
autocorrelation at that lag is unlikely to be pure noise. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trace\_width}} controls the
stroke width of each spike.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one autocorrelation spike per lag (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1..max\_lag}}), a
zero reference line, and (when enabled) two confidence\sphinxhyphen{}band reference lines.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default options: a periodic\sphinxhyphen{}looking sequence, autocorrelated out to lag 40 (or
fewer, if the data is shorter).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{wave}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{60}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{wave}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{push\PYGZus{}back}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{static\PYGZus{}cast}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{series}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signal}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{wave}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{series}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signal}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signal\PYGZus{}act.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wave}} has 60 rows, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag = 40}} (the default) fits within the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1, 59{]}}} clamp range
unchanged; expect strong spikes near lags that are multiples of the wave’s period.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. A shorter feature: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag}} is silently clamped rather than throwing.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{reading}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{7.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.5}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{small}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{reading}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reading}} has 7 rows, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag}} is clamped to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1}}) even though the requested
default is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{40}}; spikes are drawn only for lags \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1..6}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. An explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ActPlotOptions}}, narrowing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag}}, using a stricter
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{confidence\_level}}, and thickening the spikes.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{ActPlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}lag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{12}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{confidence\PYGZus{}level}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.99}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{trace\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0F}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{series}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signal}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}png}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signal\PYGZus{}act.png}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The confidence band widens (using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z = 2.575829}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.99}} instead of the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.95}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.959964}}), making it harder for a spike to appear “significant.”

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. Disabling the confidence band entirely.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{series}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{act}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{signal}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{bare\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the raw spikes and the zero reference line are drawn — no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\(\pm\)CI}} lines.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 5. A non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric feature throws.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} must resolve to exactly one numeric feature — see the shared\sphinxhyphen{}diagnostics note
above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} is never shown; spikes start at lag \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_lag}} is clamped to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1, n \sphinxhyphen{} 1{]}}}, never throwing for an over\sphinxhyphen{}large request.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature with fewer than three rows throws before any spike is drawn.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves:dataframeplotaccessor-andrews-curves}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_plot_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFramePlotAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws Andrews curves: each row’s values across the selected numeric features are combined
into a single periodic function (a truncated Fourier\sphinxhyphen{}series\sphinxhyphen{}style combination), and each
row’s curve is plotted over a shared domain. Rows with similar values across the selected
features tend to produce visually similar curves, making this another way (alongside
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radviz()}}}}}}}) to eyeball multivariate structure
across more than two features at once.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its feature\sphinxhyphen{}selection rule (empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} infers every numeric feature),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class\_feature}} behavior (accepts any feature kind, cast to text), and NaN\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}drop handling
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}} — see that page for the full explanation; this page only
covers what’s specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{andrews\_curves()}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Numeric features combined into each row’s curve. Empty infers every numeric feature —
see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact rule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{class\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Optional coloring/grouping feature, same behavior as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}}’s.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AndrewsCurvesPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct AndrewsCurvesPlotOptions \{       std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{} labels\{\};       bool normalize\{true\};       std::int64\_t points\{220\};       std::int64\_t max\_curves\{600\};       double alpha\{0.28\};       float trace\_width\{0.9F\};       bool show\_grid\{true\};       bool show\_legend\{true\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{points}} is how many points each row’s curve is evaluated at over its domain (finer
than a straight\sphinxhyphen{}line plot, since the curve is smooth). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_curves}} caps how many rows’
curves are drawn — analogous to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}}. The rest
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trace\_width}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_grid}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_legend}}) mirror
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParallelPlotOptions}}}}}}}’s fields of the same name.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one curve per row (or capped at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_curves}}), colored
by class when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class\_feature}} is given.

\item {}

view or save the result.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same shape as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} — one trace per y\sphinxhyphen{}feature over a shared x\sphinxhyphen{}axis, same
three overload families, same x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rules — but each trace is filled down to
the baseline instead of drawn as a bare line, and multiple y\sphinxhyphen{}features are drawn as
\sphinxstylestrong{independently overlapping} filled regions on the same axes (not stacked; for a stacked
composition view, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}}}}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the full explanation of the shared mechanics — this page only
covers what’s specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area()}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} / \sphinxstylestrong{y\_features}
Same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}: one or more numeric features, each drawn as its own filled
area trace, overlapping rather than stacked. At least one is required — an empty list
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().area: at least one y feature is required"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Same three\sphinxhyphen{}step resolution as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AreaPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct AreaPlotOptions \{       double alpha\{0.88\};       double line\_width\{1.3\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} defaults noticeably lower than {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} — filled regions
default to slightly translucent so overlapping areas from multiple y\sphinxhyphen{}features stay
visually distinguishable instead of one fully opaque area hiding another.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one filled area trace per requested y\sphinxhyphen{}feature.

\item {}

for the composition (accumulating) variant.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature is required.

\item {}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws several numeric y\sphinxhyphen{}features as a \sphinxstylestrong{stacked} area chart: each feature’s values
accumulate on top of the running total of the features drawn before it, so the topmost
edge of the last trace represents the sum of every requested feature at that x position.
This is the composition view — “how much does each part contribute to the whole, at each
point” — as opposed to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area()}}}}}}}, which draws independently overlapping
(non\sphinxhyphen{}accumulating) filled regions. Unlike every other line/area method on this accessor,
there is \sphinxstylestrong{no single\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}} only accepts a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initializer\_list}} of y\sphinxhyphen{}features, since stacking a single feature on its own is a
degenerate case.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the shared x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rules (explicit argument, then
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_x\_feature}}, then the frame’s row labels titled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}}) and the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} mechanics common to this whole accessor.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each layer’s fill actually reaches down to zero, not to the layer below it
Internally, each successive layer’s cumulative top is computed correctly (feature 2’s
“top” is feature 1’s top plus feature 2’s own height, and so on) — the stacking math itself
is exact. But each layer is filled from its own cumulative top down to a flat baseline of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, not down to the previous layer’s top. The correct stacked \sphinxstyleemphasis{shape} still comes through,
because each later (taller) layer is drawn on top of the earlier ones in the same pane and
visually covers the redundant region beneath it — but with the default semi\sphinxhyphen{}transparent
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.7}}), the color in an area where multiple layers overlap is a blend of every
layer drawn there, not a single flat color unique to one band. If a fully solid per\sphinxhyphen{}band
look matters, raise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} toward \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AreaStackedPlotOptions}} so each later layer’s
fill more fully occludes the ones beneath it.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})
Numeric features to stack, in the order they’re accumulated — the first feature forms
the bottom band, the last feature’s cumulative top is the total across all of them. At
least one is required — an empty list throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().area\_stacked: at least     one y feature is required"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Same three\sphinxhyphen{}step resolution as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AreaStackedPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct AreaStackedPlotOptions \{       double alpha\{0.7\};       double line\_width\{1.2\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} defaults lower than both {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}}) and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area()}}}}}}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.88}}) — see the note above for why: with several stacked, overlapping fills, a lower
default opacity keeps the underlying grid and boundary lines visible through the stack.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one filled area trace per requested y\sphinxhyphen{}feature, each
one’s top edge representing the running cumulative total up to and including that
feature.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No single\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload exists — only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initializer\_list}} forms.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature is required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each layer’s fill reaches down to a flat \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} baseline, not the previous layer’s top — see
the note above for the practical implication on overlapping\sphinxhyphen{}fill color.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/auto_plot:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Picks a chart type automatically for the requested (or inferred) numeric features and
delegates to the corresponding method on this same accessor — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{auto\_plot()}} never draws
anything itself; every branch ends by calling straight into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar\_stacked()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter\_matrix()}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_heatmap()}}. The routing is a
fully deterministic decision tree based on how many numeric features resolve, whether the
frame’s row labels are categorical/temporal, how many rows the frame has, whether a
hue\sphinxhyphen{}capable feature exists, and whether every selected column is non\sphinxhyphen{}negative. It exists for
quick, exploratory looks at a frame without having to pick a chart type by hand — for
anything beyond “show me something reasonable,” reach for the specific method directly
instead.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AutoPlotOptions}} is currently an empty struct (reserved for
future use) — it has no effect on routing or rendering today; both overloads behave
identically.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature resolution follows the same rule as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}: empty (default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}
infers every numeric feature in the frame, and an explicitly\sphinxhyphen{}passed non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric name throws
— see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact rule and throw text.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The decision tree, in order
Given the resolved feature names (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}}) and whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} was passed non\sphinxhyphen{}empty
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{explicit\_features}}), the first matching rule below wins:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exactly one numeric feature.} If the frame’s row\sphinxhyphen{}label thread is Note\sphinxhyphen{}, Timeline\sphinxhyphen{}, or
TimeIndex\sphinxhyphen{}kind (“labeled”) \sphinxstylestrong{and} the frame has 16 or fewer rows, routes to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar(names.front())}}. Otherwise routes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line(names.front())}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exactly two numeric features, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} was left empty/default.} If the frame
has \sphinxstyleemphasis{any} Note/Timeline/TimeIndex\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature (checked across the whole frame, not just
the two selected numeric ones), routes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter(names{[}0{]}, names{[}1{]}, hue)}} using the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{first} such feature (in the frame’s own column order) as the hue. This rule is skipped
entirely — even with the same two resolved features — when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} was passed
explicitly rather than left empty.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Two or three numeric features, labeled row axis, and every selected column
non\sphinxhyphen{}negative} (non\sphinxhyphen{}finite cells treated as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for this check only). If the frame has 12
or fewer rows, routes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar\_stacked()}} over the selected features; otherwise routes to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Two, three, or four numeric features, and the frame “prefers an index plot”} — true
when the row\sphinxhyphen{}label thread is labeled\sphinxhyphen{}kind, \sphinxstyleemphasis{or} the frame has more than 24 rows (either
condition alone is enough). Routes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}} with all selected features as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_features}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Five or fewer numeric features, and 256 or fewer rows.} Routes to a scatter\sphinxhyphen{}matrix
view equivalent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter\_matrix(names)}} with default options (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Full}} triangle).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Everything else} (more than five features, or too many rows for step 5 to apply).
Routes to a correlation\sphinxhyphen{}heatmap view equivalent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_heatmap(names)}} with default
options.

\end{enumerate}
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/auto_plot:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Numeric features to consider. Empty (the default) infers every numeric feature in the
frame — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact rule. Whether this
argument was left empty or passed explicitly also affects routing directly (rule 2
above only fires for the default/empty case).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AutoPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct AutoPlotOptions \{\};     }}
Currently empty; reserved for future routing controls.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/auto_plot:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
Whatever the routed\sphinxhyphen{}to method returns — the figure shape (pane count, trace kind, axis
labels) depends entirely on which rule fired.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/auto_plot:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. One numeric feature, labeled (Note\sphinxhyphen{}kind) row axis, few rows: routes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar()}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Jan}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Feb}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Mar}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Apr}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{monthly}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{auto\PYGZus{}plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{monthly\PYGZus{}auto.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{monthly.plot().bar("revenue")}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. One numeric feature, default (numeric) row axis: routes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{trend}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{temperature}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{18.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{19.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{21.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{20.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{22.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\sphinxAtStartPar
No row labels were provided, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trend}}’s row axis defaults to a plain numeric case index

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Two numeric features (default/empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}), with a hue\sphinxhyphen{}capable feature
elsewhere in the frame: routes to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}} with that feature as hue.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/auto_plot:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every branch delegates to another method on this same accessor — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{auto\_plot()}} performs
no rendering of its own.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rule 2 (hue scatter) only fires when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} is left at its empty default; an explicit
two\sphinxhyphen{}feature request skips straight past it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AutoPlotOptions}} is currently empty and has no effect.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empty (default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} infers every numeric feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s
important callout for the exact rule.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws one bar per row for a single y\sphinxhyphen{}feature, or \sphinxstylestrong{grouped} (side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side) bars per row
when several y\sphinxhyphen{}features are requested — each feature gets its own narrower bar sharing the
row’s axis position, rather than stacking (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar_stacked::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar\_stacked()}}}}}}} for the
accumulating variant). Same three overload families and x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rules as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the shared x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rules and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}}
mechanics.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} / \sphinxstylestrong{y\_features}
One or more numeric features. A single feature draws one bar series; several draw
grouped bars sharing each axis position. At least one is required — an empty list
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().bar: at least one y feature is required"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Same three\sphinxhyphen{}step resolution as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} — falls back to the frame’s row
labels (titled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}}) if omitted with no default set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BarPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct BarPlotOptions \{       bool ci\_enabled\{false\};       double ci\_level\{0.95\};       bool horizontal\{false\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{horizontal = true}} swaps the chart’s orientation: bars extend along the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis instead
of the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis, and the category axis becomes the vertical one.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
`ci\PYGZus{}enabled = true` switches from \PYGZdq{}one bar per row\PYGZdq{} to **aggregated** bars: rows sharing
the same x\PYGZhy{}axis position (same category label, or same numeric x\PYGZhy{}value) are grouped,
each bar\PYGZsq{}s height becomes the **mean** of that group, and a whisker/error\PYGZhy{}bar trace is
overlaid showing a normal\PYGZhy{}approximation confidence interval at `ci\PYGZus{}level` (default
`0.95`, i.e. roughly \(\pm\)1.96 standard errors). A group with only one row still draws a bar
(at that row\PYGZsq{}s own value, as its \PYGZdq{}mean\PYGZdq{}) but its whisker has zero width — there\PYGZsq{}s no
variance to estimate from a single sample.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one bar trace per y\sphinxhyphen{}feature (grouped side\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}side if
more than one), plus a whisker trace per y\sphinxhyphen{}feature when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci\_enabled = true}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
One y\sphinxhyphen{}feature draws a plain bar series; several draw grouped (not stacked) bars — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar_stacked::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar\_stacked()}}}}}}} for stacking.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{horizontal = true}} swaps which axis the bars extend along.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci\_enabled = true}} switches to aggregated mean\sphinxhyphen{}plus\sphinxhyphen{}confidence\sphinxhyphen{}interval bars, grouping
rows that share an x\sphinxhyphen{}axis position; a lone row in a group still bars at its own value with
a zero\sphinxhyphen{}width whisker.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar_stacked:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bar\sphinxhyphen{}chart counterpart to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}}}}}}}: each y\sphinxhyphen{}feature’s values
accumulate on top of the running total of the features stacked before it, so the topmost
bar segment’s height represents the sum of every requested feature at that x position. Like
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}}, there is \sphinxstylestrong{no single\sphinxhyphen{}feature overload} — only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initializer\_list}} forms — since stacking one feature alone is degenerate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the shared x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rules and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}}
mechanics.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same overlapping\sphinxhyphen{}fill mechanism as area\_stacked()
Exactly like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}}}}}}}, each layer is drawn as a full bar from a
baseline of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} up to its own cumulative top, not from the previous layer’s top — the
correct stacked shape comes from later (taller) bars being drawn on top of earlier ones in
the same pane. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BarStackedPlotOptions}}’s default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.65}}) is semi\sphinxhyphen{}transparent, so
overlapping regions blend colors from every layer drawn there rather than showing one flat
color per band — raise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} toward \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} for a fully solid, unambiguous per\sphinxhyphen{}band look.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar_stacked:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})
Numeric features to stack, in accumulation order — the first forms the bottom segment,
the last feature’s cumulative top is the grand total. At least one is required — an
empty list throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().bar\_stacked: at least one y feature is required"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Same three\sphinxhyphen{}step resolution as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BarStackedPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct BarStackedPlotOptions \{       double alpha\{0.65\};       double line\_width\{1.0\};     \};     }}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar_stacked:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one bar trace per requested y\sphinxhyphen{}feature, each stacked
on the cumulative total of the ones before it.

\item {}

as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area_stacked::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area\_stacked()}}}}}}} — see the note above.

view or save the result.

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bootstrap:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a bootstrap sampling\sphinxhyphen{}distribution plot for one numeric feature: repeatedly resamples
the feature’s values with replacement, computes a chosen summary statistic (mean, median, or
standard deviation) on each resample, and histograms the resulting distribution of that
statistic. A vertical reference line marks the statistic computed on the original,
un\sphinxhyphen{}resampled data. This is a way to visualize how much a summary statistic would plausibly
vary if the data collection were repeated, without assuming any particular parametric
distribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature resolution rule with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/lag::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag()}}}}}}}: the
named feature must resolve to exactly one numeric (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind) feature — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}}’s callout for the exact throw text.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least two data points are required
A feature with fewer than two rows throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"flash::bootstrapplot requires at least two points"}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bootstrap:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The single numeric feature to bootstrap. Must resolve to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}}’s shared\sphinxhyphen{}diagnostics note.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BootstrapPlotOptions}})
\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}cpp
enum class BootstrapStatistic : std::uint8\_t \{
Mean,
Median,
Std,
\};

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
struct BootstrapPlotOptions \PYGZob{}
  std::int64\PYGZus{}t samples\PYGZob{}300\PYGZcb{};
  std::int64\PYGZus{}t sample\PYGZus{}size\PYGZob{}0\PYGZcb{};
  std::uint64\PYGZus{}t seed\PYGZob{}7\PYGZcb{};
  int bins\PYGZob{}24\PYGZcb{};
  BootstrapStatistic statistic\PYGZob{}BootstrapStatistic::Mean\PYGZcb{};
  float trace\PYGZus{}width\PYGZob{}0.85F\PYGZcb{};
\PYGZcb{};
```
`samples` is how many resamples are drawn; clamped to a minimum of `8` internally.
`sample\PYGZus{}size` is how many rows (with replacement) each resample draws — `0` (the
default) means \PYGZdq{}same size as the original feature,\PYGZdq{} the conventional bootstrap setting;
a positive value overrides this. `seed` seeds the random draws deterministically — each
of the `samples` resamples uses `seed + i + 1` internally (`i` from `0` to
`samples \PYGZhy{} 1`), so the same `seed` reproduces the same sampling distribution across
runs. `statistic` chooses what\PYGZsq{}s computed per resample: `Mean` (arithmetic mean),
`Median` (via a full sort and exact quantile at `0.5`), or `Std` (population standard
deviation, i.e. divided by `n` rather than `n \PYGZhy{} 1`). `bins` controls the histogram
resolution of the resulting distribution (floored to a minimum of `4`). `trace\PYGZus{}width`
controls the histogram bars\PYGZsq{} outline width.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bootstrap:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing a histogram of the resampled statistic and a vertical
reference line at the statistic computed on the full, original data.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bootstrap:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default options: bootstrap the mean, 300 resamples, same\sphinxhyphen{}size draws.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scores}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{bootstrap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{score}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{score\PYGZus{}bootstrap.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. Bootstrapping the median instead of the mean.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Bootstrapping the standard deviation, with more resamples and a fixed seed for
reproducibility.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bootstrap:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} must resolve to exactly one numeric feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}}’s shared
note.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{samples}} is floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{8}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}} is floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_size = 0}} (the default) means each resample matches the original row count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} makes the resampling fully deterministic and reproducible across runs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}} uses the population (÷ n) formula, not the sample (÷ n − 1) formula.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a box\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}whisker distribution summary for each requested numeric feature, one box
per feature, sharing a single pane with the feature names as x\sphinxhyphen{}axis tick labels — not one
pane per feature. This is a pure distribution\sphinxhyphen{}summary method: there’s no x/y\sphinxhyphen{}feature
concept here at all, just a set of numeric features to summarize.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty features list means “every numeric feature in the frame”
Every distribution/multivariate method on this accessor that takes a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} parameter
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/violin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{violin}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/density::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{density}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_heatmap}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{andrews\_curves}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radviz}}}}}}}) shares this rule: passing an
explicit, non\sphinxhyphen{}empty list validates each named feature is a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (throwing
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textless{}method\textgreater{}: feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{} is not a numeric Series"}} if not); passing the default empty
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}} instead auto\sphinxhyphen{}selects \sphinxstylestrong{every} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature in the frame, throwing
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\textless{}method\textgreater{}: no numeric Series features available"}} if the frame has none. See Example 1 for
the empty\sphinxhyphen{}list, “infer everything” form.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}finite values are silently dropped per feature, not shown as gaps
Each feature’s values are filtered to only the finite (non\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, non\sphinxhyphen{}infinite) ones before
the box statistics are computed — an invalid or missing cell simply doesn’t contribute a
data point to its feature’s box, rather than appearing as a visible gap or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} marker.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}},
default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Numeric features to summarize, each as its own box. Leave empty (the default) to use
every numeric feature in the frame. At least one feature (explicit or inferred) is
required — an entirely non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric frame throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().box: at least one     numeric feature is required"}} after the empty list resolves to nothing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BoxPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct BoxPlotOptions \{       double alpha\{0.95\};       double line\_width\{1.1\};     \};     }}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one box per requested (or inferred) feature, x\sphinxhyphen{}axis
ticks labeled with each feature’s name.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty (default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} list infers every numeric feature in the frame — see the
important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}finite values are dropped per feature before the box statistics are computed, rather
than appearing as gaps.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every feature shares one pane, positioned side by side by feature name — not a mosaic of
separate panes (contrast {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}}}}}}’s multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature mosaic layout).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}
