\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/brief:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Renders a fixed\sphinxhyphen{}width, monospace\sphinxhyphen{}formatted text table of the requested numeric features’
raw values directly as a pane in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} — a “table as a figure” rather than any kind of
chart. Unlike every other method on this accessor, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{brief()}} doesn’t plot points, lines,
bars, or bins; it formats each selected feature’s values into aligned columns (with an
optional header, row/case index, and truncation past a configurable case limit) and draws
that text as the pane’s caption, with the grid, legend, axes, and tick labels all switched
off. This makes it useful for embedding a compact numeric summary alongside real charts —
for example, appended into the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} returned by another plot call.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two distinct overloads: fresh Studio vs. in\sphinxhyphen{}place composition
The first overload creates a brand\sphinxhyphen{}new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} and returns it, the same as every other
method on this accessor. The second overload instead takes an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio\&}} \sphinxstylestrong{by
reference}, adds the table pane into it, and returns that same reference — genuinely
appending to a figure you already have, rather than starting a new one. This is the only
method on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor}} that supports this in\sphinxhyphen{}place composition pattern; every
other method always constructs and returns a fresh \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares the “empty features means every numeric feature” rule with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}} — see
that page’s important callout for the exact rule and throw text.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/brief:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{figure} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio\&}}, in\sphinxhyphen{}place overload only)
An existing figure to append the table pane into. Must already exist (default\sphinxhyphen{}constructed
or returned from an earlier plot call); this overload never creates a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Numeric features to summarize. Empty (the default) infers every numeric feature in the
frame — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact rule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BriefPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct BriefPlotOptions \{       std::string title\{"table"\};       int precision\{4\};       bool include\_header\{true\};       std::int64\_t max\_cases\{10\};       bool transpose\{false\};       bool include\_case\_index\{true\};       std::int64\_t features\_per\_table\{0\};       std::int64\_t tables\_per\_row\{1\};       std::int64\_t table\_gap\_spaces\{4\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{title}} becomes the pane’s own title text. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{precision}} (floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}) sets fixed\sphinxhyphen{}point
decimal places for every cell; a non\sphinxhyphen{}finite value always renders as the literal text
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"nan"}} regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{precision}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_header}} toggles the column\sphinxhyphen{}name header row.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_cases}} (falling back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{≤ 0}}) caps how many rows are printed before a
trailing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"... (N more cases)"}} line is appended; it does not affect which features are
summarized, only how many rows. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transpose = true}} swaps the orientation: features become
rows and cases become columns (labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case\_0"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case\_1"}}, …) instead of the
default features\sphinxhyphen{}as\sphinxhyphen{}columns, cases\sphinxhyphen{}as\sphinxhyphen{}rows layout. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include\_case\_index}} toggles a leading
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}} index column in the non\sphinxhyphen{}transposed layout (ignored when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transpose = true}}, which
always uses its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"feature"}} label column instead). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features\_per\_table}} (falling back
to “every feature in one table” if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{≤ 0}}) splits the feature set into multiple smaller
tables of that width; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tables\_per\_row}} (floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}) then lays those sub\sphinxhyphen{}tables out
side by side, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_gap\_spaces}} (floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}) spaces between them.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/brief:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For the first overload: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}, a fresh figure with one pane containing the
formatted table as its caption text (grid, legend, axis labels, and tick labels all
suppressed).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the second overload: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio\&}}, the same reference passed in, with the table
pane appended.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/brief:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default options: every numeric feature, up to 10 cases, in a fresh \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/brief:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrame::plot().brief: feature \PYGZsq{}region\PYGZsq{} is not a numeric Series
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/brief:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empty (default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} infers every numeric feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s
important callout for the exact rule.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two\sphinxhyphen{}argument\sphinxhyphen{}plus\sphinxhyphen{}figure overload composes in place into an existing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio\&}}; every
other method on this accessor (including \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{brief()}}’s own other overload) always creates a
fresh one — see the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_cases}} truncates displayed rows, not the underlying feature selection.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}finite cell values always render as the literal text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"nan"}}, independent of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{precision}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The rendered pane has no grid, legend, or axis labels — it exists purely to display text.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio\&}} for the in\sphinxhyphen{}place overload) — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to view or save the result.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/brief:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::box}}}}}}}: the canonical explanation of the
“empty features means every numeric feature” rule shared here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/auto_plot::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::auto\_plot}}}}}}}: picks a real chart type automatically,
in contrast to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{brief()}}’s fixed textual summary.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the frame’s correlation matrix (via the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::corr()}} used elsewhere —
specifically \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.corr(false)}}, its default\sphinxhyphen{}method, non\sphinxhyphen{}render form) restricted to the
requested features, and renders it as a square heatmap: both rows and columns are the
selected feature names, and each cell \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i, j)}} is the correlation between feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} and
feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{j}}. Follows the same numeric\sphinxhyphen{}feature rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}} — an empty
(default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} list infers every numeric feature in the frame.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Numeric features to correlate. Empty (the default) infers every numeric feature in the
frame — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact rule and throw text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CorrHeatmapPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct CorrHeatmapPlotOptions \{       bool annotate\_levels\{true\};       bool scale\_guide\{true\};       bool borderless\{false\};     \};     }}
Same fields as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heatmap()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HeatmapPlotOptions}}, but note the different
default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{annotate\_levels}} defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} here (each cell’s correlation coefficient
is printed by default), where plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heatmap()}} defaults it to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{borderless =     true}} here also suppresses the default 30° y\sphinxhyphen{}tick rotation, same as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heatmap()}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing a square heatmap trace, feature names as both x and y
tick labels.

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cost}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{60.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{80.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{55.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{95.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{85.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empty (default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} infers every numeric feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s
important callout for the exact rule.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reuses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::corr()}} internally (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame.corr(false)}}) rather than recomputing
correlations from scratch.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{annotate\_levels}} defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} here, unlike plain {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heatmap()}}}}}}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} default.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/density:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a kernel\sphinxhyphen{}density estimate (a smoothed distribution curve) for one or more numeric
features. Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{density()}} \sphinxstylestrong{always} overlays every requested
feature’s curve on a single shared pane, regardless of how many features are requested —
there is no mosaic\sphinxhyphen{}grid mode here. A legend is shown automatically whenever more than one
feature is requested.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Follows the same numeric\sphinxhyphen{}feature validation as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}} for its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}
parameter, though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{density()}} has no empty\sphinxhyphen{}list “infer everything” shorthand of its own —
every overload requires at least one named feature.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/density:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
A single numeric feature to draw as one density curve.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})
Several numeric features, each drawn as its own curve on the shared pane.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{points} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{128}})
The number of evaluation points used to draw each curve. Internally clamped to a
minimum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{16}} regardless of what’s passed — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{density(feature, 1)}} still draws a
16\sphinxhyphen{}point curve, not a degenerate one\sphinxhyphen{}point line.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DensityPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct DensityPlotOptions \{       std::int64\_t points\{128\};       double alpha\{1.0\};       double line\_width\{1.5\};     \};     }}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/density:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one kernel\sphinxhyphen{}density curve per requested feature,
x\sphinxhyphen{}axis labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}}, y\sphinxhyphen{}axis labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"density"}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/density:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always overlays every requested feature on one shared pane — never a mosaic, unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{points}} is clamped to a minimum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{16}} regardless of what’s requested.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No empty\sphinxhyphen{}list “infer everything” shorthand — at least one feature must be named
explicitly on every overload.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two genuinely different modes, chosen by which overload is called:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Direct (wide) mode} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heatmap(features{[}, options{]})}}: each requested numeric feature
becomes one \sphinxstylestrong{row} of the heatmap matrix; the frame’s own row labels become the
\sphinxstylestrong{columns}. This renders the raw values of a “wide” table directly as a matrix — no
aggregation happens.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Grouped (long/pivot) mode} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heatmap(case\_feature, feature\_feature, value\_feature, op{[}, options{]})}}: internally calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::pivot\_table(case\_feature, feature\_feature, value\_feature, op, /*dropnull\_keys=*/true, /*render=*/false)}} first, turning “long”
rows (one row per case/feature/value triple) into a two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional grid — rows are
distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}} values, columns are distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}} values, and each
cell is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} aggregated across the matching rows using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} (default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp::Mean}}; also accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Median}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mode}}). This is the method to reach for when the data isn’t already
laid out as a matrix and needs pivoting first.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Direct mode preserves NaN in the matrix; grouped mode fills it with zero
The two modes differ in how non\sphinxhyphen{}finite cells are handled once built into the underlying
matrix: direct mode passes the raw values through unmodified (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} stays \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, and how
that renders depends on the heatmap trace’s own handling of non\sphinxhyphen{}finite cells); grouped mode
explicitly replaces any non\sphinxhyphen{}finite aggregated cell (e.g. a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_feature}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature\_feature}}
combination with no matching rows at all) with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} before rendering.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, direct mode)
Numeric features to render as heatmap rows. At least one is required — an empty list
throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().heatmap: at least one feature is required"}} (this overload
does \sphinxstylestrong{not} have the “infer every numeric feature” shorthand that
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}}}}}}/etc. have).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{case\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, grouped mode)
Feature whose distinct values become the output heatmap’s rows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, grouped mode)
Feature whose distinct values become the output heatmap’s columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, grouped mode)
Feature aggregated into each cell.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{op} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}}, grouped mode, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})
The aggregation applied per cell: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Median}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mode}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HeatmapPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct HeatmapPlotOptions \{       bool annotate\_levels\{false\};       bool scale\_guide\{true\};       bool borderless\{false\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{annotate\_levels = true}} prints each cell’s numeric value directly on the heatmap.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scale\_guide}} controls whether a color\sphinxhyphen{}scale legend/guide is drawn alongside the
matrix. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{borderless = true}} removes cell borders and also suppresses the default 30°
y\sphinxhyphen{}axis tick label rotation that’s otherwise applied automatically.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing a single heatmap trace.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subparagraph{Output}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two distinct modes selected entirely by overload shape — direct (raw matrix) versus
grouped (pivot\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}aggregate).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Direct mode’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} has no empty\sphinxhyphen{}list shorthand — at least one must be named.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Direct mode preserves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}; grouped mode zero\sphinxhyphen{}fills non\sphinxhyphen{}finite aggregated cells.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{borderless = true}} also suppresses the default 30° y\sphinxhyphen{}tick rotation, not just cell
borders.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::corr\_heatmap}}}}}}}: a specialized heatmap of a
correlation matrix, reusing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::corr()}} internally.

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::bar}}}}}}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ci\_enabled = true}}: a one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional
aggregation view, contrasted with this method’s two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional grid.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bins one or more numeric features into frequency\sphinxhyphen{}count histograms. With \sphinxstylestrong{exactly one}
feature (named explicitly, or because the frame/selection resolves to just one numeric
feature), the result is a single pane with one histogram. With \sphinxstylestrong{more than one} feature,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}} doesn’t overlay them on one pane — it lays out a \sphinxstylestrong{mosaic grid} of separate panes,
roughly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ceil(sqrt(n))}} columns by however many rows that needs, one histogram per feature,
each with its own x/y labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_label}} = feature name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_label}} = \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"count"}}).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{danger}{Danger:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
bins == 20 is ambiguous between “explicit” and “still the default”
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resolve\_bins()}} treats a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}} value of exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}} (the literal default written into
every overload’s signature) as “the caller didn’t customize this,” and substitutes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options\_.default\_bins}} (from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotOptions}}, itself defaulting to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}) whenever
that default has been changed from its own default. Concretely: if you call
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.plot(options).hist("x")}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_bins = 30}}, you get 30 bins — as
expected. But \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.plot(options).hist("x", 20)}}, passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}} \sphinxstylestrong{explicitly} because you
genuinely want exactly 20 bins, \sphinxstyleemphasis{also} gets overridden to 30, because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resolve\_bins()}} has
no way to distinguish “the caller explicitly asked for 20” from “the caller left it at the
signature’s default of 20.” If you need to force exactly 20 bins on an accessor whose
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_bins}} has been customized to something else, pass any other value and adjust, or
avoid setting a custom \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_bins}} and pass the bin count explicitly on each call
instead. Any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}} value other than exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}= 0}}, which always falls back to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_bins}}) is used exactly as given.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bins} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::int64\_t}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}})
Requested bin count — subject to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resolve\_bins()}} ambiguity described above. Values
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}= 0}} always fall back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options\_.default\_bins}} (clamped to at least \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HistPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct HistPlotOptions \{       std::int64\_t bins\{20\};       double alpha\{0.95\};       double line\_width\{1.0\};     \};     }}
Same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}} ambiguity applies to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.bins}} as to the plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins}} argument.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
A single numeric feature to histogram, drawn on one pane.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})
Several numeric features. If this resolves to exactly one name (including via the
empty\sphinxhyphen{}list “infer everything” rule, on a frame with only one numeric feature), it’s
routed through the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature path automatically. Otherwise each feature gets its
own pane in a mosaic grid. Follows the same empty\sphinxhyphen{}list\sphinxhyphen{}means\sphinxhyphen{}“every numeric feature”
rule described on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s page.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A single\sphinxhyphen{}pane figure for one feature, or a mosaic\sphinxhyphen{}grid figure (one pane per feature)
for several.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
More than one feature produces a mosaic grid of separate panes, not one overlaid pane —
contrast {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/density::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{density()}}}}}}}, which always overlays multiple features on one pane.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins == 20}} is ambiguous with “left at the default” whenever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_bins}} has been
customized — see the danger box above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins \textless{}= 0}} always falls back to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_bins}} (clamped to at least \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} list infers every numeric feature, following the same rule as
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/lag:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a lag plot for one numeric feature: a scatter of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x(t)}} against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x(t + lag)}} — each
point’s horizontal position is a value from the series, and its vertical position is the
value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}} steps later in the same series. A cloud of points scattered along the diagonal
suggests strong positive autocorrelation at that lag; a cloud with no visible structure
suggests the series behaves close to random noise at that lag. This is the single\sphinxhyphen{}lag,
scatter\sphinxhyphen{}based sibling of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}}, which instead sweeps every lag and reduces each
one to a single correlation coefficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature resolution rule with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}} and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bootstrap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bootstrap()}}}}}}}: the named feature must resolve to exactly one numeric
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind) feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}}’s callout for the exact throw text.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least two data points are required
A feature with fewer than two rows throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"flash::lagplot requires at least two points"}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/lag:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The single numeric feature to lag against itself. Must resolve to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind
feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}}’s shared\sphinxhyphen{}diagnostics note.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LagPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct LagPlotOptions \{       std::int64\_t lag\{1\};       std::int64\_t max\_points\{2500\};       double marker\_area\{16.0\};       float trace\_width\{0.55F\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}} is clamped internally to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1, n \sphinxhyphen{} 1{]}}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} is the feature’s row count — a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}} of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} or larger than the data supports is silently clamped rather than throwing.
Given \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} rows and a clamped \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usable = n \sphinxhyphen{} lag}} points are plotted: the point at
index \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..usable}}) is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x{[}i{]}, x{[}i + lag{]})}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}} caps how many of
these \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usable}} points are actually drawn — when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usable}} exceeds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}}, points are
subsampled at a stride (not randomly chosen) so the count stays within budget while still
spanning the full range. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{marker\_area}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trace\_width}} control point size and marker
outline width respectively (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{marker\_area}} is floored to a minimum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.0}}).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/lag:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing a single scatter (“cloud”) trace of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x(t)}} vs.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x(t + lag)}}, axis\sphinxhyphen{}labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"x(t)"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"x(t + lag)"}}.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/lag:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default options (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag = 1}}): each point compares a value to the very next one in
the series.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{level}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{11.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.8}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{11.2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{11.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{11.3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{11.8}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{level}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{level\PYGZus{}lag1.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n = 8}} rows and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag = 1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usable = 7}} points are plotted: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10.0, 10.5)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10.5, 11.0)}}, …, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(11.3, 11.8)}} — a tight, mostly increasing sequence suggests strong positive
lag\sphinxhyphen{}1 autocorrelation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. An explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LagPlotOptions}} with a larger lag.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{LagPlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{level}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag = 3}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usable = 8 \sphinxhyphen{} 3 = 5}} points are plotted: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10.0, 10.8)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10.5, 11.2)}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(11.0, 11.5)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10.8, 11.3)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(11.2, 11.8)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}} request larger than the data supports is silently clamped, not thrown.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{oversized}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{readings}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{level}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{oversized}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With only 8 rows, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}} is clamped to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n \sphinxhyphen{} 1 = 7}}, leaving exactly one usable point: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x{[}0{]}, x{[}7{]})}}, i.e. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(10.0, 11.8)}}.

\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5000}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{big}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{trend}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{long\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{LagPlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{capped}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{capped}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}points}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{500}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{big}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{trend}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{capped}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/lag:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{feature}} must resolve to exactly one numeric feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/act::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{act()}}}}}}}’s shared
note.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lag}} is clamped to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1, n \sphinxhyphen{} 1{]}}}, never throwing for an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}range request.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}} subsamples by stride, not randomly, when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usable}} exceeds it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature with fewer than two rows throws before any point is drawn.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws one line trace per requested y\sphinxhyphen{}feature over a shared x\sphinxhyphen{}axis, returning a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} figure. This page also explains mechanics shared by every method on
this accessor — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar()}}, and the rest all follow the same
“nothing is drawn until you export it” and x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rules described here, so their
own pages link back to this one instead of repeating it.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every plot method returns a Studio, not a DataFrame — and nothing prints
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}} (like every method on this accessor) builds and returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — a
figure object from the separate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}} plotting library. It does \sphinxstylestrong{not} print a table,
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}}, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} chart}} will not compile. To actually see
or persist the result, call one of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}’s own methods afterward:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart.show()}} — opens the figure in a native window or the OS default browser/viewer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart.save\_svg("out.svg")}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart.save\_pdf("out.pdf")}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart.save\_png("out.png", dpi)}}
— write the figure to a file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_png}} shells out to an external SVG\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}raster
converter such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rsvg\sphinxhyphen{}convert}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inkscape}}, or ImageMagick, and throws if none is found).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart.to\_svg()}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart.to\_pdf()}} — return the rendered markup as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string}}, for
embedding elsewhere instead of writing a file.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every example on this page ends with one of these calls to make that visible; none of them
show a rendered “Output” block the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} method pages do, because there
is no text form of a chart to display.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Choosing the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis: three ways to end up with an x\sphinxhyphen{}feature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line:choosing-the-x-axis-three-ways-to-end-up-with-an-x-feature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every 2D chart method that takes an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} argument resolves it the same way:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pass it explicitly} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot.line("sales", "month")}} always wins, regardless of any
accessor\sphinxhyphen{}level default.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Set a shared default on the accessor} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.plot(options)}} where
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_x\_feature = "month"}} lets every subsequent chart method omit
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} and still use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"month"}}. An explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} argument on a given call
still takes precedence over this default.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Omit it entirely, with no default set} — the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis becomes the frame’s own \sphinxstylestrong{row
labels} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::label()}}), not a bare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..n\sphinxhyphen{}1}} index, and the axis title becomes
the literal string \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}}. If the row labels are text, a timestamp, or a time index,
the axis renders as evenly spaced categorical positions with those values as tick
labels; if the row labels are themselves numeric, they’re used as real numeric x
coordinates.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See Examples 1, 2, and 3 below for each of these three paths in turn.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
A single numeric feature to draw as one line trace.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})
Several numeric features, each drawn as its own line trace on the same axes. A legend
is shown automatically whenever more than one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature is requested (and suppressed
for a single feature). At least one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature is required — an empty list throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().line: at least one y feature is required"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
The feature to use as the shared x\sphinxhyphen{}axis. See “Choosing the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis” above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LinePlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct LinePlotOptions \{       double alpha\{1.0\};       double line\_width\{1.6\};       std::optional\textless{}pluss::pl::LimitMethod\textgreater{} y\_limit\_method\{pluss::pl::LimitMethod::Padded\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} controls trace opacity, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_width}} the stroke width. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_limit\_method}} chooses
how the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis auto\sphinxhyphen{}fits to the data: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Padded}} (the default) adds a small margin beyond
the data’s min/max, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tight}} fits exactly to the data range with no margin, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TickAligned}} snaps the limits outward to the nearest tick boundaries.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one line trace per requested y\sphinxhyphen{}feature.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Explicit x\sphinxhyphen{}feature: the most common and clearest form.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Jan}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Feb}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Mar}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Apr}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{120.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{90.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{150.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cost}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{60.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{80.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{55.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{95.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{monthly\PYGZus{}amount.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales.plot()}} enters the accessor with no shared options; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.line("amount", "month")}} draws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{amount}} on the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis against the text feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{month}} on the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis (rendered as four
evenly spaced categorical positions labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Jan"}}..\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Apr"}}), producing a single unlabeled
(no\sphinxhyphen{}legend, since there’s only one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature) line trace. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_svg}} is what actually writes
pixels — nothing above it touches disk.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. A shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_x\_feature}} set once on the accessor, used implicitly by
multiple chart calls.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}x\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{// x defaults to \PYGZdq{}month\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cost}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{// also defaults to \PYGZdq{}month\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cost}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{// explicit x\PYGZus{}feature=\PYGZdq{}cost\PYGZdq{} overrides the default}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart2}} both use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"month"}} as their x\sphinxhyphen{}axis without repeating it. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart3}}
demonstrates that an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} argument (here, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cost"}}) always wins over
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_x\_feature}}, even when both are present in the same call.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{untitled}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{by\PYGZus{}case.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{untitled}} was built with explicit row labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Q1"}}..\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Q4"}}) and no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{month}}\sphinxhyphen{}style feature
at all. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line("amount")}} with no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} and no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_x\_feature}} set falls back to
those row labels: the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis renders \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Q1"}}..\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Q4"}} as categorical positions, and the axis
title becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}} (not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"amount"}} and not the row\sphinxhyphen{}label feature’s own name — literally
the string \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 4. Multiple y\sphinxhyphen{}features overlaid on one pane, drawn from a brace\sphinxhyphen{}init list.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cost}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two line traces share the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{month}} x\sphinxhyphen{}axis and the same pane; a legend appears
automatically (labeled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"amount"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cost"}}) because more than one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature was
requested. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chart.show()}} opens the figure directly instead of writing a file — useful
during interactive exploration.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 5. The same multi\sphinxhyphen{}feature call using a reusable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}} instead of a brace\sphinxhyphen{}init
list — useful when the feature list is built at runtime rather than known at the call site.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}names}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cost}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{msharp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Of}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}names}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}pdf}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{monthly\PYGZus{}lines.pdf}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Behaves identically to Example 4 — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}} overload and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initializer\_list}}
overload are the same underlying call, just accepting the y\sphinxhyphen{}feature list in different forms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 6. An explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LinePlotOptions}}, tuning opacity, stroke width, and y\sphinxhyphen{}axis fit.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{LinePlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.85}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.5}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}limit\PYGZus{}method}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pl}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{LimitMethod}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Tight}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}png}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{monthly\PYGZus{}amount.png}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cm}{/*dpi=*/}\PYG{l+m+mi}{300}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The line is drawn slightly translucent (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha = 0.85}}), thicker (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_width = 2.5}}), and
the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis is fit tightly to the data’s actual min/max instead of the default padded
margin. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_png}} additionally takes an explicit DPI for the rasterized output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 7. Multiple y\sphinxhyphen{}features with an explicit options object — the three\sphinxhyphen{}argument
overload works the same way for the list\sphinxhyphen{}based forms as it does for the single\sphinxhyphen{}feature form.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cost}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{month}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{line\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}, never a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} and never printed text — see the
important callout above for how to actually view or save the result.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature is required; an empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_features}} list throws.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A legend is shown automatically once more than one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature is requested.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The x\sphinxhyphen{}axis resolves in three steps — explicit argument, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_x\_feature}},
then the frame’s own row labels titled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}} — see “Choosing the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis” above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_limit\_method}} only affects how the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis auto\sphinxhyphen{}fits; it does not change the data drawn.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFramePlotAccessor::parallel}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel:dataframeplotaccessor-parallel}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_plot_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFramePlotAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{parallel}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{msharp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Of}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{class\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ParallelPlotOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pl}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Studio}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a parallel\sphinxhyphen{}coordinates plot: one vertical axis per selected numeric feature, laid out
side by side, and one connected line per row threading through each axis at that row’s
value for that feature. This is a way to see multivariate structure across many features at
once — rows that behave similarly across several dimensions trace visually similar paths.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page also establishes mechanics shared with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{andrews\_curves()}}}}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radviz()}}}}}}}, which follow the same feature\sphinxhyphen{}selection, class\sphinxhyphen{}coloring, and
NaN\sphinxhyphen{}handling rules described here.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Masked/invalid cells become NaN gaps, not dropped rows — unlike box()/violin()
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/violin::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{violin()}}}}}}}, which silently drop non\sphinxhyphen{}finite values
entirely before plotting, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}} (and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{andrews\_curves()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radviz()}}) convert an
invalid cell to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} and keep the row’s position in the data — the underlying per\sphinxhyphen{}row line
simply has a gap or break at that feature’s axis rather than the row being omitted from the
figure altogether.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Numeric features to use as axes, in the given order. Empty (the default) infers every
numeric feature in the frame — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact
rule and throw text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{class\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
An optional feature used to color/group the per\sphinxhyphen{}row lines. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}}, this accepts \sphinxstylestrong{any} feature kind — it’s
converted to text via a Note cast if it isn’t already Note\sphinxhyphen{}kind, so a numeric class
feature works too (each distinct value, stringified, becomes its own class), not just
a text\sphinxhyphen{}like one.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParallelPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct ParallelPlotOptions \{       std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{} labels\{\};       bool normalize\{true\};       std::int64\_t max\_points\{1200\};       double alpha\{0.24\};       float trace\_width\{0.9F\};       bool show\_grid\{true\};       bool show\_legend\{true\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}, left empty, defaults to the resolved feature names — set it explicitly for
custom axis labels (must match the feature count). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize = true}} (the default)
rescales each axis independently so features on very different numeric ranges remain
visually comparable. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} defaults quite low (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.24}}) since parallel\sphinxhyphen{}coordinates
plots are typically drawn with many overlapping, semi\sphinxhyphen{}transparent lines. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}}
caps how many rows are drawn (for large frames, a subsample rather than every row).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing the parallel\sphinxhyphen{}coordinates trace(s) — one combined
trace, or one per class when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class\_feature}} is given.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. No explicit features, no class: every numeric feature in the frame, one plain
trace per row.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flowers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.7}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.8}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.3}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.7}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.3}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{petal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.4}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{species}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{setosa}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{virginica}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{virginica}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{virginica}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flowers}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{parallel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{flowers\PYGZus{}parallel.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}} with no arguments uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sepal\_length}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sepal\_width}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{petal\_length}} (the
three \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind features) as axes; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{species}} (Note\sphinxhyphen{}kind) is excluded from the axes
since it isn’t numeric.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. An explicit feature subset, colored by a class feature.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flowers}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{parallel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{petal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{species}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each row’s line is colored/grouped by its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{species}} value; a legend labeled with each
distinct species appears (since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_legend}} defaults to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. An explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParallelPlotOptions}}, with custom axis labels and reduced
transparency for a small dataset where overplotting isn’t a concern.

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.7}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{normalize}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{flowers}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{parallel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{petal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{species}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize = false}} plots each axis on its own raw numeric scale instead of a normalized

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empty (default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} infers every numeric feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s
important callout for the exact rule.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Masked/invalid cells become \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} gaps in a row’s line rather than dropping the row
entirely — see the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class\_feature}} accepts any feature kind (cast to text internally), unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}}}}}}’s stricter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}, if set explicitly, must match the resolved feature count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/pie:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a pie chart from one numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}}, with slice labels coming either from an
explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_feature}} or (if omitted) from the frame’s own row labels.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}positive and non\sphinxhyphen{}finite values are silently dropped, not zero\sphinxhyphen{}sized slices
Before drawing, every row is filtered: only rows where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} is both \sphinxstylestrong{finite}
and \sphinxstylestrong{strictly greater than zero} are kept. A row with a zero, negative, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}, or
infinite value doesn’t appear as a zero\sphinxhyphen{}width sliver — it’s removed from the chart
entirely, and its label never appears (including in the legend). If every row gets
filtered out, the call throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().pie: feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{} has no positive finite values"}}. This matters for percentage calculations too: the percentage shown for
each slice is computed against the total of the \sphinxstylestrong{surviving} (positive, finite) values
only, not the original column’s total.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/pie:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
The numeric feature whose values become slice sizes. Only finite, strictly positive
values are plotted — see the important callout above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{label\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
The feature whose values label each slice. When omitted, the frame’s own row labels are
used instead (the axis/slice label falls back the same conceptual way
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s x\sphinxhyphen{}axis does when no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} is given, though \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pie()}} has no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_x\_feature}}\sphinxhyphen{}style shortcut of its own — it’s just “explicit label\_feature, or
the row labels”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PiePlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct PiePlotOptions \{       bool show\_label\{true\};       bool show\_percent\{true\};       bool show\_value\{false\};       int precision\{1\};       std::string separator\{" | "\};     \};     }}
Each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_*}} flag independently controls whether that piece of text appears on a
slice; when more than one is enabled, the pieces are joined with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{separator}} in the
order label, then percent, then value. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{precision}} (clamped to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..12}}) controls decimal
places for both the percentage and the raw value text. If all three \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_*}} flags are
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, no per\sphinxhyphen{}slice text is rendered at all (slices are still drawn and colored, just
unlabeled).


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/pie:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing a single pie trace.

Since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_feature}} is omitted, each slice is labeled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{by\_case}}’s own row labels
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"eng"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sales"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"support"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"marketing"}}) instead of a separate feature column.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 3. Non\sphinxhyphen{}positive and non\sphinxhyphen{}finite values are dropped — and the remaining slices’
percentages are computed against the smaller, filtered total.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mixed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{category}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{A}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{B}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{C}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{D}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{spend}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{\PYGZhy{}50.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{300.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mixed}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{pie}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{spend}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{category}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"A"}} (100.0) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"D"}} (300.0) survive the filter; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"B"}} (negative) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"C"}} (zero)
are dropped entirely — they never appear as slices or in the legend. The percentages shown
are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{25.0\%}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{75.0\%}} — computed against \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{100 + 300 = 400}}, not the original four\sphinxhyphen{}row
