\subparagraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/pie:output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
DataFrame::plot().pie: feature \PYGZsq{}spend\PYGZsq{} has no positive finite values
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/pie:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only finite, strictly positive values are plotted; everything else is silently dropped,
and percentages are computed against the filtered total — see the important callout
above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_feature}} omitted falls back to the frame’s own row labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{precision}} is shared between the percentage and value text, clamped to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..12}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An entirely\sphinxhyphen{}filtered\sphinxhyphen{}out feature throws rather than producing an empty chart.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/pie:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::bar}}}}}}}: a composition\sphinxhyphen{}friendly alternative when exact
comparison between category sizes matters more than “share of a whole.”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::heatmap}}}}}}}: another way to summarize categorical
breakdowns, for two grouping dimensions at once instead of one.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFramePlotAccessor::radviz}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz:dataframeplotaccessor-radviz}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_plot_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFramePlotAccessor API Reference}}}}}}


\subparagraph{Signature}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz:signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{radviz}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{msharp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RangeView}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Of}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{optional}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{class\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nullopt}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{RadvizPlotOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pl}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Studio}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a RadViz (radial visualization): one anchor point per selected numeric feature is
placed evenly around the circumference of a circle, and each row is placed inside the circle
at the position where it would come to rest if pulled toward every anchor by a spring whose
strength is proportional to that row’s (normalized) value for that feature. Rows dominated
by one feature are pulled close to that feature’s anchor; rows balanced across several
features settle nearer the center. This is a third way (alongside {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/andrews_curves::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{andrews\_curves()}}}}}}}) to eyeball multivariate structure across more
than two features at once.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its feature\sphinxhyphen{}selection rule (empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} infers every numeric feature),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class\_feature}} behavior (accepts any feature kind, cast to text), and NaN\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}drop handling
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}} — see that page for the full explanation; this page only
covers what’s specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radviz()}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Numeric features that become anchor points, in the given order around the circle. Empty
infers every numeric feature — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact
rule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{class\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Optional coloring/grouping feature, same behavior as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}}’s.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RadvizPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct RadvizPlotOptions \{       std::vector\textless{}std::string\textgreater{} labels\{\};       bool normalize\{true\};       std::int64\_t max\_points\{3000\};       double marker\_area\{18.0\};       float trace\_width\{0.55F\};       bool show\_grid\{true\};       bool show\_anchors\{true\};       bool show\_legend\{true\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{labels}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_grid}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_legend}} mirror
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParallelPlotOptions}}}}}}}’s fields of the same name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}} here caps
how many rows are plotted as points, analogous to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{andrews\_curves()}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_curves}}
capping curves). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{marker\_area}} sizes each row’s point marker; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trace\_width}} here controls
marker outline width rather than a line’s stroke width, since radviz plots points rather
than lines. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_anchors}} toggles whether the per\sphinxhyphen{}feature anchor points and labels are
drawn around the circle’s rim — turning it off leaves only the plotted rows and the
circle outline.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one point per row (or capped at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_points}}), anchor
points around the circle’s rim (when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_anchors}} is true), colored by class when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class\_feature}} is given.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/radviz:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares its feature\sphinxhyphen{}selection, class\sphinxhyphen{}coloring, and NaN\sphinxhyphen{}handling rules with
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}} — see that page for the full explanation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Needs at least three anchors to be visually meaningful (two anchors collapse the circle to
a line), though the underlying feature\sphinxhyphen{}selection rule itself doesn’t special\sphinxhyphen{}case fewer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show\_anchors}} toggles the rim labels/points, independent of whether rows are plotted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws one point per row at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x\_feature, y\_feature)}}, optionally split into separate,
distinctly colored/labeled point groups by a categorical \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}}. Unlike
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/step::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/area::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{area()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/bar::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar()}}}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}
takes \sphinxstylestrong{both x and y as required, plain (non\sphinxhyphen{}optional) arguments} — there is no “fall back
to the frame’s row labels” behavior here, since a scatter plot needs two independent
numeric axes, not one axis plus a case index.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} mechanics shared by this whole
accessor.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
hue\_feature has its own default\sphinxhyphen{}resolution and a stricter type requirement
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}} resolves the same way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} does elsewhere on this accessor: an
explicit argument wins, otherwise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_hue\_feature}} (set via
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.plot(options)}}) is used if present, otherwise there’s no hue at all and every point is
drawn as one plain trace. Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{andrews\_curves()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{radviz()}}’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{class\_feature}} (which accepts any feature and converts it to text), a resolved
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}} here \sphinxstylestrong{must} already be Note\sphinxhyphen{}, Timeline\sphinxhyphen{}, or TimeIndex\sphinxhyphen{}kind — a plain
numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} hue feature throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().scatter: hue feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{} must be note\sphinxhyphen{}like or time\sphinxhyphen{}like"}}. If you want to color by a numeric value, bucket or cast it to
text first (e.g. with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bucketize()}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{note()}}\sphinxhyphen{}family conversions).
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, required)
The feature for the horizontal axis. Always numeric\sphinxhyphen{}plotted (see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{require\_plot\_size}}
validation) — not resolved from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_x\_feature}} the way other chart methods’
optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} is.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, required)
The feature for the vertical axis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{hue\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Optional categorical feature to split points into separate colored/labeled groups. See
the important callout above for its resolution and type requirements.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScatterPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct ScatterPlotOptions \{       double alpha\{0.92\};       double line\_width\{1.1\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line\_width}} here affects marker outline stroke width rather than a connecting line,
since scatter points aren’t connected.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane: a single point trace with no hue, or one point trace per
distinct hue value (each its own color, with a legend) when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}} resolves to
something.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cohort}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Morning}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Evening}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Morning}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Evening}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Morning}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{students}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{midterm}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{final}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2. With a categorical hue feature: points split into one trace per distinct cohort
value, each its own color.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{students}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{midterm}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{final}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{cohort}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two traces are drawn — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Morning"}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Evening"}} — in the order those values first appear
in the data (row 0 is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"Morning"}}, so it becomes the first group; row 1 introduces

cohort value is shown automatically.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}} are required, non\sphinxhyphen{}optional arguments — there is no row\sphinxhyphen{}label
fallback the way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar()}}/etc. have for a single axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}} resolves through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_hue\_feature}} the same way \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}
resolves through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_x\_feature}} elsewhere, but a resolved hue feature must be
Note\sphinxhyphen{}, Timeline\sphinxhyphen{}, or TimeIndex\sphinxhyphen{}kind or the call throws — see the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hue groups are ordered by first appearance in the data, not sorted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter_matrix:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Builds a grid of every pairwise scatter plot among the selected numeric features — an
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}}×\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} grid of small panes, where off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal cell \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i, j)}} is a scatter of feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}
against feature \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{j}}, and diagonal cells show each feature’s own distribution (a histogram
by default). This is the classic “pairs plot” for eyeballing every two\sphinxhyphen{}way relationship in
a small\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}medium numeric feature set at once.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least two numeric features are required
Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}/etc.’s “any nonzero count of numeric features is fine,” a scatter
matrix is inherently pairwise — fewer than two numeric features throws
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().scatter\_matrix: need at least two numeric features"}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature selection here doesn’t validate non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric names — it filters instead
Unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}}}}}}/{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/corr_heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_heatmap()}}}}}}}, an
explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} list here is first narrowed to the requested columns and then filtered
down to only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind ones — passing a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric feature name doesn’t throw,
it’s simply excluded from the matrix. If that filtering leaves fewer than two features, the
“at least two” check above still throws.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter_matrix:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}})
Features to scope the matrix to before filtering down to the numeric ones. Empty (the
default) considers every feature in the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{triangle} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScatterMatrixTriangle}}, two\sphinxhyphen{}argument overload)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Full}} (the default elsewhere too), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lower}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Upper}} — restricts the grid to only the
lower or upper triangle (plus the diagonal) instead of drawing every cell twice
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i, j)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(j, i)}} are mirror images of the same pairwise relationship).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ScatterMatrixPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct ScatterMatrixPlotOptions \{       bool corner\{false\};       pluss::pl::flash::PairPlotOptions pair\{\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corner = true}} is a shorthand: if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pair.triangle}} is still at its default (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Full}}), it
gets switched to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lower}} automatically — a “corner\sphinxhyphen{}style” pairs plot with the diagonal
at the top\sphinxhyphen{}left and only the lower triangle filled in. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pair}} is the full underlying
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PairPlotOptions}} struct (triangle, diagonal kind, point vs. regression cells,
grid sizing, point limits, and more); only the fields most relevant here are called out
on this page — the rest are documented in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}}’s own reference.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter_matrix:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure containing the full grid of pairwise panes.

Example 2. An explicit feature subset via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}}.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter_matrix:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least two numeric features are required after filtering — see the important callout
above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric feature names in an explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} list are silently filtered out
instead of throwing — see the note above (contrast most other methods on this accessor).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corner = true}} only overrides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pair.triangle}} if it’s still at its default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Full}}; an
explicitly set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pair.triangle}} is left alone.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/step:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identical in shape to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} — one trace per y\sphinxhyphen{}feature over a shared x\sphinxhyphen{}axis,
same three overload families (single feature, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{initializer\_list}}), same
x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution rules (explicit argument, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_x\_feature}}, then the
frame’s own row labels titled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"case"}}) — but each trace is drawn as a \sphinxstylestrong{step function}
(horizontal\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}vertical jumps between points) instead of straight line segments between
consecutive points. This is the natural chart for a value that stays constant between
discrete changes (a price that only updates at known events, a rate that steps between
tiers) rather than one that continuously interpolates.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the full explanation of the shared mechanics (the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} behavior, and the three\sphinxhyphen{}step x\sphinxhyphen{}axis resolution) — this page
only covers what’s specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step()}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/step:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} / \sphinxstylestrong{y\_features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} /
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}})
Same as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}: one or more numeric features, each drawn as its own step
trace. At least one is required — an empty list throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot().step: at     least one y feature is required"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Same three\sphinxhyphen{}step resolution as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StepPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct StepPlotOptions \{       double alpha\{1.0\};       double line\_width\{1.5\};     \};     }}
Only opacity and stroke width — unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LinePlotOptions}}}}}}}, there is no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_limit\_method}} field on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StepPlotOptions}}; the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis always uses the figure’s default
auto\sphinxhyphen{}fit behavior for step charts.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/step:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one step trace per requested y\sphinxhyphen{}feature.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/step:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. A single feature, explicit x\sphinxhyphen{}axis.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/step:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shares every mechanic described on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s page except the step\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}line
trace shape and the smaller \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{StepPlotOptions}} struct (no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_limit\_method}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
At least one y\sphinxhyphen{}feature is required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — nothing is printed; see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important
callout for how to view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/violin:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a kernel\sphinxhyphen{}density\sphinxhyphen{}shaped violin (full distribution shape, not just quartiles) for each
requested numeric feature or group. There are genuinely \sphinxstylestrong{two different modes}, chosen by
which overload is called:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Feature\sphinxhyphen{}list mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{violin(features{[}, options{]})}}): exactly like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}} —
one violin per requested numeric feature, all sharing one pane, feature names as x\sphinxhyphen{}axis
labels. An empty (default) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}} list infers every numeric feature in the frame,
under the same rules described on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s page.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Value/group mode} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{violin(value\_feature, group\_feature{[}, options{]})}}): a single numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}}, split into one violin per distinct value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} — the
“distribution of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}}, broken down by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}}” view.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Value/group mode accepts a numeric group\_feature too — unlike scatter()’s hue
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} in the two\sphinxhyphen{}argument form is \sphinxstylestrong{not} restricted to Note/Timeline/TimeIndex
the way {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}} is. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} is text\sphinxhyphen{}like
(Note, Timeline, or TimeIndex), its distinct text values become the violin groups. If it’s
a plain numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} instead, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{violin()}} doesn’t reject it — it uses the raw numeric
values directly as violin group positions along the axis, so each \sphinxstylestrong{distinct numeric
value} present in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} gets its own violin at that value’s own x position (not
converted to text labels). This is a genuinely more permissive design than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}’s
hue check; a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} with mostly\sphinxhyphen{}unique values (rather than a handful of
repeated category codes) will produce one near\sphinxhyphen{}empty violin per row, which is rarely what’s
wanted — reserve a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}} for columns that really are small\sphinxhyphen{}cardinality
codes.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/violin:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{features} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RangeView\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::initializer\_list\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}},
default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}, feature\sphinxhyphen{}list mode)
Numeric features to summarize, each as its own violin. Empty means “every numeric
feature” — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the exact rule and throw text.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{value\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, value/group mode)
The numeric feature whose distribution is drawn.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{group\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, value/group mode)
The feature defining violin groups — text\sphinxhyphen{}like or numeric, see the important callout
above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ViolinPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct ViolinPlotOptions \{       double alpha\{0.92\};       double line\_width\{1.1\};       double width\{0.8\};       double bw\_adjust\{1.0\};       double cut\{2.0\};       pluss::pl::ViolinScale scale\{pluss::pl::ViolinScale::Area\};       pluss::pl::ViolinInner inner\{pluss::pl::ViolinInner::Box\};       pluss::pl::ViolinSide side\{pluss::pl::ViolinSide::Full\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}} is the maximum horizontal extent of each violin. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bw\_adjust}} scales the kernel
density bandwidth (above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} smooths the shape further, below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}} shows more
fine\sphinxhyphen{}grained detail). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cut}} controls how far the drawn shape extends past the observed
data’s min/max, in bandwidth units. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scale}} picks how multiple violins are normalized
against each other: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Area}} (equal area under each violin regardless of sample count),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}} (area proportional to each group’s sample count), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Width}} (equal max width
regardless of shape). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inner}} chooses what’s drawn inside the violin body: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Box}} (a mini box plot), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Quartile}} (quartile lines), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stick}} (individual observation
ticks), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Point}} (individual observation dots). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{side}} can restrict each violin to a
half\sphinxhyphen{}shape (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Right}}) instead of the default symmetric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Full}} shape.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/violin:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one pane containing one violin per requested feature (feature\sphinxhyphen{}list mode)
or one violin per distinct group value (value/group mode).

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/violin:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two distinct modes selected by overload: feature\sphinxhyphen{}list (like {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}) versus
value/group (splits one feature’s values by another feature).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature\sphinxhyphen{}list mode’s empty\sphinxhyphen{}list default and non\sphinxhyphen{}finite\sphinxhyphen{}value handling follow the same
rules as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/box::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{box()}}}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Value/group mode accepts a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_feature}}, unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}}}}}}’s
stricter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}} — see the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{DataFramePlot3DAccessor API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_plot3d_accessor_api_reference:dataframeplot3daccessor-api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe_plot3d_accessor_api_reference::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This page documents the public 3D plotting accessor returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::plot3d()}}.


\paragraph{Using This Reference}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_plot3d_accessor_api_reference:using-this-reference}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the left sidebar to open one method page at a time.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each method page contains its own signatures, parameter details, notes, and working previous/next navigation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This landing page stays intentionally short so the content panel is not one giant scroll of every method.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every method returns a Studio, not a DataFrame
None of these methods print a table or draw anything to the console. Each one builds and
returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} figure object from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussPl}} plotting library — nothing is
rendered until you call one of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}’s own methods (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_svg(path)}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_png(path)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_pdf(path)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_svg()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pdf()}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} has no
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}}, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} figure}} does not compile — see each page’s examples for the
actual pattern.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\paragraph{Method Pages}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_plot3d_accessor_api_reference:method-pages}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The sidebar lists methods alphabetically. You can also use the search box to jump directly to a method name.

\sphinxstepscope

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/hist:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a 3D (bivariate) histogram: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}} are jointly binned into a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_x}} × \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_y}} grid over their combined ranges, and each grid cell’s count (or, with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize = true}}, its share of the total) becomes that cell’s height. By default this
height is rendered as a field of vertical bars — one per grid cell — but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}} can
switch the same underlying grid to a continuous surface or a wireframe mesh instead. This
is the two\sphinxhyphen{}feature analog of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::hist}}}}}}},
which bins a single feature into a 2D bar chart.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} mechanics, feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}
axis conversion rules, and the full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DSceneOptions}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DTraceOptions}} layering
explanation — this page only covers what’s specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}.


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/hist:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature}, \sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, both required)
The two numeric features jointly binned into the grid. Both must resolve to numeric
values — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s note on feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}axis conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Hist3DPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct Hist3DPlotOptions \{       std::int64\_t bins\_x\{26\};       std::int64\_t bins\_y\{20\};       bool normalize\{false\};       bool smooth\{false\};       std::int64\_t smooth\_passes\{1\};       bool as\_surface\{false\};       bool as\_wireframe\{false\};       Plot3DSceneOptions scene\{\};       Plot3DTraceOptions trace\{\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_x}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_y}} are floored to a minimum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}} each — a request below that is
silently clamped up, never throwing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize = true}} divides every cell by the grid’s
total count, turning raw counts into a density\sphinxhyphen{}like share (skipped if the total is
non\sphinxhyphen{}finite or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, in which case the raw counts pass through unchanged). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smooth = true}}
applies a smoothing pass to the grid before rendering, repeated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smooth\_passes}} times
(floored to a minimum of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}); this softens sharp bin\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}bin jumps at the cost of
blurring the exact counts. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_wireframe}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_surface}} control the render shape —
see the note below for exactly how they interact.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
```\PYGZob{}note\PYGZcb{} Three mutually exclusive render shapes, checked in a fixed order
`as\PYGZus{}wireframe` is checked first: if `true`, the grid is drawn as a **wireframe mesh**
(same shape [`wireframe()`](wireframe.md) draws), regardless of `as\PYGZus{}surface`. Otherwise,
if `as\PYGZus{}surface` is `true`, the grid is drawn as a **continuous surface** (same shape
[`surface()`](surface.md) draws). If neither flag is set (the default for both), the
grid is drawn as a field of **3D bars** — one vertical \PYGZdq{}spire\PYGZdq{} per grid cell, the
conventional 3D\PYGZhy{}histogram look. Setting both flags is legal; `as\PYGZus{}wireframe` simply wins.
```
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/hist:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one 3D pane containing a single trace over the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_x}} × \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_y}} grid,
shaped as bars, a surface, or a wireframe depending on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 7. Requesting fewer than 4 bins on either axis is silently clamped, not thrown.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Hist3DPlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tiny}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{tiny}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{bins\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{chart}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{samples}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{hist}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{a}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{b}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{tiny}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_x}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_y}} are clamped up to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}, the minimum, rather than producing a
degenerate grid or throwing.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/hist:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_x}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bins\_y}} are floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smooth\_passes}} is floored to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normalize}} divides by the grid total only when that total is finite and positive;
otherwise raw counts pass through unchanged.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The render shape is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_wireframe}} \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_surface}} \(\rightarrow\) default bars, checked in that fixed
order — see the note above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line:dataframeplot3daccessor-line}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFramePlot3DAccessor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Line3DPlotOptions}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pl}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Studio}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a single connected 3D path: row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x, y, z)}} triple becomes point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} on the
line, and consecutive rows are joined in \sphinxstylestrong{frame row order} — there is no sorting by any
axis first. This is the 3D counterpart of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::line}}}}}}},
but every axis here is an explicit, required feature; there is no x\sphinxhyphen{}axis\sphinxhyphen{}resolution fallback
to row labels the way the 2D accessor has.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page also establishes mechanics shared by every method on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlot3DAccessor}} — {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/scatter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/hist::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hist()}}}}}}},
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/wireframe::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wireframe()}}}}}}} all work the same way with
respect to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}, feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}axis conversion, and the two 3D options structs described
below.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every method returns a Studio, same as the 2D accessor
Nothing is drawn to the console. Every method on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlot3DAccessor}} builds and
returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}, exactly like every method on the 2D
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} has no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{operator\textless{}\textless{}}}, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout \textless{}\textless{} chart}} does not compile. Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_svg(path)}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_png(path)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.save\_pdf(path)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_svg()}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pdf()}} to actually view or
persist the figure. Every example on this page ends with one of these calls instead of a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::cout}} block.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
How a feature becomes a numeric axis value
Every 3D method resolves each named feature to a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} per row before plotting:
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature is used as\sphinxhyphen{}is; a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}\sphinxhyphen{} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature is
converted to \sphinxstylestrong{epoch nanoseconds} (so a genuine timestamp feature can be used directly as
an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}} axis, plotted on a raw nanosecond scale); a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}\sphinxhyphen{}kind feature is cast to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} (a text\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}number parse, which produces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} for text that doesn’t parse as a
number rather than throwing outright). Any other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot: unsupported Thread kind for numeric plotting"}}. A resolved axis whose length doesn’t match
the frame’s row count throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot: feature \textquotesingle{}\textless{}name\textgreater{}\textquotesingle{} length mismatch with cases"}} — note this shared low\sphinxhyphen{}level check’s message always says \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::plot"}}, even
when it fires from a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot3d()}} call.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature}, \sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature}, \sphinxstylestrong{z\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, all required)
The three features providing each row’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}} coordinate — see the note
above for how each is converted to a numeric value. Unlike the 2D accessor’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}
arguments, none of these are optional and there is no frame\sphinxhyphen{}row\sphinxhyphen{}label fallback.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Line3DPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct Line3DPlotOptions \{       Plot3DSceneOptions scene\{\};       Plot3DTraceOptions trace\{\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scene}} controls the 3D pane’s camera, lighting, theme, and grid style; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trace}}
controls the drawn line’s shading, lighting response, material, stroke width, and
transparency. Both are described in full below, since every method on this accessor
shares the exact same two structs.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
```cpp
enum class ScenePreset3D \PYGZob{} Survey, Presentation, Studio, Topology \PYGZcb{};
enum class ThemePreset3D \PYGZob{} Paper, Ocean, Slate, Mist \PYGZcb{};
enum class CameraPreset3D \PYGZob{} Spatial, TopDown, Front, Side, Isometric \PYGZcb{};
enum class ProjectionKind \PYGZob{} Perspective, Orthographic \PYGZcb{};

struct Camera3DOptions \PYGZob{}
  double azimuth\PYGZus{}deg\PYGZob{}\PYGZhy{}37.5\PYGZcb{};
  double elevation\PYGZus{}deg\PYGZob{}30.0\PYGZcb{};
  double view\PYGZus{}angle\PYGZus{}deg\PYGZob{}30.0\PYGZcb{};
  ProjectionKind projection\PYGZob{}ProjectionKind::Orthographic\PYGZcb{};
\PYGZcb{};

struct Lighting3DOptions \PYGZob{}
  bool clear\PYGZus{}first\PYGZob{}true\PYGZcb{};
  bool headlight\PYGZob{}true\PYGZcb{};
  bool lamp\PYGZus{}left\PYGZob{}false\PYGZcb{};
  bool lamp\PYGZus{}right\PYGZob{}false\PYGZcb{};
  bool sun\PYGZus{}key\PYGZob{}false\PYGZcb{};
\PYGZcb{};

struct Plot3DSceneOptions \PYGZob{}
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}ScenePreset3D\PYGZgt{} preset\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}ThemePreset3D\PYGZgt{} theme\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}CameraPreset3D\PYGZgt{} camera\PYGZus{}preset\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}Camera3DOptions\PYGZgt{} camera\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}Lighting3DOptions\PYGZgt{} lighting\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}pluss::pl::GridStyle\PYGZgt{} grid\PYGZus{}style\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
\PYGZcb{};
```

Every field in `Plot3DSceneOptions` is a `std::optional` that defaults to
`std::nullopt`, meaning \PYGZdq{}leave the pane\PYGZsq{}s built\PYGZhy{}in default alone.\PYGZdq{} When several
fields *are* set, they\PYGZsq{}re applied in a fixed order, each one layering on top of
(and able to override) whatever came before: **`preset`** first (a bundle that sets
a theme, grid style, camera angle, and a lighting rig all at once — see the preset
table below), then **`theme`** (overrides just the color theme), then
**`grid\PYGZus{}style`** (`None`, `Major`, or `MajorMinor`), then **`camera\PYGZus{}preset`**
(overrides just the camera angle), then **`camera`** (an explicit
`Camera3DOptions`, overriding any preset\PYGZsq{}s angle with exact numbers), then
**`lighting`** (an explicit `Lighting3DOptions`, overriding any preset\PYGZsq{}s lights).
Setting both `camera\PYGZus{}preset` and `camera` is legal — `camera` applies last and wins.

| `ScenePreset3D` | Theme | Camera | Lighting |
|\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}|\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}|\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}|\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}|
| `Survey` | Ocean | Isometric | headlight + left lamp |
| `Presentation` | Paper | perspective, low/wide angle | headlight + right lamp + sun key |
| `Studio` | Slate | Spatial (the library\PYGZhy{}wide default angle) | headlight + both lamps |
| `Topology` | Mist | TopDown | headlight only |

```cpp
enum class TracePreset3D \PYGZob{} Path, Cloud, Surface, Wireframe, Spire, Volume \PYGZcb{};
enum class ShadeMode \PYGZob{} Faceted, Flat, Smooth \PYGZcb{};
enum class LightingMode \PYGZob{} None, Flat, Gouraud \PYGZcb{};
enum class MaterialProfile \PYGZob{} Default, Dull, Shiny, Metal \PYGZcb{};

struct Plot3DTraceOptions \PYGZob{}
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}TracePreset3D\PYGZgt{} preset\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}ShadeMode\PYGZgt{} shade\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}LightingMode\PYGZgt{} lighting\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}MaterialProfile\PYGZgt{} material\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}float\PYGZgt{} line\PYGZus{}width\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
  std::optional\PYGZlt{}bool\PYGZgt{} transparent\PYGZob{}std::nullopt\PYGZcb{};
\PYGZcb{};
```

Same layering rule as `Plot3DSceneOptions`: **`preset`** applies first (a bundle of
shade/lighting/material/width/transparency tuned for one trace shape — `Path` is
tuned for line traces, `Cloud` for scatter, `Surface` for filled meshes,
`Wireframe` for mesh edges, `Spire` for 3D\PYGZhy{}bar histograms, `Volume` for
translucent solids), then any explicitly\PYGZhy{}set `shade`, `lighting`, `material`,
`line\PYGZus{}width`, or `transparent` fields override just that one aspect of the preset.
None of `line()`\PYGZsq{}s example calls below set a `preset`, so the pane/trace defaults
(not any preset\PYGZsq{}s values) are what\PYGZsq{}s actually drawn unless noted otherwise.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one 3D pane containing a single connected line trace through the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x, y, z)}} points, in row order.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scene}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{camera}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pl}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{flash}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Camera3DOptions}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{azimuth\PYGZus{}deg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{60.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{elevation\PYGZus{}deg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{15.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{measured\_at}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} coordinates are its epoch\sphinxhyphen{}nanosecond values — a very large numeric
range compared to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth\_m}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{temp\_c}}, so the pane’s own auto\sphinxhyphen{}scaling handles the disparity;
this call does not reformat the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis into calendar tick labels the way the 2D accessor’s
Timeline\sphinxhyphen{}aware axis labeling does.


\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every axis argument is required — there is no optional\sphinxhyphen{}argument or row\sphinxhyphen{}label fallback
here, unlike {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::line}}}}}}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Points are connected strictly in frame row order, never sorted by any axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DSceneOptions}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DTraceOptions}} both apply their fields in a fixed
preset\sphinxhyphen{}then\sphinxhyphen{}explicit\sphinxhyphen{}override order — see the callouts above; this same layering rule
applies to every method on this accessor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} feature used as an axis is converted to epoch nanoseconds, not
calendar\sphinxhyphen{}aware tick labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see the important callout above for how to view or save
the result.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/scatter:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws an unconnected 3D point cloud: row \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x, y, z)}} triple becomes one point, with
two optional per\sphinxhyphen{}point encodings layered on top — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} scales each point’s marker
size, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_feature}} maps each point’s numeric value onto the trace’s color scale. This
is the 3D counterpart of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::scatter}}}}}}},
though the two differ meaningfully: the 2D \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}} accepts a categorical \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}}
that splits points into separate colored/labeled traces, while this method’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_feature}} is a single continuous numeric gradient across one trace, closer in spirit
to a heatmap’s color scale than to the 2D accessor’s hue grouping.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} mechanics, feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}
axis conversion rules, and the full \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DSceneOptions}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DTraceOptions}} layering
explanation — this page only covers what’s specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter()}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
size\_feature and color\_feature combine independently
There are effectively four call shapes, chosen entirely by which of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_feature}} are present: neither present draws uniform points at the pane’s default
marker size; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} alone scales marker size per point; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_feature}} alone
colors every point by its value while marker size stays fixed at
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_marker\_size}}; both present scale size \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} color together. There is no
overload that lets you set a per\sphinxhyphen{}point color without also implicitly sizing every point
uniformly at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_marker\_size}} when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} is omitted — the size argument
passed to the underlying trace call is always populated, just filled with a constant when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} isn’t given.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/scatter:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature}, \sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature}, \sphinxstylestrong{z\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}}, all required)
The three features providing each point’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z}} coordinate — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s note on feature\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}axis conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{size\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Optional numeric feature controlling each point’s marker size. Omitted means every
point uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.default\_marker\_size}} uniformly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{color\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::optional\textless{}std::string\_view\textgreater{}}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::nullopt}})
Optional numeric feature mapped onto the trace’s color scale, one continuous gradient
across all points (not a categorical split into separate traces — contrast the 2D
accessor’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Scatter3DPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct Scatter3DPlotOptions \{       Plot3DSceneOptions scene\{\};       Plot3DTraceOptions trace\{\};       double default\_marker\_size\{12.0\};     \};     }}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_marker\_size}} is only consulted when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} is omitted; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scene}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trace}}
are the same shared structs documented in full on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/scatter:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one 3D pane containing a single point\sphinxhyphen{}cloud trace of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x, y, z)}}
points.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/scatter:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_feature}} are independent optional encodings — see the note
above for exactly how the four combinations behave.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_marker\_size}} only applies when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size\_feature}} is omitted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike the 2D accessor’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_feature}} is a single continuous gradient
across one trace, not a split into separate colored/labeled traces.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/scatter:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/scatter::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::scatter}}}}}}}: the 2D counterpart,
with a categorical \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hue\_feature}} instead of a continuous \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color\_feature}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlot3DAccessor::line}}}}}}}: connected points in row order, instead of an
unconnected cloud.

\end{itemize}

\subparagraph{DataFramePlot3DAccessor::surface}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface:dataframeplot3daccessor-surface}}\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{dataframe_plot3d_accessor_api_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Back to DataFramePlot3DAccessor API Reference}}}}}}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{y\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{string\PYGZus{}view}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{z\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{p}{,}

\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a continuous 3D surface mesh over an aggregated grid: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}}’s distinct values
become the grid’s rows, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}’s distinct values become the grid’s columns, and each
cell’s height is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z\_feature}} aggregated (using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}) across every row sharing that
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x, y)}} combination. Internally this is built by calling
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{frame\_.pivot\_table(y\_feature, x\_feature, z\_feature, op, /*dropnull\_keys=*/true, /*render=*/false)}} — the same pivot machinery {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::heatmap}}}}}}}’s
grouped mode uses, but the resulting grid is rendered as a 3D mesh instead of a flat
2D color grid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} mechanics and the full
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DSceneOptions}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DTraceOptions}} layering explanation — this page only covers what
is specific to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
op is more restricted here than DataFrame::GroupOp’s own ten values
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} is typed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Median}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mode}}), but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} itself only implements seven of those:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Sum}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Median}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Min}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Max}}. Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mode}} compiles fine but throws at call time: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::pivot\_table: unsupported aggregation op"}}. For any of the seven supported numeric aggregations (everything except
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z\_feature}} must already be a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} — a non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z\_feature}} throws \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::pivot\_table: numeric aggregations require a numeric Series value feature"}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
How each axis gets its grid coordinates
The \sphinxstylestrong{y\sphinxhyphen{}axis} comes from the pivoted table’s row labels (the distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}}
values): if a label converts to a finite number, that number is used directly as the
y\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate; otherwise (categorical/text \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}} values) the row falls back to its
positional index (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, …) instead. The \sphinxstylestrong{x\sphinxhyphen{}axis} comes from the pivoted
table’s column names (the distinct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} values, stringified): each name is parsed
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{strtod}} — if the entire string parses cleanly as a number, that’s the x\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate;
otherwise it falls back to its positional column index the same way. In practice this
means a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}} produces a genuinely numeric, meaningfully\sphinxhyphen{}spaced
grid, while a categorical one produces evenly spaced integer positions — visually similar
to {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}}’s grid always being “rectangular” regardless of the original
features’ actual value distribution.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rows where x\_feature or y\_feature is invalid are silently dropped
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} is always called with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropnull\_keys = true}} here — a row whose
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}} value is invalid (masked/null) is excluded from the pivot
entirely, rather than becoming its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"NULL"}} row or column.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing (x, y) combinations fill to zero, not NaN
Once the pivot grid is built, any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x, y)}} cell with no matching rows at all becomes
non\sphinxhyphen{}finite in the underlying aggregation and is then replaced with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} before rendering —
the same zero\sphinxhyphen{}fill behavior documented for {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{heatmap()}}}}}}}’s
grouped mode, not the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}\sphinxhyphen{}gap behavior of {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/parallel::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parallel()}}}}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
Feature whose distinct values become the grid’s columns (x\sphinxhyphen{}axis).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
Feature whose distinct values become the grid’s rows (y\sphinxhyphen{}axis).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{z\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
Feature aggregated into each grid cell’s height.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{op} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})
The aggregation applied per cell — see the important callout above for which values
are actually supported.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Surface3DPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct Surface3DPlotOptions \{       Plot3DSceneOptions scene\{\};       Plot3DTraceOptions trace\{\};     \};     }}
The same shared structs documented in full on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}} has no
fields of its own beyond these two.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one 3D pane containing a single continuous surface\sphinxhyphen{}mesh trace over the
aggregated grid.


\subparagraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1. Default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}}): a numeric x/y grid, aggregated by mean.

\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{table}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{hour}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{12.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{12.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{12.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hour}}’s two distinct values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{12.0}}) become x\sphinxhyphen{}columns; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth\_m}}’s three distinct
values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10.0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20.0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{30.0}}) become y\sphinxhyphen{}rows; each cell is the mean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{temp\_c}} for that
hour/depth combination — here, each combination happens to have exactly one matching row,
so the “mean” is just that row’s own value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pivot grid is 2×2 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} values \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y}} values \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.0}}), but only the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(1.0, 1.0)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(2.0, 2.0)}} cells have matching rows; the other two cells (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(1.0, 2.0)}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(2.0, 1.0)}}) have no matching data and render at height \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, not as gaps.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only 7 of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}}’s 10 values are supported (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mode}} throw) — see
the important callout above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric aggregations (everything but \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Count}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Nunique}}) require \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z\_feature}} to already be
a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x/y grid coordinates are parsed\sphinxhyphen{}as\sphinxhyphen{}number\sphinxhyphen{}or\sphinxhyphen{}positional\sphinxhyphen{}fallback — see the note above.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rows with an invalid \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}} are dropped; missing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(x, y)}} cells fill to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}


\subparagraph{See Also}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

aggregated\sphinxhyphen{}value grid, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_surface = true}} producing a visually similar mesh.

\item {}

{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot/heatmap::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotAccessor::heatmap}}}}}}}: the 2D counterpart,
reusing the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}\sphinxhyphen{}based grouped mode.

\end{itemize}
