\subparagraph{What It Does}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/wireframe:what-it-does}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws the same aggregated 3D grid as {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{y\_feature}}’s distinct
values as rows, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\_feature}}’s distinct values as columns, each cell aggregating
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{z\_feature}} via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} — but rendered as a \sphinxstylestrong{wireframe mesh} (grid edges only) instead of a
filled, continuous surface. Every construction detail (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}} call, the
grid\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate resolution, the restricted set of supported \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} values, the dropped\sphinxhyphen{}row
and zero\sphinxhyphen{}fill behavior) is identical to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}; only the final trace call differs
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flash::lattice(...)}} here instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flash::sheet(...)}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}} for the full explanation of how the grid is built, and
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}} for the shared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}}\sphinxhyphen{}return / no\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cout}} mechanics and the full
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DSceneOptions}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Plot3DTraceOptions}} layering explanation.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same op restriction as surface()
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}} accepts the same 7 of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}}’s 10 values that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}} does —
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mode}} throw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"DataFrame::pivot\_table: unsupported aggregation op"}}. See
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}}’s important callout for the full explanation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subparagraph{Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/wireframe:parameters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{x\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
Feature whose distinct values become the grid’s columns (x\sphinxhyphen{}axis) — see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}}’s note on grid\sphinxhyphen{}coordinate resolution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{y\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
Feature whose distinct values become the grid’s rows (y\sphinxhyphen{}axis).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{z\_feature} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{std::string\_view}})
Feature aggregated into each grid cell’s height.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{op} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}}, default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mean}})
The aggregation applied per cell — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}}’s important callout
for which values are actually supported.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Wireframe3DPlotOptions}})
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cpp     struct Wireframe3DPlotOptions \{       Plot3DSceneOptions scene\{\};       Plot3DTraceOptions trace\{\};     \};     }}
The same shared structs documented in full on {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wireframe()}} has no
fields of its own beyond these two. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Wireframe}} trace preset (tuned lighting/shading
for mesh edges) is available via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{options.trace.preset}}.


\subparagraph{Returns}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/wireframe:returns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}
A figure with one 3D pane containing a single wireframe\sphinxhyphen{}mesh trace over the aggregated
grid.

\subparagraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/wireframe:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every construction detail is shared with {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{surface()}}}}}}} — only the final
trace shape differs (mesh edges vs. a filled surface).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only 7 of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}}’s 10 values are supported; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Std}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Var}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Mode}} throw.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}} — see {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/line::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line()}}}}}}}’s important callout for how to
view or save the result.

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/wireframe:see-also}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api/dataframe-plot3d/surface::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlot3DAccessor::surface}}}}}}}: the identical grid, rendered as a
filled continuous mesh instead of edges.

\item {}

aggregated\sphinxhyphen{}value grid, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_wireframe = true}} producing a visually similar mesh.

\subsubsection{DataFrame Display And Popup Viewer}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:dataframe-display-and-popup-viewer}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display::doc}}

\paragraph{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic supports two display paths for table\sphinxhyphen{}style inspection:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
terminal rendering

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
popup rendering through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The popup viewer is opt\sphinxhyphen{}in.
Nothing opens automatically unless the user explicitly calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}}.


\paragraph{Which Methods Support \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.show()}}}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:which-methods-support-show}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}} is available on methods that return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::table::DataFrameView}}.
Those are the table\sphinxhyphen{}rendering methods.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Current examples include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view()}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot()}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table()}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count\_by()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean\_by()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resample()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{               }\PYG{c+c1}{// terminal preview}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{// popup if available, else terminal fallback}

\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{c+c1}{// terminal preview}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// popup if available, else terminal fallback}

\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{avg\PYGZus{}sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{GroupOp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a method returns a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, then it does not participate in this deferred popup\sphinxhyphen{}preview flow.


\paragraph{How The Display Policy Works}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:how-the-display-policy-works}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The behavior is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{// prints in the terminal}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// suppresses terminal auto\PYGZhy{}preview and requests popup instead}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This works because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe()}}, and the other preview verbs return a lightweight \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}.
That wrapper delays the terminal render until the expression ends.
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}} is called first, the pending terminal render is consumed and the popup path is used instead.


\paragraph{What \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.show()}} Takes}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:what-show-takes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The primary overload is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{view}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is also an overload that accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DisplayOptions}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DisplayOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{view}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is also a stream\sphinxhyphen{}oriented overload:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{view}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In practice, the appropriate argument for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DisplayOptions}}.


\paragraph{Useful \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{DisplayOptions}}}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:useful-displayoptions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The most relevant display options for popup/table preview are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backend}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{viewer\_width}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{viewer\_height}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window\_title}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{html\_sortable}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{html\_search}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{html\_copy\_button}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DisplayOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{viewer\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1440}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{viewer\PYGZus{}height}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{900}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{html\PYGZus{}search}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{html\PYGZus{}sortable}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Notes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backend = DisplayBackend::Terminal}} forces terminal rendering

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}} policy prefers the built\sphinxhyphen{}in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussWebView}} renderer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backend = DisplayBackend::NativeWebView}} explicitly requests the platform web view

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backend = DisplayBackend::PlussWebView}} explicitly requires the built\sphinxhyphen{}in renderer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window\_title}} is available, but for most users the better pattern is to name the frame with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{title(...)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{title\_(...)}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicit native\sphinxhyphen{}renderer example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DisplayOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{backend}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DisplayBackend}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NativeWebView}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{opts}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{DataFrame Titles}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:dataframe-titles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Frames can carry display metadata:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{title}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{prices}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or mutate in place:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{title\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{prices}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Behavior:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
untitled frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame \sphinxhyphen{} head}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
untitled frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame \sphinxhyphen{} describe}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
titled frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prices \sphinxhyphen{} head}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
titled frame: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prices \sphinxhyphen{} describe}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The title is replaceable metadata.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{title\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{some title}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{title\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{some other title}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Immutable behavior:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{title}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{prices}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// df unchanged}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{prices}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{title}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{derived}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{// prices unchanged}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{OS Support}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:os-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Current popup support is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
macOS: built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView and native WebKit

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Linux: built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView through X11/XWayland, with native WebKitGTK optional

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Windows: built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView through Win32, with native WebView2 optional

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}} policy tries PlussWebView first, then the available native
platform backend. If neither popup backend is available, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}} falls back
to the normal terminal rendering path.


\paragraph{macOS Backend}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:macos-backend}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On macOS, the popup viewer uses native Apple frameworks:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Cocoa}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WebKit}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QuartzCore}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UniformTypeIdentifiers}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
That means the current macOS popup path does not depend on Conda GUI packages.
It uses OS\sphinxhyphen{}provided frameworks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Practical consequence:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a Conda environment is fine for the compiler/toolchain

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the popup viewer itself is not coming from Conda on macOS

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Linux Backend}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:linux-backend}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default Linux popup uses the built\sphinxhyphen{}in renderer in a direct X11 or
XWayland window. It does not require GTK or WebKitGTK. FreeType is used for
native\sphinxhyphen{}quality text when it is available, and XInput2 provides high\sphinxhyphen{}resolution
touchpad and mouse\sphinxhyphen{}wheel input when it is available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Typical packages for building the staged SDK, or linking a downstream
application to the current static SDK, are:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ubuntu:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }libx11\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }libxi\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }libfreetype\PYGZhy{}dev
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fedora:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }dnf\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }libX11\PYGZhy{}devel\PYG{+w}{ }libXi\PYGZhy{}devel\PYG{+w}{ }freetype\PYGZhy{}devel
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The staged application needs an X11 server or XWayland at runtime. A
Wayland\sphinxhyphen{}only session with XWayland disabled cannot currently open the built\sphinxhyphen{}in
window; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}} then tries the optional native backend before falling back to
terminal output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
GTK and WebKitGTK are needed only when building and explicitly selecting
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DisplayBackend::NativeWebView}}.


\paragraph{Windows Status}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:windows-status}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The default Windows popup uses the built\sphinxhyphen{}in renderer in a native Win32 window.
It uses Windows system APIs for windowing, input, clipboard, saving, and text,
so neither the WebView2 SDK nor the WebView2 Runtime is required for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.show()}}.


\paragraph{Windows Build Setup}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:windows-build-setup}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No additional viewer SDK is required for the built\sphinxhyphen{}in Windows renderer. A
normal staged Pluss SDK built for the target architecture includes it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
WebView2 remains an optional native web\sphinxhyphen{}view backend. To build it, Pluss looks
for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cache variable: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PLUSSTILS\_VIEW\_WEBVIEW2\_SDK\_DIR}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
environment variable: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WEBVIEW2\_SDK\_DIR}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
common NuGet cache location under the user profile

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Typical configure command:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}S\PYG{+w}{ }.\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}B\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZca{}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}DPLUSSTILS\PYGZus{}VIEW\PYGZus{}WEBVIEW2\PYGZus{}SDK\PYGZus{}DIR\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}C:/path/to/Microsoft.Web.WebView2.\PYGZlt{}version\PYGZgt{}\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Disabling WebView2 does not disable the built\sphinxhyphen{}in popup:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}S\PYG{+w}{ }.\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}B\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DPLUSSTILS\PYGZus{}VIEW\PYGZus{}ENABLE\PYGZus{}WINDOWS\PYGZus{}WEBVIEW2\PYG{o}{=}OFF
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
What the SDK directory should contain:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build/native/include/WebView2.h}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build/native/x64/WebView2LoaderStatic.lib}}
or the equivalent \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x86}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arm64}} loader library for the target architecture

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Conda On Windows}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:conda-on-windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conda can provide the compiler and normal dependencies. The default popup
itself comes from the built\sphinxhyphen{}in renderer and Windows system APIs. WebView2 is
relevant only when the optional native backend is requested.


\paragraph{Are The Popup Windows Native}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:are-the-popup-windows-native}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Partly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The host window is native to the selected presentation backend:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView on macOS: Cocoa window with software\sphinxhyphen{}rendered content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView on Linux: X11/XWayland window with software\sphinxhyphen{}rendered content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView on Windows: Win32 window with software\sphinxhyphen{}rendered content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
native macOS backend: Cocoa window with embedded WebKit

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
native Linux backend: GTK window with embedded WebKitGTK

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
native Windows backend: Win32 window with embedded WebView2

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussWebView parses and renders the supported HTML/CSS itself. Native backends
render the same document inside the platform web view.

\sphinxAtStartPar
So the actual behavior is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
window chrome feels native to the OS/toolkit

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
table content stays visually consistent across platforms because it is HTML\sphinxhyphen{}driven

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Conda Notes}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:conda-notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conda support differs by platform.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
macOS:
no GTK/WebKitGTK package is needed for the current implementation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Linux:
built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView needs the standard X11 runtime (or XWayland); FreeType
is used when available for native\sphinxhyphen{}quality fonts. GTK/WebKitGTK is needed only
when explicitly selecting the native web\sphinxhyphen{}view backend

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Windows:
built\sphinxhyphen{}in PlussWebView uses Windows system APIs and does not require WebView2.
The WebView2 SDK and Runtime are needed only for the optional native backend

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Recommended User Guidance}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_display:recommended-user-guidance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simplest explanation for users is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{          }\PYG{c+c1}{// terminal}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// popup if supported, else terminal}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If they want better popup titles:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{DataFrame Benchmark Results}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_benchmarks:dataframe-benchmark-results}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe_benchmarks::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This gate compares equivalent PlussMic and pandas workloads for alignment,
grouping, key unification, wide\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}long reshaping, fixed windows, and covariance.
It is a reproducible engineering benchmark, not a claim that the two runtimes
have identical allocation, caching, or process\sphinxhyphen{}startup behavior.


\paragraph{Reproduce}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_benchmarks:reproduce}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYGZus{}cpp\PYGZus{}env\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}target\PYG{+w}{ }plussmic\PYGZus{}table\PYGZus{}gap\PYGZus{}benchmark
conda\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}n\PYG{+w}{ }cpp\PYGZus{}env\PYG{+w}{ }python\PYG{+w}{ }PlussMic/benchmarks/compare\PYGZus{}dataframe\PYGZus{}ops.py\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rows\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1000000}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }PlussMic/benchmarks/latest\PYGZus{}dataframe\PYGZus{}ops.json
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Latest million\sphinxhyphen{}case run}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe_benchmarks:latest-million-case-run}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

because the repeated\sphinxhyphen{}key fixture produces 10 million joined rows.

\label{\detokenize{quickstart:terminal-vs-popup-preview}}

Table preview methods such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}

\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{preview}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// preview is a DataFrameView}
\PYG{n}{preview}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{              }\PYG{c+c1}{// explicit popup/terminal fallback}

\chapter{PlussMic User Manual}
\label{\detokenize{manual:plussmic-user-manual}}\label{\detokenize{manual::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual is the long\sphinxhyphen{}form guide for PlussMic, the data\sphinxhyphen{}analysis layer of the
Pluss ecosystem. It is written for readers who want to use PlussMic as a daily
tool, not only look up signatures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic has three related models:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
table  \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} DataFrame, Thread, Atlas
kindle \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Stream, Catalog, Archive
bundle \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Slot, Registry, Aisle
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most users start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, because it is the table abstraction used for
CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet, feature engineering, exploratory analysis, plotting,
and export. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is the typed column model underneath \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}
stacks related frames. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kindle}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bundle}} are lower\sphinxhyphen{}level record/stream
models used when the data is not naturally just a rectangular table.


\section{How to read this manual}
\label{\detokenize{manual:how-to-read-this-manual}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read Part I and Part II in order. After that, jump to the chapters that match
your task:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading files: Part III.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading and saving files: Part IV.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cleaning and transforming tables: Part V.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Column\sphinxhyphen{}level operations: Part VI.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query expressions and SQL: Part VII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Time series: Part VIII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Plotting: Part IX.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multi\sphinxhyphen{}frame Atlas data: Part X.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kindle and Bundle models: Part XI and Part XII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recipes: Part XIII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Production debugging: Part XIV.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The API reference pages remain the authority for exact overload lists. This
manual explains how to choose and combine those APIs.


\section{Example policy}
\label{\detokenize{manual:example-policy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual does not use one token example per feature. Important APIs are
shown in several contexts: a minimal call, a realistic workflow, option and
error cases, and combinations with adjacent APIs. A short example teaches the
shape of a call; later examples teach how to use it in a program.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In\sphinxhyphen{}memory frames are created directly when the lesson is about table
operations. I/O chapters use files such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sales.csv"}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"transactions.parquet"}}, assumed to be in the program’s working directory.
The manual shows the relevant input file contents before the code. Public
examples never contain paths from the author’s machine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pluss values are passed directly where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} conversion is implicit:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{7.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} construction appears only when the example needs Thread
metadata, a validity mask, or a named standalone column.


\section{Verified examples}
\label{\detokenize{manual:verified-examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Examples marked as verified are backed by this source file:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
PlussMic/docs/sphinx/manual/examples/plussmic\PYGZus{}manual\PYGZus{}examples.cpp
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is compiled as an external SDK consumer with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}S\PYG{+w}{ }PlussMic/docs/sphinx/manual/examples\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}B\PYG{+w}{ }/tmp/plussmic\PYGZus{}manual\PYGZus{}examples\PYGZus{}build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}DCMAKE\PYGZus{}PREFIX\PYGZus{}PATH\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}/path/to/pluss\PYGZhy{}sdk;/path/to/cpp\PYGZus{}env\PYGZdq{}}

cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build\PYG{+w}{ }/tmp/plussmic\PYGZus{}manual\PYGZus{}examples\PYGZus{}build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}target\PYG{+w}{ }plussmic\PYGZus{}manual\PYGZus{}examples
/tmp/plussmic\PYGZus{}manual\PYGZus{}examples\PYGZus{}build/plussmic\PYGZus{}manual\PYGZus{}examples
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The printed outputs in this manual come from running the exact displayed
operations against the current PlussMic build. A table shown after
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.to\_string()}} is its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_string()}} result; output from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show()}}, or
another renderer is never substituted. When output reveals surprising
behavior, the source and tests are checked first; source\sphinxhyphen{}level defects are
fixed before the manual teaches the behavior as correct.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Part I: Orientation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:part-i-orientation}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic exists to make C++ data work practical. It gives you table loading,
typed columns, missing\sphinxhyphen{}data handling, display, summarization, plotting,
time\sphinxhyphen{}series operations, and conversions into more general record models.


\subsubsection{What PlussMic is for}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:what-plussmic-is-for}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use PlussMic when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
load CSV, TXT, Excel, JSON, or Parquet data into C++;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
inspect and summarize a dataset;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
select, rename, reorder, assign, and transform features;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filter cases with masks or query expressions;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
handle missing numeric, text, and time values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group, aggregate, pivot, and correlate data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
build plotting outputs from table data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
represent a stack of related tables with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
convert rectangular data into stream/catalog or registry/slot models;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
save cleaned data back to common file formats.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{The core table model}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:the-core-table-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic uses this table hierarchy:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Atlas \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} DataFrame \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Thread \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Series / Note / Timeline / TimeIndex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} owns feature names and feature columns. Each feature is a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} wraps one core PlussQit payload kind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} for numeric and boolean data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} for text data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} for datetime\sphinxhyphen{}like data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} for time\sphinxhyphen{}index data.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This design is why a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} can contain numeric, text, and time features
without losing type\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations.


\subsubsection{Cases and features}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:cases-and-features}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic documentation uses two axis names:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{case} is a row\sphinxhyphen{}like observation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{feature} is a column\sphinxhyphen{}like variable.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Common shape calls:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rows}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ncases}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cols}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{nfeatures}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{names}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this language when reading APIs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(...)}} selects or returns columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_study(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{observe(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(...)}} operate in row space.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{relabel().set(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\_cases(...)}} manage the case axis.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Functional style}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:functional-style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most table operations return a new object:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cleaned}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cleaned}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{balance}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Mutating operations use a trailing underscore:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rename\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{old\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{new\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer the non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating form while learning. Use mutating methods only when you
intentionally want to update an owned object.


\subsubsection{What a beginner should learn first}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:what-a-beginner-should-learn-first}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load a CSV with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_csv}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inspect with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select features with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter cases with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Derive features with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Summarize with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet}}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Everything else in PlussMic builds on those ideas.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Part II: Installation, Includes, and Build Setup}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:part-ii-installation-includes-and-build-setup}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic is usually consumed through the Pluss SDK. In a downstream project,
link \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pluss::SDK}} and include either the Pluss umbrella header or the PlussMic
module header.


\subsubsection{Recommended include}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:recommended-include}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For applications:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For code that only wants PlussMic:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/mic.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}pluss/mic.h\textgreater{}}} includes table, loader, Kindle, and Bundle surfaces:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/bundle/bundle.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/kindle/kindle.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/loader/loader.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/table/table.h\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It also includes PlussPl when available, which enables table plotting.


\subsubsection{Minimal consumer CMake}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:minimal-consumer-cmake}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cmake\PYGZus{}minimum\PYGZus{}required}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{VERSION}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{3.28}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{project}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{plussmic\PYGZus{}app}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{LANGUAGES}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{CXX}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}STANDARD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}STANDARD\PYGZus{}REQUIRED}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{ON}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}EXTENSIONS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{OFF}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{find\PYGZus{}package}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{Pluss}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{CONFIG}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{REQUIRED}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{add\PYGZus{}executable}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{plussmic\PYGZus{}app}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{main.cpp}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{target\PYGZus{}link\PYGZus{}libraries}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{plussmic\PYGZus{}app}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{PRIVATE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{Pluss::SDK}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Configure against a staged SDK:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}S\PYG{+w}{ }.\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}B\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DCMAKE\PYGZus{}PREFIX\PYGZus{}PATH\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/pluss\PYGZhy{}sdk
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build\PYG{+w}{ }build

\subsubsection{Development build inside this repository}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:development-build-inside-this-repository}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
From the repository root:

PlussMic/examples/bundle/

\subsubsection{Header choices}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:header-choices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use broad headers while learning:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use module headers for production libraries with tighter dependencies:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/mic.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/table/table.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/loader/loader.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/kindle/kindle.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/bundle/bundle.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use source\sphinxhyphen{}local headers only when working inside the Pluss repository.

\subsection{Part III: The Table Model}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:part-iii-the-table-model}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This part explains how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}
relate. Understanding these types makes the rest of PlussMic predictable.


\subsubsection{Thread}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:thread}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is one typed column. It can hold one of four payload kinds:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{numeric}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{red}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{green}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{blue}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dates}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}timeline}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}02T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}03T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Inspect a thread:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{defined}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Access the payload only after you know the kind:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadKind}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Series}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{as\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Missingness and validity}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:missingness-and-validity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} can carry a validity mask. Loader\sphinxhyphen{}created columns use this to represent
missing values from input files.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{missing}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{present}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{notnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filled}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{complete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric threads also support \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnan}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isfinite}}.


\subsubsection{DataFrame}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:dataframe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} is a set of named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} features with an optional case axis.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{region}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{north}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{south}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{12.5}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Cases}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:cases}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The case axis is the row label/index axis. It may be default integer labels or
loaded from a feature.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first\PYGZus{}ten}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}study}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indexed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reset}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indexed}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{reset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set("id", true)}} uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} as the case axis and drops it from features.

\subsubsection{Atlas}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Atlas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{atlas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{january}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{february}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} for:
\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
time\sphinxhyphen{}sliced frames;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
multi\sphinxhyphen{}sheet workbook\sphinxhyphen{}like data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3D plotting and depth aggregation.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Part IV: Loading and Saving Data}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:part-iv-loading-and-saving-data}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic has two public I/O styles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_*}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.save\_*}} convenience methods.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::loader::*}} functions and option structs for lower\sphinxhyphen{}level control.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most users should start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} convenience methods.


\subsubsection{CSV}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:csv}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimal CSV load:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{data.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the correct first call when the file is a conventional comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated
file with a header row. PlussMic reads the header, infers feature types, creates
default numeric case labels, and returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The loader has two public configuration styles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
initializer\sphinxhyphen{}list config entries, which are compact and convenient;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
typed option structs, which are explicit and better for production code.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Limit cases and select features with config entries:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{bank\PYGZhy{}full.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ncases}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{features}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{age}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{job}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{balance}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{duration}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{;}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ncases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{job}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Warn}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{bank\PYGZhy{}full.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} when the ingestion behavior matters. It is easier to
read in code review, safer to extend, and maps directly to the source\sphinxhyphen{}level CSV
loader API.


\subsubsection{CSV mental model}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:csv-mental-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV loading has five stages:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read records from the source.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide the header and feature names.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide which input columns become features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide whether one input column becomes the case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert selected columns into typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} values.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most surprising loading behavior comes from mixing up stages 3 and 4. If a
column is selected as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}}, it becomes the DataFrame case axis and is not
also emitted as a normal feature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ReadCsvOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} column is still used, but it is used as the case axis. The output
features are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}.


\subsubsection{Header handling}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:header-handling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For ordinary files:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header\PYGZus{}row}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For files without a header:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{names}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}} is false and you do not provide names, PlussMic generates feature
names from column positions. For durable code, provide \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header\_row}} when the actual header is not the first physical row:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header\PYGZus{}row}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rows before the header row are skipped from data interpretation.


\subsubsection{Feature projection}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:feature-projection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use names when the file has stable headers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use indices when working with headerless files or unstable external labels:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats\_idx}} are empty, all non\sphinxhyphen{}case columns are
loaded. If a requested name is missing, loading fails. If a requested index is
out of range, loading fails.


\subsubsection{Case columns}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:case-columns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The case axis is PlussMic’s row\sphinxhyphen{}label axis. It is similar to an index in other
dataframe libraries, but the public method names use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a named case column:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a positional case column:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After loading, inspect the case axis:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Move a case axis back into the feature axis later with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}id\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{reset}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{case dtype=}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Type inference and explicit dtypes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:type-inference-and-explicit-dtypes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV data starts as text. PlussMic converts each selected column into a typed
Thread. Common inferred outputs are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
integer Series for integral values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
floating Series for decimal values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
boolean Series for configured true/false tokens;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note for general text;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Timeline or TimeIndex when date parsing is requested.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default boolean token sets include values such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{yes}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{no}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype}} when a column must have a specific interpretation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{customer\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{string}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{int64}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{float64}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parse\_dates}} when text columns should become time payloads:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{parse\PYGZus{}dates}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{created\PYGZus{}at}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{updated\PYGZus{}at}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infer\PYGZus{}datetime\PYGZus{}format}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dayfirst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use explicit dtypes for identifiers that look numeric. Postal codes, account
numbers, and product IDs should usually be loaded as text, not numbers.


\subsubsection{Missing values}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:missing-values}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV missing\sphinxhyphen{}value handling is controlled by:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{na\PYGZus{}filter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}default\PYGZus{}na}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{na\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{insert}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{missing}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{na\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{insert}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{N/A}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{na\_filter = false}} disables missing\sphinxhyphen{}value detection. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_default\_na = true}}
keeps the built\sphinxhyphen{}in missing tokens. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{na\_values}} adds project\sphinxhyphen{}specific tokens.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Missingness becomes a Thread validity mask. That means a numeric feature can
still have an integer or floating dtype even when some rows display as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NA}}.


\subsubsection{Bad lines}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:bad-lines}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Malformed rows are rows whose field count does not match the expected layout.
The policy is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Error}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Warn}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Skip}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Error}} for production ingestion when malformed data should stop the job.
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Warn}} when you want diagnostics and can tolerate dropped rows. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Skip}}
only when silent row loss is acceptable in that context.


\subsubsection{Engine selection}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:engine-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The CSV engine can be selected explicitly:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{CsvCaseReader::next}}}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:csvcasereader-next}}

\paragraph{API Signature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:api-signature}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
CsvCaseReader::next(output: DataFrame\PYGZam{}) \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} bool
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads the next bounded case batch. The first emitted batch establishes the
inferred feature kinds and numeric dtypes. A later inferred schema change fails
if conversion to that schema would discard an observed value; compatible batches,
including all\sphinxhyphen{}null batches, are converted to the established schema. Supply
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions::dtype}} when a source column contains mixed lexical forms.


\paragraph{Inputs}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:inputs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{output: DataFrame\&}}
Destination replaced with the next batch when the method returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.


\paragraph{Output}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:output}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} when a batch was emitted and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} after the source is exhausted.


\paragraph{Options}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:options}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Constructor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_batch\_size}} controls the maximum cases per batch.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions::dtype}} fixes feature types across every batch.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions::ncases}} limits the total cases emitted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipcases}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipfooter}} are rejected because they cannot be honored
predictably by this streaming contract.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 1: read every batch.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CsvCaseReader}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reader}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{data.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4096}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{batch}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{while}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{reader}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{next}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{batch}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{batch}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Expected output}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:expected-output}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Each successful iteration contains at most 4096 cases; the loop ends at EOF.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example 2: enforce a text schema.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ReadCsvOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{account}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{string}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CsvCaseReader}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reader}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{data.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2048}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subparagraph{Expected output}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:id1}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
account is Note\PYGZhy{}backed in every emitted batch.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename}} changes one feature name, applies several renames, or replaces the
entire feature axis depending on the overload. Full\sphinxhyphen{}axis renaming requires the
number of new names to match the current feature count. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder}} also requires
the full feature set; it is not a selector. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(\{...\})}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(\{...\})}}
when you want to keep only part of the frame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Practical rule:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename("old", "new")}} for one feature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename(\{\{"old1", "new1"\}, \{"old2", "new2"\}\})}} for many features

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sampled}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sample}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view}} are preview\sphinxhyphen{}oriented and return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample}} return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(start, stop)}} uses half\sphinxhyphen{}open row positions: it keeps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} and stops
before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}. Negative slice bounds are normalized against the frame size by
the implementation. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(indices)}} uses the exact row positions you provide
and keeps them in that order. Both preserve the selected rows’ original case
labels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first table is sorted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{price}} descending. The case labels still show
the original row labels, so the first row displays case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} because Tamale was
the fourth row in the input.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second table is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(1, 3)}}. It keeps row positions 1 and 2 and stops
before position 3. The third table is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(\{3, 0\})}}; it keeps exactly Tamale
then Accra because that is the order of the indices.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fourth table demonstrates feature\sphinxhyphen{}axis work. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename("units", "quantity")}}
changes the feature name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(\{"region"\})}} removes the region feature, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder(\{"city", "price", "quantity"\})}} arranges the full remaining feature
set in the requested order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fifth table shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label().set("city", true)}}. City values become case labels,
and the original \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} feature is removed because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_feature}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.
The sixth table shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{relabel().set("city\_case")}}, which turns the case axis
back into a normal feature named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city\_case}} and restores default numeric case
labels.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} when two frames already have compatible row counts and you want to
append features. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unify}} when rows must be matched by key values. Use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}} when the right frame should patch values into the left frame. Use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine}} when you need the configurable primitive behind \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The names are precise:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} is feature\sphinxhyphen{}wise combination. It requires the same case count and
appends right\sphinxhyphen{}hand features by row position. Duplicate feature names receive
the collision suffix.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}} is schema\sphinxhyphen{}preserving patching. It only updates overlapping features
and ignores right\sphinxhyphen{}hand features that do not exist on the left.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unify}} is key\sphinxhyphen{}based matching. It creates rows for matching key values
and appends right\sphinxhyphen{}hand payload features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine}} is the configurable primitive underneath \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}}. The left frame has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sku}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}}; the patch frame
has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}}. Because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} exists on both sides, PlussMic keeps the
left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} and appends the right feature as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty\_patch}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}} is appended
without renaming.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}}. Only overlapping features are considered, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} is replaced by the patch values and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}} is ignored. This is useful
when the right frame is a correction frame rather than a source of new columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stitch\_on("sku", right, "sku", "\_right")}}. This is the
key\sphinxhyphen{}based operation. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}} appear because those keys exist in both
frames. The right key feature is not duplicated because both key names are
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sku}}. The right \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} collides with the left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}}, so it becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty\_right}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cost}} is appended as a new payload feature.
