\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{unit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TimeUnit}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Months}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TimelineSpanMode}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Complete}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{full\PYGZus{}months}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{span}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TimelineSpanMode}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Boundary}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{crossed\PYGZus{}month\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{span}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimelineSpanMode::Complete}} counts fully completed calendar units. January 31
to February 1 is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} complete months. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimelineSpanMode::Boundary}} counts crossed
calendar labels, so January 31 to February 1 crosses one month boundary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default completion anchor is strict day\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}month matching. If your domain
uses end\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}month accounting rules, opt in explicitly:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mode}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TimelineSpanMode}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Complete}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{anchor}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TimelineSpanAnchor}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{MonthEnd}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{accounting\PYGZus{}months}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{span}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{months}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MonthEnd}}, January 31 to February 29 counts as one complete month, and
February 29 to February 28 in a non\sphinxhyphen{}leap year counts as one complete year when
the unit is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Years}}.

\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{unit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TimeUnit}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BusinessDays}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{closed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TimelineSpanClosed}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Right}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{// (start, end]}
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ExampleCorp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{region}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{CA\PYGZhy{}AB}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{holidays}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}timeline}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}03T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{epoch\PYGZus{}days}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{business\PYGZus{}days}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{start}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{span}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{end}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BusinessCalendar}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{monfri}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BusinessCalendar}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{usa\PYGZus{}federal}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BusinessCalendar}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{canada\PYGZus{}federal}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BusinessCalendar}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{uk\PYGZus{}bank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{business}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{calendar}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BusinessCalendar}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{nyse}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2026}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Built\sphinxhyphen{}in presets intentionally stop at broad federal/national/market calendars.
Provincial, territorial, state, municipal, and employer\sphinxhyphen{}specific calendars can
be expressed by constructing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessCalendar}} with custom holidays. This
keeps the public API from growing a preset for every local jurisdiction.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uk\_bank}} currently means England/Wales bank holidays. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target2}} means Euro
TARGET closing days. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nyse}} means New York Stock Exchange full\sphinxhyphen{}day closures; it
is not the same as U.S. federal holidays.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default business calendar is Monday through Friday, with no holidays. The
default interval is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(start, end{]}}}: exclude the start date, include the end date.
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closed}} to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Left}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Both}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Neither}} when your domain needs a different
convention. Holidays are local epoch\sphinxhyphen{}day labels, so generate them in the same
timezone as the timeline being measured. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BusinessCalendar::timezone}} is
provided, it must match the timeline timezone. Calendar and business spans also
require the left and right timelines to have matching timezones; convert first
when necessary.

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For features \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{close}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{volume}}, that emits:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{close\_lag1}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{close\_lag2}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{close\_lag5}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{volume\_lag1}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{volume\_lag2}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{volume\_lag5}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use lag blocks for supervised learning datasets, event studies, or feature
engineering.

\label{\detokenize{manual/part08_time_series:rolling-blocks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rolling\_block}} creates many rolling features in one pass:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{TsRollingBlockOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{include\PYGZus{}mean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{include\PYGZus{}std}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{include\PYGZus{}min}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}

The output demonstrates several important details:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The first one\sphinxhyphen{}period return is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nan}} because no previous value exists.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The strict two\sphinxhyphen{}row rolling mean is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nan}} for the first row because
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods = 2}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Daily resampling uses the resample labels as DataFrame cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calendar extraction keeps the original case count.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lag blocks create one output feature for each selected feature and lag.

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Production checklist}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part08_time_series:production-checklist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before using a time\sphinxhyphen{}series result in a report, model, or downstream pipeline:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Confirm the time feature is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sort by the time feature before order\sphinxhyphen{}dependent calculations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Know whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{periods}} means rows, not calendar units.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods}} deliberately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide whether early undefined numeric positions should remain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nan}} or be
converted to table missingness.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use resampling when observations need calendar bins.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use reindexing when outputs must match a target schedule.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep the original time feature available unless the resampled labels have
replaced it as cases.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate output row counts after resampling or reindexing.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Common mistakes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part08_time_series:common-mistakes}}

\paragraph{Calling the wrong accessor}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part08_time_series:calling-the-wrong-accessor}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{returns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{returns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose based on the return shape you need.


\paragraph{Treating row periods as calendar periods}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part08_time_series:treating-row-periods-as-calendar-periods}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a one\sphinxhyphen{}row return:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{out}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{returns}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is not necessarily a one\sphinxhyphen{}day return. If the frame has hourly rows, it is a
one\sphinxhyphen{}hour return. If the frame has irregular rows, it is a one\sphinxhyphen{}observation
return. Resample first when the calendar interval matters.


\paragraph{Resampling a non\sphinxhyphen{}time feature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part08_time_series:resampling-a-non-time-feature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fails when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"date"}} is not a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{daily}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{resample}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{D}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fix the schema first:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{cast}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CastSpec}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadCastTarget}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Timeline}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{daily}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fixed}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{label}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{resample}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{D}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Rolling unsorted data}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part08_time_series:rolling-unsorted-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compiles but can be wrong:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}} is not sorted by time, the rolling window follows row order. Sort first:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ArrangeSpec}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ts}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rolling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{WindowStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Part IX: Plotting}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:part-ix-plotting}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic plotting turns a table workflow into a report workflow. You clean a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, choose the features that should become axes, groups, or values, and
receive a PlussPl \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} object that can be inspected, saved, or further
customized. This chapter teaches the table\sphinxhyphen{}level plotting API. It is not a
replacement for the lower\sphinxhyphen{}level PlussPl manual; it is the layer you use when the
data already lives in PlussMic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The most important idea is that PlussMic does not plot directly from a CSV file,
a SQL query, or an aggregation object. It plots from a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}.
That means all the table skills from the earlier chapters still apply:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load the data into a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert columns to the correct \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kind.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clean missing values deliberately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter, aggregate, pivot, or assign features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Call \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot3d()}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas::plot()}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save the returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The plotting API is intentionally high\sphinxhyphen{}level. You ask for a line plot,
histogram, heatmap, scatter matrix, or surface plot, and PlussMic builds the
appropriate PlussPl trace objects.


\subsubsection{Plotting namespaces and includes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:plotting-namespaces-and-includes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most user programs include the umbrella header:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The plotting classes used most often are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{LinePlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScatterPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BarPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{HistPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{HeatmapPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CorrHeatmapPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScatterMatrixPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ParallelPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{AndrewsCurvesPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BootstrapPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BriefPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Scatter3DPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Line3DPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Hist3DPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Surface3DPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Wireframe3DPlotOptions}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pl}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Studio}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::plot()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::plot3d()}} methods return
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::pl::Studio}}. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} is a figure container. It can have one or more
panes, and each pane can contain one or more traces.


\subsubsection{The plotting accessors}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:the-plotting-accessors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There are three user\sphinxhyphen{}facing entry points:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{two\PYGZus{}d}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{two\PYGZus{}d\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{three\PYGZus{}d}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{three\PYGZus{}d\PYGZus{}with\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atlas\PYGZus{}plots}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atlas}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.plot()}} for ordinary 2D charts: line, scatter, bar, histogram,
density, heatmap, correlation, scatter matrix, parallel coordinates, Andrews
curves, radviz, lag plots, autocorrelation, bootstrap plots, pie plots, and
brief table summaries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.plot3d()}} for 3D traces: 3D scatter, 3D line, 3D histogram, surface,
and wireframe.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{atlas.plot()}} when the depth axis matters. An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} contains multiple
frames with compatible shape. That is useful for comparing scenarios, dates,
simulation paths, or model versions.


\subsubsection{What PlussMic expects from the data}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:what-plussmic-expects-from-the-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Plotting methods use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} kinds to decide how a feature can participate in a
plot.


\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering
\begin{tabulary}{\linewidth}[t]{TT}
\sphinxtoprule
\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxstyletheadfamily \sphinxAtStartPar
Thread kind
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
&\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxstyletheadfamily \sphinxAtStartPar
Plotting role
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
\\
\sphinxmidrule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
&\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric y\sphinxhyphen{}values, x\sphinxhyphen{}values, histogram input, heatmap values, correlation input, 3D coordinates.
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
\\
\sphinxhline\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
&\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Labels, categories, hue groups, case labels, and tick labels.
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
\\
\sphinxhline\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
&\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Labeled temporal axes; numeric coordinates are epoch nanoseconds internally.
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
\\
\sphinxhline\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}}
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
&\begin{varwidth}[t]{\sphinxcolwidth{1}{2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Labeled temporal axes through the contained timeline.
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabulary}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most numeric plot families require \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features. If you pass a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}
feature to a method that requires a numeric feature, PlussMic throws an error
instead of silently producing a misleading chart. A few axis paths can cast to
labels because labeled axes are expected to be textual.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The distinction matters. In a CSV file, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2026\sphinxhyphen{}01\sphinxhyphen{}01}} might be inferred as text,
a timeline, or a case label depending on the loader options and schema. A line
plot will behave differently in each case:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{by\PYGZus{}date}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}} is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis uses positional coordinates with rendered
date or datetime tick labels. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}} is a numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis uses
the numeric values directly. If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}} is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis uses positional
coordinates with note tick labels.


\subsubsection{Missing values in plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:missing-values-in-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic keeps table\sphinxhyphen{}level missingness through validity masks. For plotting,
numeric missing values are converted to floating\sphinxhyphen{}point \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} before PlussPl
receives the values. That makes the missing point explicit to the plotting
engine while preserving the original table data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This behavior is useful, but it is not a substitute for cleaning. Before
plotting, decide whether missing values should be dropped, filled, or kept as
gaps:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{report}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{raw}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{timestamp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{volume}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{report}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{volume}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{timestamp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not let plotting be the first time you think about null semantics. For a
production report, missingness is part of the analysis.


\subsubsection{Figure and axis defaults}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:figure-and-axis-defaults}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotOptions}} configures the accessor. It does not mutate the frame.
You pass it once to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot(options)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot3d(options)}}, and every plot created
by that accessor inherits those defaults.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}x\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}hue\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{symbol}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}bins}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{30}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{width}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{900.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{height}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{520.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{use\PYGZus{}tight\PYGZus{}layout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tight\PYGZus{}layout\PYGZus{}padding}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plots}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plots}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{volume}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plots}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{hist}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{volume}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{spread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plots}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{bid}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ask}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In that example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{line("close")}} uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"date"}} as the x feature because
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_x\_feature}} is set. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter("bid", "ask")}} uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"symbol"}} as the hue
feature because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default\_hue\_feature}} is set and no hue feature was passed to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scatter}}.

\subsubsection{Line plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:line-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a line plot when the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis has an ordering and the y feature changes over
that order. Common examples include prices over dates, cumulative quantities
over event number, or metrics over training step.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For multiple y features, pass an initializer list:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{open}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{high}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{low}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each y feature becomes one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Trend}} trace. If there is more than one y feature,
the pane shows a legend. The y\sphinxhyphen{}axis label is the feature name for a single y
feature and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"value"}} for multiple y features.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Stacked area plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:stacked-area-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a stacked area plot when the y features are components of a total:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{area\PYGZus{}stacked}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{desktop}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{mobile}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{tablet}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

All y features should be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative unless you have a very specific reason to
stack signed values. The implementation builds cumulative heights from the

later features stack on top.

\subsubsection{Scatter plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:scatter-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a scatter plot to inspect relationships between two numeric features.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{temperature}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add a hue feature to split the points into groups:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{temperature}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{region}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or configure a default hue feature once:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}hue\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{region}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{temperature}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When hue is used, PlussMic creates one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Cloud}} trace per hue label. Hue features
should be \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} threads. The typical hue feature is
a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} category such as region, class, symbol, status, or cohort.

\subsubsection{Pie plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:pie-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a pie plot when values are parts of a whole and the number of categories is
small:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{pie}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{revenue}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{region}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value\_feature}} must be numeric. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_feature}} is optional. If the label
feature is omitted, PlussMic uses generated labels.

\subsubsection{Heatmaps}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:heatmaps}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic has two heatmap styles:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Feature matrix heatmaps.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pivot heatmaps.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A feature matrix heatmap uses several numeric features as columns and cases as
rows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{heatmap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{bid}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ask}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{mid}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A pivot heatmap uses three columns: row category, column category, and numeric
value:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{heatmap}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maturity}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{delta\PYGZus{}bucket}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{implied\PYGZus{}vol}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{GroupOp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The pivot form groups repeated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(case\_feature, feature\_feature)}} pairs using the
requested \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}}. The default operation is mean.

\subsubsection{Correlation heatmaps}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:correlation-heatmaps}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr\_heatmap()}} to visualize pairwise correlations among numeric features:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}heatmap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{open}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{high}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{low}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you pass no features, PlussMic uses all numeric \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} features:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr\PYGZus{}heatmap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Scatter matrices}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:scatter-matrices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a scatter matrix to inspect pairwise relationships among several numeric
features:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sepal\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{                                     }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{petal\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{petal\PYGZus{}width}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default full matrix can become large. For compact reports, render only the
lower triangle:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScatterMatrixPlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corner}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also configure the underlying PlussPl pair plot options:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScatterMatrixPlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{triangle}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScatterMatrixTriangle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Lower}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{pair}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{auto\PYGZus{}tick\PYGZus{}decimals}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Lag plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:lag-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a lag plot to compare a feature against a shifted version of itself:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

period:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}points}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2500}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lag}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BootstrapPlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{samples}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{bins}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{30}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{statistic}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BootstrapStatistic}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Median}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{bootstrap}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{latency\PYGZus{}ms}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Auto plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:auto-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{auto\_plot()}} chooses a simple plot based on the selected numeric features:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{auto\PYGZus{}plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{y}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Auto plotting is useful for exploration and examples. For production reports,
prefer an explicit plot family so a schema change does not silently change the
visual design.


\subsubsection{3D plotting}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:d-plotting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot3d()}} returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlot3DAccessor}}. It shares the top\sphinxhyphen{}level
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFramePlotOptions}} for figure size and layout, then each 3D method accepts
family\sphinxhyphen{}specific options.

\paragraph{Surfaces and wireframes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:surfaces-and-wireframes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a surface when x and y coordinates define a grid or a pivotable set of
points:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{surface}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{strike}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maturity}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{implied\PYGZus{}vol}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a wireframe for the same data when the grid structure matters more than the
filled surface:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{wireframe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{strike}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maturity}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{implied\PYGZus{}vol}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both methods accept a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::GroupOp}} for repeated coordinate pairs:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot3d}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{surface}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{strike}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maturity}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{implied\PYGZus{}vol}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{GroupOp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Mean}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Surface3DPlotOptions}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Wireframe3DPlotOptions}} contain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scene}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trace}}
option groups.

\subsubsection{Atlas plotting}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:atlas-plotting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}} is a stack of frames. Plotting an atlas is useful when the depth
dimension is meaningful:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scenarios}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{base}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{stress}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{upside}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Atlas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{atlas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{base}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{stressed}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{optimistic}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{scenarios}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{atlas}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{revenue}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Good atlas plotting cases include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
scenarios in risk analysis;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
repeated simulations;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one frame per model version;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one frame per date or reporting period;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
one frame per cohort.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The same data hygiene rules apply. The frames should have compatible features,
case counts, and feature meanings. If the depth labels are meaningful, keep them
as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} data so plots and legends can explain the
depth axis.


\subsubsection{Exporting plots}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:exporting-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Studio}} can be saved directly:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}pdf}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close.pdf}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}png}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close.png}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{180}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use SVG for documentation, web pages, and source\sphinxhyphen{}controlled report assets. Use
PDF for print workflows. Use PNG when the target system cannot render vector
graphics or when you need a fixed raster result.

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can also get serialized output in memory:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{svg}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pdf}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pdf}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{filesystem}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{create\PYGZus{}directories}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}svg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{out\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ohlc\PYGZhy{}corr.svg}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Production plotting checklist}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:production-plotting-checklist}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before sending a plot to users, check:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The frame is sorted when the plot depends on order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missing values are intentionally dropped, filled, or left as gaps.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric features are really \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} threads.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Categorical labels are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} threads or are safely convertible to labels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Large datasets are sampled or aggregated before high\sphinxhyphen{}density plots.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Long category labels use rotated ticks or horizontal bars.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{width}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{height}}, and tight layout are set for the target document.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Export format matches the destination: SVG/PDF for vector, PNG for raster.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The plot can be regenerated from source data and code.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Common plotting failures}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:common-plotting-failures}}

\paragraph{Missing feature names}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:missing-feature-names}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fails:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{x}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{missing\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The accessor asks the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"missing\_feature"}} and the frame throws.
Check \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df.features()}} before building dynamic plotting code.


\paragraph{Non\sphinxhyphen{}numeric features in numeric methods}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:non-numeric-features-in-numeric-methods}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This fails when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}} is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{hist}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{status}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A histogram needs numeric values. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bar()}} on an aggregated count table, or
encode the category intentionally before plotting numeric distributions.


\paragraph{Unsorted time series}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:unsorted-time-series}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This compiles but may lie:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{df}} is not sorted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}}, the line connects points in row order. Sort
first:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ArrangeSpec}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{line}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Too many labels}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:too-many-labels}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When an axis has labels, PlussMic samples labeled ticks using
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_labeled\_ticks}}. If you still have crowding, rotate ticks or aggregate:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFramePlotOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}labeled\PYGZus{}ticks}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{When to use PlussPl directly}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part09_plotting:when-to-use-plusspl-directly}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the DataFrame plotting API when the chart maps directly from table features.
Use PlussPl directly when you need:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
custom multi\sphinxhyphen{}pane layouts not represented by the DataFrame API;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
manual trace construction;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
custom annotations beyond \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{brief()}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
precise theme and mark control;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
composition of non\sphinxhyphen{}table graphics with table plots.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A good workflow is to use PlussMic for data preparation, then pass the resulting
vectors, labels, or summaries into PlussPl for final composition.

\sphinxstepscope

\subsubsection{Catalog}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part11_kindle:catalog}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}} is a named set of streams. Convert from DataFrame:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kindelize}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Catalog operations include stream selection, mutation, merge, transform, text
preprocessing, and export.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cleaned}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{catalog}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{apply}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{balance}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{kindle}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Stream}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{s}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{s}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cleaned}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}table}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use Catalog when:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stream metadata matters;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
you want named\sphinxhyphen{}stream transformations outside a DataFrame;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
your workflow moves between typed streams and table display;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
text\sphinxhyphen{}oriented catalog operations are useful.

\end{itemize}

Bundle is PlussMic’s heterogeneous record model. It is useful when values are
not naturally represented as one typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}.

\label{\detokenize{manual/part12_bundle:slot}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{Verified output does not match what you expected}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part14_troubleshooting:verified-output-does-not-match-what-you-expected}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The manual examples are compiled and run against the current SDK. If an output
looks surprising, do not assume the manual should normalize it. Check the
source path, add a focused regression test, and fix source\sphinxhyphen{}level defects before
teaching the behavior as correct.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For missing values, the expected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull}} contract is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
existing non\sphinxhyphen{}null values remain unchanged;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
null values in selected features are replaced;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the validity mask is cleared when all null values in the filled thread are
resolved.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When writing production code around missing values, keep a small regression
test for the exact operation and version you depend on.


\subsubsection{Missing values break math}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part14_troubleshooting:missing-values-break-math}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Audit, then fill or drop:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isna}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{clean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{amount}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{complete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{clean}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dropnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Check:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
grouping features have the expected type;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the selected value feature is numeric for numeric operations;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{Plot is empty or too dense}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part14_troubleshooting:plot-is-empty-or-too-dense}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
selected features contain finite values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
x/y features have the same length;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
missing values are handled;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
high\sphinxhyphen{}cardinality groups are aggregated first;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max point options are set for dense plot families.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{date}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{close}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{info}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Excel or Parquet API fails at runtime}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part14_troubleshooting:excel-or-parquet-api-fails-at-runtime}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These formats depend on optional build dependencies. Rebuild the SDK with the
needed dependency available, then rebuild the consumer project.


\subsubsection{Popup display does not open}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part14_troubleshooting:popup-display-does-not-open}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic falls back to terminal display when popup display support is not
available. Use terminal output as the reliable path in headless environments:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{manual/part14_troubleshooting:large-csv-is-slow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Try:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ReadCsvOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{parallel\PYGZus{}threads}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{only}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{needed}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{columns}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{profile}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also avoid loading columns you will drop immediately.


\subsubsection{Production checklist}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part14_troubleshooting:production-checklist}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use typed option structs for non\sphinxhyphen{}trivial I/O.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate schema with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info()}} after loading.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep feature names stable and documented.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide case\sphinxhyphen{}axis semantics early.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating transforms in reusable code.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save cleaned and intermediate outputs in deterministic locations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keep plotting outputs separate from data outputs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use API reference pages for exact overloads.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

\chapter{DataFrame Guide}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe:dataframe-guide}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe::doc}}

\section{What DataFrame Is Good At}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe:what-dataframe-is-good-at}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::table::DataFrame}} is the main table\sphinxhyphen{}analysis surface in PlussMic.
Use it when you want:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
named features with mixed typed columns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a case axis that can be numeric, note\sphinxhyphen{}based, timeline\sphinxhyphen{}based, or time\sphinxhyphen{}index based

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
table verbs such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillnull}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
import/export across CSV, TXT, JSON, Excel, and Parquet

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{dataframe:match-frames-by-cases-and-features}}

Frame\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}frame arithmetic and comparisons match both axes automatically. The
default is a stable union: left\sphinxhyphen{}side case and feature order is retained, then

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{total}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{rules}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{cases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{FrameMatchRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Common}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{rules}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{features}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{FrameMatchRule}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{KeepLeft}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{matched}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{match}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rules}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{total}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{matched}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{matched}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\section{When To Use Kindle Types}
\label{\detokenize{kindle:when-to-use-kindle-types}}

The kindle model is stream\sphinxhyphen{}first:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}: one typed vector plus optional validity mask and case labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}}: named collection of streams

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Archive}}: depth stack of catalogs

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{When To Use Bundle Types}
\label{\detokenize{bundle:when-to-use-bundle-types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The bundle model is the heterogeneous record layer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Slot}}: sequence of heterogeneous Pluss values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Registry}}: named set of slots

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}}: depth stack of registries

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use it when one field can hold different domain types, or when you want a lighter record/batch abstraction than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.
